C1.def: (of a restaurant meal) ordered as separate items from a menu rather than as a fixed set meal
C1.example: We skipped the tasting menu and ordered à la carte instead.
C1.ielts_writing: Restaurants that offer à la carte options tend to attract customers with varied dietary needs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I prefer à la carte because I can choose exactly what I feel like eating."
C1.mistake: Wird als Adjektiv oder Adverb benutzt, nicht als Nomen; also "the à la carte menu", nicht "the a la carte".

C1.def: a bomb whose explosive power comes from nuclear fission
C1.example: The A-bomb was first used in warfare in 1945.
C1.ielts_writing: The development of the A-bomb fundamentally changed international security policy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We visited a museum in Hiroshima that explains what the A-bomb did to the city."
C1.mistake: "A-bomb" ist die Kurzform; in formalen Texten ist "atomic bomb" oder "nuclear weapon" üblicher.

C1.def: having the power, skill, or opportunity to do something; skilled and competent
C1.example: She is an able negotiator who rarely loses her temper.
C1.ielts_writing: Able leadership is essential during periods of economic uncertainty.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I wasn't able to finish the book, but I really liked the first half."
C1.mistake: Nach "be able" folgt der to-Infinitiv ("able to do"), nicht "able for" oder "able of".

C1.def: to formally put an end to a law, system, or practice
C1.example: The country abolished the death penalty in 1998.
C1.ielts_writing: Many economists argue that abolishing tuition fees would widen access to higher education.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I think they should abolish homework for younger kids."
C1.mistake: "abolish" gilt für Gesetze und Systeme, nicht für Termine; einen Termin absagen heißt "cancel".

C1.def: the formal ending of a system, practice, or institution
C1.example: The abolition of child labor transformed working-class families.
C1.ielts_writing: The abolition of the slave trade was a turning point in the history of human rights.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We learned about the abolition of slavery in history class."
C1.mistake: Das Nomen ist "abolition", nicht "abolishment" (selten) und nicht "abolation".

C1.def: the deliberate ending of a pregnancy
C1.example: The debate over abortion remains deeply divisive in many countries.
C1.ielts_writing: Public opinion on abortion varies widely according to religion and region.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Abortion is a topic people often avoid at the dinner table."
C1.mistake: Das Verb "abort" bedeutet auch "abbrechen" (z. B. eine Mission); das Nomen "abortion" bezieht sich nur auf Schwangerschaft.

C1.def: the state of being away from a place, or the fact that something does not exist
C1.example: In his absence, the deputy manager ran the meeting.
C1.ielts_writing: The absence of reliable data makes long-term forecasting difficult.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I noticed his absence right away because he usually sits next to me."
C1.mistake: Die feste Wendung heißt "in the absence of" (mit "the"), nicht "in absence of".

C1.def: not present in a place or at an event
C1.example: Three students were absent because of the flu.
C1.ielts_writing: Social trust is often absent in societies with high levels of corruption.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was absent last week, so I need to catch up."
C1.mistake: Das Verb "absent (oneself)" wird /æbˈsent/ betont, das Adjektiv /ˈæbsənt/; die Betonung unterscheidet die Wortart.

C1.def: so interested in something that you give it all your attention
C1.example: He was so absorbed in his novel that he missed his stop.
C1.ielts_writing: Students who are fully absorbed in a task often retain information longer.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I get completely absorbed in a good puzzle."
C1.mistake: Die Präposition ist "absorbed IN", nicht "absorbed by" (das bedeutet "aufgesaugt von").

C1.def: existing as an idea or concept rather than as something physical
C1.example: Justice is an abstract idea that different cultures define differently.
C1.ielts_writing: Abstract concepts such as freedom are difficult to measure empirically.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I like abstract art because everyone sees something different."
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv und Nomen /ˈæbstrækt/, als Verb (zusammenfassen) /æbˈstrækt/: die Betonung wechselt.

C1.def: wildly unreasonable, illogical, or inappropriate
C1.example: It seemed absurd to wait two hours for a five-minute meeting.
C1.ielts_writing: It would be absurd to expect a single policy to solve such a complex problem.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The price of that coffee was absurd."
C1.mistake: Die Betonung liegt auf der zweiten Silbe (/əbˈsɜːrd/), nicht auf der ersten.

C1.def: a very large quantity of something
C1.example: The valley is known for its abundance of wildflowers in spring.
C1.ielts_writing: An abundance of cheap labor helped the region attract foreign investment.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There was an abundance of food at the wedding."
C1.mistake: Es heißt "an abundance OF" und nicht "abundance with"; "in abundance" steht ohne Artikel am Satzende.

C1.def: the improper use of something, or cruel and violent treatment of a person
C1.example: The charity supports children who have suffered abuse.
C1.ielts_writing: Drug abuse places a considerable burden on public health systems.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Verbal abuse online is a serious problem."
C1.mistake: Aussprache: Nomen mit /s/, Verb mit /z/; wer beide gleich spricht, verändert die Wortart.

C1.def: relating to education and scholarship, especially at college or university level
C1.example: She chose an academic career rather than working in industry.
C1.ielts_writing: Academic performance is strongly linked to access to learning resources.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My brother is more academic than I am; he loves research."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen "an academic" meint es einen Wissenschaftler/eine Wissenschaftlerin, nicht jeden Hochschulabsolventen.

C1.def: a school or institution for specialized training, or a society of scholars
C1.example: He trained at a military academy before joining the navy.
C1.ielts_writing: Art academies have historically shaped how aesthetic standards are defined.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My sister goes to a dance academy after school."
C1.mistake: Die Betonung liegt auf der zweiten Silbe (/əˈkæd-/), anders als bei "academic" (/ˌæk-/).

C1.def: to happen or make something happen faster
C1.example: The company hopes to accelerate the launch by two months.
C1.ielts_writing: Rising temperatures can accelerate the melting of polar ice.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The car accelerated so fast that I felt pressed against my seat."
C1.mistake: Das "cc" wird /ks/ gesprochen (/əkˈsel-/), nicht wie "z" oder "ts".

C1.def: the act of agreeing to receive something, or the willingness to approve of something
C1.example: Her acceptance of the job offer surprised her colleagues.
C1.ielts_writing: Wider acceptance of remote work has reshaped urban commuting patterns.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Acceptance is something I had to learn after moving abroad."
C1.mistake: "Akzeptanz in der Bevölkerung" heißt "public acceptance", nicht "acceptance in the population".

C1.def: able to be reached, entered, used, or understood
C1.example: The museum is fully accessible to visitors in wheelchairs.
C1.ielts_writing: Accessible public transport is a prerequisite for an inclusive city.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I like books that are accessible to ordinary readers, not only experts."
C1.mistake: Die gebräuchliche Präposition ist "accessible TO" (für jemanden), nicht "accessible for".

C1.def: an extra item that adds to the use or appearance of something, or a person who helps in a crime
C1.example: A scarf is a simple accessory that can transform an outfit.
C1.ielts_writing: The market for smartphone accessories shows how deeply mobile devices have become part of daily life.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I never leave the house without at least one accessory, usually a scarf."
C1.mistake: Die Aussprache beginnt mit /æk/ + /s/: "ak-SES-uh-ree", nicht "a-ze-".

C1.def: an award or privilege granted as a special honor or as an acknowledgment of merit
C1.example: The film received numerous accolades at the festival.
C1.ielts_writing: International accolades often bring greater visibility and funding to young researchers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Being named team captain was the biggest accolade of my school years."
C1.mistake: Die Betonung liegt auf der ersten Silbe: /ˈækəleɪd/.

C1.def: a person who helps another person commit a crime
C1.example: The police arrested the thief and his accomplice at the border.
C1.ielts_writing: Courts distinguish between the principal offender and an accomplice when deciding sentences.
C1.ielts_speaking: "In the movie, the hero's best friend turns out to be an accomplice."
C1.mistake: Die zweite Silbe wird betont (/əˈkɑːm-/), das "o" ist kein langes "o".

C1.def: highly skilled or talented, usually after training
C1.example: She is an accomplished pianist who has performed across Europe.
C1.ielts_writing: Accomplished professionals often serve as mentors for younger staff.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My uncle is an accomplished cook, and he never uses a recipe."
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv bedeutet es "begabt, versiert", nicht nur "erreicht"; erledigte Aufgabe: "a task accomplished".

C1.def: something that has been achieved successfully
C1.example: Finishing the marathon was her proudest accomplishment.
C1.ielts_writing: Technological accomplishments should be assessed alongside their social costs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Learning German was a big accomplishment for me."
C1.mistake: Die feste Wendung lautet "a sense of accomplishment", nicht "a feeling of accomplishing".

C1.def: agreement or conformity with a rule, standard, or wish
C1.example: The ceremony was held in accordance with local tradition.
C1.ielts_writing: All research must be conducted in accordance with ethical guidelines.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I did it in accordance with the instructions I was given."
C1.mistake: Fast nur in der Wendung "in accordance WITH", nicht "in accordance to".

C1.def: in a way that is appropriate to the particular circumstances
C1.example: The weather turned cold, and we dressed accordingly.
C1.ielts_writing: Policies should be adjusted accordingly as new evidence emerges.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I told them my budget, and they planned accordingly."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "according to" (laut, gemäß) verwechseln.

C1.def: the fact of being responsible for your decisions and actions
C1.example: Voters expect greater accountability from elected officials.
C1.ielts_writing: Greater accountability in public spending can restore trust in institutions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "In my last job, accountability was a big part of the culture."
C1.mistake: Es geht um moralische oder politische Verantwortung, nicht um "Rechnungslegung" (das wäre "financial reporting").

C1.def: required or expected to justify your actions or decisions
C1.example: Managers must be held accountable for safety failures.
C1.ielts_writing: Elected representatives should remain accountable to the people they serve.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I hold myself accountable for the mistakes I make."
C1.mistake: Präpositionen: "accountable TO" (Person) und "accountable FOR" (Sache).

C1.def: the profession or practice of keeping and checking financial records
C1.example: He studied accountancy and now works for an auditing firm.
C1.ielts_writing: Accountancy requires both accuracy and ethical judgment.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My cousin works in accountancy, and she's always busy in March."
C1.mistake: Gleichbedeutend mit "accounting", das im Alltag häufiger vorkommt; "accountancy" klingt formeller.

C1.def: to gather or build up gradually over time
C1.example: Dust had accumulated on every shelf in the empty house.
C1.ielts_writing: Heavy metals can accumulate in the food chain and harm predators.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I accumulated a lot of books over the years."
C1.mistake: "accumulate" betont den allmählichen Prozess; bei einmaligem Sammeln ist "collect" besser.

C1.def: the gradual gathering of a quantity of something
C1.example: The accumulation of snow closed several mountain roads.
C1.ielts_writing: The accumulation of capital is central to many economic theories.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The accumulation of small tasks made my week exhausting."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der vorletzten Silbe (/-ˈleɪ-/); nicht mit "acclamation" (Beifall) verwechseln.

C1.def: a claim that someone has done something illegal or wrong
C1.example: He denied the accusation and demanded an apology.
C1.ielts_writing: False accusations can permanently damage a person's reputation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I didn't like his accusation that I was lazy."
C1.mistake: Es heißt "accusation OF something", analog "accuse someone OF".

C1.def: the person or people charged with a crime
C1.example: The accused pleaded not guilty.
C1.ielts_writing: The accused has the right to a prompt and fair trial.
C1.ielts_speaking: "In the film, the accused is finally proven innocent."
C1.mistake: Singular und Plural sind gleich: "the accused" (nie "accuseds").

C1.def: to do extremely well, especially in an exam or test
C1.example: She aced her chemistry exam without studying much.
C1.ielts_writing: Candidates who ace the speaking section often practice daily with native speakers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I aced my driving test on the first try."
C1.mistake: Das Nomen "ace" bedeutet "Ass" (Karte/Tennis); als Verb ist es umgangssprachlich.

C1.def: a person who succeeds in what they set out to do
C1.example: Her teachers described her as a quiet achiever.
C1.ielts_writing: High achievers often experience considerable pressure to maintain their performance.
C1.ielts_speaking: "In my family, everyone is a high achiever."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise: "achiever" mit "ie", nicht "achiver"; das "ch" wird /tʃ/ gesprochen.

C1.def: chemically sour, or sharp and bitter in tone; a chemical substance with a pH below 7
C1.example: She made an acid comment about his cooking.
C1.ielts_writing: Acid rain damages forests and freshwater lakes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandmother always made acid remarks about my hair."
C1.mistake: Für den sauren Geschmack nimmt man meist "sour"; "acid" als Adjektiv ist eher fachsprachlich oder bildlich (scharfe Bemerkung).

C1.def: relating to sound, or (of an instrument) not electrically amplified
C1.example: He played an acoustic guitar at the small café.
C1.ielts_writing: Acoustic design in classrooms can improve students' concentration.
C1.mistake: Die Betonung liegt auf der zweiten Silbe (/əˈkuː-/), die erste ist unbetont.

C1.def: a person you know slightly, or knowledge of something
C1.example: She is a business acquaintance, not a close friend.
C1.ielts_writing: Social media blurs the boundary between friends and mere acquaintances.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I met a few acquaintances at the party."
C1.mistake: "acquaintance" ist ein Bekannter, "friend" ist enger; nicht beide gleichsetzen.

C1.def: to accept something reluctantly but without protest
C1.example: Rather than argue, he acquiesced and signed the form.
C1.ielts_writing: Citizens may acquiesce to restrictive measures when they believe public safety is at stake.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I didn't love the idea, but I acquiesced to keep the peace."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "acquiesce IN" oder "TO", nicht "with".

C1.def: the act of obtaining something, or a company or asset bought by another
C1.example: The acquisition of the smaller firm doubled the company's market share.
C1.ielts_writing: Language acquisition in early childhood is faster than in adulthood.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The museum's latest acquisition is a painting from the 1800s."
C1.mistake: "acquisition" ist nicht "Akquise" im Sinne von Kundengewinnung; das heißt "customer acquisition" oder "sales prospecting".

C1.def: to formally declare in court that someone is not guilty
C1.example: The jury acquitted him of all charges.
C1.ielts_writing: Courts must acquit defendants when the evidence is insufficient.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I watched a documentary about a man who was acquitted after ten years in prison."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "acquit someone OF something"; "acquit oneself well" bedeutet "sich gut schlagen".

C1.def: a unit of land area equal to about 4,047 square meters
C1.example: The farm covers about two hundred acres.
C1.ielts_writing: Large areas of rainforest, measured in thousands of acres, are lost each year.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandparents own five acres of land in the countryside."
C1.mistake: Ein Acre entspricht etwa 0,4 Hektar; nicht mit "Hektar" gleichsetzen.

C1.def: spectacular gymnastic feats, or a display of great skill and agility
C1.example: The circus performers amazed the audience with their acrobatics.
C1.ielts_writing: Mental acrobatics are sometimes needed to reconcile conflicting policy goals.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was impressed by the aerial acrobatics at the festival."
C1.mistake: Endet auf -s, ist aber kein Plural; das Adjektiv lautet "acrobatic", die Person "acrobat".

C1.de: nach etwas handeln, auf etwas hin handeln
C1.def: to take action as a result of information, advice, or a decision
C1.example: The council promised to act on the residents' complaints.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments need reliable data before they can act on public-health recommendations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I acted on my friend's advice and applied for the job."
C1.mistake: "act on" bedeutet "handeln aufgrund von"; nicht mit "act for" (jemanden vertreten) verwechseln.

C1.def: the process of making something active or operational
C1.example: The activation of the alarm system took only a few seconds.
C1.ielts_writing: Brain imaging studies show activation of different regions during reading.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I needed an activation code to start the software."
C1.mistake: Das Verb heißt "activate", nicht "active"; das Nomen endet auf "-ation".

C1.def: the use of vigorous campaigning to bring about political or social change
C1.example: Student activism helped bring attention to the housing crisis.
C1.ielts_writing: Online activism lowers the barrier to political participation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She got into activism after seeing how bad the pollution was."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "Aktivität" (activity) gleichsetzen; "activism" ist immer politisch oder gesellschaftlich.

C1.def: a person who campaigns for social or political change
C1.example: Environmental activists blocked the entrance to the factory.
C1.ielts_writing: Activists play a significant role in drawing attention to neglected issues.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My neighbor is an activist and organizes a cleanup every month."
C1.mistake: Das Adjektiv für "aktiv" ist "active"; "activist" ist ein Nomen (Person).

C1.de: Schauspieler und Theaterleiter in einer Person
C1.def: an actor who is also in charge of running a theater company
C1.example: The actor-manager chose the plays, cast the roles, and starred in most of them.
C1.ielts_writing: In the nineteenth century, many leading theaters were run by actor-managers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I read about an actor-manager who ran a famous theater in London."
C1.mistake: Der Begriff gehört vor allem zur Theatergeschichte des 19. Jahrhunderts.

C1.def: (of something bad) severe or intense, or (of a sense) very sharp
C1.example: The city faces an acute shortage of affordable housing.
C1.ielts_writing: Acute pain usually has a clear cause, whereas chronic pain persists for longer.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My dog has an acute sense of smell."
C1.mistake: "acute" (akut, plötzlich) ist das Gegenteil von "chronic" (chronisch); "acute angle" ist ein spitzer Winkel.

C1.def: to a severe or very strong degree
C1.example: She was acutely aware of the silence in the room.
C1.ielts_writing: Developing countries are acutely vulnerable to rising sea levels.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm acutely aware of how much time I waste on my phone."
C1.mistake: Steht meist vor Adjektiven wie "aware" oder "vulnerable"; nicht als einfaches "sehr" benutzen.

C1.def: informal short form of advertisement
C1.example: I saw an ad for a new café on my way to work.
C1.ielts_writing: Targeted ads rely on the collection of large amounts of personal data.
C1.mistake: "ad" ist eine Kurzform von "advertisement" und kein Adverb.

C1.def: refusing to be persuaded or to change your mind
C1.example: He was adamant that he had locked the door before leaving.
C1.ielts_writing: Opposition groups remain adamant that the proposed policy will harm local communities.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My sister is adamant about not moving back home."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "adamant ABOUT sth" oder "adamant THAT + Satz", nicht "adamant to".

C1.def: the process of changing to suit a new situation, or a version of a work made for a different medium
C1.example: The film is an adaptation of a nineteenth-century novel.
C1.ielts_writing: Adaptation to climate change will require changes in farming, housing, and transport.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The adaptation of the book was better than I expected."
C1.mistake: Standard ist "adaptation"; die Form "adaption" ist selten. Nicht mit "adoption" (Annahme) verwechseln.

C1.def: a person who cannot stop doing or using something harmful
C1.example: He became a coffee addict during his exams.
C1.ielts_writing: Treating an addict requires both medical support and social reintegration.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm a bit of a news addict; I check headlines all day."
C1.mistake: Das Verb heißt "to be addicted TO sth", nicht "addicted of"; Nomen /ˈædɪkt/, Verb /əˈdɪkt/ (andere Betonung).

C1.def: the act of adding something, or something that has been added
C1.example: The new wing is a recent addition to the hospital.
C1.ielts_writing: The addition of renewable sources to the national grid has reduced emissions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "In addition to English, I speak a little Spanish."
C1.mistake: Es heißt "in addition TO" + Nomen/Gerund, nicht "in addition of".

C1.def: very skilled at doing something that is difficult
C1.example: She is adept at solving problems under pressure.
C1.ielts_writing: Modern managers must be adept at using digital tools.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm not very adept at cooking, but I'm learning."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "adept AT sth" (auch "in"), nicht "adept for".

C1.def: to stick firmly to a surface or substance
C1.example: The tape adheres to almost any surface.
C1.ielts_writing: Adhesive materials must adhere firmly to both surfaces to ensure a lasting bond.
C1.ielts_speaking: "This sticker doesn't adhere well to glass."
C1.mistake: Im physischen Sinn sagt man meist "stick"; "adhere" klingt technisch und steht mit "to".

C1.def: to follow a rule, standard, or belief closely
C1.example: All staff must adhere to the company's code of conduct.
C1.ielts_writing: Schools must adhere to national curriculum standards.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I try to adhere to my budget every month."
C1.mistake: "adhere to" steht mit abstrakten Objekten (Regeln, Prinzipien); "adhere with" gibt es nicht.

C1.def: next to or very near something
C1.example: The hotel is adjacent to a quiet park.
C1.ielts_writing: Land adjacent to rivers is especially vulnerable to flooding.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My office is adjacent to the kitchen, so it always smells like coffee."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "adjacent TO", nicht "adjacent of"; "adjoining" meint zusätzlich eine direkte Verbindung (z. B. Tür).

C1.def: a small change made to improve something or to cope with a new situation
C1.example: The tailor made a slight adjustment to the jacket.
C1.ielts_writing: Economic adjustment after a crisis often involves difficult budget cuts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It took me a while to make the adjustment to a new city."
C1.mistake: Die Verbindung ist "make an adjustment", nicht "do an adjustment".

C1.def: to manage or organize something, or to give a drug or treatment
C1.example: A nurse administered the medicine every four hours.
C1.ielts_writing: A national agency administers the scholarship program.
C1.mistake: "administer" bedeutet auch "verabreichen" (Medizin), nicht nur "verwalten".

C1.def: relating to the running of an organization or institution
C1.example: The job involves a lot of administrative work.
C1.ielts_writing: Excessive administrative procedures can slow economic growth.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I spend half my day on administrative tasks."
C1.mistake: Die Hauptbetonung liegt auf der zweiten Silbe (-MIN-), nicht auf "-stra-".

C1.def: a person responsible for running an organization or system
C1.example: The hospital administrator announced a new visitor policy.
C1.ielts_writing: School administrators must balance budgets with educational needs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My friend works as a systems administrator."
C1.mistake: Die Endung ist "-or" (administrator), nicht "-er"; Hauptbetonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-MIN-).

C1.def: the commander of a fleet or a very senior naval officer
C1.example: The admiral ordered the fleet to change course.
C1.ielts_writing: Naval history is often told through the decisions of its admirals.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandfather was an admiral in the navy."
C1.mistake: Endet auf "-al" mit nur einem "l"; nicht mit "admire" (bewundern) verwechseln.

C1.def: respect and warm approval
C1.example: She spoke of her teacher with great admiration.
C1.ielts_writing: Public admiration for scientists increased during the pandemic.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have a lot of admiration for people who work with animals."
C1.mistake: Üblich ist "admiration FOR sb", seltener "admiration of".

C1.def: permission to enter or join, or a statement admitting that something is true
C1.example: Admission to the museum is free on Sundays.
C1.ielts_writing: University admission policies influence social mobility.
C1.ielts_speaking: "His admission that he had lied surprised everyone."
C1.mistake: Der Eintrittspreis heißt "admission fee" oder "admission", nicht "entry money".

C1.def: to agree that something is true, often reluctantly, or to allow someone to enter
C1.example: He admitted that he had forgotten the appointment.
C1.ielts_writing: Experts admit that long-term forecasts are uncertain.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have to admit I didn't read the instructions."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "admit TO + Gerund" oder "admit THAT + Satz", nicht "admit to do".

C1.def: a young person who is developing from a child into an adult
C1.example: Many adolescents struggle with sleep because of early school hours.
C1.ielts_writing: Adolescent mental health has become a priority for public policy.
C1.mistake: "adolescent" klingt klinisch oder wissenschaftlich; im Alltag sagt man "teenager".

C1.def: the legal taking of a child as your own, or the choice to start using an idea or method
C1.example: The adoption of electric buses cut the city's emissions.
C1.ielts_writing: Early adoption of new technology can give firms a competitive advantage.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My parents considered adoption before they had children."
C1.mistake: "adoption" (Annahme) und "adaptation" (Anpassung) sind leicht zu verwechseln.

C1.def: relating to someone who has legally adopted a child, or to the country someone has chosen to live in
C1.example: She grew up with her adoptive parents in Canada.
C1.ielts_writing: Adoptive families receive support from social services in many countries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My adoptive country has really become my home."
C1.mistake: Die Eltern sind "adoptive parents", das Kind ist "an adopted child"; nicht vertauschen.

C1.def: a hormone released in situations of stress or excitement
C1.example: The adrenaline kept her going through the final lap.
C1.ielts_writing: Adrenaline increases heart rate and prepares the body for a rapid reaction.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love the adrenaline rush of skiing fast."
C1.mistake: Im Deutschen "Adrenalin" ohne "e", im Englischen "adrenaline" mit "e"; medizinisch auch "epinephrine".

C1.def: progress or promotion, or the act of moving something forward
C1.example: The firm offers real opportunities for career advancement.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientific advancement depends on public funding for basic research.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm hoping for advancement at work next year."
C1.mistake: "advancement" meint den Fortschritt als Prozess; ein einzelner Durchbruch ist "an advance".

C1.def: travel to remote or challenging places that involves activity, such as hiking or rafting
C1.example: Adventure travel is growing in popularity among younger tourists.
C1.ielts_writing: Adventure travel can support local economies, but it may also damage fragile ecosystems.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I prefer adventure travel to lying on a beach."
C1.mistake: Als Sammelbegriff ohne Plural: "adventure travel", nicht "adventure travels".

C1.def: harmful or unfavorable
C1.example: Adverse weather forced the airline to cancel several flights.
C1.ielts_writing: Adverse effects of the drug were reported in a small number of patients.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Adverse weather ruined our plans for the weekend."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "averse" verwechseln; "averse to" bedeutet "abgeneigt".

C1.def: having the role of giving advice or recommendations
C1.example: She sits on an advisory board for the museum.
C1.ielts_writing: Advisory committees help governments make informed decisions on complex issues.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I work on an advisory team at my company."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen bedeutet "an advisory" einen Warnhinweis, z. B. "a travel advisory".

C1.def: public support for a cause or policy
C1.example: Her advocacy for refugees led to new legislation.
C1.ielts_writing: Patient advocacy groups play an important role in shaping health policy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I admire her advocacy for animal rights."
C1.mistake: Das Nomen endet auf "-cy" (advocacy), das Verb heißt "advocate"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a person who publicly supports a cause (n.), or to publicly recommend something (v.)
C1.example: She is a strong advocate of public libraries.
C1.ielts_writing: Several scientists advocate a gradual reduction in fossil-fuel use.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I advocate for more bike lanes in my neighborhood."
C1.mistake: Aussprache: Nomen mit /-kət/, Verb mit /-keɪt/; "advocate" steht direkt oder mit "for", nicht mit "to".

C1.def: the branch of technology and industry dealing with aircraft and space flight
C1.example: The region's economy relies on its aerospace industry.
C1.ielts_writing: Aerospace engineering demands extremely precise testing standards.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My uncle works in aerospace, building parts for satellites."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "airspace" (Luftraum) verwechseln.

C1.def: concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty
C1.example: The designer chose the colors for aesthetic reasons.
C1.ielts_writing: Aesthetic considerations should not outweigh safety in urban planning.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I like the aesthetic of old bookshops."
C1.mistake: Das "th" wird als /θ/ gesprochen (wie in "thin"); die Schreibweise "esthetic" gibt es nur selten.

C1.def: friendly, good-natured, and easy to talk to
C1.example: The host was an affable man who made everyone feel welcome.
C1.ielts_writing: Affable leaders often build stronger team loyalty.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My new neighbor is very affable, and we chat every morning."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "affordable" (erschwinglich) verwechseln; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a gentle feeling of fondness or liking
C1.example: The old dog showed his affection by resting his head on her knee.
C1.ielts_writing: Expressions of affection differ across cultures.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have a lot of affection for my hometown."
C1.mistake: "affection" ist nicht "Affekt" (starke Gefühlsregung); Präposition: "affection FOR".

C1.def: showing fondness and caring
C1.example: She is an affectionate child who loves hugs.
C1.ielts_writing: Affectionate parenting contributes to children's emotional development.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My cat is very affectionate and follows me around."
C1.mistake: "affectionate" (liebevoll) nicht mit "affected" (gekünstelt oder betroffen) verwechseln.

C1.def: agreeing with or saying yes to something
C1.example: The committee gave an affirmative answer to the request.
C1.ielts_writing: An affirmative vote from at least two thirds of members is required.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She gave an affirmative nod when I asked if she was ready."
C1.mistake: "affirmative action" ist ein fester Begriff (gezielte Förderung benachteiligter Gruppen), nicht wörtlich zu übersetzen.

C1.def: the period following an unpleasant event, and its consequences
C1.example: In the aftermath of the storm, volunteers helped clear the streets.
C1.ielts_writing: In the aftermath of the financial crisis, many governments tightened bank regulation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The aftermath of the argument was awkward."
C1.mistake: Meist in der Wendung "in the aftermath OF"; nicht "after the aftermath".

C1.def: hostile or violent behavior or attitudes toward another
C1.example: Teachers noticed an increase in aggression among the students.
C1.ielts_writing: Studies suggest that exposure to violent media may be linked to aggression.
C1.mistake: "aggression" ist negativ; die positive Eigenschaft heißt "assertiveness".

C1.def: feeling or appearing troubled and nervous
C1.example: He grew agitated when the flight was delayed again.
C1.ielts_writing: Agitated patients may require a calm and quiet environment.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I get agitated when I'm stuck in traffic."
C1.mistake: "agitated" ist negativ; nicht mit "excited" (freudig aufgeregt) verwechseln.

C1.de: sich quälen, sich den Kopf zerbrechen
C1.def: to worry or struggle painfully over a decision or problem
C1.example: She agonized for weeks over whether to accept the job in Berlin.
C1.ielts_writing: Policymakers often agonize over difficult trade-offs between growth and sustainability.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I agonized over what to wear to the interview."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "agonize OVER" oder "agonize ABOUT", nicht "agonize for".

C1.def: extreme physical or mental suffering
C1.example: He was in agony after twisting his ankle on the stairs.
C1.ielts_writing: The agony of waiting for medical results can be as stressful as the diagnosis itself.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Waiting for the exam results was pure agony."
C1.mistake: "agony" (Qual) ist nicht "Agonie" (Todeskampf); "agony aunt" ist eine Kummerkastentante.

C1.def: relating to farming and the growing of crops
C1.example: The region is mostly agricultural, with large wheat fields.
C1.ielts_writing: Agricultural subsidies have a major influence on global food prices.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "agricultural", Nomen "agriculture"; Betonung auf "-CUL-".

C1.def: a person who assists someone, especially a political leader
C1.example: A presidential aide read the statement to reporters.
C1.ielts_writing: Senior aides often shape policy decisions behind the scenes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My mother works as a classroom aide."
C1.mistake: Klingt genauso wie "aid" (Hilfe); nur die Schreibweise unterscheidet die beiden.

C1.def: an illness, typically a minor one
C1.example: Rest and fluids are often enough to treat common ailments.
C1.ielts_writing: Herbal remedies are widely used for minor ailments in many cultures.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandmother has a few small ailments but stays active."
C1.mistake: "ailment" ist leichter als "disease"; für schwere Erkrankungen nicht verwenden.

C1.def: a large passenger aircraft, or (capitalized) a brand of aircraft
C1.example: We boarded an Airbus for the flight to Berlin.
C1.ielts_writing: The Airbus program supports thousands of skilled jobs across Europe.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The Airbus was packed with holiday travelers."
C1.mistake: Als Markenname wird er großgeschrieben ("Airbus"); allgemein sagt man "airliner".

C1.def: a large passenger aircraft
C1.example: A commercial airliner landed safely despite the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: Modern airliners are significantly more fuel efficient than older models.
C1.mistake: "airline" ist die Fluggesellschaft, "airliner" das Flugzeug.

C1.def: although; used to introduce a contrasting qualification
C1.example: The plan worked, albeit more slowly than expected.
C1.ielts_writing: The new curriculum has improved results, albeit only marginally.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I enjoyed the film, albeit a little long."
C1.mistake: Folgt meist ein Adjektiv oder Adverb ("albeit small"), kein vollständiger Nebensatz mit Verb.

C1.def: a type of beer made with top-fermenting yeast
C1.example: He ordered a pint of ale at the pub.
C1.ielts_writing: Craft ales have become a significant part of the brewing industry.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My dad loves a good ale after work."
C1.mistake: "ginger ale" ist eine alkoholfreie Ingwerlimonade, kein Bier.

C1.def: quick to notice danger or change; a warning signal; to warn someone
C1.example: A good guard dog stays alert at night.
C1.ielts_writing: Public authorities issued an alert about rising flood risks.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need a coffee to stay alert in the afternoon."
C1.mistake: Auch Verb: "alert someone TO a danger"; nicht mit "alarm" gleichsetzen (alarm = lauter, stärker).

C1.def: simple plant-like organisms that grow in water
C1.example: Algae turned the lake bright green during the summer.
C1.ielts_writing: Excessive algae growth, caused by fertilizer runoff, can deplete oxygen in rivers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The pond was covered in green algae."
C1.mistake: "algae" ist ein Plural (Singular: "alga"); das "g" wird /dʒ/ gesprochen, nicht wie in "Garten".

C1.def: the branch of mathematics that uses letters and symbols to represent numbers
C1.example: She struggled with algebra but loved geometry.
C1.ielts_writing: Algebra provides the foundation for many fields of engineering.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I hated algebra at school, but I use it in my job now."
C1.mistake: Das "g" wird /dʒ/ gesprochen, nicht /g/.

C1.def: a set of rules or steps for solving a problem, especially by a computer
C1.example: The app's algorithm suggests songs based on what you have already heard.
C1.ielts_writing: Search algorithms strongly influence what information people see online.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I don't understand how the algorithm chooses my videos."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise "algorithm" (nicht "algorythm"); das "th" wird als /ð/ gesprochen.

C1.def: evidence that a person was elsewhere when a crime occurred, or an excuse
C1.example: He had a solid alibi because he was in a meeting all afternoon.
C1.ielts_writing: A strong alibi can lead to the dismissal of charges.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need a good alibi if I skip the party."
C1.mistake: Im umgangssprachlichen Englisch auch "Ausrede"; die Aussprache lautet /ˈæləbaɪ/.

C1.def: belonging to another country or foreign, or a being from another world
C1.example: The customs of the village felt alien to the visitors.
C1.ielts_writing: Alien species often outcompete native plants and animals.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Big cities felt alien to me at first."
C1.mistake: Für Menschen kann "alien" abwertend wirken; besser "foreign national" oder "immigrant".

C1.def: the state of feeling isolated or estranged from others or from society
C1.example: Many migrants describe a deep sense of alienation during their first year abroad.
C1.ielts_writing: Social alienation is frequently linked to long working hours and weak community ties.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt a kind of alienation when I moved to a huge city."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "alienation FROM sb/sth", nicht "alienation of".

C1.def: to arrange in a straight line, or to bring into agreement with something
C1.example: Please align the text with the left margin.
C1.ielts_writing: Companies must align their strategies with long-term environmental goals.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My values don't really align with my boss's."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "align WITH sth"; reflexiv: "align yourself with".

C1.def: arrangement in a straight line, or close agreement between groups or ideas
C1.example: The mechanic checked the alignment of the front wheels.
C1.ielts_writing: Policy alignment between neighboring countries makes trade smoother.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I want better alignment between what I say and what I do."
C1.mistake: Es heißt "in alignment WITH"; die Spureinstellung beim Auto ist "wheel alignment".

C1.def: similar to each other; in the same way
C1.example: The twins look so alike that even their teachers confuse them.
C1.ielts_writing: Young and old alike benefit from access to public parks.
C1.mistake: "alike" steht nach dem Nomen oder Verb ("look alike"), nicht direkt vor dem Nomen.

C1.def: including everything; (of a holiday) covering meals, drinks, and activities in one price
C1.example: We booked an all-inclusive resort so we wouldn't have to worry about meals.
C1.ielts_writing: All-inclusive packages appeal to travelers who prefer predictable costs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'd choose an all-inclusive hotel to avoid the stress of planning."
C1.mistake: Schreibung mit Bindestrich; das Gegenteil im Preissinn ist nicht "exclusive", sondern z. B. "à la carte".

C1.def: better or worse than any other at any time in the past
C1.example: The team set an all-time record for goals in a season.
C1.ielts_writing: Gold prices reached an all-time high last year.
C1.mistake: Vor dem Nomen mit Bindestrich ("all-time high"); nachgestellt ohne: "of all time".

C1.def: a claim, not yet proven, that someone has done something wrong
C1.example: The company denied the allegation of unfair practices.
C1.ielts_writing: Serious allegations should be investigated independently before conclusions are drawn.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He made allegations about his boss, but there was no proof."
C1.mistake: "allegation" ist unbewiesen; nicht mit "Allegorie" (allegory) verwechseln.

C1.def: to claim that someone has done something wrong, usually without proof
C1.example: The report alleges that the factory ignored safety rules.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics allege that the new policy favors wealthy households.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They alleged that I broke the rules, but I hadn't."
C1.mistake: Schreibung mit "-ge" (allege), nicht "alledge"; Konstruktion "allege THAT + Satz".

C1.def: according to what some people say, but without proof
C1.example: He allegedly left the building at midnight, but nobody saw him.
C1.ielts_writing: The firm allegedly ignored warnings from its own engineers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She allegedly won the lottery, but I don't believe it."
C1.mistake: "allegedly" signalisiert Unsicherheit; es hat drei Silben (/-ɪdli/), nicht "-ledgli".

C1.def: a union formed for mutual benefit, especially between countries or groups
C1.example: The two parties formed an alliance to win the election.
C1.ielts_writing: Military alliances have shaped the balance of power in Europe for decades.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We formed an alliance at work to push for better schedules."
C1.mistake: "alliance" bezeichnet ein Bündnis; "Allianz" als Versicherungsname ist kein englisches Wort.

C1.def: a spring-loaded metal clip with teeth, used to make temporary electrical connections
C1.example: He attached the wire to the battery with an alligator clip.
C1.ielts_writing: Alligator clips are used in laboratories to connect circuits quickly.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I borrowed some alligator clips for my science project."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "paper clip" (Büroklammer) verwechseln; die Zähne der Klemme geben ihr den Namen.

C1.def: to distribute resources or duties for a particular purpose
C1.example: The city allocated funds for new bicycle lanes.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments must allocate limited budgets to competing priorities.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I allocate an hour every evening to reading."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "allocate sth TO sb/sth" (oder "for" für den Zweck); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: the act of distributing resources, or the amount distributed
C1.example: The department's annual allocation was cut by ten percent.
C1.ielts_writing: Efficient allocation of water resources is critical in dry regions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The allocation of tasks in our team feels fair."
C1.mistake: Üblich ist "allocation OF funds"; die Betonung liegt auf der dritten Silbe (-KA-).

C1.def: an amount of money or something given regularly or for a purpose
C1.example: Children in the village receive a small weekly allowance.
C1.ielts_writing: Tax allowances can reduce the financial burden on low-income families.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I got a monthly allowance when I was a student."
C1.mistake: "make allowances FOR sb" bedeutet "Nachsicht üben"; das Taschengeld heißt einfach "allowance".

C1.def: powerfully and mysteriously attractive
C1.example: The alluring smell of fresh bread drew us into the café.
C1.ielts_writing: The alluring promise of quick profit leads many investors to take excessive risks.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The idea of living by the sea sounds alluring."
C1.mistake: Die Betonung liegt auf der zweiten Silbe; nicht mit "alarming" (beunruhigend) verwechseln.

C1.def: a person or state that cooperates with another for a common purpose
C1.example: Germany is a close ally of France.
C1.ielts_writing: Strong allies can strengthen a country's position in international negotiations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She was my biggest ally at work."
C1.mistake: Verb: "ally oneself WITH"; die Betonung wechselt: Nomen /ˈælaɪ/, Verb /əˈlaɪ/.

C1.def: next to, or together with
C1.example: He worked alongside his father for many years.
C1.ielts_writing: Economic growth must be pursued alongside environmental protection.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I like to work alongside people I trust."
C1.mistake: Schreibung in einem Wort ("alongside"), nicht "along side".

C1.def: occurring or arranged one after another in turn
C1.example: The two teams use the field on alternate days.
C1.ielts_writing: Alternate periods of rainfall and drought threaten crop yields.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I go to the gym on alternate days."
C1.mistake: "alternate" (abwechselnd) und "alternative" (alternativ) nicht vertauschen.

C1.def: the height of something above sea level or the ground
C1.example: The plane reached its cruising altitude within twenty minutes.
C1.ielts_writing: Altitude affects both temperature and oxygen levels.
C1.mistake: Leicht zu verwechseln mit "attitude" (Haltung): "altitude" hat ein "l" in der Mitte.

C1.def: showing a selfless concern for the well-being of others
C1.example: He made an altruistic decision to donate half of his savings.
C1.ielts_writing: Altruistic behavior can strengthen social cohesion.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I think volunteering can be both altruistic and good for you."
C1.mistake: Das Gegenteil ist "selfish"; nicht mit "alternative" verwechseln.

C1.def: a light, silvery-white metal used for cans, foil, and aircraft
C1.example: The soda can is made of recycled aluminum.
C1.ielts_writing: Aluminum is valued for its low weight and resistance to corrosion.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I wrapped the sandwiches in aluminum foil."
C1.mistake: Vier Silben mit Betonung auf der zweiten (a-LOO-mi-num).

C1.def: a person who does something for pleasure rather than as a job; also lacking professional skill
C1.example: The festival is open to amateur and professional musicians.
C1.ielts_writing: Amateur participation in citizen-science projects has improved environmental data.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm only an amateur photographer, but I enjoy it."
C1.mistake: "amateurish" ist abwertend (stümperhaft); "amateur" allein ist neutral.

C1.def: an official representing a country abroad, or a person who promotes something
C1.example: The ambassador met the foreign minister to discuss trade.
C1.ielts_writing: Ambassadors play a key role in maintaining diplomatic relations between nations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She's a brand ambassador for a sports company."
C1.mistake: Der Botschafter leitet die "embassy" (Botschaft als Gebäude); "Botschaft" als Nachricht ist "message".

C1.def: a hard yellow-brown fossilized resin, or a warm orange-yellow color
C1.example: The traffic light turned amber just before we reached it.
C1.ielts_writing: Amber has been valued as a gemstone and trade good for thousands of years.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love the warm amber light in the evening."
C1.mistake: Als Ampelfarbe sagt man "yellow light"; "amber" ist der Bernstein oder die orange-gelbe Farbe.

C1.def: having more than one possible meaning; unclear
C1.example: The instructions were so ambiguous that nobody knew what to do.
C1.ielts_writing: Ambiguous legal wording can lead to inconsistent court rulings.
C1.ielts_speaking: "His answer was ambiguous, so I asked again."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "ambivalent" (zwiespältig) verwechseln; das Gegenteil ist "unambiguous".

C1.def: to make a change to a text, law, or document in order to improve it
C1.example: Parliament voted to amend the constitution.
C1.ielts_writing: Laws must be amended regularly to reflect technological change.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Could you amend the date on the invoice?"
C1.mistake: "make amends" ist eine andere Wendung (Wiedergutmachung leisten) und gehört nicht zu "amend".

C1.def: a formal change made to a law or document
C1.example: The committee proposed an amendment to the bill.
C1.ielts_writing: The First Amendment protects freedom of speech in the United States.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We made a small amendment to the contract."
C1.mistake: "amendment" (Änderung) und "amends" (Wiedergutmachung) nicht verwechseln.

C1.def: surrounded by, or in the middle of a situation where something is happening
C1.example: The company thrived amid fierce competition.
C1.ielts_writing: Prices continued to rise amid fears of shortages.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He stayed calm amid all the chaos."
C1.mistake: Steht meist vor abstrakten oder unzählbaren Nomen; vor zählbaren, getrennten Personen sagt man "among".

C1.def: a cold-blooded animal, such as a frog, that lives partly in water and partly on land
C1.example: The pond is home to several amphibians, including frogs and newts.
C1.ielts_writing: Amphibian populations are an important indicator of ecosystem health.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I saw a small amphibian by the stream."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "amphibious" (amphibisch), Nomen "amphibian"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-FIB-).

C1.def: a device that increases the strength of an electrical signal such as sound
C1.example: He plugged his guitar into a large amplifier.
C1.ielts_writing: The amplifier increases the signal without distorting it.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need a bigger amplifier to practice with my band."
C1.mistake: Verb "amplify" (verstärken), Nomen "amplifier"; im Alltag sagt man oft kurz "amp".

C1.def: using signals or information represented by continuously variable quantities; not digital
C1.example: He still prefers an analog watch to a smartwatch.
C1.ielts_writing: Analog technology has been replaced by digital formats in most communication systems.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love the sound of analog records."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "analogy" (Analogie) verwechseln; das Gegenteil von "analog" ist "digital".

C1.def: a comparison between two things to explain or clarify an idea
C1.example: The teacher used an analogy between the heart and a pump.
C1.ielts_writing: The writer draws an analogy between the internet and a public library.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Let me use an analogy to explain my point."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "analogy BETWEEN A and B" oder "analogy WITH/TO"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-NAL-).

C1.def: the systematic computational analysis of data or statistics
C1.example: The marketing team uses analytics to track customer behavior.
C1.ielts_writing: Advances in analytics allow cities to predict traffic congestion.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My job involves a lot of web analytics."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "analysis" (eine einzelne Untersuchung) gleichsetzen; "analytics" meint Verfahren und Werkzeuge insgesamt.

C1.def: the structure of a living thing, or the study of that structure
C1.example: Medical students study human anatomy in their first year.
C1.ielts_writing: Understanding anatomy is essential for diagnosing injuries correctly.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I studied the anatomy of a frog in biology class."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-NAT-); bildlich auch "Aufbau" ("the anatomy of a crisis").

C1.def: the people from whom you are descended
C1.example: She traced her ancestry back to the seventeenth century.
C1.ielts_writing: Genetic testing allows individuals to explore their ancestry.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My ancestry is partly Irish and partly Polish."
C1.mistake: "ancestry" (Abstammung, unzählbar) ist nicht "ancestor" (einzelner Vorfahre).

C1.def: a heavy object that keeps a ship in place; a source of stability; a TV presenter
C1.example: The captain dropped the anchor near the shore.
C1.ielts_writing: Strong families act as an emotional anchor in times of crisis.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandmother was the anchor of our family."
C1.mistake: Bildlich "Stütze"; der TV-Nachrichtensprecher heißt "news anchor".

C1.def: a substance that causes loss of sensation, used in surgery
C1.example: The dentist gave me a local anesthetic before the procedure.
C1.ielts_writing: General anesthetics allow surgeons to perform complex operations without causing pain.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was afraid of the anesthetic before my surgery."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-THET-); Schreibweise ohne "a" nach "an-": "anesthetic".

C1.def: a spiritual being believed to serve as a messenger of God, or a very kind person
C1.example: She was an angel to look after my dog while I was away.
C1.ielts_writing: In many religious texts, angels act as messengers between humans and the divine.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My neighbor is an angel; she always helps me."
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈeɪndʒəl/; nicht mit "angle" (Winkel, /ˈæŋɡəl/) verwechseln.

C1.def: not identified by name, or of unknown authorship
C1.example: The donor wishes to remain anonymous.
C1.ielts_writing: Anonymous surveys often produce more honest responses.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (/əˈnɑːn-/); Schreibweise mit einem "n" nach "ano-": "anonymous", nicht "annonymous".

C1.def: a device for receiving or sending radio waves, or an insect's sensory feeler
C1.example: The radio picks up a better signal with a longer antenna.
C1.ielts_writing: Antennas on rooftops allow households to receive television broadcasts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My phone has no signal because the antenna is broken."
C1.mistake: Plural: "antennas" (Geräte) und "antennae" (Fühler von Insekten).

C1.def: a rousing song identified with a group, nation, or cause
C1.example: The crowd stood to sing the national anthem.
C1.ielts_writing: National anthems often reflect a country's history and values.
C1.ielts_speaking: "That song became the anthem of my generation."
C1.mistake: Das "th" wird /θ/ gesprochen; "anthem" ist nicht "hymn" (kirchliches Lied).

C1.def: the study of human societies, cultures, and their development
C1.example: She studied anthropology to understand how cultures differ.
C1.ielts_writing: Cultural anthropology explores how communities organize family, work, and belief.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm taking an anthropology course this term."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-POL-); nicht mit "anthropomorphism" (Vermenschlichung) verwechseln.

C1.def: opposed to something
C1.example: He is strongly anti any increase in taxes.
C1.ielts_writing: Several groups are anti the proposal because of its cost.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm anti spoilers when I watch a series."
C1.mistake: Als Präfix mit Bindestrich oder zusammen ("anti-war", "antibiotic"); alleinstehend ist "anti" informell.

C1.def: a substance that prevents infection by killing germs
C1.example: The nurse cleaned the wound with antiseptic.
C1.ielts_writing: Antiseptic solutions are commonly used before minor surgery.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I always carry antiseptic wipes in my bag."
C1.mistake: "antiseptic" wirkt auf der Haut, "disinfectant" auf Oberflächen.

C1.def: designed to detect and remove computer viruses
C1.example: Make sure your antivirus software is up to date.
C1.ielts_writing: Antivirus programs are an essential layer of cyber security.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I installed an antivirus program after my laptop got infected."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben ("antivirus"), nicht "anti virus".

C1.def: greatly shocked or disgusted
C1.example: Residents were appalled by the state of the abandoned building.
C1.ielts_writing: Many readers were appalled by the editorial's lack of empathy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was appalled when I saw how much waste there was."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "appalled AT/BY", nicht "appalled with".

C1.def: the equipment needed for a particular activity, or the structure of an organization
C1.example: The laboratory has special apparatus for measuring tiny particles.
C1.ielts_writing: The state's bureaucratic apparatus influences how quickly policies are implemented.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The diving apparatus was heavy but reliable."
C1.mistake: Plural: "apparatuses" oder unverändert "apparatus", nicht "apparati".

C1.def: clothing, especially in a commercial or formal context
C1.example: The store specializes in athletic apparel.
C1.ielts_writing: The apparel industry is one of the world's largest consumers of water.
C1.mistake: "apparel" ist unzählbar (kein Plural) und formeller als "clothes".

C1.def: attractive or interesting
C1.example: The idea of a quiet weekend in the mountains sounds very appealing.
C1.ielts_writing: Flexible working hours are appealing to many young professionals.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I find the idea of living abroad really appealing."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "appealing TO sb"; das Verb "appeal" bedeutet auch "Berufung einlegen" (juristisch).

C1.def: the act of satisfying the demands of an aggressor in order to avoid conflict
C1.example: Critics called the treaty a policy of appeasement toward a hostile neighbor.
C1.ielts_writing: History shows that appeasement rarely deters determined aggressors.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Giving in to him every time felt like appeasement, not a real solution."
C1.mistake: Das Verb heißt "appease"; das Nomen endet auf "-ment" (appeasement), nicht auf "-ing".

C1.def: a section of supplementary material at the end of a book or document, or a small organ attached to the intestine
C1.example: Full survey results are listed in the appendix.
C1.ielts_writing: The raw data are provided in an appendix so readers can verify the calculations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He had his appendix removed when he was twelve."
C1.mistake: Plural meist "appendices"; der Blinddarm heißt "appendix", die Entzündung "appendicitis".

C1.def: a natural desire for food, or a strong wish to do something
C1.example: The long walk gave us a healthy appetite.
C1.ielts_writing: Investors' appetite for risk tends to fall during periods of economic uncertainty.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I lost my appetite after the long flight."
C1.mistake: Das Wort endet auf /-taɪt/ (wie "tight"), nicht auf /-tɪt/.

C1.def: a small dish served before the main course
C1.example: We shared a plate of fried calamari as an appetizer.
C1.ielts_writing: Appetizers are often priced lower to encourage customers to order a full meal.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I always order the soup as an appetizer."
C1.mistake: "appetizer" ist die Vorspeise, nicht der "Appetit" (appetite).

C1.def: to show approval by clapping, or to praise publicly
C1.example: The audience stood and applauded for several minutes.
C1.ielts_writing: Environmental groups applauded the government's decision to ban single-use plastics.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I applaud anyone who learns a language as an adult."
C1.mistake: Das Nomen heißt "applause" (unzählbar), nicht "applaudment".

C1.def: relevant or appropriate to a particular situation
C1.example: This rule is not applicable to part-time employees.
C1.ielts_writing: Safety regulations should be applicable to all manufacturers, regardless of their size.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Please skip any questions that aren't applicable to you."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "applicable TO sb/sth"; "where applicable" bedeutet "falls zutreffend".

C1.def: a formal request for something, or the practical use of something
C1.example: Her application for a scholarship was approved.
C1.ielts_writing: The practical application of the theory remains limited.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I sent in an application for the job yesterday."
C1.mistake: "application" heißt Bewerbung, Antrag oder Anwendung; "Applikation" im Sinne von Software ist im Englischen "app".

C1.def: to officially choose someone for a job or position
C1.example: The board appointed a new director last month.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments often appoint independent experts to review controversial policies.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They appointed my cousin as the team's coach."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "appoint sb AS sth"; "an appointment" ist auch der Termin, den man "makes", nicht "appoints".

C1.def: to assess the value, quality, or performance of something
C1.example: An expert appraised the necklace at five thousand dollars.
C1.ielts_writing: Managers should appraise employees' performance at regular intervals.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I asked a friend to appraise my new apartment."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "apprise" (benachrichtigen) verwechseln: "appraise" = bewerten, "apprise" = informieren.

C1.de: schätzen, dankbar sein, zu schätzen wissen
C1.def: to recognize the value of something or to be grateful for it
C1.example: I really appreciate your help with the move.
C1.ielts_writing: Employees who feel appreciated tend to be more productive.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I appreciate it when people are honest with me."
C1.mistake: Es heißt "I'd appreciate IT if you could...", nicht "I'd appreciate if"; "appreciate" braucht immer ein Objekt.

C1.def: gratitude, understanding of value, or an increase in value
C1.example: She sent flowers as a token of appreciation.
C1.ielts_writing: Property appreciation in coastal cities has outpaced average wage growth.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have a deep appreciation for classical music."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "appreciation FOR sth" oder "in appreciation OF"; im Finanzkontext ist das Gegenteil "depreciation".

C1.def: anxious or fearful that something bad will happen
C1.example: He felt apprehensive before his first day at the new school.
C1.ielts_writing: Many consumers remain apprehensive about sharing personal data online.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was a bit apprehensive about the exam results."
C1.mistake: "apprehensive" heißt besorgt, nicht "verständnisvoll"; Präposition: "apprehensive ABOUT".

C1.def: based on random choice or personal whim rather than reason
C1.example: The decision seemed arbitrary because no criteria were published.
C1.ielts_writing: Arbitrary detention violates basic principles of the rule of law.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The teacher's grading felt arbitrary to a lot of us."
C1.mistake: "arbitrary" (willkürlich) ist nicht "arbiter" (Schiedsrichter); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a curved structure that spans an opening, such as a doorway or bridge
C1.example: A stone arch marks the entrance to the old town.
C1.ielts_writing: The Roman arch allowed builders to span wider openings than flat beams could.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We walked under a huge arch to get into the square."
C1.mistake: Aussprache mit "tsch" am Ende (/ɑːrtʃ/), nicht wie "ark".

C1.def: a bishop of the highest rank, in charge of an archdiocese
C1.example: The archbishop delivered a sermon at the cathedral.
C1.ielts_writing: Archbishops have historically played a role in both religious and political life.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I met the archbishop at a charity dinner once."
C1.mistake: "arch-" wird /ɑːrtʃ/ gesprochen, nicht /ɑːrk/.

C1.def: the study of the past through excavated remains such as buildings and tools
C1.example: She studied archeology to learn how ancient communities lived.
C1.ielts_writing: Archeology offers evidence of how early societies organized trade and settlement.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I once volunteered on an archeology dig in the summer."
C1.mistake: Das "ch" wird /k/ gesprochen; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-OL-).

C1.def: relating to the design and construction of buildings
C1.example: The city is known for its architectural diversity.
C1.ielts_writing: Architectural heritage can help cities attract tourism.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love the architectural details of old churches."
C1.mistake: Das Adjektiv heißt "architectural", das Nomen "architecture"; das "ch" wird /k/ gesprochen.

C1.def: a collection of historical documents or records
C1.example: The researcher spent weeks in the national archive.
C1.ielts_writing: Digital archives make rare historical documents accessible to a global audience.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I found my grandparents' wedding photos in an old family archive."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; das Verb "to archive" (archivieren) wird genauso betont.

C1.def: a large enclosed area for sports or entertainment, or a field of activity
C1.example: The concert was held in a packed indoor arena.
C1.ielts_writing: The international arena has become more competitive as new powers emerge.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's well known in the political arena."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (/əˈriː-/), nicht "AH-re-na".

C1.def: used to introduce a statement that you believe can be supported by good reasons
C1.example: She is arguably the best chess player in the country.
C1.ielts_writing: Social media is arguably the most influential force in modern politics.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Pizza is arguably the world's favorite food."
C1.mistake: "arguably" heißt "wohl, durchaus", nicht "streitbar" oder "umstritten".

C1.def: fond of arguing, or (of writing) presenting reasons for a viewpoint
C1.example: My brother gets argumentative whenever we discuss politics.
C1.ielts_writing: An argumentative essay presents a clear position and supports it with evidence.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm not argumentative, but I do like a good debate."
C1.mistake: Im Alltag meist negativ ("streitsüchtig"); "mit Argumenten" bedeutet es nur bei "argumentative essay".

C1.def: (of land or climate) having little or no rain; extremely dry
C1.example: Few plants can survive in the arid desert.
C1.ielts_writing: Arid regions are especially vulnerable to the effects of climate change.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The landscape in Arizona is dry and arid."
C1.mistake: "arid" gilt für Klima und Land, nicht für trockene Haut oder Hände (dafür "dry").

C1.def: a member of the highest social class, typically with a noble title
C1.example: The painting shows an aristocrat in elegant clothing.
C1.ielts_writing: Aristocrats once held most of the political power in many European countries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My friend acts like an aristocrat, even though his family is quite ordinary."
C1.mistake: Die Betonung liegt auf der zweiten Silbe (-RIS-); bei "aristocracy" verschiebt sie sich auf die dritte (-STOC-).

C1.def: the branch of mathematics dealing with numbers and basic operations
C1.example: Children learn basic arithmetic in elementary school.
C1.ielts_writing: Simple arithmetic shows that the budget cannot cover all the proposed projects.
C1.mistake: Das Nomen wird auf der zweiten Silbe betont (-RITH-), das Adjektiv "arithmetic" auf "-MET-".

C1.def: to supply a person or group with weapons, or with something useful
C1.example: The rebels were armed with rifles.
C1.ielts_writing: Teachers should arm students with the critical thinking skills they need.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I armed myself with a map and a flashlight before the hike."
C1.mistake: Als Verb nur "bewaffnen, ausrüsten"; Konstruktion: "arm sb WITH sth".

C1.def: the use of fragrant plant oils to improve mood or well-being
C1.example: The spa offers aromatherapy massages with lavender oil.
C1.ielts_writing: Aromatherapy is popular, although scientific evidence for its effects remains limited.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I use aromatherapy candles when I'm stressed."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf "-THER-"; im Englischen eine alternative Praxis, keine anerkannte medizinische Therapie.

C1.def: all day and all night without stopping
C1.example: Nurses care for patients around the clock.
C1.ielts_writing: Emergency services operate around the clock to protect public safety.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We worked around the clock to finish the project."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung ohne Plural: "around the clock", nicht "around the clocks".

C1.def: an impressive range or collection of things
C1.example: The shop offers a dazzling array of handmade soaps.
C1.ielts_writing: The report presents an array of evidence supporting the proposed reform.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There was a huge array of desserts at the wedding."
C1.mistake: Die Wendung lautet "an array OF + Plural"; die Betonung liegt hinten (/əˈreɪ/).

C1.def: the crime of deliberately setting fire to property
C1.example: Police suspect arson in the warehouse fire.
C1.ielts_writing: Arson is treated as a serious crime because it endangers lives and property.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The fire turned out to be arson."
C1.mistake: Der Täter heißt "arsonist"; nicht mit "arsenal" (Waffenlager) verwechseln.

C1.def: a person who is very knowledgeable about and enthusiastic about art
C1.example: The gallery attracts art aficionados from across the country.
C1.ielts_writing: Art aficionados often travel specifically to attend major exhibitions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My aunt is a real art aficionado; she knows every museum."
C1.mistake: "aficionado" wird /əˌfɪʃəˈnɑːdoʊ/ gesprochen; das "c" klingt wie "sch", die Betonung liegt auf "-NA-".

C1.def: a person in charge of the visual style of a film, magazine, or advertisement
C1.example: The art director chose a muted color palette for the film.
C1.ielts_writing: An art director coordinates designers, photographers, and illustrators to keep a campaign visually consistent.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She works as an art director at an ad agency."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit dem Leiter eines Museums gleichsetzen (dort "museum director" oder "curator").

C1.def: a thistle-like vegetable whose fleshy flower-bud base is eaten
C1.example: She served steamed artichoke with melted butter.
C1.ielts_writing: Artichokes are cultivated mainly in Mediterranean regions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I had artichoke for the first time in Italy."
C1.mistake: Das "ch" wird /tʃ/ gesprochen ("ar-ti-choke"), nicht wie "sch".

C1.def: able to express ideas clearly and effectively; to express something in words
C1.example: She is a thoughtful and articulate speaker.
C1.ielts_writing: Articulate communication is a core skill in leadership.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I find it hard to articulate how I feel sometimes."
C1.mistake: Aussprache: Adjektiv /-lət/, Verb /-leɪt/; als Verb heißt es auch "deutlich aussprechen".

C1.def: an object made by a human being, typically of historical interest
C1.example: Museums display artifacts from ancient civilizations.
C1.ielts_writing: Artifacts provide archaeologists with evidence about daily life in the past.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I found an old coin that might be an artifact."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; geschrieben wird "artifact" mit "i".

C1.def: large guns used in warfare on land
C1.example: The army advanced under cover of artillery fire.
C1.ielts_writing: The use of long-range artillery transformed warfare in the twentieth century.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw old artillery pieces in the military museum."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-TIL-); "heavy artillery" wird auch bildlich für "schwere Argumente" benutzt.

C1.def: used to add information that is true and often surprising, or to correct something
C1.example: "Did you enjoy the film?" "As a matter of fact, I walked out halfway through."
C1.ielts_writing: As a matter of fact, many assumptions about this issue are not supported by data.
C1.ielts_speaking: "As a matter of fact, I've never been to Paris."
C1.mistake: Leitet eine Korrektur oder überraschende Tatsache ein, bedeutet nicht "nebenbei"; Wortlaut fest: "as a matter of fact".

C1.def: the powder left after something has burned; a type of tree
C1.example: A thick layer of ash covered the town after the eruption.
C1.ielts_writing: Volcanic ash can disrupt air travel across entire continents.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandfather's ashtray was always full of cigarette ash."
C1.mistake: "ash" bedeutet Asche und Esche; "ashes" (Plural) meint oft die Asche nach einem Brand oder einer Einäscherung.

C1.def: a plant whose young green or white shoots are eaten as a vegetable
C1.example: We grilled asparagus and served it with lemon.
C1.ielts_writing: Asparagus is grown commercially in many temperate regions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love white asparagus in the springtime."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some asparagus", "a bunch of asparagus"; kein Plural mit "-s".

C1.def: a hope or ambition of achieving something
C1.example: Her aspiration was to become a pilot.
C1.ielts_writing: Many young people hold aspirations that exceed what their local labor markets can offer.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My aspiration is to write a novel one day."
C1.mistake: Im Englischen meist im Plural ("aspirations"); medizinisch bedeutet "aspiration" auch "Absaugung".

C1.def: to direct your hopes or ambitions toward achieving something
C1.example: Many students aspire to study abroad.
C1.ielts_writing: Societies should provide opportunities for citizens who aspire to better lives.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I aspire to run a marathon someday."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "aspire TO + Infinitiv oder Nomen", nicht "aspire for".

C1.def: a person who murders an important person, usually for political reasons
C1.example: The assassin was caught within hours of the attack.
C1.ielts_writing: Historians still debate the motives of the assassin.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The movie is about a retired assassin."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit je zwei "s" (assassin), nicht "asassin".

C1.def: to murder an important person, usually for political reasons
C1.example: The president was assassinated in 1963.
C1.ielts_writing: Plans to assassinate political leaders have often reshaped national history.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They tried to assassinate him, but the attempt failed."
C1.mistake: "assassinate" gilt nur für bedeutende Personen aus politischen oder ideologischen Gründen, nicht für gewöhnliche Morde.

C1.def: the killing of an important person for political reasons
C1.example: The assassination shocked the entire nation.
C1.ielts_writing: The assassination of the archduke triggered a chain of events that led to war.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We learned about the assassination in history class."
C1.mistake: Es heißt "assassination attempt", nicht "attempt of assassination"; Betonung auf der vierten Silbe (-NA-).

C1.def: a violent physical attack, or a military attack
C1.example: The two men were charged with assault.
C1.ielts_writing: Assault cases are often difficult to prosecute without independent witnesses.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The city started a campaign to reduce street assaults."
C1.mistake: Im Strafrecht meint "assault" die Körperverletzung; das Verb steht ohne Präposition: "assault sb".

C1.def: to gather together, or to fit parts together
C1.example: Workers assemble the cars in just a few hours.
C1.ielts_writing: Teams are assembled according to the skills required for each project.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I spent all weekend trying to assemble a bookshelf."
C1.mistake: "assemble" bedeutet zusammenbauen oder versammeln; nicht mit "assimilate" (aufnehmen, angleichen) verwechseln.

C1.def: a group of people gathered together for a common purpose, or the process of putting parts together
C1.example: The school held an assembly on the first day of term.
C1.ielts_writing: A national assembly is responsible for passing legislation in many countries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The factory has an assembly line for building cars."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-SEM-); "assembly line" ist das Fließband.

C1.def: to state something confidently as true, or to make others recognize your authority
C1.example: He asserted that the data had been checked twice.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers assert that early childhood education improves long-term outcomes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I had to assert myself to get a fair deal."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "insert" (einfügen) verwechseln; "assert yourself" bedeutet "sich durchsetzen".

C1.def: a confident statement that something is true
C1.example: His assertion that he had been at home was proven false.
C1.ielts_writing: An assertion without supporting evidence carries little weight in academic writing.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I disagree with his assertion that money buys happiness."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "assertion THAT + Satz" oder "assertion OF"; Schreibweise "assertion", nicht "assertation".

C1.def: having or showing confidence and clearly stating what you want
C1.example: She became more assertive after the training course.
C1.ielts_writing: Assertive communication allows employees to express needs without hostility.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm learning to be more assertive at work."
C1.mistake: "assertive" ist positiv (selbstbewusst, klar), "aggressive" ist negativ.

C1.def: the evaluation of the quality, value, or importance of something
C1.example: The assessment of each student takes place at the end of the term.
C1.ielts_writing: A thorough risk assessment should precede any major construction project.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My manager gave me an honest assessment of my work."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit doppeltem "s" an beiden Stellen: "as-sess-ment", nicht "assesment".

C1.def: a person connected with another in business or at work; to connect something in your mind
C1.example: She is a business associate of my father's.
C1.ielts_writing: Many consumers associate expensive brands with higher quality.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I always associate the smell of pine with Christmas."
C1.mistake: Aussprache: Nomen /-siət/, Verb /-sieɪt/; Konstruktion: "associate WITH sth", nicht "associate to".

C1.def: a positive declaration intended to give confidence, or confidence in your own abilities
C1.example: The manager gave us his assurance that the repairs would be finished by Friday.
C1.ielts_writing: Official assurances that the water is safe have not convinced local residents.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I spoke with calm assurance at the meeting."
C1.mistake: "assurance" (Zusicherung) ist nicht "insurance" (Versicherung).

C1.def: to tell someone confidently that something is true, or to make certain
C1.example: I assure you that the package will arrive tomorrow.
C1.ielts_writing: Authorities assured citizens that the supply of electricity would not be interrupted.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He assured me that everything was under control."
C1.mistake: "assure sb THAT" (jemandem versichern), "ensure" (sicherstellen) und "insure" (versichern, Versicherung) sind verschiedene Wörter.

C1.def: confident, or certain to happen
C1.example: She gave an assured performance on stage.
C1.ielts_writing: A steady income gives young families an assured base for planning their future.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt assured after I talked to the doctor."
C1.mistake: "assured of sth" (einer Sache sicher); nicht mit "insured" (versichert) verwechseln.

C1.def: a respiratory condition that causes breathing difficulties and wheezing
C1.example: He uses an inhaler to control his asthma.
C1.ielts_writing: Air pollution is a major factor in the rising number of asthma cases in cities.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I had asthma as a child, but it went away."
C1.mistake: Das "th" wird nicht gesprochen: /ˈæzmə/, nicht "ast-ma".

C1.def: to surprise someone greatly
C1.example: Her speed astonished the coaches.
C1.ielts_writing: The scale of the discovery astonished even experienced geologists.
