C1.ielts_speaking: "It astonishes me how fast kids learn languages."
C1.mistake: "astonish" ist stärker als "surprise"; im Passiv: "be astonished AT/BY".

C1.def: shocked or very surprised
C1.example: We were astounded by the generosity of the strangers.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics were astounded by the speed with which the project was completed.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was astounded when I saw the final bill."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "astounded BY/AT"; der Stamm wird mit /aʊ/ gesprochen (wie in "sound").

C1.def: the study of the possibility of life elsewhere in the universe
C1.example: Astrobiology looks for signs of life on other planets.
C1.ielts_writing: Astrobiology combines biology, chemistry, and astronomy to explore how life might begin.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I read an article about astrobiology and Mars."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben ("astrobiology"); Betonung auf der vierten Silbe (-OL-).

C1.def: the study of the supposed influence of stars and planets on human lives
C1.example: She doesn't believe in astrology, but she reads her horoscope for fun.
C1.ielts_writing: Astrology has no scientific basis, yet it remains widely popular.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My friend is really into astrology and always asks for my birth time."
C1.mistake: "astrology" (Sterndeutung) nicht mit "astronomy" (Astronomie) verwechseln.

C1.def: protection given by a state to someone fleeing persecution in their own country
C1.example: He applied for asylum after fleeing the war.
C1.ielts_writing: Countries differ widely in how quickly they process asylum applications.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She came here seeking asylum from political persecution."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (/əˈsaɪ-/); in der Bedeutung "Anstalt" ist das Wort veraltet und kann verletzend wirken.

C1.def: used to emphasize a negative or a question; in any way
C1.example: I don't mind at all if you borrow it.
C1.ielts_writing: Nothing in the data suggests at all that the policy has failed.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I didn't like the film at all."
C1.mistake: Steht in Verneinungen und Fragen ("Do you smoke at all?"); als Antwort auf "Danke" bedeutet "Not at all" "gern geschehen".

C1.def: with harm or disadvantage to something or someone else
C1.example: He built a successful career at the expense of his health.
C1.ielts_writing: Short-term profit should not be pursued at the expense of long-term sustainability.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I don't want to get ahead at the expense of my friends."
C1.mistake: Es heißt "at the expense OF", nicht "on the expense of"; "at my expense" kann auch "auf meine Kosten (im Scherz)" bedeuten.

C1.def: simultaneously, or used to add a contrasting point
C1.example: The two trains arrived at the same time.
C1.ielts_writing: At the same time, the policy has imposed costs on small businesses.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I want to travel, but at the same time I want to save money."
C1.mistake: "at the same time" kann "gleichzeitig" oder "allerdings" bedeuten; "in the meantime" heißt "inzwischen".

C1.def: physical sports and exercises, especially competitive team and individual sports
C1.example: She competes in athletics at the national level.
C1.ielts_writing: Investment in school athletics can improve students' physical and mental health.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I took part in school athletics when I was young."
C1.mistake: "athletics" steht für Sport allgemein; Leichtathletik im engeren Sinn heißt "track and field".

C1.def: relating to the earth's atmosphere, or creating a distinct mood
C1.example: Atmospheric pressure drops before a storm.
C1.ielts_writing: Atmospheric pollution has been linked to respiratory problems in urban areas.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I like atmospheric cafés with old books and dim lights."
C1.mistake: "atmospheric" bedeutet Luft oder Stimmung; "stimmungsvoll" gilt nur für Orte, Musik oder Filme.

C1.def: relating to atoms or to nuclear energy
C1.example: The atomic number of carbon is six.
C1.ielts_writing: Atomic energy offers a low-carbon alternative to fossil fuels but raises safety concerns.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We studied atomic structure in physics class."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-TOM-); das Nomen "atom" wird auf der ersten betont.

C1.def: an extremely cruel and wicked act, especially one involving violence
C1.example: The report documented atrocities committed during the war.
C1.ielts_writing: International courts prosecute atrocities such as genocide and crimes against humanity.
C1.mistake: Das Adjektiv "atrocious" bedeutet umgangssprachlich auch "miserabel" ("atrocious weather").

C1.def: to succeed in achieving something, usually after effort
C1.example: She attained her goal of qualifying for the national team.
C1.ielts_writing: Few countries have attained full gender equality in the workplace.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I hope to attain a high level of fluency by next year."
C1.mistake: "attain" ist formeller als "reach" und steht ohne Präposition ("attain sth").

C1.def: the fact of being present at a place or event, or the number of people present
C1.example: Attendance at the lecture was low because of the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular school attendance is strongly correlated with academic success.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My attendance record is perfect this semester."
C1.mistake: "attendance" bedeutet Anwesenheit, nicht "Aufmerksamkeit" (das ist "attention").

C1.def: paying close attention to something or someone, or being considerate
C1.example: The waiter was friendly and attentive throughout the meal.
C1.ielts_writing: Attentive teachers can recognize early signs of learning difficulties.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My doctor is very attentive and always listens."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "attentive TO sth"; auch im Sinne von "zuvorkommend" üblich.

C1.def: a lawyer, especially one who represents clients in court
C1.example: The attorney advised her client not to answer questions.
C1.ielts_writing: A defense attorney has a duty to present the strongest possible case for the accused.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My sister is an attorney at a small law firm."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-TOR-); "district attorney" ist der Staatsanwalt, nicht ein "Bezirksanwalt".

C1.def: a quality or feature of someone or something; to regard something as being caused by someone or something
C1.example: Patience is her best attribute.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers often attribute rising obesity rates to changes in diet and lifestyle.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I attribute my success to hard work and good luck."
C1.mistake: Die Betonung wechselt: Nomen ATtribute, Verb atTRIbute; Konstruktion: "attribute sth TO sb/sth".

C1.def: a young foreigner who helps with housework and childcare in exchange for room and board
C1.example: They hired an au pair from Spain to help with the children.
C1.ielts_writing: Au pair arrangements allow young people to experience another culture while earning a small allowance.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I worked as an au pair in Boston for a year."
C1.mistake: Plural "au pairs"; das "au" wird /oʊ/ gesprochen, nicht wie im Deutschen.

C1.def: a business that sells goods to the highest bidder
C1.example: The painting was sold through a well-known auction house in New York.
C1.ielts_writing: Auction houses play an important role in the global art market.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My uncle works at an auction house."
C1.mistake: "auction" wird /ˈɔːkʃən/ gesprochen, ohne ein "t" hörbar; kein "auktion" mit "k-t".

C1.def: an official inspection of an organization's accounts, or a systematic review of something
C1.example: The company underwent an external audit last spring.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular audits help detect financial irregularities at an early stage.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Our team did an energy audit of the building."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "audition" (Vorsprechen) verwechseln; ein "audit" ist eine Prüfung.

C1.def: genuine, real, or true to its original
C1.example: The restaurant serves authentic Italian pizza baked in a wood oven.
C1.ielts_writing: Authentic materials such as news articles help learners acquire natural language.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I want to find an authentic local market when I travel."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-THEN-); das "th" wird /θ/ gesprochen.

C1.def: to give official permission for something to happen
C1.example: The manager authorized the purchase of new equipment.
C1.ielts_writing: Only licensed professionals are authorized to perform such procedures.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need your boss to authorize this request."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "authorize sb TO do sth"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: short for automobile
C1.example: The auto industry employs millions of people in the United States.
C1.ielts_writing: Auto manufacturers are shifting toward electric vehicles in response to new regulations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My dad works in the auto business."
C1.mistake: Im Alltag sagt man meist "car"; "auto" steht vor allem in Zusammensetzungen wie "auto repair".

C1.def: an account of a person's life written by that person
C1.example: Her autobiography became a bestseller.
C1.ielts_writing: An autobiography offers insight into the private thoughts behind public events.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm reading an autobiography of a famous chef."
C1.mistake: Eine "autobiography" schreibt die Person selbst, eine "biography" jemand anderes.

C1.def: a road vehicle with an engine, typically with four wheels
C1.example: The automobile changed the way cities were planned.
C1.ielts_writing: Automobile ownership has risen sharply as incomes have increased.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; "automobile" klingt formell, im Alltag sagt man "car".

C1.def: the right or condition of self-government, or independence in decisions
C1.example: Employees want more autonomy in how they organize their work.
C1.ielts_writing: Greater regional autonomy can reduce tensions between central and local government.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I value my autonomy, so I prefer to work alone."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-TON-); Präpositionen: "autonomy OVER sth", "autonomy FROM sb".

C1.def: the state of being able to be used or obtained
C1.example: Check the availability of rooms before you book.
C1.ielts_writing: The availability of clean water remains a critical issue in many regions.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "availability OF sth", nicht "availability for".

C1.def: to prevent something unpleasant from happening, or to turn away your eyes
C1.example: Quick action by the pilot averted a disaster.
C1.ielts_writing: Early intervention can avert serious health complications.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I averted my eyes when the scene got too violent."
C1.mistake: "avert" bedeutet abwenden; nicht mit "avoid" (vermeiden) gleichsetzen.

C1.def: to wait for something, or (of a thing) to be in store for someone
C1.example: A warm welcome awaits visitors to the village.
C1.ielts_writing: The results of the investigation are eagerly awaited by the public.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm awaiting a reply from the university."
C1.mistake: "await" steht ohne Präposition ("await sth"), im Unterschied zu "wait FOR sth".

C1.def: a prize or honor given for achievement; to give something officially
C1.example: The film won an award for best director.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments sometimes award contracts to companies with a proven track record.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She received an award for her volunteer work."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "award sb sth" oder "award sth TO sb"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: extremely good or impressive (slang)
C1.example: The concert was absolutely awesomesauce!
C1.ielts_writing: Slang such as "awesomesauce" should be avoided in formal writing.
C1.mistake: Reine Umgangssprache; in formellen Texten und im IELTS vermeiden.

C1.def: causing difficulty or embarrassment, or clumsy
C1.example: There was an awkward silence after his comment.
C1.ielts_writing: Awkward working conditions reduce productivity.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I feel awkward when I have to speak in front of a crowd."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit "w": "awkward", nicht "akward"; Aussprache /ˈɔːkwərd/.

C1.def: absent without leave; (informal) missing or unavailable
C1.example: Two soldiers went AWOL during the exercise.
C1.ielts_writing: Employees who go AWOL without notice can damage team morale.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My manager has been AWOL all week."
C1.mistake: Wird als ein Wort /ˈeɪwɔːl/ gesprochen, nicht als Buchstaben "A-W-O-L".

C1.def: an imaginary line around which a body rotates, or a reference line on a graph
C1.example: The earth rotates on its axis once every twenty-four hours.
C1.ielts_writing: The horizontal axis of the graph shows time in years.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I couldn't read the y-axis on the chart."
C1.mistake: Plural: "axes" /ˈæksiːz/ (nicht "axises"); gleich geschrieben wie "axes" (Äxte).

C1.def: a large monkey with a long face found in Africa and Asia
C1.example: A baboon watched us from a rock beside the road.
C1.ielts_writing: Baboons live in complex social groups with clear hierarchies.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw baboons at the safari park."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (/bæˈbuːn/), nicht "BAboon".

C1.def: one of the first set of teeth in a young child, later replaced by permanent ones
C1.example: She lost her first baby tooth at the age of six.
C1.ielts_writing: Baby teeth guide the growth of permanent teeth and help children speak clearly.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My son has a wobbly baby tooth."
C1.mistake: Plural "baby teeth" (nicht "baby tooths"); in der Fachsprache "primary teeth".

C1.def: to support someone or something, especially financially
C1.example: Several investors have backed the start-up.
C1.ielts_writing: Public opinion backs stricter laws on plastic waste.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My family backed me when I changed careers."
C1.mistake: "back" als Verb bedeutet unterstützen; "back up" heißt auch "sichern" (Daten) oder "rückwärts fahren".

C1.def: the scenery at the back of a stage, or the setting of an event
C1.example: The mountains formed a dramatic backdrop for the wedding photos.
C1.ielts_writing: Against the backdrop of rising inflation, central banks raised interest rates.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The old castle was the perfect backdrop for the festival."
C1.mistake: Wendung: "against the backdrop OF", nicht "on the backdrop".

C1.def: the part of a scene behind the main subject, or a person's origin, education, and experience
C1.example: Her background in medicine made her a strong candidate.
C1.ielts_writing: Students from disadvantaged backgrounds face additional barriers to higher education.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I come from a very mixed background."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise "background" mit "g" in der Mitte, nicht "backround"; zählbar: "backgrounds".

C1.def: support or help, especially financial
C1.example: The project received strong backing from local businesses.
C1.ielts_writing: Political backing is often necessary for large infrastructure projects.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She has the backing of her whole family."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; musikalisch bedeutet "backing" auch "Begleitung" ("backing vocals").

C1.def: in the area behind the stage in a theater
C1.example: The actors waited backstage before their entrance.
C1.ielts_writing: Backstage staff play a vital but often invisible role in successful productions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I got to go backstage after the concert."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben ("backstage"); als Adverb ohne "to": "go backstage".

C1.def: the history or background of a character or situation
C1.example: The film gives the villain a tragic backstory.
C1.ielts_writing: A well-developed backstory can make fictional characters feel more realistic.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love the backstory of this series; it's so detailed."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben ("backstory"); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a copy of data kept in case the original is lost, or extra support
C1.example: Always keep a backup of your important files.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular backups protect organizations against the loss of critical data.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have a backup plan in case it rains."
C1.mistake: Nomen "backup" (zusammen), Verb "back up" (getrennt): "Please back up your files."

C1.def: easily annoyed and often irritable
C1.example: He gets bad-tempered when he doesn't get enough sleep.
C1.ielts_writing: A bad-tempered manager can quickly damage staff morale.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandfather was bad-tempered in the mornings."
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich: "bad-tempered"; nicht mit "bad temper" (Nomen: Jähzorn) verwechseln.

C1.def: a nocturnal mammal with a black and white striped face, living in burrows; to pester someone
C1.example: A badger crossed the road in front of us.
C1.ielts_writing: Badger populations have declined in some regions because of habitat loss.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My brother keeps badgering me to lend him money."
C1.mistake: Als Verb "to badger sb" bedeutet belästigen, bedrängen; nicht nur das Tier.

C1.def: a wind instrument with a bag that holds air and several pipes
C1.example: A piper played the bagpipe at the Scottish festival.
C1.ielts_writing: The bagpipe is closely associated with Scottish and Irish folk traditions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My uncle plays the bagpipe at parades."
C1.mistake: Meist im Plural gebraucht: "bagpipes"; Dudelsack heißt nicht "Sackpfeife" im Englischen.

C1.def: money paid to a court so an accused person can stay free until trial
C1.example: The judge set bail at fifty thousand dollars.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics argue that cash bail penalizes poorer defendants before they have been convicted.
C1.mistake: "bail out" bedeutet auch "jemanden retten" und "aussteigen"; "bail" (Kaution) ist nicht "Bahnhof".

C1.def: food made by baking, such as bread, cakes, and pastries
C1.example: The bakery sells fresh baked goods every morning.
C1.ielts_writing: Baked goods account for a large share of the store's weekend sales.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I brought some baked goods to the office party."
C1.mistake: Immer Plural ("baked goods"), nicht "a baked good".

C1.def: extremely hot (informal, of weather)
C1.example: It was a baking afternoon, and nobody wanted to leave the shade.
C1.ielts_writing: Baking temperatures in the desert make midday work dangerous.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's baking out there; bring some water."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "backen" verwechseln; "baking hot" ist umgangssprachlich für "glühend heiß".

C1.def: a slow sentimental song, or a narrative poem
C1.example: She sang a haunting ballad about lost love.
C1.ielts_writing: The folk ballad preserved stories of local history through generations.
C1.mistake: Heißt auf Deutsch nicht immer "Ballade" im literarischen Sinn: "power ballad" ist ein Rocksong.

C1.def: a system of secret voting, or the paper used for voting
C1.example: Voters cast their ballots on Tuesday.
C1.ielts_writing: Secret ballots protect citizens from pressure when they vote.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I mailed in my ballot last week."
C1.mistake: "ballot" ist der Stimmzettel oder der Wahlgang, nicht die "Ballade".

C1.def: a pen with a small ball at its tip that rolls ink onto paper
C1.example: She signed the form with a blue ballpoint.
C1.ielts_writing: Ballpoint pens replaced fountain pens in most offices during the twentieth century.
C1.mistake: Kurzform "ballpoint"; Kugelschreiber ist nicht "ball pen".

C1.def: a formal style of partner dancing, such as the waltz or tango
C1.example: They took ballroom dancing lessons before the wedding.
C1.ielts_writing: Ballroom dancing has become popular through televised competitions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My parents met at a ballroom dancing class."
C1.mistake: Als Gesellschaftstanz nicht mit "Ballett" (ballet) gleichsetzen.

C1.def: crazy or very enthusiastic (informal)
C1.example: The crowd went bananas when the band came on stage.
C1.ielts_writing: Informal expressions like "go bananas" are better avoided in academic writing.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My dog goes bananas when she sees a squirrel."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "go bananas" oder "drive sb bananas", nicht "go banana".

C1.def: a robber, especially one of an armed gang
C1.example: Bandits attacked the stagecoach in the canyon.
C1.ielts_writing: Roving bandits have long threatened trade routes in remote regions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The movie is about a bandit in the Wild West."
C1.mistake: "one-armed bandit" bedeutet Spielautomat; Plural "bandits".

C1.def: to hit something hard with a loud noise, or a sudden loud noise
C1.example: He banged on the door until someone answered.
C1.ielts_writing: Residents were woken by a bang from the construction site.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I banged my knee on the table."
C1.mistake: "bang on the door" heißt "an die Tür hämmern"; "bang" ist laut, kein leises "klopfen" (knock).

C1.def: unable to pay debts and legally declared insolvent
C1.example: The company went bankrupt after losing its largest customer.
C1.ielts_writing: Many small retailers have been driven bankrupt by rising rents and online competition.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'd be bankrupt if I paid for that."
C1.mistake: "bankrupt" ist ein Adjektiv ("go bankrupt"), das Nomen heißt "bankruptcy".

C1.def: a long strip of cloth with a slogan or design, or a prominent heading on a website
C1.example: Protesters carried a banner reading "Save Our Park."
C1.ielts_writing: A banner at the top of the page announced the sale.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We hung a banner for her birthday."
C1.mistake: "banner headline" ist die große Titelschlagzeile in einer Zeitung.

C1.def: a large formal meal for many people, often to celebrate something
C1.example: The mayor hosted a banquet for the visiting delegation.
C1.ielts_writing: Annual banquets bring members of the association together to celebrate achievements.
C1.mistake: "banquet" bezeichnet ein offizielles Festessen, nicht "Bankett" im Sinne von Straßenrand (das ist "shoulder").

C1.def: a place where drinks are served, a long piece of material, or an obstacle
C1.example: We met at a bar near the station.
C1.ielts_writing: Language can be a bar to social mobility for newcomers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'll grab a candy bar on the way."
C1.mistake: Vielfältig: "behind bars" heißt "hinter Gittern", "raise the bar" heißt "die Messlatte höher legen".

C1.def: a sweet and smoky sauce used for grilled meat
C1.example: He brushed barbecue sauce on the ribs.
C1.ielts_writing: Regional variations in barbecue sauce reflect local culinary traditions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I like extra barbecue sauce on my burger."
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "BBQ"; "barbecue" schreibt man nicht "barbeque" in formellen Texten.

C1.def: a pattern of lines that stores product information when scanned
C1.example: The cashier scanned the barcode on the box.
C1.ielts_writing: Barcodes allow retailers to track inventory in real time.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I can't scan this barcode; it's damaged."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; Strichcode ist nicht "strip code".

C1.def: without covering or decoration; to reveal something
C1.example: The room had only a bed and bare walls.
C1.ielts_writing: The investigation bared evidence of widespread corruption.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She walked on the beach in bare feet."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "bear" (tragen, Bär) verwechseln; "barely" heißt "kaum", nicht "nackt".

C1.def: something bought for less than its usual price, or to negotiate
C1.example: The jacket was a real bargain at half price.
C1.ielts_writing: Trade unions bargain with employers over wages and conditions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I found a great bargain at the flea market."
C1.mistake: "bargain for sth" bedeutet "mit etwas rechnen" ("more than I bargained for").

C1.def: the outer covering of a tree, or the sound a dog makes
C1.example: The bark of the oak was rough and deeply furrowed.
C1.ielts_writing: Cork is harvested from the bark of a particular type of oak.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Baumrinde und Bellen; "bark orders" heißt "Befehle bellen".

C1.def: a nobleman of the lowest rank, or a powerful businessperson
C1.example: The baron inherited the castle from his father.
C1.ielts_writing: Media barons wield considerable influence over public opinion.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's a cattle baron with thousands of acres."
C1.mistake: "baron" kann auch einen mächtigen Geschäftsmann bezeichnen ("oil baron").

C1.def: a large round container for liquids, or the tube of a gun
C1.example: The wine is aged in oak barrels.
C1.ielts_writing: Oil prices are quoted per barrel on international markets.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We rolled the barrel down the ramp."
collocations: scrape the bottom of the barrel
C1.mistake: Als Ölmaß ("barrel"): ca. 159 Liter; "barrel" bezeichnet auch den Gewehrlauf.

C1.def: unable to support plant growth, or unable to bear children
C1.example: The island was a barren rock with no vegetation.
C1.ielts_writing: Overgrazing can turn productive grassland into barren land.
C1.mistake: Bei Menschen veraltet und unsensibel; heute sagt man "infertile".

C1.def: to exchange goods or services without using money
C1.example: Villagers bartered eggs for flour at the market.
C1.ielts_writing: Before currency existed, communities bartered goods to meet their needs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I bartered my old bike for a guitar."
C1.mistake: Nomen und Verb gleich; Konstruktion: "barter sth FOR sth".

C1.def: a fragrant herb used in Italian cooking
C1.example: She tore fresh basil over the pasta.
C1.ielts_writing: Basil is traditionally paired with tomatoes in Mediterranean cuisine.
C1.mistake: Im Amerikanischen /ˈbeɪzəl/; unzählbar: "some basil".

C1.def: the lowest range of musical sound, or a male singer with a deep voice
C1.example: He plays bass in a local band.
C1.ielts_writing: The bass line gives the song its rhythmic foundation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I like music with a heavy bass."
C1.mistake: Zwei Aussprachen: /beɪs/ (Musik) und /bæs/ (Fisch, Barsch).

C1.def: a wooden club used to hit a ball, a flying mammal, or to hit a ball
C1.example: He swung the bat and hit a home run.
C1.ielts_writing: Bats play an important role in pollinating plants.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I didn't bat an eye when he said it."
C1.mistake: Drei Bedeutungen; "bat an eye" bedeutet "mit der Wimper zucken".

C1.def: a liquid mixture of flour, eggs, and milk used for cooking, or a baseball hitter
C1.example: Pour the pancake batter into a hot pan.
C1.ielts_writing: Fried foods are coated in batter before they are cooked.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The batter hit a double in the ninth inning."
C1.mistake: Der "batter" ist auch der Schlagmann im Baseball; das Verb "batter" bedeutet "schlagen, misshandeln".

C1.def: the place where a battle is or was fought
C1.example: Tourists visit the battlefield where the army was defeated.
C1.ielts_writing: The battlefield for the election has shifted to social media.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Gettysburg is one of the best-known battlefields."
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich verwendbar für "Schauplatz eines Konflikts".

C1.def: a broad inlet of the sea where the land curves inward
C1.example: The boats were anchored in a quiet bay.
C1.ielts_writing: Pollution in the bay has affected local fishing communities.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We spent the afternoon walking along the bay."
C1.mistake: "hold at bay" heißt "in Schach halten"; "bay window" ist ein Erkerfenster.

C1.def: before the birth of Christ, used with dates
C1.example: The Roman Republic was founded in 509 BC.
C1.ielts_writing: Ancient Greek democracy emerged around the fifth century BC.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He lived in the third century BC."
C1.mistake: Steht hinter der Jahreszahl ("500 BC"), während "AD" davor steht ("AD 500").

C1.def: (of an activity) to be something a person enjoys or is good at
C1.example: Skiing isn't really my thing.
C1.ielts_writing: Not every colleague will find that kind of work to be their thing.
C1.mistake: Meist in der Verneinung: "That's not my thing" bedeutet "das ist nichts für mich".

C1.def: a small piece of glass or wood with a hole through it, strung on a thread
C1.example: She wore a necklace of colorful beads.
C1.ielts_writing: Beads of sweat formed on his forehead.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I made a bracelet out of wooden beads."
C1.mistake: Auch für Tropfen (Schweiß, Wasser): "beads of sweat".

C1.def: a ray of light, a long piece of wood or metal, or to smile broadly
C1.example: A beam of sunlight shone through the window.
C1.ielts_writing: Steel beams support the structure of the building.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She beamed with pride at her daughter's success."
C1.mistake: Das Verb "beam" heißt auch "strahlend lächeln" und "senden" ("beam a signal").

C1.def: a large or dangerous animal, or a cruel person
C1.example: The beast roared and charged at the hunters.
C1.ielts_writing: Folklore across many cultures features a fearsome beast in the forest.
C1.mistake: Meist für wilde Tiere oder bildlich für brutale Menschen; neutral kann es "tough" ("a beast of a job") bedeuten.

C1.def: a person who gives beauty treatments, such as facials and manicures
C1.example: She works as a beautician at a salon.
C1.ielts_writing: Beauticians must complete training and pass a licensing exam in many states.
C1.mistake: "beautician" ist weiblich konnotiert, "cosmetologist" ist die Berufsbezeichnung.

C1.def: a place of business offering hair and skin treatments
C1.example: She booked an appointment at the beauty salon.
C1.ielts_writing: Beauty salons form an important part of the local service economy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a beauty salon next to the post office."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (salon); der Friseur heißt "hair salon" oder "barbershop".

C1.def: earlier than an event or action
C1.example: Please let us know beforehand if you cannot attend.
C1.ielts_writing: Candidates should read the material beforehand to participate fully.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I called beforehand to make sure they were open."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; steht am Satzende, nicht vor einem Nomen.

C1.def: in the interests of or as a representative of someone
C1.example: She accepted the award on behalf of the whole team.
C1.ielts_writing: The lawyer spoke on behalf of her clients.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm calling on behalf of my boss."
C1.mistake: Nur in "on behalf OF" oder "in someone's behalf" verwendet; nicht als "on behalf to".

C1.def: pale sandy fawn color
C1.example: She wore a beige coat and brown boots.
C1.ielts_writing: The walls were painted a neutral beige to make the room feel larger.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /beɪʒ/, mit "sch" wie in "Garage".

C1.def: a hollow, mild-flavored vegetable, usually green, red, or yellow
C1.example: She chopped a red bell pepper for the salad.
C1.ielts_writing: Bell peppers are rich in vitamin C.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I put sliced bell peppers on the pizza."
C1.mistake: Paprika heißt "bell pepper", nicht "paprika" (das ist das Gewürz).

C1.def: a dance from the Middle East with movements of the hips and abdomen
C1.example: She takes belly dance classes on weekends.
C1.ielts_writing: Belly dance is both a performance art and a fitness practice.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen oft getrennt ("belly dance"), die Tänzerin ist "belly dancer".

C1.def: a feeling of being accepted as part of a group, or one's personal possessions
C1.example: Newcomers need a sense of belonging to feel at home.
C1.ielts_writing: A strong sense of belonging reduces loneliness among young adults.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Please take all your belongings with you."
C1.mistake: Im Plural "belongings" = Habseligkeiten; im Singular = Zugehörigkeitsgefühl.

C1.def: dearly loved
C1.example: She was a beloved teacher.
C1.ielts_writing: The beloved author's final novel was published after his death.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My beloved grandmother passed away last year."
C1.mistake: Zwei Aussprachen: als Adjektiv oft /bɪˈlʌvɪd/, als Partizip /bɪˈlʌvd/.

C1.def: a long seat for several people, or the position of a judge
C1.example: We sat on a bench in the park.
C1.ielts_writing: The judge on the bench ruled in favor of the defendant.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's been on the bench for years."
C1.mistake: "bench" kann auch Reservebank im Sport bedeuten ("sit on the bench").

C1.def: a standard against which things are compared
C1.example: The test sets a benchmark for student performance.
C1.ielts_writing: Industry benchmarks help companies assess their efficiency against competitors.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We use last year's numbers as a benchmark."
C1.mistake: Als Verb: "to benchmark sth against sth"; Präposition beim Nomen: "benchmark FOR".

C1.def: in a lower position than something
C1.example: The treasure was buried beneath the old oak tree.
C1.ielts_writing: Beneath the surface of the dispute lies a conflict over resources.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt the ground tremble beneath my feet."
C1.mistake: Formeller als "under"; "beneath your dignity" bedeutet "unter deiner Würde".

C1.def: a person who receives money or benefit, especially from a will or policy
C1.example: She is the sole beneficiary of her aunt's will.
C1.ielts_writing: Low-income households are the main beneficiaries of the new subsidy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My name is listed as the beneficiary on his policy."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-FISH-); Plural: "beneficiaries".

C1.def: kind and generous toward others
C1.example: The benevolent donor funded a new library.
C1.ielts_writing: Some companies adopt a benevolent attitude toward employees by offering generous benefits.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She is a benevolent leader who cares about her team."
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "malevolent" (böswillig); beide enden auf "-volent".

C1.def: (of a tumor) not harmful, or gentle and kindly
C1.example: The doctor said the tumor was benign.
C1.ielts_writing: A benign smile spread across his face.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /bɪˈnaɪn/ mit Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Gegensatz: "malignant".

C1.def: to be disloyal to someone who trusts you, or to reveal something unintentionally
C1.example: He betrayed his friends by sharing their secrets.
C1.ielts_writing: Her expression betrayed her nervousness despite her calm words.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt betrayed when I found out she had lied."
C1.mistake: Nomen "betrayal"; "betray" kann auch "unbewusst verraten" bedeuten ("betray your emotions").

C1.def: to be careful because something may be dangerous
C1.example: Beware of the dog.
C1.ielts_writing: Consumers should beware of offers that seem too good to be true.
C1.mistake: Nur im Imperativ oder Infinitiv gebräuchlich; immer mit "of": "beware OF sth".

C1.def: so clearly that no reasonable person could disagree
C1.example: The defendant's guilt was proven beyond doubt.
C1.ielts_writing: The evidence shows beyond doubt that emissions have risen.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's beyond doubt that she is the best candidate."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung ohne Artikel; juristisch: "beyond a reasonable doubt".

C1.def: a very close friend (informal abbreviation of "best friends forever")
C1.example: She is my BFF, and we tell each other everything.
C1.ielts_writing: Abbreviations such as "BFF" are common in texting but unsuitable for academic essays.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My BFF is coming to visit this weekend."
C1.mistake: Wird als Buchstabenfolge gesprochen; nur in Chat und lockerer Sprache.

C1.def: an unfair preference for or against someone or something
C1.example: The report revealed a bias against older applicants.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers must take steps to minimize bias in their data collection.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I try not to let my own bias affect my decisions."
C1.mistake: Präpositionen: "bias AGAINST sb", "bias TOWARD/IN FAVOR OF sb"; Adjektiv "biased", nicht "biasing".

C1.def: a piece of cloth tied under a baby's chin to protect clothing while eating
C1.example: She tied a bib around the baby's neck.
C1.ielts_writing: Parents often use a bib to prevent food stains on clothes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The baby wore a bib with a little duck on it."
C1.mistake: Lätzchen ist nicht "bid" (Gebot); Plural "bibs".

C1.def: a list of books and sources used in a piece of research
C1.example: Include a bibliography at the end of your essay.
C1.ielts_writing: A comprehensive bibliography demonstrates the breadth of the writer's research.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm still compiling the bibliography for my thesis."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der vierten Silbe (-OG-); "annotated bibliography" enthält Kommentare zu jeder Quelle.

C1.def: the explosive event from which the universe is thought to have expanded
C1.example: Scientists believe the universe began with the Big Bang about 13.8 billion years ago.
C1.ielts_writing: The Big Bang theory is supported by observations of background radiation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We learned about the Big Bang in physics class."
C1.mistake: Meist groß geschrieben ("the Big Bang"); mit Artikel verwenden.

C1.def: (informal) to a great extent or in a major way
C1.example: He messed up big time during the presentation.
C1.ielts_writing: The company has hit the big time with its new product line.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I owe you big time for helping me move."
C1.mistake: Als Adverb: "mess up big time"; als Nomen "the big time" bedeutet "der große Durchbruch".

C1.def: having a large, strong body frame
C1.example: My sister is big-boned, so she wears larger sizes.
C1.ielts_writing: Terms like "big-boned" can reinforce stereotypes about body shape.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's tall and big-boned like his father."
C1.mistake: Kann als Euphemismus für "dick" verstanden werden; vorsichtig verwenden.

C1.def: to tie or fasten something, or to legally or morally oblige someone
C1.example: The contract binds both parties to its terms.
C1.ielts_writing: Shared values bind communities together.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I had to bind the papers with a rubber band."
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: bind, bound, bound; "bound" bedeutet auch "verpflichtet" ("duty-bound").

C1.def: watching several episodes of a series in one sitting
C1.example: Binge-watching a whole season in one night left me exhausted.
C1.ielts_writing: Streaming platforms have encouraged binge-watching by releasing entire seasons at once.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I did some binge-watching over the weekend."
C1.mistake: Verb "binge-watch" (binge-watched); nicht mit "bingen" (Zahnrad) oder "binge drinking" verwechseln.

C1.def: able to be broken down naturally by bacteria or other organisms
C1.example: These biodegradable bags dissolve in compost within weeks.
C1.ielts_writing: Biodegradable packaging can reduce the amount of waste that ends up in landfills.
C1.mistake: "biodegradable" heißt biologisch abbaubar, nicht "kompostierbar" (compostable) im strengen Sinn.

C1.def: the variety of plant and animal life in a habitat or on earth
C1.example: The rainforest is famous for its biodiversity.
C1.ielts_writing: Habitat destruction is a leading cause of declining biodiversity worldwide.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We need to protect biodiversity in our local parks."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar, daher "biodiversity is" (nicht "biodiversities").

C1.def: a written account of someone's life by another person
C1.example: She wrote a biography of the physicist.
C1.ielts_writing: A well-researched biography can change how readers see a historical figure.
C1.mistake: Von einem anderen geschrieben; die eigene Lebensgeschichte heißt "autobiography".

C1.def: the scientific study of living organisms
C1.example: She studied biology at university.
C1.ielts_writing: Advances in molecular biology have transformed medical research.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My favorite subject in school was biology."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-OL-); Adjektiv "biological".

C1.def: having parents from two different racial or ethnic groups
C1.example: The study surveyed biracial young adults about their identities.
C1.ielts_writing: Biracial people often navigate complex questions about identity and belonging.
C1.mistake: Sensibler Begriff; heute verwenden viele Menschen "multiracial" oder "mixed".

C1.def: a viral infection of birds that can spread to humans
C1.example: The outbreak of bird flu led to the culling of thousands of chickens.
C1.ielts_writing: Authorities monitor bird flu closely because new strains could infect people.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Many poultry farms were affected by bird flu."
C1.mistake: Fachsprache: "avian influenza"; Vogelgrippe ist nicht "bird grippe".

C1.def: a ballpoint pen
C1.example: He signed the form with a biro.
C1.ielts_writing: The biro became a symbol of affordable writing tools.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Do you have a biro I can borrow?"
C1.mistake: Markenname, im Alltag allgemein für Kugelschreiber; wird klein geschrieben.

C1.def: attracted to both men and women
C1.example: She came out as bisexual last year.
C1.ielts_writing: Bisexual individuals have historically been less visible in public debates.
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv und Nomen verwendbar; "bi" ist die Kurzform.

C1.def: a senior Christian clergyman, or a chess piece
C1.example: The bishop led the service at the cathedral.
C1.ielts_writing: The bishop spoke out against the proposed law on moral grounds.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I moved my bishop diagonally across the board."
C1.mistake: "bishop" bedeutet auch Läufer im Schach.

C1.def: a small, informal restaurant
C1.example: We had lunch at a cozy French bistro.
C1.ielts_writing: Bistros often offer simple meals at moderate prices.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I met my friend at a small bistro."
C1.mistake: Plural "bistros"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: very strange or unusual
C1.example: The film had a bizarre ending that left everyone confused.
C1.ielts_writing: The bizarre behavior of the stock market surprised many analysts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's bizarre how quickly the weather changes here."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise "bizarre" mit "z", nicht "bizzare".

C1.def: the crime of forcing someone to do something by threatening to reveal secrets
C1.example: He was arrested for attempting to blackmail his boss.
C1.ielts_writing: Emotional blackmail damages trust in personal relationships.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They tried to blackmail him with embarrassing photos."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "blackmail sb INTO doing sth"; "mail" hat hier keine Verbindung zur Post.

C1.def: the sharp part of a knife or tool, or a flat leaf of grass
C1.example: The blade of the knife was very sharp.
C1.ielts_writing: Wind turbine blades can span more than sixty meters.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I cut myself on the razor blade."
C1.mistake: "blade" ist auch Rollschuh- oder Schlittschuhkufe ("rollerblade").

C1.def: lacking strong flavor or character
C1.example: The soup was bland and needed more salt.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics described the film's script as bland and predictable.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I prefer bland food when I'm sick."
C1.mistake: Bezieht sich auf Geschmack und Ausdruck; nicht "blind".

C1.def: a powerful explosion or strong gust of air, or to destroy something with explosives
C1.example: The blast shook the windows of nearby houses.
C1.ielts_writing: Rescue workers rushed to the scene of the blast.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We had a blast at the party."
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich: "have a blast" bedeutet "sich großartig amüsieren".

C1.def: a large, fierce fire, or to burn brightly
C1.example: Firefighters battled the blaze for hours.
C1.ielts_writing: The blaze destroyed several historic buildings in the town center.
C1.mistake: Redewendung: "blaze a trail" bedeutet "neue Wege bahnen".

C1.def: to lose blood from the body
C1.example: He cut his finger and it began to bleed.
C1.ielts_writing: A bleeding wound should be pressed firmly with a clean cloth.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My nose bleeds easily in dry weather."
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: bleed, bled, bled; Nomen "blood", Adjektiv "bloody".

C1.def: to mix things together so that they form a smooth combination
C1.example: Blend the ingredients until the mixture is smooth.
C1.ielts_writing: The architect blended modern and traditional elements in the design.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She blended in easily with the crowd."
C1.mistake: "blend in" bedeutet "sich einfügen, nicht auffallen"; "blend" ist regelmäßig (blended).

C1.def: to ask God's favor for someone, or to make something holy
C1.example: The priest blessed the couple at their wedding.
C1.ielts_writing: The community gathered to bless the new school.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Bless you!" she said when I sneezed.
C1.mistake: Als Interjektion nach dem Niesen: "Bless you!" (nicht "Gesundheit").

C1.def: God's favor, or something that brings good fortune
C1.example: The rain was a blessing for the dry fields.
C1.ielts_writing: Parents' blessing can be important in some cultural traditions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's a blessing in disguise that I missed that flight."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "a blessing in disguise" (ein Glück im Unglück); "give your blessing" = zustimmen.

C1.def: a plant disease or something that spoils or damages something
C1.example: Blight destroyed the potato harvest.
C1.ielts_writing: Urban blight is a persistent issue in many post-industrial cities.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The abandoned factory is a blight on the neighborhood."
C1.mistake: Als Verb "blight" heißt "ruinieren"; auch bildlich ("a blight on society").

C1.def: a small bubble on the skin filled with fluid, caused by friction or burns
C1.example: New shoes gave her a blister on her heel.
C1.ielts_writing: Prolonged walking in damp socks can cause painful blisters.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I got a blister from the long hike."
C1.mistake: "blister pack" bedeutet Durchdrückverpackung für Tabletten.

C1.def: a mass of thickened blood
C1.example: A blood clot formed in his leg after the surgery.
C1.ielts_writing: Blood clots can be life-threatening if they travel to the lungs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The doctor warned me about the risk of blood clots."
C1.mistake: Fachsprache: "thrombus" oder "clot"; Verb "to clot" heißt "gerinnen".

C1.def: one of the groups into which blood is classified, such as A, B, AB, or O
C1.example: My blood type is O negative.
C1.ielts_writing: Knowing your blood type is vital for emergency transfusions.
C1.mistake: Es heißt "blood type" (z. B. "type O"), nicht "blood group".

C1.def: a line of descent from an ancestor
C1.example: The king's bloodline stretched back for centuries.
C1.ielts_writing: Pedigree dogs are bred to preserve their bloodline.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "blood vessel" (Blutgefäß) verwechseln.

C1.def: covered with blood, or used as a mild curse
C1.example: The soldier returned with a bloody bandage.
C1.ielts_writing: The conflict became one of the bloodiest in modern history.
C1.mistake: Als Fluch derb und salopp; in formellen Texten und im IELTS vermeiden.

C1.def: the flower of a tree, or to produce flowers or to develop
C1.example: The cherry trees are in full blossom.
C1.ielts_writing: Their friendship blossomed into something deeper over the years.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The garden bursts into blossom every spring."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "blossom into sth"; im Singular unzählbar: "in full blossom".

C1.def: a hard hit with the hand or an object, or a shock or disappointment
C1.example: He took a blow to the head during the fight.
C1.ielts_writing: The closure of the factory was a severe blow to the local economy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It was a blow when I didn't get the job."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "a blow TO sth"; "come to blows" bedeutet "handgreiflich werden".

C1.def: to explode, to inflate something, or to enlarge a photo
C1.example: The bridge was blown up during the war.
C1.ielts_writing: Please blow up the balloons before the guests arrive.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I had the photo blown up to poster size."
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutiges Phrasal Verb; "blow up at sb" heißt "jemanden anfahren".

C1.def: a tube from which a small dart is blown
C1.example: The hunter used a blowgun to shoot darts at birds.
C1.ielts_writing: Blowguns are still used for hunting in some parts of the Amazon.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw a blowgun in the museum."
C1.mistake: Zusammengeschrieben; als Waffe oder Jagdgerät nicht mit "Blasebalg" (bellows) verwechseln.

C1.def: a high-definition optical disc format for video and data
C1.example: I bought the film on Blu-ray.
C1.ielts_writing: Blu-ray offers a higher-resolution picture than a standard DVD.
C1.mistake: Schreibweise "Blu-ray", nicht "Blue-ray".

C1.def: a style of slow, melancholy music, or a feeling of sadness
C1.example: He plays blues on the guitar.
C1.ielts_writing: The blues emerged from African American communities in the American South.
C1.mistake: Im Plural ("the blues"); auch Verb-Form "feel blue" für "traurig sein".

C1.def: a wireless technology for exchanging data over short distances
C1.example: My phone connects to the speaker via Bluetooth.
C1.ielts_writing: Bluetooth devices communicate using short-range radio waves.
C1.mistake: Eigenname, immer groß geschrieben; Aussprache /ˈbluːtuːθ/.

C1.def: a school where students live during the term
C1.example: He went to a boarding school in New England.
C1.ielts_writing: Boarding schools offer structured environments but can be expensive.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "boardwalk" oder "boarding pass" verwechseln; Internat = "boarding school".

C1.def: a room where a company's directors hold meetings
C1.example: The CEO called an emergency meeting in the boardroom.
C1.ielts_writing: Boardroom decisions often shape the direction of entire industries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The boardroom was packed for the annual meeting."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; "board" meint hier den Vorstand.

C1.def: to talk with excessive pride about your achievements
C1.example: He boasted about his new car to everyone.
C1.ielts_writing: The city boasts several award-winning restaurants.
C1.mistake: Auch für Sachen: "the hotel boasts a pool" (hat vorzuweisen).

C1.def: the activity of traveling or racing in boats for pleasure
C1.example: We spent the weekend boating on the lake.
C1.ielts_writing: Recreational boating contributes to the economy of many coastal towns.
C1.mistake: Meist als "go boating"; nicht mit "bowling" verwechseln.

C1.def: the practice of lifting weights to build muscle for competition
C1.example: He took up bodybuilding after high school.
C1.ielts_writing: Bodybuilding requires disciplined diet and consistent training.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My brother does bodybuilding at the gym."
C1.mistake: "bodybuilding" ist ein Hobby oder Sport, nicht dasselbe wie "fitness".

C1.def: willingness to take risks and act in a confident, daring way
C1.example: The boldness of her plan impressed the investors.
C1.ielts_writing: Political boldness is often required to introduce unpopular but necessary reforms.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I admire his boldness in asking for a raise."
C1.mistake: Nomen zu "bold"; nicht mit "Boldheit" bilden.

C1.def: the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai
C1.example: She loves watching Bollywood movies with big dance numbers.
C1.ielts_writing: Bollywood has gained a global audience through streaming platforms.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We went to a Bollywood night at the cinema."
C1.mistake: Eigenname, immer groß; der Name verbindet "Bombay" und "Hollywood".

C1.def: to strengthen or support something
C1.example: The new evidence bolstered her argument.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments introduced measures to bolster the struggling economy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I took a course to bolster my confidence."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion ohne Präposition: "bolster sth"; "bolster" ist auch ein Kissen (Nomen).

C1.def: to attack with bombs or to overwhelm someone with questions or information
C1.example: Reporters bombarded the minister with questions.
C1.ielts_writing: Young people are bombarded with advertising on social media every day.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was bombarded with emails after the announcement."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "bombard sb WITH sth"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a close connection between people, a financial security, or to establish a connection
C1.example: The two sisters share a strong bond.
C1.ielts_writing: Government bonds are considered a low-risk investment.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I bonded with my coworkers over lunch."
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: "bond with sb" heißt "eine Beziehung aufbauen", "bond" auch Anleihe oder Kaution.

C1.def: an extra payment given in addition to salary, or an additional advantage
C1.example: Employees received a bonus at the end of the year.
C1.ielts_writing: Performance-related bonuses can motivate staff to meet ambitious targets.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's a bonus that the hotel includes breakfast."
C1.mistake: Plural "bonuses" (nicht "bonusses" oder "boni"); auch als Vorteil: "a bonus".

C1.def: to reserve a room in a hotel in advance
C1.example: I'd like to book a room for two nights, please.
C1.ielts_writing: Travelers are advised to book a room well in advance during the peak season.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I booked a room at a small hotel by the beach."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "book a room FOR two nights"; "reserve a room" ist gleichbedeutend.

C1.def: a period of rapid economic growth, or a deep loud sound
C1.example: The tech boom created thousands of new jobs.
C1.ielts_writing: Housing booms are often followed by sharp corrections.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "boom and bust" (Aufschwung und Absturz); "boom" kann auch ein lauter Knall sein.

C1.def: to increase or improve something, or an increase
C1.example: The new policy should boost exports.
C1.ielts_writing: A morning run gives me a boost of energy.
C1.mistake: Nomen "boost" und Nomen "booster" (z. B. Auffrischimpfung: "booster shot").

C1.def: to spring back after hitting a surface, or (of a check) to be refused
C1.example: The ball bounced off the wall.
C1.ielts_writing: The company's shares bounced after the announcement.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My check bounced because I had no funds."
C1.mistake: "bounce ideas off sb" bedeutet "Ideen mit jemandem besprechen"; ein "bouncer" ist ein Türsteher.

C1.def: to recover quickly after a setback
C1.example: The economy bounced back after the recession.
C1.ielts_writing: Resilient communities bounce back from natural disasters more quickly.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She bounced back from the injury within weeks."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "bounce back FROM sth"; nicht "bounce back to".

C1.def: a line that marks the limit of an area, or a limit of acceptable behavior
C1.example: A river forms the boundary between the two countries.
C1.ielts_writing: Setting boundaries at work protects employees' personal time.
C1.mistake: Immer mit "boundary", nicht "boundry"; Präposition: "boundary BETWEEN".

C1.def: the middle class, especially in Marxist theory the property-owning class
C1.example: Marx described the conflict between the bourgeoisie and the proletariat.
C1.ielts_writing: The rise of the bourgeoisie transformed European society in the nineteenth century.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He criticized bourgeois values in his novel."
C1.mistake: Das Nomen ist kollektiv ("the bourgeoisie"), das Adjektiv heißt "bourgeois".

C1.def: a short period of illness or intense activity, or a boxing match
C1.example: He suffered a bout of flu last winter.
C1.ielts_writing: A bout of heavy rain caused flooding across the region.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have a nasty bout of insomnia."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "a bout OF sth"; als Kampf: "boxing bout".

C1.def: a small shop selling fashionable clothes or accessories
C1.example: She bought the dress at a trendy boutique.
C1.ielts_writing: Boutique hotels offer personalized service in a small, stylish setting.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a cute boutique around the corner."
C1.mistake: Das Wort "boutique" bezeichnet Mode oder Hotels, nicht jeden kleinen Laden.

C1.def: a knot with loops, a weapon for shooting arrows, or to bend forward as a sign of respect
C1.example: She wore a red bow in her hair.
C1.ielts_writing: The actors took a bow at the end of the play.
C1.mistake: Zwei Aussprachen: /boʊ/ (Bogen, Schleife) und /baʊ/ (verbeugen, Bug eines Schiffs).

C1.def: a game in which a heavy ball is rolled to knock down pins
C1.example: We went bowling on Friday night.
C1.ielts_writing: Bowling remains a popular social activity in the United States.
C1.mistake: "go bowling" ohne Artikel; "bowling alley" ist die Bowlingbahn.

C1.def: loose-fitting men's underwear shorts
C1.example: He packed three pairs of boxers for the trip.
C1.ielts_writing: Retailers have noticed shifts in preferences between briefs and boxers.
C1.mistake: Immer Plural ("boxers", "a pair of boxers"); auch Boxer (Sportler) heißt "boxer".

C1.def: a printed symbol around text, or a group within a range, such as an income level
C1.example: Put the extra information in brackets.
C1.ielts_writing: Higher tax brackets apply to people with larger incomes.
C1.mistake: "in brackets" bedeutet "in Klammern"; in der Wirtschaft "tax bracket" (Steuerklasse).

C1.def: (informal) very intelligent
C1.example: My brainy cousin always gets top grades.
C1.ielts_writing: The film portrays a brainy teenager who builds a robot.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich und leicht wertend; vgl. "clever" oder "intelligent".

C1.def: a part of a tree, an office of a company, or a department of a field
C1.example: A branch fell onto the road during the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: The bank opened a new branch in the city center.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I work at the local branch of the library."
C1.mistake: "branch out" bedeutet "sich verzweigen, Neues ausprobieren"; "branch of" für Fachgebiete.

C1.def: a yellow metal alloy, or musical instruments made of brass
C1.example: The doorknob was made of brass.
C1.ielts_writing: Brass instruments such as trumpets and trombones are common in marching bands.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I played brass in the school orchestra."
C1.mistake: "top brass" bedeutet "hohe Tiere, Führungsebene"; Betonung /bræs/ mit kurzem "a".

C1.def: a failure to obey a law or agreement, or a gap in a defense
C1.example: The company was sued for breach of contract.
C1.ielts_writing: A data breach exposed millions of customers' personal details.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They made a breach in the wall to get inside."
C1.mistake: Nomen "breach OF sth"; Verb "to breach" (verletzen); nicht mit "breech" verwechseln.

C1.def: small dry pieces of bread used for coating food
C1.example: Coat the chicken in breadcrumbs before frying it.
C1.ielts_writing: Dry breadcrumbs add crunch to baked dishes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need some breadcrumbs for this recipe."
C1.mistake: Immer Plural ("breadcrumbs"), nie "a breadcrumb" im Rezept.

C1.def: an illegal entry into a building to steal something
C1.example: Police are investigating a break-in at the museum.
C1.ielts_writing: Break-ins tend to rise during the holiday season.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There was a break-in at our neighbor's house."
C1.mistake: Nomen mit Bindestrich, Verb getrennt: "to break in".

C1.def: a failure or collapse, or a detailed analysis of figures
C1.example: The car had a breakdown on the highway.
C1.ielts_writing: A breakdown of the figures reveals where costs are rising.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She had a nervous breakdown after the divorce."
C1.mistake: Nomen "breakdown" zusammen, Verb "break down" getrennt.

C1.def: an important discovery or development that solves a problem
C1.example: Scientists announced a major breakthrough in cancer research.
C1.ielts_writing: A breakthrough in battery technology could accelerate the shift to electric vehicles.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We finally had a breakthrough in negotiations."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "breakthrough IN sth"; Verb "break through" getrennt.

C1.def: the end of a relationship or an organization
C1.example: Their breakup came as a shock to everyone.
C1.ielts_writing: The breakup of the empire led to decades of instability.
C1.ielts_speaking: "After the breakup, she moved to another city."
C1.mistake: Nomen "breakup" zusammen, Verb "break up" getrennt.

C1.def: out of breath, or excited and anxious
C1.example: She arrived breathless after running up the stairs.
C1.ielts_writing: The audience watched in breathless anticipation as the results were announced.
C1.mistake: Bedeutung "atemlos"; nicht mit "breathing" (Atmung) verwechseln.

C1.def: a view so impressive that it takes your breath away
C1.example: The hotel offers a breathtaking view of the mountains.
C1.ielts_writing: Travelers are often drawn to destinations with breathtaking views.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The breathtaking view from the top was worth the climb."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "breathtaking" zusammen; nicht "breathtakeing" schreiben.

C1.def: to keep animals to produce young, or a particular type of animal
C1.example: Farmers breed cattle for meat and milk.
C1.ielts_writing: Poverty can breed resentment and instability.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: breed, bred, bred; auch bildlich: "breed resentment" (Groll erzeugen).

C1.def: pleasantly windy, or casual and carefree
C1.example: It was a breezy day at the beach.
C1.ielts_writing: A breezy tone makes the article easy to read.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She gave a breezy wave and left."
C1.mistake: "breezy" ist positiv; Nomen "breeze" bedeutet "leichter Wind" oder "mühelos" ("a breeze").

C1.def: the quality of expressing something in few words
C1.example: The brevity of his speech surprised the audience.
C1.ielts_writing: Brevity is highly valued in academic abstracts.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "for the sake of brevity" (der Kürze halber).

C1.def: the process of making beer or tea, or something developing
C1.example: Home brewing has become a popular hobby.
C1.ielts_writing: A crisis is brewing in the global energy markets.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm brewing a fresh pot of coffee."
C1.mistake: "brewing" auch bildlich: "a storm is brewing" (ein Sturm zieht auf).

C1.def: money or a favor offered to persuade someone to act dishonestly
C1.example: The official was caught accepting a bribe.
C1.ielts_writing: Bribery undermines public trust in democratic institutions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They tried to bribe the guard with cash."
C1.mistake: Das Verb heißt "bribe sb", das Nomen für die Tat "bribery"; Konstruktion: "bribe sb to do sth".

C1.def: lasting a short time, or using few words
C1.example: She gave a brief summary of the report.
C1.ielts_writing: A brief interruption caused no lasting damage to the project.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /briːf/; Verb "to brief" bedeutet "informieren, einweisen".

C1.def: to cause something to happen
C1.example: The new law brought about major changes in healthcare.
C1.ielts_writing: Technological innovation can bring about profound shifts in society.
C1.mistake: Trennbar nur mit Objekt: "bring sth about"; nicht "bring around" (überzeugen).

C1.def: high-speed internet access
C1.example: We upgraded to a faster broadband plan.
C1.ielts_writing: Access to broadband is increasingly regarded as essential for rural communities.
C1.mistake: Nomen unzählbar: "broadband is...", nicht "a broadband" ohne Zusatz.

C1.def: a famous street in New York City, known for its theaters
C1.example: She dreams of performing on Broadway.
C1.ielts_writing: Broadway productions draw millions of visitors to New York each year.
C1.mistake: Eigenname, groß; Präposition: "on Broadway", nicht "at Broadway".

C1.def: (informal) having no money
C1.example: I'm broke until payday.
C1.ielts_writing: Many students are broke by the end of the month.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We went broke after the restaurant failed."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "broke" (Umgangssprache); "broken" bedeutet defekt; "go broke" = pleitegehen.

C1.def: damaged or no longer working, or violated
C1.example: The window was broken in the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: A broken promise can destroy trust in a relationship.
C1.mistake: Partizip von "break"; "broken English" bezeichnet fehlerhaftes Englisch.

C1.def: (informal) a very close friendship between two men
C1.example: Their bromance is obvious from the way they joke around.
C1.ielts_writing: The film centers on an unlikely bromance between two coworkers.
C1.mistake: Wortverbindung aus "brother" und "romance"; ausschließlich Alltagssprache.

C1.def: a brownish metal alloy of copper and tin, or its color
C1.example: The statue was cast in bronze.
C1.ielts_writing: Ancient civilizations used bronze for tools and weapons.
C1.mistake: "bronze medal" ist Bronzemedaille; "bronzed" bedeutet "gebräunt".

C1.def: the period when people used bronze tools, before iron
C1.example: Archaeologists found a Bronze Age settlement near the river.
C1.ielts_writing: Bronze Age societies developed trade networks across long distances.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We visited a Bronze Age burial site."
C1.mistake: Meist groß geschrieben: "the Bronze Age"; steht vor dem "Iron Age".

C1.def: a male sibling, or a member of a religious order
C1.example: My brother lives in Chicago.
C1.ielts_writing: The brothers took a vow of silence.
C1.mistake: Plural "brothers" oder, in religiösen Kreisen, "brethren"; "bro" ist die Kurzform.

C1.def: a feeling of fellowship, or an association of people with a common interest
C1.example: The brotherhood of workers fought for better conditions.
C1.ielts_writing: Many ideologies promote universal brotherhood as an ideal.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They share a strong sense of brotherhood."
C1.mistake: Kann auch eine Organisation meinen; geschlechtsneutral oft "solidarity" oder "fellowship".

C1.def: to look through a book, shop, or website casually
C1.example: We spent an hour browsing in the bookstore.
C1.ielts_writing: Shoppers often browse online before buying in stores.
C1.mistake: "I'm just browsing" ist die Standardantwort im Laden; kein Gebrauch mit "search".

C1.def: a program used to access web pages
C1.example: Please clear your browser's cache.
C1.ielts_writing: Different browsers may display the same web page differently.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I use a different browser for work."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit dem Menschen "browser" (Stöberer) verwechseln; im Alltag fast nur Computerbedeutung.

C1.def: a meal eaten in late morning that combines breakfast and lunch
C1.example: We met for brunch on Sunday.
C1.ielts_writing: Brunch has become a social ritual in many urban neighborhoods.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Let's have brunch at that new café."
C1.mistake: Wortmischung aus "breakfast" und "lunch"; "have brunch" ohne Artikel.

C1.def: extremely cruel or harsh, or very direct
C1.example: The film contains brutal scenes of violence.
C1.ielts_writing: The brutal reality is that many small businesses fail within five years.
C1.mistake: "brutal honesty" bedeutet "schonungslose Ehrlichkeit"; Nomen "brutality".

C1.def: (informal) a dollar, or a male deer
C1.example: That coffee cost me five bucks.
C1.ielts_writing: Consumers are looking for more bang for their buck.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He earns good bucks as a consultant."
C1.mistake: "pass the buck" bedeutet "die Verantwortung abschieben"; "buck" im Plural: "bucks".

C1.def: a metal fastener on a belt or strap, or to bend under pressure
C1.example: He fastened the buckle on his belt.
C1.ielts_writing: The bridge began to buckle under the weight of the traffic.
C1.mistake: "buckle up" bedeutet "sich anschnallen"; "buckle under pressure" heißt "dem Druck nachgeben".

C1.def: a follower of Buddhism
C1.example: She became a Buddhist in her twenties.
C1.ielts_writing: Buddhist monks play a central role in many Southeast Asian communities.
C1.mistake: Immer groß geschrieben; die Religion heißt "Buddhism".

C1.def: (informal) a close friend or companion
C1.example: He went hiking with his buddy.
C1.ielts_writing: A buddy system can help new employees feel welcome.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Hey buddy, can you give me a hand?"
C1.mistake: Wird auch als freundliche Anrede an Fremde benutzt; kann aber herablassend klingen.

C1.def: (informal) having a strong, muscular body
C1.example: He got really buff after a year of training.
C1.ielts_writing: The ad campaign featured a buff athlete promoting protein shakes.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen: "film buff" bedeutet "Filmkenner"; als Verb "buff" bedeutet "polieren".

C1.def: a large wild ox, or in North America, a bison
C1.example: Herds of buffalo once roamed the Great Plains.
C1.ielts_writing: Conservation programs helped restore the buffalo population.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw a herd of buffalo at the national park."
C1.mistake: Plural: "buffalo" oder "buffaloes"; in Nordamerika oft für "bison".

C1.def: something that reduces the impact of shocks, or temporary storage of data
C1.example: Savings act as a buffer against unexpected expenses.
C1.ielts_writing: A buffer state separates two rival powers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The video kept buffering because of my slow connection."
C1.mistake: Nomen: "a buffer AGAINST sth"; als Verb in der Technik: "the video is buffering".

C1.def: a meal where guests serve themselves from dishes laid out on a table
C1.example: The hotel offers a generous breakfast buffet.
C1.ielts_writing: All-you-can-eat buffets have lost popularity during recent health trends.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We went to a buffet for dinner."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; das Wort "buffet" wird hier /bəˈfeɪ/ und nicht /ˈbʌfɪt/ gesprochen.

C1.def: an error in software, a small insect, or to annoy someone
C1.example: The update fixed a bug in the app.
C1.ielts_writing: Developers use testing to detect bugs early in the process.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It bugs me when people are late."
C1.mistake: Als Verb "bug sb" bedeutet "nerven, belästigen"; "bug" ist auch ein Abhörgerät.

C1.def: a glass globe that produces light, or the rounded base of some plants
C1.example: I need to replace the light bulb in the kitchen.
C1.ielts_writing: Tulip bulbs are planted in the autumn for spring flowers.
C1.mistake: "light bulb" ist Glühbirne; "bulb" allein wird auch für Blumenzwiebeln benutzt.

C1.def: the main part of something, or large size
C1.example: The bulk of the work was completed last year.
C1.ielts_writing: Buying in bulk can reduce per-unit costs significantly.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I buy rice in bulk to save money."
C1.mistake: Wendung: "the bulk OF + Nomen"; "buy in bulk" bedeutet "in großen Mengen kaufen".

C1.def: a short official announcement or news report
C1.example: The school posted a bulletin about the schedule change.
C1.ielts_writing: A news bulletin interrupted the regular broadcast.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I read the bulletin on the notice board."
C1.mistake: "bulletin board" ist die Pinnwand (auch digital: Forum).

C1.def: designed to stop bullets from penetrating
C1.example: The president rides in a bulletproof car.
C1.ielts_writing: Bulletproof vests are standard equipment for police officers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He wore a bulletproof vest during the operation."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; "bulletproof" bedeutet auch "unfehlbar" im übertragenen Sinn.

C1.def: a traditional spectacle in which a matador fights a bull
C1.example: They watched a bullfight in Madrid.
C1.ielts_writing: Bullfighting remains controversial because of animal welfare concerns.
C1.mistake: Zusammengeschrieben; der Kämpfer heißt "bullfighter" oder "matador".

C1.def: a small soft bread roll, or a hairstyle gathered at the back of the head
C1.example: She ate a cinnamon bun with her coffee.
C1.ielts_writing: The bakery sells fresh buns every morning.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She wore her hair in a bun."
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Brötchen und Haarknoten; "bun in the oven" heißt umgangssprachlich "schwanger".

C1.def: a single-story house
C1.example: They live in a small bungalow near the coast.
C1.ielts_writing: Retirees often prefer bungalows because they avoid stairs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We rented a bungalow for the summer."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Plural "bungalows".

C1.def: a sport in which a person jumps from a height while attached to an elastic cord
C1.example: He went bungee jumping in New Zealand.
C1.ielts_writing: Bungee jumping carries risks, so participants must follow strict safety rules.
C1.mistake: "go bungee jumping" ohne Artikel; "bungee cord" ist das elastische Seil.

C1.def: something that is difficult to bear, such as a responsibility
C1.example: The cost of care became a heavy burden on the family.
C1.ielts_writing: Public debt places a burden on future generations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I don't want to be a burden to anyone."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "a burden ON/TO sb"; juristisch: "burden of proof" (Beweislast).

C1.def: a system of government with many rules and officials, often slow and complicated
C1.example: Dealing with bureaucracy can be frustrating.
C1.ielts_writing: Excessive bureaucracy discourages entrepreneurs from starting new businesses.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I spent weeks stuck in bureaucracy to get my visa."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-ROC-); Nomen unzählbar, meist negativ.

C1.def: to begin to grow or increase rapidly
C1.example: A burgeoning tech sector has transformed the city.
C1.ielts_writing: Concerns about data privacy have burgeoned in recent years.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Her burgeoning career took off after the award."
C1.mistake: Meist als Adjektiv "burgeoning" benutzt; nicht mit "bourgeois" verwechseln.

C1.def: a deep reddish-purple color
C1.example: She wore a burgundy dress to the gala.
C1.ielts_writing: Burgundy is a popular color for autumn collections.
C1.mistake: Als Farbe klein, als Region "Burgundy" (Burgund) und Wein "Burgundy" groß.

C1.def: the act of putting a dead body into the ground
C1.example: The burial took place in a quiet cemetery.
C1.ielts_writing: Ancient burial sites reveal much about funeral customs.
C1.mistake: Schreibweise "burial" von "bury"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a Mexican dish of a tortilla filled with meat, beans, or cheese
C1.example: I ordered a chicken burrito for lunch.
C1.ielts_writing: Fast-food chains have popularized burritos across the United States.
C1.mistake: Aussprache mit "rr" wie "r" und "i" als /iː/: "buh-REE-toh".

C1.def: to break open suddenly, or to move or appear suddenly
C1.example: The pipe burst during the cold snap.
C1.ielts_writing: Tensions burst into open conflict after the election.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She burst into tears when she heard the news."
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: burst, burst, burst; "burst into tears" (in Tränen ausbrechen).

C1.def: (informal) a person who often drops things
C1.example: Don't hand him the glasses; he's a butterfingers.
C1.ielts_writing: The term "butterfingers" is used humorously for people who drop things.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm such a butterfingers; I dropped my phone again."
C1.mistake: Wird als Singular und Plural benutzt; humorvoll, aber nicht böse gemeint.

C1.def: to make a low humming sound, or a feeling of excitement
C1.example: Bees buzzed around the flowers.
C1.ielts_writing: A buzz of excitement ran through the crowd.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My phone buzzed with a new message."
C1.mistake: Auch "buzzword" (Schlagwort); "buzz off" bedeutet "verschwinde".

C1.def: strictly following the rules
C1.example: The inspector did everything by the book.
C1.ielts_writing: Auditors must conduct investigations by the book to ensure fairness.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I always play it by the book at work."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung ohne Plural: "by the book", nicht "by the books".

C1.def: a unit of digital information, usually eight bits
C1.example: A kilobyte consists of 1,024 bytes.
C1.ielts_writing: A byte is the basic unit for measuring computer storage.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "bite" (beißen) verwechseln; gleiche Aussprache.

C1.def: a car with a driver that carries passengers for payment
C1.example: We took a cab to the airport.
C1.ielts_writing: Cab fares in the city have increased steadily.
C1.mistake: Kurzform von "taxicab"; "hail a cab" bedeutet "ein Taxi herbeiwinken".

C1.def: a group of senior government ministers, or a piece of furniture with shelves or drawers
C1.example: The president appointed a new cabinet.
C1.ielts_writing: Cabinet members meet regularly to discuss policy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I keep the medicine in the bathroom cabinet."
C1.mistake: Als Regierungsgremium unzählbar im Singular: "the cabinet is meeting" (Gruppe).

C1.def: to find a number or amount using mathematics
C1.example: The software calculates the total automatically.
C1.ielts_writing: Economists calculate growth rates using statistical models.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I calculated how much I would save each month."
C1.mistake: Nomen "calculation", Gerät "calculator"; "calculated risk" bedeutet "bewusstes Risiko".

C1.def: the process of working out a number, or careful judgment of what is advantageous
C1.example: The calculation showed a small profit.
C1.ielts_writing: Careful calculation is required when designing a bridge.
C1.ielts_speaking: "By my calculation, we'll arrive at noon."
C1.mistake: Das Nomen ist zählbar: "a calculation"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-LAY-).

C1.def: a radio or TV show in which listeners phone in to comment
C1.example: The radio call-in discusses politics every Friday.
C1.ielts_writing: Call-in programs give ordinary citizens a platform to voice their opinions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I called in to the radio show to complain."
C1.mistake: Nomen mit Bindestrich, Verb ohne: "call in".

C1.def: the art of beautiful handwriting
C1.example: She practices calligraphy as a hobby.
C1.ielts_writing: Calligraphy is highly valued in East Asian art traditions.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-LIG-); "calligraphy" bezeichnet die Kunst, nicht die Schrift selbst.

C1.def: the way a film or video is shot by the camera operator
C1.example: The film is praised for its outstanding camerawork.
C1.ielts_writing: Skilled camerawork can heighten the emotional impact of a scene.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The camerawork was shaky in the documentary."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; unzählbar: "good camerawork".

C1.def: to hide something by making it blend in with its surroundings
C1.example: The soldiers camouflaged their tent with branches.
C1.ielts_writing: Some animals camouflage themselves to avoid predators.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She camouflaged the stain with a scarf."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit "ou" und "age" am Ende; das "g" wird /ʒ/ gesprochen.

C1.def: a person who stays in a tent, or a recreational vehicle
C1.example: The campers set up their tents by the lake.
C1.ielts_writing: Campers are asked to dispose of waste properly in protected areas.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We rented a camper for the road trip."
C1.mistake: "happy camper" bedeutet "zufriedene Person" (meist verneint: "not a happy camper").

C1.def: the act of canceling something that was planned
C1.example: The airline announced the cancellation of the flight.
C1.ielts_writing: A late cancellation can result in a penalty fee.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I received an email about the cancellation."
C1.mistake: Das Nomen "cancellation" schreibt man mit doppeltem "l", das Verb "cancel" mit einfachem "l" in "canceled".

C1.def: honest and straightforward
C1.example: He was candid about his mistakes.
C1.ielts_writing: In a candid interview, the CEO admitted the company had been wrong.
C1.ielts_speaking: "To be candid, I didn't like the movie."
C1.mistake: Nomen "candor"; "to be candid" leitet ehrliche Meinung ein, nicht "kandid" (Kandidat).

C1.def: a walking stick, or the tall stem of some plants like sugar
C1.example: The old man walked slowly with a cane.
C1.ielts_writing: Sugar cane is cultivated in tropical climates.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandmother uses a cane to walk."
C1.mistake: Wird auch als Verb "to cane" (mit einem Stock schlagen) benutzt; Aussprache /keɪn/.

C1.def: a large heavy gun that fires heavy metal balls
C1.example: The cannon fired a salute at noon.
C1.ielts_writing: Cannons transformed siege warfare in the fifteenth century.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw an old cannon at the fort."
