C1.mistake: "cannon" bezeichnet die Kanone, "canon" (mit einem "n") den Kanon (Regelwerk).

C1.def: a light narrow boat propelled by paddles
C1.example: We paddled a canoe down the river.
C1.ielts_writing: Indigenous communities built canoes long before modern boats existed.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; "canoe" ist das Boot, "kayak" eine andere Bootsart.

C1.def: a strong cloth used for tents and sails, or the surface for oil paintings
C1.example: The artist painted on a large canvas.
C1.ielts_writing: Canvas shoes are popular for their comfort and durability.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I bought a canvas bag for shopping."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "canvass" (Stimmen werben) verwechseln, das ein Verb mit doppeltem "s" ist.

C1.def: the ability to do something
C1.example: The system has the capability to process large amounts of data.
C1.ielts_writing: Military capability depends on both technology and trained personnel.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I doubt his capability to handle this project."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "capability TO do sth" oder "OF doing sth"; Plural häufig: "capabilities".

C1.def: a point of land extending into the sea, or a sleeveless cloak
C1.example: The ship rounded the cape at dawn.
C1.ielts_writing: The superhero wore a red cape.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Landzunge und Umhang; als Eigenname groß: "Cape Town".

C1.def: the legal killing of someone convicted of a serious crime
C1.example: Some states have abolished capital punishment.
C1.ielts_writing: Opponents of capital punishment argue that it cannot be corrected if errors occur.
C1.mistake: "capital" bedeutet hier "mit dem Tod bestraft"; synonym "the death penalty".

C1.def: an economic system based on private ownership and profit
C1.example: Capitalism encourages competition among businesses.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics argue that capitalism increases inequality, while supporters stress its role in economic growth.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They studied the history of capitalism in class."
C1.mistake: Nomen unzählbar, kein Plural im Alltag; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: relating to capitalism, or a person who invests money in business
C1.example: The country adopted a capitalist economy in the 1990s.
C1.ielts_writing: Capitalist societies tend to reward innovation and risk-taking.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He is a successful capitalist who owns several companies."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen: "a capitalist"; "venture capitalist" ist ein Wagniskapitalgeber.

C1.def: a method of determining the age of an object by measuring its carbon content
C1.example: Carbon dating showed the bones were nearly ten thousand years old.
C1.ielts_writing: Carbon dating has revolutionized archaeology by providing precise age estimates.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The museum used carbon dating to authenticate the manuscript."
C1.mistake: Das "dating" hier bedeutet Datierung, nicht Verabredung; nur zusammen "carbon dating".

C1.def: a poisonous gas produced when carbon-based fuels burn without enough oxygen
C1.example: A carbon monoxide detector saved the family from poisoning.
C1.ielts_writing: Carbon monoxide is a silent threat because it is invisible and odorless.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Always install a carbon monoxide alarm at home."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe von "monoxide"; nicht mit "carbon dioxide" (Kohlendioxid) verwechseln.

C1.def: thin paper coated with carbon on one side, used to make copies
C1.example: She slipped a sheet of carbon paper between the forms.
C1.ielts_writing: Carbon paper was once essential in offices before photocopiers became common.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I found some old carbon paper in the drawer."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "a sheet of carbon paper"; "carbon copy" ist die Durchschrift oder bildlich "Ebenbild".

C1.def: having no net release of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
C1.example: The company pledged to become carbon-neutral by 2030.
C1.ielts_writing: Carbon-neutral policies often rely on offsetting emissions through reforestation.
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich als Adjektiv vor dem Nomen; Nomen: "carbon neutrality".

C1.def: a cabinet of index cards listing the books in a library
C1.example: Students once searched the card catalog to find books.
C1.ielts_writing: The card catalog was replaced by digital databases in most libraries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My grandfather remembers using the card catalog."
C1.mistake: Veraltet geworden; heute meist "online catalog" oder "database".

C1.def: a person who looks after someone who is ill, elderly, or disabled
C1.example: The caregiver helped her mother get dressed every morning.
C1.ielts_writing: Family caregivers often lack financial and emotional support.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm the primary caregiver for my father."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise zusammen "caregiver"; unterscheidet sich von professionellem "nurse".

C1.def: goods carried on a ship, aircraft, or truck
C1.example: The cargo was unloaded at the port.
C1.ielts_writing: Cargo ships carry the majority of the world's traded goods.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The plane was carrying cargo, not passengers."
C1.mistake: Plural "cargoes" oder "cargos"; meist unzählbar im Sinn von Ladung.

C1.def: a horse-drawn passenger vehicle, or a railway car
C1.example: The royal couple arrived in an elegant carriage.
C1.ielts_writing: Horse-drawn carriages are a popular tourist attraction in some cities.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We rode in a carriage through the park."
C1.mistake: "baby carriage" ist der Kinderwagen; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a person or company that transports goods, or someone who carries a disease
C1.example: The mobile carrier offers a new data plan.
C1.ielts_writing: Asymptomatic carriers can spread the virus without knowing it.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The airline is a major carrier on this route."
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Fluggesellschaft, Handyanbieter oder Krankheitsüberträger.

C1.def: to cut something into a shape, or to cut cooked meat into slices
C1.example: He carved a small bird out of wood.
C1.ielts_writing: Early civilizations carved symbols into stone to record events.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My father carves the turkey every Thanksgiving."
C1.mistake: "carve out a niche" bedeutet "sich eine Nische erarbeiten"; Konstruktion: "carve sth OUT OF sth".

C1.def: money returned to a customer after a purchase
C1.example: The credit card offers two percent cash-back on groceries.
C1.ielts_writing: Cash-back offers encourage consumers to use particular payment methods.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I earned cash-back on my last purchase."
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich als Nomen; nicht mit "money back guarantee" gleichzusetzen.

C1.def: a public room or building for gambling
C1.example: They lost a lot of money at the casino.
C1.ielts_writing: Casinos often provide free drinks to encourage players to stay longer.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We spent a weekend at a casino in Las Vegas."
C1.mistake: Plural "casinos"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-SEE-).

C1.def: the choice of actors for a film or play, or the act of shaping molten metal
C1.example: The casting for the lead role took months.
C1.ielts_writing: Diverse casting can broaden audiences' perspectives.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm going to a casting call tomorrow."
C1.mistake: "casting call" ist ein offenes Vorsprechen für Rollen; "casting" auch Gießen von Metall.

C1.def: a person killed or injured in an accident or war
C1.example: The explosion caused many casualties.
C1.ielts_writing: Civilian casualties increased as the conflict intensified.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The company was a casualty of the recession."
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "casualties" meint Tote und Verletzte, nicht nur Tote.

C1.def: a complete list of items, such as for sale or in a library
C1.example: The store sent me its spring catalog.
C1.ielts_writing: Libraries catalog every book so patrons can find it easily.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I flipped through the catalog for ideas."
C1.mistake: Nomen und Verb sind gleich: "to catalog sth" heißt "etwas erfassen, katalogisieren".

C1.def: a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction, or a person or event that causes change
C1.example: The accident was a catalyst for new safety laws.
C1.ielts_writing: Technology can act as a catalyst for social change.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She was the catalyst that brought the team together."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "a catalyst FOR sth"; nicht mit "catalytic converter" (Autokatalysator) verwechseln.

C1.def: a sudden event that causes great damage or suffering
C1.example: The flood was a catastrophe for the region.
C1.ielts_writing: Climate scientists warn that inaction could lead to ecological catastrophe.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Forgetting the tickets would be a catastrophe."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-TAS-); "catastrophe" endet auf "-phe" und wird wie "-fee" gesprochen.

C1.def: to board a plane or get to the airport in time to depart
C1.example: I have to catch a flight at six in the morning.
C1.ielts_writing: Passengers who catch a flight at peak times often face delays.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We nearly missed it, but we managed to catch our flight."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "catch a flight TO + Ort"; Gegensatz: "miss a flight".

C1.def: to provide food and drinks, or to supply what is needed for a specific group
C1.example: The company caters weddings and corporate events.
C1.ielts_writing: Schools must cater to students with different learning needs.
C1.mistake: "cater TO sb's needs" (sich auf Bedürfnisse einstellen); auch "cater an event" (Veranstaltung beliefern).

C1.def: relating to the Roman Catholic Church, or universal in scope
C1.example: She was raised in a Catholic family.
C1.ielts_writing: The library has a catholic collection of books from many countries.
C1.mistake: Großgeschrieben meint die Kirche, kleingeschrieben "umfassend"; Nomen "Catholicism".

C1.def: cows and bulls kept for milk or meat
C1.example: The farmer raises cattle on a large ranch.
C1.ielts_writing: Overgrazing by cattle can degrade soil quality.
C1.mistake: Immer Plural, kein Artikel mit "a cattle"; Verb im Plural: "the cattle are".

C1.def: a vegetable with a large white head of florets
C1.example: She roasted the cauliflower with olive oil.
C1.ielts_writing: Cauliflower rice has become a popular low-carbohydrate alternative.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈkɔːlɪflaʊər/; unzählbar im Gebrauch ("some cauliflower").

C1.def: relating to or acting as a cause
C1.example: The study found a causal link between smoking and lung cancer.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers must distinguish between correlation and a causal relationship.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's no causal connection between the two events."
C1.mistake: Wird oft mit "correlation" kontrastiert: Korrelation heißt nicht Ursache.

C1.def: acting as a cause, or (in grammar) expressing cause
C1.example: Scientists identified the causative agent of the disease.
C1.ielts_writing: A causative verb such as "make" or "have" indicates that someone causes an action.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The causative factor was a faulty valve."
C1.mistake: In der Grammatik: "causative verb" (z. B. "have sth done").

C1.def: care taken to avoid risk, or to warn someone
C1.example: Proceed with caution on the icy road.
C1.ielts_writing: Doctors caution patients against taking antibiotics unnecessarily.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "caution sb AGAINST doing sth"; "cautionary tale" ist eine warnende Geschichte.

C1.def: careful to avoid problems or danger
C1.example: She is cautious about investing in new companies.
C1.ielts_writing: Cautious optimism characterized the economists' forecast.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "cautious ABOUT/OF sth"; nicht mit "caution" als Nomen verwechseln.

C1.def: salted eggs of sturgeon, eaten as a delicacy
C1.example: They served caviar and champagne at the reception.
C1.ielts_writing: Caviar remains a symbol of luxury and wealth.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "caviar" ist Störrogen, nicht jeder Fischrogen.

C1.def: common era, used in dates as a neutral alternative to AD
C1.example: The temple was built in the second century CE.
C1.ielts_writing: Historians use CE and BCE to date events without religious reference.
C1.mistake: Steht hinter der Jahreszahl wie "BCE"; keine Punkte (nicht "C.E.").

C1.def: to stop or come to an end
C1.example: The factory ceased production last year.
C1.ielts_writing: Hostilities ceased after the ceasefire agreement.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "cease doing" oder "cease to do"; "cease and desist" ist eine juristische Unterlassungsaufforderung.

C1.def: a natural object in space, such as a star or planet
C1.example: The moon is the closest celestial body to Earth.
C1.ielts_writing: Astronomers catalog thousands of celestial bodies each year.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I can see a bright celestial body in the sky."
C1.mistake: Plural "celestial bodies"; "celestial" bedeutet "himmlisch" und "astronomisch".

C1.def: relating to biological cells, or to mobile phones
C1.example: Cellular growth is controlled by genetic signals.
C1.ielts_writing: Cellular networks cover most areas of the country.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My cellular service is poor in the mountains."
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: biologische Zelle und Mobilfunk ("cellular network").

C1.def: a gray powder that hardens when mixed with water, used in construction
C1.example: Workers mixed cement for the foundation.
C1.ielts_writing: Cement production is a significant source of carbon dioxide emissions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The cement is still wet; don't walk on it."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "concrete" (fertiger Beton) verwechseln; Verb "cement a relationship" (festigen).

C1.def: a place where dead people are buried
C1.example: She visited her grandfather's grave in the cemetery.
C1.ielts_writing: Many historic cemeteries have become protected cultural sites.
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit "e" in der Mitte: "cemetery", nicht "cemetary".

C1.def: to remove or suppress parts of a text, film, or speech considered unacceptable
C1.example: The government censored the news report.
C1.ielts_writing: Authoritarian regimes often censor the media to control public opinion.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The film was censored in several countries."
C1.mistake: Nomen "censorship"; "censor" ist auch Nomen für den Zensor; nicht mit "censure" (Tadel) verwechseln.

C1.def: a hard material made by baking clay, or an object made of this
C1.example: She bought a handmade ceramic bowl.
C1.ielts_writing: Ceramics have been used in cooking and storage since ancient times.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen oft Plural: "ceramics" bezeichnet Keramikwaren oder die Kunst.

C1.def: the top executive responsible for a company's financial planning
C1.example: The CFO presented the budget to the board.
C1.ielts_writing: A CFO oversees financial reporting and risk management.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "chief financial officer"; als einzelne Buchstaben gesprochen.

C1.def: to make or become sore by rubbing, or to feel irritated
C1.example: His collar chafed his neck.
C1.ielts_writing: Employees began to chafe against the strict regulations.
C1.mistake: "chafe at sth" bedeutet "sich über etwas ärgern".

C1.def: one of a group of shops owned by the same company
C1.example: The chain store replaced several small businesses.
C1.ielts_writing: Chain stores benefit from economies of scale but may reduce local diversity.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I prefer local shops to chain stores."
C1.mistake: Plural "chain stores"; im Gegensatz zu "mom-and-pop store" (kleiner Familienbetrieb).

C1.def: a seat for one person, or a person in charge of a meeting
C1.example: She pulled up a chair and sat down.
C1.ielts_writing: The chair of the committee called the meeting to order.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "chair a meeting" (leiten); auch Lehrstuhl: "chair of history".

C1.def: a wooden house in the mountains, typically in the Alps
C1.example: We rented a chalet in the Alps for the winter.
C1.ielts_writing: Chalets are popular holiday homes in ski resorts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The chalet had a fireplace and a wonderful view."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (/ʃæˈleɪ/); das "ch" klingt wie "sch".

C1.def: testing one's abilities, in a stimulating way
C1.example: It was a challenging project, but we enjoyed it.
C1.ielts_writing: Challenging economic conditions have pushed many firms to restructure.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My job is stressful but challenging in a good way."
C1.mistake: Positiver als "difficult" (impliziert Anreiz); nicht mit "challenged" (Euphemismus) verwechseln.

C1.def: a room used for a particular purpose, or a body in a legislature
C1.example: The senators gathered in the chamber.
C1.ielts_writing: The upper chamber of parliament reviews legislation passed by the lower house.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She works at the chamber of commerce."
C1.mistake: "chamber of commerce" ist die Handelskammer; "chamber music" ist Kammermusik.

C1.def: the quality of being able to change or be changed
C1.example: The changeability of the weather ruined our plans.
C1.ielts_writing: The changeability of public opinion makes forecasting election results difficult.
C1.mistake: Selten und formell; üblicher ist "variability" oder das Adjektiv "changeable".

C1.def: a state of complete disorder
C1.example: The sudden power cut caused chaos in the city.
C1.ielts_writing: Political chaos often leads to economic instability.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The kitchen was total chaos after the party."
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈkeɪɑːs/, nicht wie "ch" in "church"; Adjektiv "chaotic".

C1.def: a main division of a book, or a period in someone's life
C1.example: I finished the first chapter last night.
C1.ielts_writing: The collapse of the factory closed a chapter in the town's history.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A new chapter of my life is starting."
C1.mistake: Wendung: "chapter and verse" bedeutet "genaue Einzelheiten".

C1.def: the way a writer creates and presents a character
C1.example: The novel is praised for its subtle characterization.
C1.ielts_writing: Characterization in the play relies heavily on dialogue.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I liked the characterization of the villain."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "character" (Figur) verwechseln; es ist die Art der Darstellung.

C1.def: to describe the quality of someone or something, or to be typical of
C1.example: Critics characterized the policy as ineffective.
C1.ielts_writing: Rapid urbanization characterizes many developing economies.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "characterize sth AS sth" oder "be characterized BY sth".

C1.def: a formal accusation, a price asked, or to fill with electricity
C1.example: He was arrested on a charge of theft.
C1.ielts_writing: Banks may charge fees for withdrawing cash abroad.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Please charge my phone; the battery is low."
C1.mistake: "in charge OF" bedeutet "verantwortlich für"; "charge sb with sth" bedeutet "jemanden anklagen".

C1.def: a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used in ancient warfare and races
C1.example: The Roman chariot raced around the arena.
C1.ielts_writing: Chariots were a decisive weapon in many ancient battles.
C1.ielts_speaking: "In the movie, a chariot race was the main scene."
C1.mistake: Der Fahrer heißt "charioteer"; nicht mit "carriage" verwechseln.

C1.def: relating to charity, or generous in judging others
C1.example: She donated to several charitable organizations.
C1.ielts_writing: Charitable giving rises during economic downturns in some countries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "That's not a very charitable thing to say."
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "uncharitable" (unfreundlich); "charitable" kann auch "wohlwollend" bedeuten.

C1.def: the power of delighting people, or a small ornament
C1.example: The old village has a lot of charm.
C1.ielts_writing: The charm of the proposal lies in its simplicity.
C1.mistake: Wendung: "third time's the charm" (beim dritten Mal klappt es); "lucky charm" = Glücksbringer.

C1.def: pleasant and attractive
C1.example: He is a charming host.
C1.ielts_writing: The charming old town draws many visitors each summer.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; "charming" ist positiver als "nice".

C1.def: a written document defining rights or an organization's principles, or to hire a vehicle
C1.example: The UN Charter was signed in 1945.
C1.ielts_writing: A charter sets out the rights and duties of members of an organization.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We chartered a boat for the day."
C1.mistake: Als Verb "to charter" (mieten); nicht mit "chart" (Diagramm) verwechseln.

C1.def: a flight on a plane hired for a specific group or purpose
C1.example: They booked a charter flight to Greece.
C1.ielts_writing: Charter flights are often cheaper than regularly scheduled flights.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We took a charter flight to the island."
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "scheduled flight" (Linienflug); Konstruktion: "charter flight TO + Ort".

C1.def: a person employed to drive a private car, or to drive someone around
C1.example: The chauffeur opened the car door for the guest.
C1.ielts_writing: Many executives rely on a chauffeur to save time during travel.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm not your chauffeur; take the bus."
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈʃoʊfər/ mit "sch"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to examine something or someone to make sure they are all right
C1.example: Please check on the baby while I'm out.
C1.ielts_writing: The manager checks on the progress of each project every week.
C1.mistake: "check on" heißt nachsehen; nicht mit "check in" (einchecken) oder "check out" verwechseln.

C1.def: having a pattern of squares, or examined
C1.example: He wore a checked shirt.
C1.ielts_writing: The checked tablecloth gave the café a homey feel.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I put my checked bag on the belt."
C1.mistake: "checked baggage" ist aufgegebenes Gepäck; im Amerikanischen auch "checked" für kariert.

C1.def: having a pattern of squares, or having a varied history
C1.example: The film follows his checkered career.
C1.ielts_writing: A checkered flag signals the end of a race.
C1.mistake: "checkered past" bedeutet "bewegte, auch zwielichtige Vergangenheit".

C1.def: the bone below the eye
C1.example: She has high cheekbones.
C1.ielts_writing: A fall fractured his cheekbone.
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben ("cheekbone"); Plural "cheekbones".

C1.def: playful and slightly rude in a way that is amusing
C1.example: The cheeky boy stuck out his tongue.
C1.ielts_writing: Cheeky advertising can attract younger audiences when used with care.
C1.mistake: Meist liebevoll gemeint; weniger scharf als "rude".

C1.def: reddish-brown in color
C1.example: She has long chestnut hair.
C1.ielts_writing: The horse had a glossy chestnut coat.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love the chestnut color of the leather."
C1.mistake: "old chestnut" bedeutet "abgedroschener Witz"; Nomen: Kastanie.

C1.def: needing a lot of chewing
C1.example: The caramel was soft and chewy.
C1.ielts_writing: Chewy cookies are made with more brown sugar.
C1.mistake: Beschreibt eine angenehme zähe Konsistenz, nicht "taff".

C1.def: a cool feeling, or to relax
C1.example: A chill ran down my spine.
C1.ielts_writing: Leaders must learn to chill and avoid overreacting to criticism.
C1.mistake: "chill out" bedeutet "sich entspannen"; als Nomen: "a chill in the air".

C1.def: a fatty substance found in blood and body cells
C1.example: High cholesterol increases the risk of heart disease.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular exercise can help lower cholesterol levels.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-LES-); unzählbares Nomen.

C1.def: the title given to Jesus, regarded as the Messiah
C1.example: Christians believe that Christ rose from the dead.
C1.ielts_writing: The teachings of Christ shaped Western civilization.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The painting shows Christ on the cross."
C1.mistake: Immer groß; als Ausruf "Christ!" kann es als gotteslästerlich verstanden werden.

C1.def: a Christian ceremony in which a baby is baptized and named
C1.example: The christening took place at the village church.
C1.ielts_writing: Christenings often bring extended families together.
C1.mistake: Auch das Taufen eines Schiffes: "christen a ship"; Verb "christen".

C1.def: (of a disease) lasting a long time, or persistent
C1.example: She suffers from chronic back pain.
C1.ielts_writing: Chronic stress can weaken the immune system.
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "acute" (akut); "chronic" heißt nicht "ständig im Sinne von häufig" in jedem Kontext.

C1.def: in the order in which events happened
C1.example: The events are listed chronologically.
C1.ielts_writing: Archivists arrange documents chronologically to ease research.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "chronological order"; Adverb endet auf "-ically".

C1.def: a thick piece of something
C1.example: She cut the cheese into thick chunks.
C1.ielts_writing: A large chunk of the budget was spent on advertising.
C1.mistake: "a chunk of change" bedeutet "ein hübsches Sümmchen Geld".

C1.def: thick and heavy, or containing large pieces
C1.example: She wore a chunky wool sweater.
C1.ielts_writing: Chunky jewelry has returned as a fashion trend.
C1.mistake: Bei Menschen kann es als "stämmig" abwertend wirken; vorsichtig verwenden.

C1.def: shaped like a circle, or a letter sent to many people
C1.example: The room has a circular table.
C1.ielts_writing: The company sent a circular to all employees about the new policy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The argument was circular and went nowhere."
C1.mistake: "circular economy" (Kreislaufwirtschaft); "circular reasoning" bedeutet Zirkelschluss.

C1.def: to move around freely, or to spread among people
C1.example: Blood circulates through the body.
C1.ielts_writing: False information circulates rapidly on social media.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A rumor is circulating about the boss."
C1.mistake: Intransitiv und transitiv: "a rumor circulates", "circulate a memo".

C1.def: the movement of blood in the body, or the number of copies of a newspaper sold
C1.example: Poor circulation can cause cold hands and feet.
C1.ielts_writing: The newspaper's circulation has fallen significantly.
C1.mistake: Bedeutungen: Blutkreislauf, Zeitungsauflage und "in Umlauf"; kein Plural im Alltag.

C1.def: a reference to a source, or an official notice
C1.example: The essay needs a citation for each source.
C1.ielts_writing: Citation errors can reduce the credibility of academic papers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I received a citation for illegal parking."
C1.mistake: Verb "cite" (zitieren) mit "e"; nicht mit "quote" verwechseln: citation = Quellenangabe.

C1.def: news reporting by ordinary people rather than professional journalists
C1.example: Citizen journalism played a key role in documenting the protests.
C1.ielts_writing: Citizen journalism has expanded the range of voices in public debate.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Person: "citizen journalist"; nicht mit "Bürgerjournalist" als Plural verwechseln.

C1.def: the legal status of belonging to a country
C1.example: He applied for citizenship after ten years.
C1.ielts_writing: Dual citizenship allows people to hold two nationalities at once.
C1.mistake: Nomen: "citizenship" (Staatsangehörigkeit); "nationality" ist oft synonym.

C1.def: relating to citizens or their duties
C1.example: Voting is a civic duty.
C1.ielts_writing: Civic engagement strengthens democracy.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "civil" (Zivil-) verwechseln: "civic duty" vs. "civil rights".

C1.def: a person employed in government service
C1.example: He has worked as a civil servant for twenty years.
C1.ielts_writing: Civil servants are expected to remain politically neutral.
C1.mistake: Kein Äquivalent zu "Beamter" im strengen Sinn; "civil servant" umfasst auch Angestellte.

C1.def: a war between groups within the same country
C1.example: The country suffered a long civil war.
C1.ielts_writing: Civil wars often result in massive displacement of civilians.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She grew up during the civil war."
collocations: on the brink of civil war
C1.mistake: "the Civil War" (groß) bezeichnet in den USA meist den Krieg 1861 bis 1865.

C1.def: not belonging to the military, or a person not in the armed forces
C1.example: Many civilians were evacuated.
C1.ielts_writing: Protecting civilian lives is a fundamental principle of international law.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He left the army and returned to civilian life."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-VIL-); im Plural meint "civilians" Zivilbevölkerung.

C1.def: a group of related families, especially in Scotland
C1.example: The clan gathered for a reunion.
C1.ielts_writing: Clans traditionally controlled land and political power in the Highlands.
C1.mistake: Im Alltag auch scherzhaft für "große Familie"; Plural "clans".

C1.def: the quality of being clear and easy to understand
C1.example: Her speech had remarkable clarity.
C1.ielts_writing: Clarity of expression is essential in academic writing.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need clarity on what my role will be."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "clarity OF thought/expression" und "clarity ON sth".

C1.def: a violent confrontation, or a serious disagreement or conflict of ideas
C1.example: Police clashed with protesters outside the building.
C1.ielts_writing: A clash of cultures can lead to misunderstandings.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "clash WITH sb/sth" oder "clash OVER sth"; auch für Termine ("schedules clash").

C1.def: a lawsuit brought by one person on behalf of a group
C1.example: Thousands of customers joined the class action.
C1.ielts_writing: Class actions allow consumers to challenge powerful corporations together.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They filed a class action against the company."
C1.mistake: Als Teil von "class action lawsuit"; im deutschen Recht anders geregelt, daher keine genaue Entsprechung.

C1.def: the arrangement of things into groups according to type
C1.example: The classification of species is based on shared traits.
C1.ielts_writing: A clear classification of risks helps organizations plan responses.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Her job classification changed after the promotion."
C1.mistake: Verb "classify"; "classified information" bedeutet Verschlusssache.

C1.def: to clean thoroughly, especially the skin, or to remove something harmful
C1.example: She cleanses her face every night.
C1.ielts_writing: Rituals to cleanse the spirit exist in many cultures.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I tried a juice cleanse for three days."
C1.mistake: Aussprache /klenz/; "ethnic cleansing" bedeutet "ethnische Säuberung".

C1.def: to resolve a problem, tidy a place, or (of weather) become brighter
C1.example: The mystery was cleared up quickly.
C1.ielts_writing: Further information is needed to clear up the confusion.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I hope the weather clears up by noon."
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Missverständnis aufklären, aufräumen oder Wetter besser werden; "clear sth up".

C1.def: official permission, or the space between two objects
C1.example: The pilot received clearance to land.
C1.ielts_writing: Security clearance is required to access the documents.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The bus has only a few inches of clearance under the bridge."
C1.mistake: "clearance sale" ist der Räumungsverkauf; "clearance" ist auch Zoll-Abfertigung.

C1.def: an open space in a forest, or the process of settling payments
C1.example: We found a quiet clearing in the woods.
C1.ielts_writing: The clearing of checks can take several days.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Lichtung und Verrechnung ("clearing house").

C1.def: an overused phrase or idea that has lost its force
C1.example: The film is full of romantic cliches.
C1.ielts_writing: Writers are advised to avoid cliche and find fresh expressions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "That's such a cliche, but it's true."
collocations: used to the point of cliche
C1.mistake: Wird mit Akzent "cliché" geschrieben; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: online content designed to attract clicks with sensational headlines
C1.example: The article was nothing but clickbait.
C1.ielts_writing: Clickbait headlines undermine trust in digital news.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; kein Plural: "a lot of clickbait", nicht "clickbaits".

C1.def: the serious problems caused by climate change
C1.example: World leaders gathered to discuss the climate crisis.
C1.ielts_writing: The climate crisis threatens food security in many regions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Young people demand action on the climate crisis."
C1.mistake: Wird heute oft statt "climate change" verwendet; mit Artikel: "the climate crisis".

C1.def: relating to climate
C1.example: Climatic conditions vary widely across the region.
C1.ielts_writing: Climatic changes have forced farmers to adapt their methods.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The climatic zone affects what we can grow."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "climactic" (zum Höhepunkt gehörend) verwechseln.

C1.def: the most intense or exciting point of a story or event
C1.example: The film reaches its climax in the final scene.
C1.ielts_writing: The climax of the negotiations came after midnight.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The climax of the story was surprising."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Adjektiv "climactic".

C1.def: to hold tightly, or to refuse to give up an idea
C1.example: The child clung to his mother's hand.
C1.ielts_writing: Some leaders cling to power long after losing public support.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The wet shirt clung to his body."
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: cling, clung, clung; Konstruktion: "cling TO sb/sth".

C1.def: relating to medical treatment of patients, or detached and unemotional
C1.example: Clinical studies test new medicines on patients.
C1.ielts_writing: The clinical tone of the report conveyed no sympathy.
C1.mistake: Bei Räumen: "clinical" heißt "steril, nüchtern", nicht nur medizinisch.

C1.def: a research study that tests new treatments on people
C1.example: The drug is now in clinical trials.
C1.ielts_writing: Clinical trials must follow strict ethical guidelines.
C1.mistake: Auch "clinical study"; Plural "clinical trials"; nicht "clinical test".

C1.def: a board with a clip at the top for holding papers
C1.example: The nurse wrote notes on a clipboard.
C1.ielts_writing: Inspectors carry a clipboard to record their observations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He walked around with a clipboard and checked each item."
C1.mistake: In der IT bedeutet "clipboard" auch die Zwischenablage.

C1.def: a piece cut from a newspaper, or a small piece trimmed off
C1.example: She kept a clipping of the article.
C1.ielts_writing: Press clippings helped the company track media coverage.
C1.mistake: Im Plural "clippings" auch Schnittgut: "hedge clippings".

C1.def: a loose outer garment without sleeves, or something that hides
C1.example: The wizard wore a long black cloak.
C1.ielts_writing: The operation was carried out under a cloak of secrecy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The mountain was hidden in a cloak of mist."
C1.mistake: "cloak-and-dagger" bedeutet "geheimnisvoll, Spionage"; "cloakroom" ist die Garderobe.

C1.def: an organism genetically identical to another, or a copy
C1.example: Scientists produced a clone of the sheep.
C1.ielts_writing: Cloning raises ethical questions about identity and ownership.
C1.ielts_speaking: "This app is just a clone of a popular game."
C1.mistake: Auch in der IT: "clone a repository" (kopieren); Nomen "clone" bleibt gleich.

C1.def: to shut, or near in space or time
C1.example: Please close the door when you leave.
C1.ielts_writing: Banks close at five on weekdays.
C1.mistake: Zwei Aussprachen: Verb /kloʊz/, Adjektiv /kloʊs/; "closure" /ˈkloʊʒər/.

C1.def: a photograph or film shot taken from very near the subject
C1.example: The director used a closeup to show her tears.
C1.ielts_writing: A closeup of the painting revealed tiny brushstrokes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I took a closeup of the flower."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben als Nomen; "close-up" mit Bindestrich ist ebenfalls üblich.

C1.def: the act of closing, or a sense of emotional resolution
C1.example: The closure of the factory left hundreds jobless.
C1.ielts_writing: Families of victims often seek closure after a tragedy.
C1.mistake: "closure" ist auch das emotionale Abschließen eines Themas: "get closure".

C1.def: a sudden heavy rainfall
C1.example: A cloudburst flooded the streets within minutes.
C1.ielts_writing: Cloudbursts are becoming more frequent in some mountain regions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We got caught in a cloudburst on the way home."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; Plural "cloudbursts".

C1.def: awkward in movement or handling things
C1.example: He is so clumsy that he spilled coffee again.
C1.ielts_writing: A clumsy translation can alter the meaning of a text.
C1.mistake: Auch für ungeschickte Formulierungen: "a clumsy phrase".

C1.def: a group of similar things close together
C1.example: A cluster of houses stood by the river.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers identified a cluster of cases linked to the same event.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The stars appear in a tight cluster."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "a cluster OF + Plural"; als Verb: "cluster around" (sich scharen).

C1.def: to write a book or paper together with someone
C1.example: She co-authored a paper on climate policy.
C1.ielts_writing: Co-authoring research can speed up publication and improve quality.
C1.mistake: Als Verb: "co-author sth WITH sb"; Nomen "co-author" mit Bindestrich.

C1.def: a person who shares parenting duties with another after separation
C1.example: They are good co-parents despite the divorce.
C1.ielts_writing: Successful co-parenting requires clear communication and respect.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My ex and I are co-parents of two kids."
C1.mistake: Verb "to co-parent"; nicht mit "Stiefelternteil" (stepparent) verwechseln.

C1.def: extremely black, like coal
C1.example: He had coal-black hair.
C1.ielts_writing: The cat's coal-black fur shone in the light.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The sky turned coal-black before the storm."
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich geschrieben; Vergleich: "black as coal".

C1.def: a temporary alliance of groups, especially political parties
C1.example: The two parties formed a coalition government.
C1.ielts_writing: Coalition governments often struggle to agree on controversial reforms.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A coalition of environmental groups opposed the plan."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "a coalition OF + Gruppen"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-LI-).

C1.def: near or relating to a coast
C1.example: Coastal towns attract many tourists in summer.
C1.ielts_writing: Rising sea levels threaten coastal communities worldwide.
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "inland"; Nomen "coast" (Küste).

C1.def: a mixed alcoholic drink, or a mixture of different things
C1.example: She ordered a fruity cocktail.
C1.ielts_writing: A cocktail of factors contributed to the economic crisis.
C1.mistake: Auch ohne Alkohol möglich ("fruit cocktail"); bildlich: "a toxic cocktail".

C1.def: to persuade someone to do something using force or threats
C1.example: He was coerced into signing the contract.
C1.ielts_writing: Coercing witnesses is a serious offense in many legal systems.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "coerce sb INTO doing sth"; Nomen "coercion".

C1.def: relating to mental processes such as thinking and learning
C1.example: Cognitive skills develop rapidly in early childhood.
C1.ielts_writing: Cognitive decline can be slowed through regular mental activity.
C1.mistake: Fachbegriff aus der Psychologie; "cognitive" nicht mit "conscious" gleichsetzen.

C1.def: to happen at the same time, or to be similar
C1.example: The holiday coincides with my birthday.
C1.ielts_writing: The results coincide with earlier research.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "coincide WITH sth"; Nomen "coincidence" (Zufall).

C1.def: without feeling or pity, or (of animals) having a body temperature that varies
C1.example: The cold-blooded killer showed no remorse.
C1.ielts_writing: Reptiles are cold-blooded and depend on external heat.
C1.mistake: Bei Tieren heißt es "wechselwarm" (fachlich "ectothermic").

C1.def: to work jointly with others on a project
C1.example: The two companies collaborated on a new product.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientists collaborate across borders to tackle global problems.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "collaborate WITH sb ON sth"; "collaborator" kann auch "Kollaborateur" (im Krieg) bedeuten.

C1.def: the act of working jointly with others
C1.example: The album is a collaboration between two famous artists.
C1.ielts_writing: International collaboration is crucial for scientific progress.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "in collaboration WITH sb"; "collaboration" ist auch Kollaboration im Krieg.

C1.def: a sudden failure or fall, or to fall down
C1.example: The collapse of the bridge shocked the town.
C1.ielts_writing: The collapse of the housing market triggered a financial crisis.
C1.mistake: Nomen und Verb gleich; "a collapsible chair" ist ein Klappstuhl.

C1.def: a person you work with
C1.example: I had lunch with a colleague.
C1.ielts_writing: Respect among colleagues improves the working atmosphere.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My colleague is on vacation this week."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise "colleague" mit "-ague"; nicht mit "college" (Hochschule) verwechseln.

C1.def: done by a group together
C1.example: The team made a collective decision.
C1.ielts_writing: Collective bargaining gives workers more influence over wages.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen: "a collective" (Kollektiv); "collective" betont das Gemeinsame.

C1.def: an instance of two vehicles hitting each other, or a conflict of interests
C1.example: Two cars were involved in the collision.
C1.ielts_writing: A collision of interests can undermine a joint venture.
C1.mistake: Verb "collide WITH sb/sth"; "on a collision course" bedeutet "auf Konfrontationskurs".

C1.def: part of the large intestine, or the punctuation mark (:)
C1.example: Doctors examined his colon for signs of disease.
C1.ielts_writing: A colon introduces a list or explanation in a sentence.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Regular screening can detect colon cancer early."
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Darmabschnitt und Satzzeichen; "semicolon" ist das Semikolon.

C1.def: a senior military officer
C1.example: The colonel gave the order to advance.
C1.ielts_writing: The colonel was awarded a medal for bravery.
C1.mistake: Aussprache wie "kernel" /ˈkɜːrnəl/, nicht "colonel" wie geschrieben.

C1.def: relating to a colony or colonialism
C1.example: The building dates back to the colonial era.
C1.ielts_writing: Colonial rule shaped the borders of many African states.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The city has a lot of colonial architecture."
C1.mistake: Nomen "colonialism" (Kolonialismus); "Colonial" bezeichnet im US-Kontext oft die Zeit vor 1776.

C1.def: a journalist who writes a regular opinion column
C1.example: The columnist criticized the new tax law.
C1.ielts_writing: A well-known columnist can influence public opinion.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She works as a columnist for a newspaper."
C1.mistake: Das "n" in "column" und "columnist" wird nicht gesprochen: /ˈkɑːləmnɪst/ mit leiser "n".

C1.def: fighting between armed forces, or to try to stop something harmful
C1.example: Soldiers trained for combat.
C1.ielts_writing: New policies aim to combat climate change.
C1.mistake: Betonung beim Nomen auf der ersten Silbe, beim Verb oft auf der zweiten.

C1.def: a return to success or popularity after a period of difficulty
C1.example: The singer made a stunning comeback.
C1.ielts_writing: The team's comeback in the second half surprised everyone.
C1.mistake: Auch "a witty comeback" (schlagfertige Antwort).

C1.def: a celestial object with a tail, made of ice and dust
C1.example: A bright comet appeared in the night sky.
C1.ielts_writing: Comets are believed to contain material from the early solar system.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We watched the comet through a telescope."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "meteor" (Sternschnuppe) verwechseln; Plural "comets".

C1.def: a short series of drawings telling a story, often humorous
C1.example: He reads the comic strip in the newspaper every morning.
C1.ielts_writing: Comic strips often use satire to comment on current events.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I drew a comic strip about my cat."
C1.mistake: "comic strip" ist ein Streifen; "comic book" ist ein Heft.

C1.def: an order, control over something, or to order someone to do something
C1.example: The captain took command of the ship.
C1.ielts_writing: She has an excellent command of English.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He commands great respect among his staff."
C1.mistake: "have a good command OF a language" bedeutet "eine Sprache gut beherrschen".

C1.def: to begin
C1.example: The ceremony will commence at noon.
C1.ielts_writing: The trial is scheduled to commence next week.
C1.mistake: Sehr formell; im Alltag "begin" oder "start"; Nomen "commencement" auch Abschlussfeier.

C1.def: spoken or written remarks about an event, text, or situation
C1.example: The radio commentary described every move of the match.
C1.ielts_writing: Political commentary often reflects the author's viewpoint.
C1.ielts_speaking: "His commentary on the film was insightful."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar bei Sendungen: "live commentary"; Präposition: "commentary ON sth".

C1.def: a person who reports on events, especially in sports or politics
C1.example: The commentator praised the player's skill.
C1.ielts_writing: Political commentators debated the outcome of the debate.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; nicht mit "commentary" verwechseln.

C1.def: the activity of buying and selling, especially on a large scale
C1.example: Commerce flourished along the river.
C1.ielts_writing: E-commerce has transformed the retail sector.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The Chamber of Commerce supports local businesses."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Adjektiv "commercial".

C1.def: a person with official authority, such as a government official
C1.example: The police commissioner announced new measures.
C1.ielts_writing: The EU commissioner responsible for trade met with delegations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She was appointed commissioner of the league."
C1.mistake: Verb "commission" (beauftragen); "commissioner" ist nicht zwingend ein "Kommissar" im Krimi.

C1.def: to carry out an illegal act, or to promise to do something
C1.example: He committed a serious crime.
C1.ielts_writing: The government committed itself to reducing emissions.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: "commit a crime" und "commit TO sth" (sich festlegen); Partizip "committed".

C1.def: a promise or dedication to a cause or person
C1.example: She shows great commitment to her job.
C1.ielts_writing: A strong commitment to quality builds customer loyalty.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I made a commitment to myself to exercise daily."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "commitment TO sth"; auch "family commitments" (Verpflichtungen).

C1.def: a raw material or product that can be bought and sold
C1.example: Oil is one of the world's most traded commodities.
C1.ielts_writing: Fluctuations in commodity prices affect developing economies.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "Time is a precious commodity."

C1.def: a political system in which property is owned by the community
C1.example: The fall of communism changed Eastern Europe.
C1.ielts_writing: Communism aimed to eliminate class distinctions.
C1.mistake: Nomen unzählbar; Adjektiv und Person: "communist".

C1.def: relating to communism, or a believer in communism
C1.example: The country was ruled by a communist party.
C1.ielts_writing: Communist regimes controlled much of the economy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He was a communist in his youth."
C1.mistake: Großgeschrieben als Parteiname: "the Communist Party".

C1.def: a person who spends time with another
C1.example: The dog is her constant companion.
C1.ielts_writing: Companionship is vital for the elderly.
C1.mistake: Nomen "companionship"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: similar enough to be compared
C1.example: Their results are comparable to ours.
C1.ielts_writing: Salaries are comparable across the two regions.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "comparable TO/WITH sth"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to compare prices from different stores before buying
C1.example: She comparison-shops online before buying anything.
C1.ielts_writing: Smart consumers comparison-shop to find the best deals.
C1.mistake: Verb mit Bindestrich: "comparison-shop"; Nomen "comparison shopping".

C1.def: sympathetic concern for someone's suffering
C1.example: She showed great compassion toward the refugees.
C1.ielts_writing: Compassion is central to many religious traditions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt compassion for the lost child."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "compassion FOR sb"; "compassion fatigue" ist Mitgefühlsermüdung.

C1.def: feeling or showing sympathy and concern for others
C1.example: The nurse was gentle and compassionate.
C1.ielts_writing: A compassionate leader listens to the concerns of employees.
C1.mistake: "compassionate leave" ist Sonderurlaub bei Todesfällen.

C1.def: able to exist or work together without problems
C1.example: The software is compatible with most computers.
C1.ielts_writing: These two approaches are not compatible with each other.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "compatible WITH sth"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to force someone to do something
C1.example: The law compels employers to provide safe conditions.
C1.ielts_writing: He felt compelled to speak out against injustice.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "compel sb TO do sth"; meist im Passiv "be compelled to".

C1.def: evoking interest or attention in a powerful way, or convincing
C1.example: She gave a compelling argument.
C1.ielts_writing: The novel's compelling plot kept readers hooked.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a compelling reason to act now."
C1.mistake: Nicht "zwingend" im Sinn von "obligatorisch"; es heißt überzeugend oder fesselnd.

C1.def: to make up for loss or damage, or to pay someone for loss
C1.example: The company will compensate victims of the accident.
C1.ielts_writing: Higher wages cannot fully compensate for long working hours.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He tried to compensate for his lack of experience."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "compensate sb FOR sth" oder "compensate FOR sth".

C1.def: money paid for loss or injury, or payment for work
C1.example: The family received compensation after the accident.
C1.ielts_writing: Executive compensation has become a controversial topic.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I got no compensation for the delay."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Präposition: "compensation FOR sth".

C1.def: the ability to do something successfully
C1.example: Her competence in managing teams is widely recognized.
C1.ielts_writing: Professional competence requires both knowledge and practical experience.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I doubt his competence to handle this task."
C1.mistake: Nomen "competence" oder "competency"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: having the necessary skill or knowledge
C1.example: She is a competent driver.
C1.ielts_writing: Competent managers delegate tasks effectively.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "competent IN a field" oder "competent AT doing sth"; nicht mit "competitive" verwechseln.

C1.def: to collect information and arrange it into a list or book, or to convert code
C1.example: She compiled a list of useful websites.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers compiled data from thirty countries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need to compile the code before running it."
C1.mistake: In der Informatik: "compile code" (übersetzen); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: so satisfied with the present situation that you stop making an effort
C1.example: We can't afford to become complacent about safety.
C1.ielts_writing: Complacent leaders may overlook early warning signs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "After winning twice, the team grew complacent."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "complaisant" (gefällig) verwechseln; Präposition: "complacent ABOUT sth".

C1.def: to say that you suffer from a pain or illness
C1.example: He complained of a headache.
C1.ielts_writing: Patients often complain of fatigue before diagnosis.
C1.mistake: Medizinisch: "complain OF + Symptom"; sonst "complain ABOUT sth".

C1.def: to add to something in a way that improves it
C1.example: The wine complements the meal perfectly.
C1.ielts_writing: Good marketing should complement a strong product.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "compliment" (Kompliment) verwechseln: complement = ergänzen.

C1.def: the state of being complicated or having many parts
C1.example: The complexity of the issue surprised everyone.
C1.ielts_writing: The complexity of modern supply chains makes disruptions harder to manage.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I underestimated the complexity of the task."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Plural "complexities" (die Feinheiten).

C1.def: the act of obeying a rule or law
C1.example: The factory is in compliance with safety standards.
C1.ielts_writing: Compliance with data protection laws is mandatory.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I ensured compliance with the new policy."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "compliance WITH sth"; "compliance officer" ist ein Compliance-Beauftragter.

C1.def: a factor that makes something more difficult, especially in medicine
C1.example: The surgery went well, but there were complications.
C1.ielts_writing: An unexpected complication delayed the project.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There was a complication with my visa."
C1.mistake: Meist im Plural: "complications"; nicht mit "complicated" (Adjektiv) verwechseln.

C1.def: given free of charge, or expressing praise
C1.example: The hotel offers complimentary breakfast.
C1.ielts_writing: She received a complimentary ticket to the show.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "complementary" (ergänzend) verwechseln; Gratis-Angebote heißen "complimentary".

C1.def: to obey a rule, request, or law
C1.example: Companies must comply with environmental regulations.
C1.ielts_writing: Failure to comply may result in a fine.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I had to comply with the dress code."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "comply WITH sth" (nicht "comply to").

C1.def: to create a piece of music, or to form a whole from parts
C1.example: Mozart composed over six hundred works.
C1.ielts_writing: The committee is composed of twelve members.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I tried to compose myself before speaking."
C1.mistake: "be composed OF" bedeutet "bestehen aus"; "compose yourself" heißt "sich fassen".

C1.def: a piece of music or writing, or the way something is made up
C1.example: The piece is a beautiful composition for piano.
C1.ielts_writing: The chemical composition of the soil affects plant growth.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe; auch Schulaufsatz heißt manchmal "composition".

C1.def: to convert organic waste into fertilizer, or the resulting material
C1.example: We compost our kitchen scraps.
C1.ielts_writing: Composting reduces the amount of waste sent to landfills.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I added compost to the garden beds."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen unzählbar; "compost bin" ist die Komposttonne.

C1.def: to press something into a smaller space, or to reduce file size
C1.example: Compress the files before sending them.
C1.ielts_writing: Gases can be compressed to take up less space.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen "compress" (Kompresse) wird anders betont: /ˈkɑːmpres/.

C1.def: an agreement in which each side gives up something
C1.example: They reached a compromise on the budget.
C1.ielts_writing: Both parties must compromise to end the dispute.
C1.mistake: "compromise on sth" (Zugeständnisse machen); "compromising" kann auch "bloßstellend" heißen.

C1.def: to calculate a number or amount, especially by a machine
C1.example: The program computes the result instantly.
C1.ielts_writing: Computers compute complex equations in seconds.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I can't compute why he would say that."
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich: "That does not compute" bedeutet "Das ergibt keinen Sinn".

C1.def: to convert a process to be controlled or done by computers
C1.example: The library computerized its catalog.
C1.ielts_writing: Many banks computerized their operations during the 1980s.
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv "computerized" (computergesteuert); Nomen "computerization".

C1.def: the use of computers or the study of computer technology
C1.example: She works in cloud computing.
C1.ielts_writing: Advances in computing have transformed daily life.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "computer science" ist die Informatik als Fach.

C1.def: to hide something so that it cannot be seen or known
C1.example: He tried to conceal his disappointment.
C1.ielts_writing: The company concealed evidence of the defect.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She concealed the gift behind her back."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "conceal sth FROM sb"; Nomen "concealment".

C1.def: to admit that something is true, or to give up a position
C1.example: He conceded that he had made a mistake.
C1.ielts_writing: The candidate conceded the election after the final count.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I concede that you have a point."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "concede THAT + Satz"; "concede defeat" heißt "sich geschlagen geben".

C1.def: having an excessively high opinion of yourself
C1.example: He is too conceited to accept criticism.
C1.ielts_writing: A conceited attitude can alienate colleagues.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "conceive" (begreifen) verwechseln; Nomen "conceit" = Eitelkeit.

C1.def: to form an idea, or to become pregnant
C1.example: He conceived a plan to save the company.
C1.ielts_writing: It is hard to conceive of a world without the internet.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They conceived their first child last year."
C1.mistake: "conceive OF sth" bedeutet "sich etwas vorstellen"; auch "empfangen" im biologischen Sinn.

C1.def: a musical composition for a solo instrument with an orchestra
C1.example: She played a piano concerto by Mozart.
C1.ielts_writing: The concerto highlights the soloist's technical skill.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I attended a violin concerto last night."
C1.mistake: "concerto" ist ein Stück für Solisten mit Orchester, nicht ein normales "concert".

C1.def: something granted to end a disagreement, or a reduced price
C1.example: The union won a concession on working hours.
C1.ielts_writing: Both sides made concessions during the peace talks.
C1.mistake: "concession stand" ist der Verkaufsstand (Kino, Stadion); "concessions" bedeuten Ermäßigungen.

C1.def: specific rather than abstract, or a hard building material
C1.example: The police have no concrete evidence.
C1.ielts_writing: Concrete proposals are needed rather than general promises.
C1.mistake: Doppelte Bedeutung: konkret und Beton; "concrete jungle" ist der Betondschungel.

C1.def: to agree with someone's opinion
C1.example: The judges concurred with the verdict.
C1.ielts_writing: Most experts concur that climate change is human-driven.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "concur WITH sb" oder "concur THAT"; sehr formell.

C1.def: to express strong disapproval of someone or something
C1.example: Leaders condemned the attack.
C1.ielts_writing: The report condemns the lack of transparency.
C1.mistake: Das "n" bleibt stumm; Aussprache /kənˈdem/; Nomen "condemnation" mit /-ˈneɪʃən/.

C1.def: to accept or overlook behavior that is considered wrong
C1.example: The school does not condone bullying.
C1.ielts_writing: Condoning corruption can erode public trust.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I don't condone cheating, no matter the reason."
C1.mistake: Meist verneint: "I do not condone..."; bedeutet nicht "verurteilen".

C1.def: a person who directs an orchestra, or one who collects fares, or a material that transmits heat
C1.example: The conductor raised his baton.
C1.ielts_writing: Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Dirigent, Schaffner oder Leiter (Physik); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a solid shape with a circular base and pointed top, or an ice cream holder
C1.example: He ate an ice cream cone.
C1.ielts_writing: Traffic cones marked the closed lane.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The pine cone fell from the tree."
C1.mistake: "traffic cone" ist ein Leitkegel; "pine cone" ist ein Tannenzapfen.

C1.def: sweets and candy collectively, or a shop selling them
C1.example: The shop sells chocolates and other confectionery.
C1.ielts_writing: Confectionery manufacturers face pressure to reduce sugar content.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She bought some confectionery for the kids."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; im Alltag eher "candy"; "confectioner" ist Konditor.

C1.def: to grant a title or honor, or to discuss something with others
C1.example: The university conferred an honorary degree on her.
C1.ielts_writing: Doctors conferred about the best treatment.
C1.mistake: Zwei Konstruktionen: "confer sth ON sb" (verleihen) und "confer WITH sb" (sich beraten).

C1.def: to admit that you have done something wrong
C1.example: He confessed to the crime.
C1.ielts_writing: She confessed that she had lied.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have to confess, I've never read that book."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "confess TO sth"; "I have to confess" leitet freundliches Geständnis ein.

C1.def: a statement admitting guilt or wrongdoing
C1.example: The suspect signed a confession.
C1.ielts_writing: A confession obtained under pressure may not be admissible in court.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "Konfession" (Religion) verwechseln: das heißt "denomination".

C1.def: the arrangement of parts, or the settings of a system
C1.example: The default configuration works for most users.
C1.ielts_writing: A faulty configuration caused the network failure.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I changed the configuration of my router."
C1.mistake: Verb "configure"; nicht "configuration" mit "figuration" verwechseln.

C1.def: to keep something within limits, or to imprison
C1.example: The discussion was confined to a single topic.
C1.ielts_writing: Patients were confined to bed for a week.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was confined to the house by the snow."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "confine sth TO sth"; Nomen "confinement" (Haft, Einschränkung).

C1.def: proof or official statement that something is true or will happen
C1.example: I received an email confirmation of my booking.
C1.ielts_writing: The study requires confirmation from independent researchers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We're waiting for confirmation of the dates."
C1.mistake: Verb "confirm"; "confirmation" ist auch die kirchliche Konfirmation.

C1.def: to behave according to rules or social norms
C1.example: Students must conform to the school's dress code.
C1.ielts_writing: Products must conform to safety standards.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I don't want to conform to expectations."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "conform TO/WITH sth"; "conformist" bedeutet "Mitläufer".

C1.def: to face a difficult situation or person directly
C1.example: She confronted her boss about the unfair treatment.
C1.ielts_writing: Society must confront the problem of inequality.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "confront sb WITH sth" oder "confront sb ABOUT sth".

C1.def: a serious disagreement or fight
C1.example: The meeting ended in a heated confrontation.
C1.ielts_writing: Direct confrontation between the two powers was avoided.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I try to avoid confrontation at work."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "confrontation BETWEEN" oder "WITH"; Adjektiv "confrontational".

C1.def: to express pleasure at someone's success or good fortune
C1.example: I congratulated her on her promotion.
C1.ielts_writing: The mayor congratulated the volunteers for their efforts.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "congratulate sb ON sth"; Nomen immer Plural: "congratulations".

C1.def: a group of people gathered for religious worship
C1.example: The congregation sang the final hymn.
C1.ielts_writing: A growing congregation demanded a larger building.
C1.mistake: Meist religiös; Verb "congregate" (sich versammeln).

C1.def: relating to the US Congress
C1.example: The congressional committee held a hearing.
C1.ielts_writing: Congressional approval is required for the budget.
C1.mistake: Nur für den US-Kongress; "parliamentary" gilt für andere Systeme.

C1.def: an opinion formed without proof
C1.example: It is pure conjecture at this stage.
C1.ielts_writing: Historians often rely on conjecture where records are missing.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "to conjecture"; Präposition: "conjecture ABOUT sth".

C1.def: the state of being connected, especially to the internet
C1.example: Poor connectivity made the video call difficult.
C1.ielts_writing: Improved connectivity brings economic opportunities to remote regions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I've got no connectivity in the mountains."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; nicht mit "connection" (einzelne Verbindung) verwechseln.

C1.def: an additional meaning of a word beyond its literal sense
C1.example: The word has negative connotations.
C1.ielts_writing: Advertisers choose words with positive connotations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The term carries a connotation of laziness."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "denotation" (wörtliche Bedeutung); meist Plural.

C1.def: to take control of a place by force, or to overcome a problem
C1.example: The army conquered the city.
C1.ielts_writing: She conquered her fear of flying.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈkɑːŋkər/ (mit "k"), nicht /ˈkɑːnkwər/.

C1.def: a person who defeats and takes control of a place
C1.example: William the Conqueror invaded England in 1066.
C1.ielts_writing: Conquerors often imposed their own language on the defeated.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The conqueror was both feared and admired."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit "-or" am Ende; "conquest" ist die Eroberung.

C1.def: a person's moral sense of right and wrong
C1.example: His conscience troubled him after the lie.
C1.ielts_writing: A guilty conscience can prevent people from sleeping.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "conscious" (bewusst) oder "consciousness" verwechseln; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: careful to do work thoroughly and correctly
C1.example: She is a conscientious student who never misses a deadline.
C1.ielts_writing: Conscientious employees often take pride in the quality of their work.
C1.mistake: "conscientious objector" bedeutet "Kriegsdienstverweigerer"; nicht mit "conscious" verwechseln.

C1.def: the state of being aware of oneself and surroundings
C1.example: He lost consciousness after the fall.
C1.ielts_writing: Philosophers debate the nature of human consciousness.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Raising public consciousness about climate change is vital."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "regain consciousness" heißt "das Bewusstsein wiedererlangen".

C1.def: following one after another without a break
C1.example: It rained for five consecutive days.
C1.ielts_writing: The team won three consecutive championships.
C1.mistake: "consecutive" meint lückenlos; "successive" kann auch Lücken haben.

C1.def: general agreement among a group of people
C1.example: The committee reached a consensus on the new policy.
C1.ielts_writing: There is a broad scientific consensus on climate change.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We couldn't reach a consensus on where to eat."
C1.mistake: Schreibweise "consensus" (nicht "concensus"); "consensus of opinion" ist eine Doppelung.

C1.def: permission or agreement; to agree to something
C1.example: You need parental consent to join the trip.
C1.ielts_writing: Informed consent is a cornerstone of medical ethics.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "consent TO sth"; "informed consent" heißt "informierte Einwilligung".

C1.def: following as a result of something
C1.example: The factory closure and consequent job losses shocked the town.
C1.ielts_writing: The scandal and consequent resignation attracted attention.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The storm and consequent flooding closed the roads."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "consequent ON/UPON sth"; "consequently" ist der gebräuchlichere Adverb.

C1.def: a person who works to protect the environment
C1.example: Conservationists campaigned to save the wetlands.
C1.ielts_writing: Conservationists argue that protecting habitats is cheaper than restoring them.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "conservative" (politisch konservativ) verwechseln; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: opposed to change, or cautious
C1.example: She wears conservative clothes.
C1.ielts_writing: The conservative estimate puts the cost at ten thousand dollars.
C1.mistake: Bei Schätzungen heißt "conservative estimate" "vorsichtige Schätzung", nicht "politisch".

C1.def: to use something carefully to avoid waste
C1.example: We must conserve water during the drought.
C1.ielts_writing: Efforts to conserve forests help preserve biodiversity.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I try to conserve energy at home."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen "conserve" bezeichnet auch Konfitüre: "fruit conserve".

C1.def: careful not to hurt or inconvenience others
C1.example: He is a considerate neighbor.
C1.ielts_writing: Considerate drivers always signal before turning.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It was considerate of you to call."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "considerate OF sb"; nicht mit "considerable" (beträchtlich) verwechseln.

C1.def: the quality of being the same over time, or the thickness of a substance
C1.example: The team lacks consistency in its performance.
C1.ielts_writing: Consistency in applying the rules ensures fairness.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Mix the batter to a smooth consistency."
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Beständigkeit und Dicke/Zähflüssigkeit ("a thick consistency").

C1.def: to make something stronger or combine things into one
C1.example: The company consolidated its position in the market.
C1.ielts_writing: Banks consolidated to reduce costs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She consolidated her debts into one loan."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "consolidate A and B into C"; nicht mit "console" (trösten) verwechseln.

C1.def: clearly visible or attracting notice
C1.example: He was conspicuous in his bright red jacket.
C1.ielts_writing: The conspicuous absence of key witnesses raised questions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She made a conspicuous effort to look busy."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "conspicuous by its absence" (durch Abwesenheit auffallend).

C1.def: a person who secretly plans with others to do something illegal
C1.example: The conspirators planned to overthrow the government.
C1.ielts_writing: Historians have studied the motives of the conspirators in detail.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They arrested the conspirators before the attack."
C1.mistake: Verb "conspire"; Nomen für die Tat: "conspiracy".

C1.def: a group of stars that form a recognizable pattern
C1.example: Orion is a well-known constellation.
C1.ielts_writing: Ancient cultures named constellations after gods and animals.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I can pick out the Big Dipper constellation."
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "a constellation of factors" bedeutet "ein Zusammenspiel von Faktoren".

C1.def: a district that elects a representative, or its voters
C1.example: The candidate visited every part of the constituency.
C1.ielts_writing: Representatives must address the concerns of their constituency.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My constituency has a large rural population."
C1.mistake: Die Wähler heißen "constituents"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to be or form something
C1.example: These actions constitute a violation of the law.
C1.ielts_writing: Women constitute a majority of the student body.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion ohne Präposition: "constitute a threat"; bedeutet "ausmachen", nicht "einsetzen".

C1.def: a set of fundamental laws of a country, or physical health
C1.example: The constitution guarantees freedom of speech.
C1.ielts_writing: Amendments to the constitution require a two-thirds majority.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Verfassung und körperliche Konstitution; "unconstitutional" heißt "verfassungswidrig".

C1.def: relating to a constitution, or allowed by it
C1.example: The court ruled that the law was constitutional.
C1.ielts_writing: Constitutional rights protect citizens from government abuse.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He claimed his constitutional right to remain silent."
C1.mistake: "constitutional monarchy" ist die konstitutionelle Monarchie; Gegensatz: "unconstitutional".

C1.def: a limit or restriction
C1.example: Budget constraints limited our options.
C1.ielts_writing: Time constraints prevented a full investigation.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "constraints"; Verb "constrain" (einschränken).

C1.def: a person who gives professional advice
C1.example: The firm hired a consultant to improve efficiency.
C1.ielts_writing: Management consultants analyze organizational problems.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My brother works as an IT consultant."
C1.mistake: Verb "consult"; Nomen für die Firma: "consultancy".

C1.def: a meeting to seek advice or discuss something
C1.example: The doctor offered a free consultation.
C1.ielts_writing: Public consultation is required before the plan is approved.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We scheduled a consultation with the lawyer."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "in consultation WITH sb"; "consultation" ist auch das ärztliche Gespräch.

C1.def: a social focus on buying and consuming goods
C1.example: Critics blame consumerism for environmental damage.
C1.ielts_writing: Consumerism drives economic growth but encourages waste.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm tired of the consumerism around the holidays."
C1.mistake: Im Englischen meist negativ (Konsumkultur); "Verbraucherschutz" heißt "consumer protection".

C1.def: (of a disease) able to be passed to others by contact
C1.example: Measles is highly contagious.
C1.ielts_writing: Contagious diseases spread quickly in crowded places.
C1.mistake: "contagious" bedeutet übertragbar durch Berührung; "infectious" durch Erreger; bildlich "ansteckend".

C1.def: to make something impure or harmful by adding a substance
C1.example: Chemicals contaminated the water supply.
C1.ielts_writing: Contaminated food was the source of the outbreak.
C1.mistake: Nomen "contamination"; Konstruktion: "contaminate sth WITH sth".

C1.def: to think carefully about something
C1.example: She contemplated a career change.
C1.ielts_writing: Voters contemplate their options before elections.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He sat by the lake, contemplating life."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "contemplate doing sth" (Gerundium), nicht "contemplate to do".

C1.def: a strong feeling of disrespect for someone or something
C1.example: She looked at him with contempt.
C1.ielts_writing: Contempt for the rules led to disciplinary action.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have nothing but contempt for liars."
C1.mistake: "contempt of court" ist Missachtung des Gerichts; Präposition: "contempt FOR".

C1.def: showing contempt for someone or something
C1.example: He gave a contemptuous laugh.
C1.ielts_writing: The politician was contemptuous of his opponents.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "contemptible" (verachtenswert) verwechseln; Präposition: "contemptuous OF sb".

C1.def: to argue that something is true, or to compete for something
C1.example: He contends that the data are flawed.
C1.ielts_writing: Several teams contend for the title.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have to contend with heavy traffic every day."
C1.mistake: Drei Konstruktionen: "contend THAT" (behaupten), "contend WITH sth" (sich auseinandersetzen), "contend FOR sth" (wetteifern).

C1.def: a person who competes for a prize or position
C1.example: She is a serious contender for the gold medal.
C1.ielts_writing: Several contenders emerged in the race for the presidency.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's a top contender in the league."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "contender FOR sth"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: satisfied with what you have
C1.example: She is content with her life.
C1.ielts_writing: People who are content with little tend to be happier.
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv /kənˈtent/ (zufrieden), als Nomen /ˈkɑːntent/ (Inhalt); "content to do sth" heißt "gern bereit".

C1.def: a claim made in an argument, or disagreement
C1.example: It is my contention that the law is unfair.
C1.ielts_writing: The central contention of the report is that spending should increase.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Money is a source of contention in our family."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "bone of contention" (Zankapfel); Konstruktion: "contention THAT".

C1.def: repeated frequently, often with brief pauses
C1.example: The continual noise made it hard to focus.
C1.ielts_writing: Continual complaints forced the manager to act.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "continuous" gleichsetzen: continual = wiederholt mit Pausen, continuous = ununterbrochen.

C1.def: repeatedly and frequently
C1.example: He continually checks his phone.
C1.ielts_writing: The software is continually updated.
C1.mistake: "continually" heißt wiederholt; "continuously" heißt ohne Unterbrechung.

C1.def: a person or company that agrees to do work for another
C1.example: The contractor finished the building ahead of schedule.
C1.ielts_writing: Government contractors must follow strict procurement rules.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We hired a contractor to renovate the kitchen."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; "independent contractor" heißt "freier Mitarbeiter".

C1.def: to say the opposite of what someone else has said
C1.example: His testimony contradicts the witness's account.
C1.ielts_writing: Do not contradict your supervisor in public.
C1.mistake: Auch für Aussagen: "A contradicts B"; Nomen "contradiction".

C1.def: containing ideas or facts that cannot both be true
C1.example: The witnesses gave contradictory statements.
C1.ielts_writing: Contradictory evidence made it hard to reach a verdict.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I received contradictory advice from two doctors."
C1.mistake: Nomen "contradiction"; "contradictory" heißt nicht "gegensätzlich" im Sinn von "gegenteilig".

C1.def: opposite in nature, or the opposite
C1.example: Contrary to popular belief, bats are not blind.
C1.ielts_writing: Evidence to the contrary was ignored.
C1.ielts_speaking: "On the contrary, I enjoyed the film."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; "on the contrary" widerspricht einer Aussage ("im Gegenteil").

C1.def: a striking difference between things; to compare in order to show differences
C1.example: The contrast between rich and poor is sharp.
C1.ielts_writing: In contrast to last year, sales have increased.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The red flowers contrast with the green leaves."
C1.mistake: Betonung wechselt: Nomen CONtrast, Verb conTRAST; "in contrast TO" und "contrast WITH".

C1.def: a person who gives money, ideas, or articles
C1.example: She is a regular contributor to the magazine.
C1.ielts_writing: Major contributors to climate change include industry and transport.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He was a key contributor to the project."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "contributor TO sth"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: power over something or someone, or to direct something
C1.example: The government lost control of inflation.
C1.ielts_writing: Parents should control screen time.
C1.mistake: Redewendungen: "under control" (unter Kontrolle), "out of control" (außer Kontrolle); Verb "control" ist nicht "überprüfen" (check).

C1.def: a confusing or difficult problem
C1.example: The ethical conundrum left the committee divided.
C1.ielts_writing: Climate policy presents a conundrum for developing nations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's a real conundrum: stay or leave?"
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Plural "conundrums".

C1.def: a small shop open long hours that sells everyday items
C1.example: I bought milk at the convenience store.
C1.ielts_writing: Convenience stores often charge higher prices than supermarkets.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a convenience store near my apartment."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "Supermarkt" gleichsetzen; "convenience" heißt Bequemlichkeit.

C1.def: a social custom, a formal agreement, or a large meeting
C1.example: Shaking hands is a social convention.
C1.ielts_writing: The Geneva Convention protects prisoners of war.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Brauch, Abkommen, Tagung; Adjektiv "conventional" (herkömmlich).

C1.def: the process of changing from one form to another
C1.example: The conversion of the barn into a home took a year.
C1.ielts_writing: Currency conversion rates change daily.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Her conversion to a vegan diet surprised us."
