C1.mistake: Auch religiös: "conversion to Islam"; Präposition: "conversion FROM A TO B".

C1.def: a person who changed beliefs, or to change from one form to another
C1.example: They converted the garage into a studio.
C1.ielts_writing: Many people converted to the new religion.
C1.mistake: Betonung wechselt: Nomen CONvert, Verb conVERT; Konstruktion: "convert sth INTO sth".

C1.def: a person serving a prison sentence, or to declare someone guilty
C1.example: The convict escaped from prison.
C1.ielts_writing: He was convicted of fraud last year.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She was convicted despite the weak evidence."
C1.mistake: Betonung wechselt: Nomen CONvict, Verb conVICT; Konstruktion: "convict sb OF sth".

C1.def: a firmly held belief, or a formal declaration of guilt
C1.example: He spoke with great conviction.
C1.ielts_writing: The prosecution secured a conviction.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Überzeugung und Verurteilung; "lack conviction" heißt "überzeugungslos".

C1.def: a small sweet cake, or a small file saved by a website
C1.example: She baked chocolate chip cookies.
C1.ielts_writing: Websites ask for consent before storing cookies.
C1.mistake: Plural "cookies"; zwei Bedeutungen: Gebäck und Browser-Datei.

C1.def: to work together toward a shared goal
C1.example: The two firms agreed to cooperate on the project.
C1.ielts_writing: Witnesses must cooperate with the investigation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He refused to cooperate with the police."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "cooperate WITH sb"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: the act of working together toward a shared goal
C1.example: International cooperation is essential to fight pandemics.
C1.ielts_writing: Close cooperation between schools and parents improves student outcomes.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "cooperation WITH/BETWEEN"; "in cooperation with" heißt "in Zusammenarbeit mit".

C1.def: willing to help, or a business owned by its members
C1.example: The witness was calm and cooperative.
C1.ielts_writing: Farmers formed a cooperative to sell their produce at better prices.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen oft "co-op" abgekürzt; Gegensatz: "uncooperative".

C1.def: to organize the activities of different people so they work well together
C1.example: She coordinates the volunteer program.
C1.ielts_writing: Emergency services must coordinate their efforts during a crisis.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "coordinate sth WITH sth"; als Nomen "coordinate" bedeutet Koordinate.

C1.def: the organization of different parts so they work effectively together
C1.example: Good coordination between departments saves time.
C1.ielts_writing: Hand-eye coordination is vital for athletes.
C1.mistake: Auch körperlich: "poor coordination" bedeutet "motorische Unsicherheit".

C1.def: a person who organizes the work of a group
C1.example: The event coordinator booked the venue.
C1.ielts_writing: A project coordinator ensures that deadlines are met.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-OR-); häufig mit Bereich: "program coordinator".

C1.def: (informal) a police officer
C1.example: A cop stopped us for speeding.
C1.ielts_writing: Portrayals of cops in television dramas often differ from reality.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich und teils respektlos; offiziell "police officer".

C1.def: a reddish-brown metal used in wires and pipes
C1.example: Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity.
C1.ielts_writing: Copper mining has had significant environmental impacts in several regions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The old pipes were made of copper."
C1.mistake: Als Metall unzählbar; als Münze "coppers" (Kleingeld).

C1.def: the legal right to control the use of creative work
C1.example: The author owns the copyright to the book.
C1.ielts_writing: Copyright law protects creators from unauthorized copying.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "copyright ON/OF a work"; "public domain" bedeutet gemeinfrei.

C1.def: a tool for pulling corks out of wine bottles
C1.example: He opened the wine with a corkscrew.
C1.ielts_writing: The corkscrew is a simple but effective piece of engineering.
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; auch Adjektiv ("corkscrew curl").

C1.def: relating to a large company
C1.example: She works in corporate finance.
C1.ielts_writing: Corporate social responsibility has become increasingly important.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; nicht mit "cooperative" verwechseln.

C1.def: a change that fixes an error
C1.example: Please make the necessary corrections.
C1.ielts_writing: The newspaper printed a correction the next day.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I made a few corrections to the text."
C1.mistake: Auch die Bestrafung: "correctional facility" ist eine Justizvollzugsanstalt.

C1.def: to have a mutual connection or relationship
C1.example: Height and weight often correlate.
C1.ielts_writing: The two variables correlate strongly.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "A correlates WITH B"; Korrelation bedeutet nicht Ursache (causation).

C1.def: a mutual relationship between two things
C1.example: The study found a strong correlation between sleep and performance.
C1.ielts_writing: Correlation does not imply causation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a correlation between wealth and health."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "correlation BETWEEN A and B" oder "correlation WITH"; nicht mit "causation" gleichsetzen.

C1.def: to match or be equivalent, or to exchange letters
C1.example: The two accounts do not correspond.
C1.ielts_writing: The numbers correspond with the data in the report.
C1.mistake: "correspond TO sth" (entsprechen) und "correspond WITH sb" (Briefwechsel); Nomen "correspondence".

C1.def: a journalist who reports from a particular place or on a topic
C1.example: She is the newspaper's foreign correspondent.
C1.ielts_writing: War correspondents risk their lives to report the truth.
C1.mistake: Auch Briefpartner; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-SPON-).

C1.def: matching or similar
C1.example: Each symbol has a corresponding number.
C1.ielts_writing: The corresponding figure for last year was lower.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "corresponding TO sth"; heißt "dazugehörig", nicht "korrespondierend".

C1.def: to confirm or give support to a statement or theory
C1.example: Several witnesses corroborated his story.
C1.ielts_writing: New evidence corroborates earlier findings.
C1.mistake: Meist mit Beweisen und Zeugenaussagen; Nomen "corroboration".

C1.def: dishonest, especially by taking bribes, or to make someone morally bad
C1.example: The corrupt official took bribes.
C1.ielts_writing: Corrupt governments undermine public trust.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "corrupt sb"; in der IT: "corrupted file" (beschädigte Datei).

C1.def: dishonest or illegal behavior by powerful people
C1.example: Corruption is widespread in the region.
C1.ielts_writing: Anti-corruption laws aim to increase transparency.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Plural kaum üblich; "corruption of data" heißt Datenbeschädigung.

C1.def: relating to the universe
C1.example: Cosmic rays strike the earth constantly.
C1.ielts_writing: Cosmic events such as supernovae shape galaxies.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Meeting her felt like a cosmic coincidence."
C1.mistake: Auch umgangssprachlich: "cosmic" für "schicksalhaft, gewaltig"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a Russian or Soviet astronaut
C1.example: The cosmonaut spent months aboard the station.
C1.ielts_writing: Yuri Gagarin became the first cosmonaut to orbit the earth.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The cosmonaut returned to earth after six months."
C1.mistake: Bezeichnet speziell russische Raumfahrer; international "astronaut".

C1.def: the universe seen as an ordered system
C1.example: Ancient peoples looked to the cosmos for answers.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientists study the cosmos using powerful telescopes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We stared at the stars and wondered about the cosmos."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; bezeichnet das Universum als Ordnung, Gegenbegriff: "chaos".

C1.def: a hobby of dressing up as a character from fiction
C1.example: She spent weeks making her cosplay outfit.
C1.ielts_writing: Cosplay has grown into a vibrant fan culture.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm going to a cosplay convention this weekend."
C1.mistake: Zusammensetzung aus "costume" und "play"; Person: "cosplayer".

C1.def: expensive, or involving a high loss
C1.example: Repairing the roof will be costly.
C1.ielts_writing: A costly mistake delayed the project by months.
C1.mistake: "costly" kann auch "verlustreich" bedeuten ("a costly error").

C1.def: (informal) a person who spends a lot of time sitting and watching television
C1.example: My brother is a real couch potato.
C1.ielts_writing: Sedentary lifestyles turn many people into couch potatoes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was a couch potato all weekend."
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich; Plural "couch potatoes"; Gegensatz: "fitness fanatic".

C1.def: a large wild cat of the Americas
C1.example: A cougar was spotted near the hiking trail.
C1.ielts_writing: Cougars have a wide range across the Western Hemisphere.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We read about cougars in biology class."
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich auch "ältere Frau mit jüngerem Partner"; daher kontextabhängig.

C1.def: an elected member of a local council
C1.example: The councilor proposed a new traffic plan.
C1.ielts_writing: City councilors vote on local budgets and policies.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "counselor" (Berater) verwechseln; "council" Ratsversammlung.

C1.def: professional guidance on personal problems
C1.example: She sought counseling after the loss.
C1.ielts_writing: Counseling services are available to all students.
C1.mistake: Nomen unzählbar: "some counseling"; "counsel" ist Rechtsbeistand oder Rat.

C1.def: a person trained to give advice on personal or professional matters
C1.example: The school counselor helped him choose a college.
C1.ielts_writing: Camp counselors supervise children during activities.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I talked to a counselor about my stress."
C1.mistake: Im Recht ist "counsel" der Anwalt; "counselor" ist hier Berater, nicht Anwalt.

C1.def: to rely on someone or something
C1.example: You can count on me.
C1.ielts_writing: Citizens count on the government to protect public health.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm counting on you to be on time."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "count ON sb"; "count on" ist nicht "zählen auf" im Sinn von Rechnen.

C1.def: a long flat surface in a shop, or to argue against something
C1.example: He paid at the counter.
C1.ielts_writing: She countered that the figures were misleading.
C1.mistake: "over-the-counter" bedeutet rezeptfrei; "counter" ist auch Zähler.

C1.def: a person or thing that has the same position as another in a different place
C1.example: The president met his French counterpart.
C1.ielts_writing: Female employees earn less than their male counterparts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My counterpart in the Berlin office called me."
C1.mistake: Meist mit Possessiv: "his counterpart"; nicht mit "Gegenspieler" (opponent) gleichsetzen.

C1.def: too many to be counted
C1.example: There are countless ways to learn a language.
C1.ielts_writing: Countless studies have confirmed the benefits of exercise.
C1.mistake: Steht vor Plural: "countless times"; nicht mit "uncountable" (Grammatik) verwechseln.

C1.def: a sudden illegal seizure of power
C1.example: The army staged a coup against the government.
C1.ielts_writing: A military coup often leads to prolonged instability.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Landing that client was quite a coup."
C1.mistake: Das "p" bleibt stumm: /kuː/; "coup" bedeutet auch "großer Erfolg" (a coup).

C1.def: showing courage
C1.example: The courageous firefighter saved three children.
C1.ielts_writing: It takes a courageous leader to admit mistakes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She was courageous in the face of danger."
C1.mistake: Nomen "courage"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: work done by students during a course, not in the final exam
C1.example: The coursework counts for forty percent of the grade.
C1.ielts_writing: Continuous assessment through coursework reduces exam stress.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have a lot of coursework this term."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "much coursework"; nicht mit "Kursbuch" gleichsetzen.

C1.def: a place where legal cases are heard, an area for sports, or to seek someone's favor
C1.example: The case will go to court next month.
C1.ielts_writing: The tennis court was crowded on Sunday.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Gericht, Spielfeld oder Verb "umwerben"; "out of court" heißt "außergerichtlich".

C1.def: a legal instruction issued by a court
C1.example: The company obtained a court order to stop the demolition.
C1.ielts_writing: A court order requires the parties to comply by a set date.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They served him with a court order."
C1.mistake: Verb "to order" bei Gericht; Plural "court orders".

C1.def: polite behavior or a polite act
C1.example: The staff treated us with courtesy.
C1.ielts_writing: Common courtesy requires you to reply promptly.
C1.mistake: "courtesy of" heißt "mit freundlicher Genehmigung" (z. B. bei Fotos).

C1.def: a small sheltered bay
C1.example: A hidden cove lay beyond the rocks.
C1.ielts_writing: The cove provides a safe harbor for fishing boats.
C1.mistake: Kleiner als "bay"; nicht mit "cave" (Höhle) verwechseln.

C1.def: a person who lacks courage
C1.example: He called me a coward for running away.
C1.ielts_writing: A coward may avoid conflict at the cost of principles.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt like a coward for not speaking up."
C1.mistake: Stark abwertend; Adjektiv "cowardly".

C1.def: lack of courage
C1.example: His cowardice cost him his reputation.
C1.ielts_writing: Moral cowardice prevents many from speaking out against injustice.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Running away was an act of cowardice."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Gegenteil: "courage" oder "bravery".

C1.def: a person you work with
C1.example: I get along well with my coworkers.
C1.ielts_writing: Friendly relations among coworkers improve productivity.
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; im formalen Stil auch "colleague".

C1.def: a wild dog of North America
C1.example: A coyote howled in the distance.
C1.ielts_writing: Coyotes have adapted to living in urban areas.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe: /kaɪˈoʊti/, nicht wie im Spanischen.

C1.def: a shellfish with ten legs and pincers, or to complain
C1.example: We ate fresh crab on the dock.
C1.ielts_writing: Crabs play an important role in coastal ecosystems.
C1.mistake: "crabby" bedeutet "mürrisch"; Plural "crabs".

C1.def: a skilled activity done by hand, a boat, or to make something skillfully
C1.example: Pottery is a traditional craft.
C1.ielts_writing: The book explores the craft of writing.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She crafted a beautiful table by hand."
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Handwerk, Wasserfahrzeug (Plural: "craft") oder Verb "herstellen".

C1.def: a machine for lifting heavy things, or a large wading bird
C1.example: A crane lifted the steel beams.
C1.ielts_writing: Cranes migrate thousands of miles each year.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He craned his neck to see better."
C1.mistake: Als Verb: "crane your neck" bedeutet "den Hals recken".

C1.def: a large round hole in the ground made by an impact or explosion
C1.example: A meteor left a huge crater in the desert.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientists study craters on the moon to understand its history.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We hiked around the rim of the crater."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Plural "craters".

C1.def: to move slowly on hands and knees or with the body close to the ground
C1.example: The baby crawled across the floor.
C1.ielts_writing: Traffic crawled along the highway during rush hour.
C1.mistake: "crawling with" heißt "wimmelnd vor"; im Schwimmen ist "the crawl" der Kraulstil.

C1.def: containing cream or having a smooth soft texture
C1.example: The soup was thick and creamy.
C1.ielts_writing: A creamy texture is often achieved by adding butter or cream.
C1.mistake: Nomen "cream"; auch Farbe: "creamy white".

C1.def: an activity that lets you express your creativity
C1.example: Painting gives her a creative outlet after work.
C1.ielts_writing: A creative outlet can reduce stress and improve well-being.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need a creative outlet besides my job."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "outlet FOR sth"; nicht mit "outlet" (Steckdose, Verkaufsstelle) verwechseln.

C1.def: a person who makes or brings something into existence
C1.example: The creator of the series gave an interview.
C1.ielts_writing: Content creators earn income through advertising and sponsorships.
C1.mistake: "the Creator" (groß) bezeichnet Gott; "content creator" ist ein Beruf im Internet.

C1.def: the quality of being trusted and believed
C1.example: The scandal damaged the minister's credibility.
C1.ielts_writing: Credibility is essential for any news organization.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "credit" verwechseln; "credibility gap" ist eine Glaubwürdigkeitslücke.

C1.def: able to be believed or trusted
C1.example: The witness gave a credible account.
C1.ielts_writing: A credible threat can deter aggression.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's no credible evidence for that claim."
C1.mistake: "incredible" heißt "unglaublich" im Positiven wie Negativen; "credible" = glaubwürdig.

C1.def: to move slowly and quietly, or to increase gradually
C1.example: The cat crept toward the bird.
C1.ielts_writing: Costs tend to creep up over time.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She crept down the stairs so she wouldn't wake anyone."
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: creep, crept, crept; "creepy" bedeutet "gruselig".

C1.def: hard and dry in a pleasant way, easily broken
C1.example: The bacon was crispy and golden.
C1.ielts_writing: Crispy fried snacks are popular worldwide.
C1.mistake: "crisp" ist formeller und wird auch für Luft und Stoffe verwendet.

C1.def: a detailed analysis and assessment of something
C1.example: The professor wrote a critique of the novel.
C1.ielts_writing: A thoughtful critique highlights both strengths and weaknesses.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I appreciated her honest critique of my work."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "a critique OF sth"; meist ausführlicher als "criticism".

C1.def: a royal headdress, or to place a crown on someone
C1.example: The queen wore a golden crown.
C1.ielts_writing: The team was crowned champion after the final.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The dentist put a crown on my tooth."
C1.mistake: Auch "Zahnkrone": "a dental crown"; "crowning glory" heißt "Krönung, Höhepunkt".

C1.def: in a natural state, or lacking subtlety
C1.example: Crude oil is processed into fuel.
C1.ielts_writing: His crude jokes offended several guests.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They built a crude shelter from branches."
C1.mistake: "crude oil" ist Rohöl; "crude" bei Menschen bedeutet "derb, unanständig".

C1.def: a large warship, or a recreational motor boat
C1.example: A naval cruiser patrolled the coast.
C1.ielts_writing: Cruisers are fast and well-armed ships used for escort duties.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We rented a cabin cruiser for the weekend."
C1.mistake: "police cruiser" ist im US-Englisch ein Streifenwagen.

C1.def: firm and making a noise when chewed
C1.example: I like crunchy apples.
C1.ielts_writing: A crunchy texture adds contrast to creamy dishes.
C1.mistake: "crunchy" ist hart und laut; "crispy" eher dünn und trocken.

C1.def: to press something so that it is broken or flattened, or to defeat completely
C1.example: Crush the garlic before adding it to the pan.
C1.ielts_writing: The army crushed the rebellion.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have a crush on my classmate."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen "have a crush on sb" bedeutet "für jemanden schwärmen".

C1.def: a support for walking, or something relied on too much
C1.example: He walked on crutches after the surgery.
C1.ielts_writing: Technology should not become a crutch for critical thinking.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Don't use your phone as a crutch."
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "a pair of crutches"; bildlich als "Krücke".

C1.def: having a hidden or puzzling meaning
C1.example: She left a cryptic message on the board.
C1.ielts_writing: Cryptic remarks left the audience guessing.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "cryptography" (Kryptografie) verwechseln; "cryptic" meint nur rätselhaft.

C1.def: digital currency using cryptography to secure transactions
C1.example: Many investors bought cryptocurrency last year.
C1.ielts_writing: Cryptocurrency prices fluctuate sharply from day to day.
C1.mistake: Plural selten; Kurzform "crypto"; Beispiel: Bitcoin.

C1.def: a clear mineral or a glass-like solid with a regular structure
C1.example: The chandelier was made of crystal.
C1.ielts_writing: Salt forms crystals as it dries.
C1.mistake: "crystal clear" heißt "glasklar" und "unmissverständlich".

C1.def: a bird that lays eggs in other birds' nests, or (informal) crazy
C1.example: A cuckoo called from the forest.
C1.ielts_writing: The cuckoo is known for laying its eggs in the nests of other birds.
C1.ielts_speaking: "You must be cuckoo to try that."
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv umgangssprachlich "bekloppt"; "cuckoo clock" ist die Kuckucksuhr.

C1.def: the end part of a sleeve, or a metal ring used to restrain wrists
C1.example: He fastened the cuff of his shirt.
C1.ielts_writing: Police placed cuffs on the suspect.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Off the cuff, I'd say it costs around fifty dollars."
C1.mistake: "off the cuff" bedeutet "aus dem Stegreif"; auch Plural "cuffs" für Handschellen.

C1.def: a religious group with unusual beliefs, or a fashionable object of devotion
C1.example: Members of the cult lived in isolation.
C1.ielts_writing: The film gained cult status among fans.
C1.mistake: Im Alltag oft "Sekte" mit negativer Färbung; "cult classic" ist positiv.

C1.def: to prepare land for crops, or to develop a skill or relationship
C1.example: Farmers cultivate rice in the valley.
C1.ielts_writing: It takes years to cultivate trust.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "cultivate friendships"; Nomen "cultivation".

C1.def: (informal) a person with a keen interest in the arts
C1.example: My aunt is a real culture vulture.
C1.ielts_writing: Culture vultures flock to the city for its museums and theaters.
C1.ielts_speaking: "As a culture vulture, I never miss an exhibition."
C1.mistake: Leicht spöttisch und scherzhaft; nicht mit "Geier" im wörtlichen Sinn verbinden.

C1.def: a person who manages a museum or collection
C1.example: The curator selected the paintings for the exhibition.
C1.ielts_writing: Curators play a key role in interpreting cultural heritage.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She's the curator of a small museum."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Verb "to curate" (kuratieren).

C1.def: a rule that requires people to stay indoors during certain hours
C1.example: The city imposed a curfew after the unrest.
C1.ielts_writing: A curfew was lifted after calm returned.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My parents set a curfew of ten o'clock."
C1.mistake: Auch für Jugendliche: "a teenage curfew" (Ausgehzeit).

C1.def: a strong desire to know or learn something
C1.example: Curiosity led her to open the box.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientific progress is driven by human curiosity.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Out of curiosity, how old are you?"
C1.mistake: Redewendung: "curiosity killed the cat"; Präposition: "curiosity ABOUT sth".

C1.def: a lock of hair that bends in a spiral, or to form a curved shape
C1.example: She had long brown curls.
C1.ielts_writing: The cat curled up in front of the fire.
C1.mistake: "curl up" bedeutet "sich zusammenrollen"; Haarsprache: "curly" (lockig).

C1.def: a small dried grape or a type of berry
C1.example: The cake contains currants and spices.
C1.ielts_writing: Currants are commonly used in traditional British baking.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I bought red currants at the market."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "current" (aktuell, Strömung) verwechseln; gleiche Aussprache.

C1.def: a movable indicator on a screen
C1.example: The cursor blinked at the end of the line.
C1.ielts_writing: Moving the cursor over a link displays a preview.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I can't find the cursor on my screen."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "curser" (jemand, der flucht) verwechseln.

C1.def: having a body with attractive curves
C1.example: She is tall and curvy.
C1.ielts_writing: The road is curvy and winding.
C1.mistake: Bei Menschen eher positiv und modisch; auch für Straßen.

C1.def: legal responsibility for a child, or the state of being held by police
C1.example: She won custody of her two children.
C1.ielts_writing: The suspect remained in police custody overnight.
C1.mistake: "in custody" heißt "in Haft"; "custody of" bezieht sich auf Kinder oder Sachen.

C1.def: an opening made with a sharp tool, or to reduce something
C1.example: He got a cut on his finger.
C1.ielts_writing: The government plans to cut spending.
C1.mistake: Viele Phrasal Verbs: "cut off", "cut down", "cut back"; unregelmäßig: cut, cut, cut.

C1.def: to reduce the amount of something, or to make a tree fall
C1.example: I'm trying to cut down on sugar.
C1.ielts_writing: Cutting down trees without replanting harms ecosystems.
C1.mistake: "cut down ON sth" bedeutet "etwas verringern"; ohne "on" heißt es "fällen".

C1.def: a piece cut from a plant for growing, or an excerpt from a newspaper
C1.example: She took a cutting from the rose bush.
C1.ielts_writing: Cuttings can grow into new plants in water.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I kept a cutting of the article."
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv "cutting" heißt "scharf, beißend" ("a cutting remark").

C1.def: bullying carried out through digital communication
C1.example: Schools are working to prevent cyberbullying.
C1.ielts_writing: Cyberbullying can have serious consequences for victims' mental health.
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; Täter: "cyberbully".

C1.def: the virtual environment of computer networks
C1.example: Hackers operate in cyberspace.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments struggle to regulate cyberspace effectively.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Präposition: "IN cyberspace".

C1.def: a solid or hollow shape with parallel circular ends
C1.example: The engine has four cylinders.
C1.ielts_writing: A gas cylinder must be handled carefully.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The can is shaped like a cylinder."
C1.mistake: "firing on all cylinders" bedeutet "auf Hochtouren laufen"; Adjektiv "cylindrical".

C1.def: believing that people are motivated only by self-interest
C1.example: He is cynical about politics.
C1.ielts_writing: A cynical view of advertising assumes that all claims are lies.
C1.mistake: Nicht dasselbe wie "sarkastisch"; Nomen "cynic" (Zyniker), "cynicism".

C1.def: a short knife used as a weapon
C1.example: He drew a dagger from his belt.
C1.ielts_writing: A dagger was found at the crime scene.
C1.mistake: "cloak and dagger" bedeutet "Spionage und Geheimniskrämerei"; "look daggers" heißt "böse anstarren".

C1.def: a garden plant with large colorful flowers
C1.example: She planted dahlias along the fence.
C1.ielts_writing: Dahlias bloom from midsummer until the first frost.
C1.mistake: Plural "dahlias"; Aussprache variiert, aber meist /ˈdæliə/.

C1.def: regular activities you do each day
C1.example: My daily routines include jogging and reading.
C1.ielts_writing: Daily routines provide structure and reduce stress.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I've changed my daily routines since moving."
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "daily routines"; Singular "daily routine" ebenfalls üblich.

C1.def: a barrier built across a river to hold back water
C1.example: The dam holds back millions of gallons of water.
C1.ielts_writing: Dams provide hydroelectric power but alter river ecosystems.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "to dam a river" (aufstauen); "damn" wird gleich ausgesprochen, ist aber ein Fluch.

C1.def: causing harm or injury
C1.example: The scandal was damaging to the company.
C1.ielts_writing: Damaging rumors can ruin a reputation.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "damaging TO sth"; Gegenteil: "beneficial".

C1.def: to have the courage to do something
C1.example: He didn't dare to ask for help.
C1.ielts_writing: How dare you speak to me like that?
C1.mistake: Als Modalverb ohne "to": "I dare not go"; "I dare say" heißt "ich vermute".

C1.def: recklessly bold, or a person who takes risks
C1.example: He performed daredevil stunts on his motorcycle.
C1.ielts_writing: Daredevil sports attract thrill seekers.
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; positiver als "reckless".

C1.def: the operations performed on data by a computer
C1.example: Data processing is faster with modern computers.
C1.ielts_writing: Large-scale data processing powers modern search engines.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "data" wird als Plural oder Singular verwendet.

C1.def: able to be assigned a date or age
C1.example: The pottery is datable to the Roman period.
C1.ielts_writing: Few manuscripts are datable with precision.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The fossil is datable to millions of years ago."
C1.mistake: Seltenes Wort; Präposition: "datable TO a period".

C1.def: the first light of day, or to begin to be understood
C1.example: We left at dawn.
C1.ielts_writing: A new era dawned after the revolution.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It dawned on me that I'd forgotten the keys."
C1.mistake: "it dawned on me" heißt "mir wurde klar"; "the dawn of" bedeutet "Anfang von".

C1.def: no longer living, or not functioning
C1.example: The plant looks dead.
C1.ielts_writing: The phone battery is dead.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: "dead tired" heißt "todmüde"; "dead on time" bedeutet "pünktlich".

C1.def: a street closed at one end, or a situation with no progress
C1.example: The road ended in a dead end.
C1.ielts_writing: Many young people feel they are stuck in a dead-end job.
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv "dead-end" mit Bindestrich: "a dead-end job".

C1.def: unable to hear, or refusing to listen
C1.example: My grandfather is partially deaf.
C1.ielts_writing: Politicians who remain deaf to public concern risk losing support.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The crowd was deaf to his appeals."
C1.mistake: Aussprache /def/, nicht /diːf/; "turn a deaf ear" bedeutet "sich taub stellen".

C1.def: an armed group that carries out unlawful killings
C1.example: Human rights groups denounced the death squad.
C1.ielts_writing: Death squads have operated in several conflict zones.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The film shows how a death squad terrorized the village."
C1.mistake: Plural "death squads"; meist im politischen oder militärischen Kontext.

C1.def: the total number of people killed in a disaster or war
C1.example: The death toll rose to fifty.
C1.ielts_writing: Rescuers expect the death toll to increase.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The death toll of the accident is still unclear."
C1.mistake: Wird mit "rise" oder "climb" kombiniert: "the death toll rose".

C1.def: open to question or argument
C1.example: It is debatable whether the plan will succeed.
C1.ielts_writing: Whether tax cuts stimulate growth is debatable.
C1.mistake: Steht mit "whether": "It is debatable whether..."; nicht "debatable that".

C1.def: scattered pieces of something destroyed or discarded
C1.example: The street was covered with debris after the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: Space debris poses a risk to satellites.
C1.mistake: Das "s" ist stumm: /dəˈbriː/; unzählbar.

C1.def: a first public appearance
C1.example: The singer made her debut at nineteen.
C1.ielts_writing: The novel was a remarkable debut for the young author.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /deɪˈbjuː/ mit stummem "t"; Verb "to debut".

C1.def: moral or cultural decline, often shown through luxury
C1.example: Critics saw the lavish party as a sign of decadence.
C1.ielts_writing: The decadence of the late empire is a recurring theme in history.
C1.mistake: Heute oft positiv gebraucht für Luxus ("decadent dessert"); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: self-indulgent or luxuriously rich
C1.example: We shared a decadent chocolate cake.
C1.ielts_writing: Decadent lifestyles often coincide with social inequality.
C1.mistake: Positiv bei Essen, negativ bei Lebensstil; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to rot or break down gradually
C1.example: Leaves decay and enrich the soil.
C1.ielts_writing: Urban areas decayed as industries closed.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen: "urban decay"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: the act of making someone believe something false
C1.example: The scheme relied on deception.
C1.ielts_writing: Deception in advertising is illegal in many countries.
C1.mistake: Verb "deceive"; Adjektiv "deceptive" (trügerisch); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a fraction written with a decimal point, or relating to tens
C1.example: Write the answer as a decimal.
C1.ielts_writing: The decimal system is based on ten.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Round the number to two decimal places."
C1.mistake: Im Englischen mit Punkt statt Komma: "3.5" (three point five).

C1.def: the process of making choices, especially in organizations
C1.example: Good decision-making requires clear information.
C1.ielts_writing: Participation of employees in decision-making improves morale.
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich als Nomen; auch Adjektiv: "decision-making skills".

C1.def: having a major effect, or able to make quick, firm decisions
C1.example: The goal was decisive for the match.
C1.ielts_writing: A decisive leader can guide a team through crisis.
C1.mistake: Nomen "decisiveness"; Gegenteil: "indecisive".

C1.def: a formal statement announcing something
C1.example: The declaration was read before parliament.
C1.ielts_writing: The Declaration of Independence outlined American principles.
C1.mistake: "declaration of war" heißt Kriegserklärung; am Zoll "customs declaration".

C1.def: to announce something officially or firmly
C1.example: The government declared a state of emergency.
C1.ielts_writing: She declared her intention to run for office.
C1.mistake: Am Zoll: "anything to declare?"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: serving to make something look attractive
C1.example: The bowl is purely decorative.
C1.ielts_writing: Decorative patterns appear in many ancient cultures.
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "functional"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a person who designs interiors or paints and papers walls
C1.example: The decorator chose a soft blue for the walls.
C1.ielts_writing: An interior decorator coordinates colors, furniture, and lighting.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We hired a decorator to redo the living room."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "interior designer" gleichzusetzen: ein decorator gestaltet vor allem Oberflächen.

C1.def: committed to a task or purpose
C1.example: She is a dedicated nurse.
C1.ielts_writing: Dedicated teachers inspire their students.
C1.mistake: Auch "gewidmet": "dedicated to the memory of..."; Technisch: "dedicated line".

C1.def: commitment to a task, or a message honoring someone in a book
C1.example: His dedication to training paid off.
C1.ielts_writing: The book carries a dedication to her mother.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "dedication TO sth"; zwei Bedeutungen: Einsatz und Widmung.

C1.def: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence
C1.example: The detective deduced that the butler was lying.
C1.ielts_writing: From the data, researchers deduced a link between diet and mood.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I deduced from his tone that he was upset."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "deduce sth FROM sth"; nicht mit "deduct" (abziehen) verwechseln.

C1.def: an action, or a legal document
C1.example: He was praised for his brave deeds.
C1.ielts_writing: The deed to the house was transferred to the buyer.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A good deed brings its own reward."
C1.mistake: "in deed" (in Tat) im Gegensatz zu "in word"; "title deed" ist die Eigentumsurkunde.

C1.def: to consider or judge something in a particular way
C1.example: The proposal was deemed unacceptable.
C1.ielts_writing: The court deemed the evidence inadmissible.
C1.mistake: Meist im Passiv: "be deemed + Adjektiv"; sehr formell.

C1.def: to cook food in a large amount of hot oil
C1.example: They deep-fry the chicken in vegetable oil.
C1.ielts_writing: Deep-fried snacks are common at fairs.
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich geschrieben; Partizip "deep-fried".

C1.def: a preset option, or failure to pay a debt
C1.example: The default language is English.
C1.ielts_writing: The country is at risk of default on its debts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The program will revert to default settings."
C1.mistake: "by default" bedeutet "standardmäßig"; auch Verb "to default on a loan" (Kredit nicht bedienen).

C1.def: a fault or imperfection, or to leave one's country for another
C1.example: The product had a manufacturing defect.
C1.ielts_writing: Genetic defects can cause serious diseases.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He defected to the West during the Cold War."
C1.mistake: Betonung: Nomen DEfect, Verb deFECT; "defector" bedeutet Überläufer.

C1.def: a person accused in a court of law
C1.example: The defendant pleaded not guilty.
C1.ielts_writing: Defendants have the right to a fair trial.
C1.mistake: Gegenstück: "plaintiff" (Kläger); im Strafprozess "accused".

C1.def: intended to protect, or quick to feel criticized
C1.example: He became defensive when asked about the error.
C1.ielts_writing: Defensive driving reduces the risk of accidents.
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "offensive"; "get defensive" heißt "sich verteidigen müssen".

C1.def: polite respect for someone's authority or opinion
C1.example: They treated the guest with great deference.
C1.ielts_writing: Deference to authority has declined in many societies.
C1.ielts_speaking: "In deference to your wishes, we postponed the meeting."
C1.mistake: Wendung: "in deference TO sb" (aus Rücksicht auf); nicht mit "difference" verwechseln.

C1.def: a lack of something essential
C1.example: Iron deficiency can cause fatigue.
C1.ielts_writing: A deficiency in funding delayed the project.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "deficiency OF/IN sth"; Adjektiv "deficient".

C1.def: the amount by which spending exceeds income
C1.example: The country has a large budget deficit.
C1.ielts_writing: Reducing the deficit requires cutting spending or raising taxes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We have a trade deficit with China."
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "surplus"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: the clearing of forests on a large scale
C1.example: Deforestation threatens the Amazon.
C1.ielts_writing: Deforestation contributes to climate change and loss of species.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Gegenteil: "reforestation" (Wiederaufforstung).

C1.def: to remove ice from a refrigerator or thaw frozen food
C1.example: I need to defrost the chicken.
C1.ielts_writing: Defrost the freezer regularly to maintain efficiency.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Please defrost the soup in the microwave."
C1.mistake: Auch "defrost the windshield" (Scheibe enteisen); nicht "unfreeze".

C1.def: to refuse to obey, or to resist openly
C1.example: Protesters defied the curfew.
C1.ielts_writing: The results defy explanation.
C1.mistake: "defy explanation" bedeutet "sich nicht erklären lassen"; Nomen "defiance".

C1.def: a person chosen to represent others, or to assign tasks
C1.example: Each country sent a delegate to the summit.
C1.ielts_writing: Effective managers delegate tasks to their teams.
C1.mistake: Aussprache wechselt: Nomen /-ɡət/, Verb /-ɡeɪt/; Konstruktion: "delegate sth TO sb".

C1.def: a group of representatives, or the act of assigning tasks
C1.example: A delegation visited the capital.
C1.ielts_writing: Delegation of responsibilities improves efficiency.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Gruppe und Aufgabenverteilung; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses, and prepared foods
C1.example: I bought a sandwich from the deli.
C1.ielts_writing: A neighborhood deli offers fresh sandwiches and salads.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We picked up some cheese at the deli."
C1.mistake: Kurzform von "delicatessen"; "deli counter" ist die Frischetheke.

C1.def: fragile, or requiring careful handling
C1.example: The vase is very delicate.
C1.ielts_writing: A delicate situation requires careful diplomacy.
C1.mistake: "a delicate balance" heißt "ein empfindliches Gleichgewicht"; Nomen "delicacy" (Delikatesse).

C1.def: a particular section of the population, or relating to population statistics
C1.example: Advertisers target the younger demographic.
C1.ielts_writing: Changes in demographics affect healthcare planning.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The show appeals to a broad demographic."
C1.mistake: Nomen: "demographics" (Plural) für Bevölkerungsstatistik.

C1.def: to pull down a building, or to destroy completely
C1.example: The old factory will be demolished.
C1.ielts_writing: The team demolished their opponents in the final.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He demolished the argument with one question."
C1.mistake: Nomen "demolition"; auch bildlich "demolish an argument".

C1.def: an evil spirit, or a very skilled person
C1.example: The story tells of a demon in the forest.
C1.ielts_writing: Fear can become a demon that haunts us for years.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's a demon on the football field."
C1.mistake: "inner demons" bedeutet "innere Dämonen, quälende Gedanken"; "a demon at sth" ist "ein Ass".

C1.def: a public protest, or a practical display of how something works
C1.example: Thousands joined the demonstration downtown.
C1.ielts_writing: The professor gave a demonstration of the experiment.
C1.mistake: "demo" ist die Kurzform; Präposition: "demonstration AGAINST sth".

C1.def: the home of a wild animal, or a cozy private room
C1.example: The lion returned to its den.
C1.ielts_writing: The police raided an illegal gambling den.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Dad is in his den watching football."
C1.mistake: Auch ein gemütliches Wohn- oder Arbeitszimmer; "den of iniquity" heißt "Sündenpfuhl".

C1.def: a refusal to accept or admit something
C1.example: He was in denial about his illness.
C1.ielts_writing: The company issued a denial of the allegations.
C1.mistake: "in denial" heißt "etwas nicht wahrhaben wollen"; Verb "deny".

C1.def: to publicly condemn something as wrong
C1.example: Leaders denounced the violence.
C1.ielts_writing: The report denounces corruption in the police force.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "denounce sb/sth AS sth"; Nomen "denunciation".

C1.def: closely packed, or difficult to understand
C1.example: A dense fog covered the valley.
C1.ielts_writing: Dense urban areas face challenges in housing and transport.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The text is too dense for me."
C1.mistake: Bei Menschen bedeutet "dense" umgangssprachlich "begriffsstutzig".

C1.def: the amount of something per unit of space
C1.example: Population density is high in coastal cities.
C1.ielts_writing: Water has a higher density than oil.
C1.mistake: Plural "densities"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: the state of relying on something or someone
C1.example: The country reduced its dependence on oil.
C1.ielts_writing: Dependence on digital devices raises concerns about attention.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "dependence ON sth"; Adjektiv "dependent" mit "-ent".

C1.def: to show something in a painting, drawing, or words
C1.example: The mural depicts village life.
C1.ielts_writing: The film depicts the struggles of immigrants.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "depict sb AS sth"; Nomen "depiction".

C1.def: to reduce something gradually until little remains
C1.example: Overfishing depletes fish stocks.
C1.ielts_writing: Resources are being depleted faster than they can be replaced.
C1.mistake: Nomen "depletion"; "ozone depletion" ist der Ozonabbau.

C1.def: to strongly disapprove of or feel sad about something
C1.example: Many deplore the lack of affordable housing.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics deplore the declining quality of public debate.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "deplorable" (bedauerlich, schändlich); bedeutet nicht nur "traurig".

C1.def: to put something or someone into effective use or position
C1.example: The army deployed troops along the border.
C1.ielts_writing: Companies deploy new software in stages to limit risk.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The hospital deployed extra staff during the flu season."
C1.mistake: Nomen "deployment"; auch IT: "deploy an app" (veröffentlichen).

C1.def: the movement of forces or resources into position
C1.example: The deployment of troops began at dawn.
C1.ielts_writing: Rapid deployment of vaccines saved many lives.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar oder zählbar; in der IT auch "Bereitstellung von Software".

C1.def: a sum of money paid as a first payment or into a bank
C1.example: He paid a deposit on the apartment.
C1.ielts_writing: She deposited her paycheck at the bank.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a mineral deposit under the mountain."
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Kaution, Einzahlung, Lagerstätte; "security deposit" ist die Mietkaution.

C1.def: a medical condition of deep sadness, a period of economic decline, or a hollow in a surface
C1.example: She was treated for depression.
C1.ielts_writing: The Great Depression devastated the American economy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a small depression in the lawn."
C1.mistake: Drei Bedeutungen: psychisch, wirtschaftlich, geografisch; "depressed" ist die Folge.

C1.def: to prevent someone from having or using something
C1.example: Prisoners were deprived of sleep.
C1.ielts_writing: Poverty can deprive children of educational opportunities.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "deprive sb OF sth"; Nomen "deprivation".

C1.def: the distance from top to bottom or front to back
C1.example: The pool has a depth of two meters.
C1.ielts_writing: Her analysis lacks depth.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was out of my depth in the conversation."
C1.mistake: "in depth" heißt "ausführlich"; "out of your depth" bedeutet "überfordert".

C1.def: a person appointed to act for another
C1.example: The deputy led the meeting while the director was away.
C1.ielts_writing: A deputy mayor assists with day-to-day administration.
C1.mistake: Im US-Kontext ist "deputy" auch ein Hilfspolizist ("deputy sheriff").

C1.def: abandoned and in poor condition
C1.example: The derelict factory stood empty for years.
C1.ielts_writing: Derelict buildings often attract vandalism.
C1.mistake: Nomen "dereliction of duty" bedeutet "Pflichtverletzung".

C1.def: to move downward
C1.example: The plane began to descend.
C1.ielts_writing: Darkness descended over the valley.
C1.mistake: "descend from sb" bedeutet "von jemandem abstammen"; "descend into chaos" bedeutet "ins Chaos abrutschen".

C1.def: a person who comes from a particular ancestor
C1.example: She is a descendant of a famous poet.
C1.ielts_writing: Descendants of settlers still live in the region.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "descendant OF sb"; Gegenteil: "ancestor".

C1.def: the act of going down, or family origin
C1.example: The descent was steep and dangerous.
C1.ielts_writing: She is of Italian descent.
C1.mistake: "of ... descent" bedeutet "von ... Abstammung"; Gegenteil: "ascent".

C1.def: to damage or treat a holy place with disrespect
C1.example: Vandals desecrated the cemetery.
C1.ielts_writing: Desecration of religious sites is condemned worldwide.
C1.mistake: Nomen "desecration"; Gegenteil: "consecrate" (weihen).

C1.def: to officially choose someone or something for a role or purpose
C1.example: The area was designated a nature reserve.
C1.ielts_writing: The committee designated a spokesperson for the group.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He was designated as the team captain."
C1.mistake: Betonung beim Verb auf der ersten Silbe; "designated driver" ist der nüchterne Fahrer.

C1.def: worth having or doing
C1.example: It is desirable to arrive early.
C1.ielts_writing: Affordable housing is a desirable goal for cities.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "undesirable"; nicht mit "begehrenswert" im sexuellen Sinn gleichsetzen.

C1.def: the main screen of a computer, or a desktop computer
C1.example: I saved the file on my desktop.
C1.ielts_writing: Many offices still rely on desktop computers.
C1.mistake: Unterscheidet sich von "laptop"; auch Bildschirmoberfläche.

C1.def: empty and bleak, or feeling alone
C1.example: The desert was a desolate landscape.
C1.ielts_writing: Desolate villages dot the abandoned region.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Verb "to desolate" ist selten.

C1.def: to feel contempt for someone or something
C1.example: He despised cowards.
C1.ielts_writing: Many citizens despise corrupt officials.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "despicable" (verachtenswert); stärker als "dislike".

C1.def: causing great damage
C1.example: The storm had a destructive effect on crops.
C1.ielts_writing: Destructive criticism can harm a team's morale.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "constructive"; Nomen "destruction".

C1.def: to keep someone in official custody, or to delay someone
C1.example: Police detained three suspects.
C1.ielts_writing: Travelers were detained at the border for hours.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I don't want to detain you any longer."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "retain" (behalten) verwechseln; Nomen "detainee".

C1.def: able to be discovered or noticed
C1.example: The disease is not detectable in early stages.
C1.ielts_writing: Detectable levels of toxins were found in the water.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "undetectable"; Nomen "detection".

C1.def: the act of discovering something hidden
C1.example: Early detection improves survival rates.
C1.ielts_writing: Smoke detection systems must be tested regularly.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The detection of the error took hours."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "detection OF sth"; "detector" ist das Gerät.

C1.def: the act of keeping someone in custody, or a school punishment
C1.example: He was held in detention for weeks.
C1.ielts_writing: The student had to stay in detention after class.
C1.mistake: "detention" ist in der Schule das Nachsitzen; nicht mit "retention" verwechseln.

C1.def: to become worse over time
C1.example: The patient's condition deteriorated overnight.
C1.ielts_writing: Relations between the two countries have deteriorated sharply.
C1.mistake: Nomen "deterioration"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-TIR-).

C1.def: harm or damage, especially in the phrase "to the detriment of"
C1.example: He worked long hours to the detriment of his health.
C1.ielts_writing: Cutting education budgets is to the detriment of future growth.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "to the detriment OF sth"; Adjektiv "detrimental".

C1.def: to cause great damage, or to shock someone deeply
C1.example: The hurricane devastated the coast.
C1.ielts_writing: The news devastated the family.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was devastated when I lost my job."
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv "devastated" heißt auch "am Boden zerstört" (emotional).

C1.def: causing great damage or distress
C1.example: The earthquake had devastating consequences.
C1.ielts_writing: A devastating blow to the economy followed the crisis.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It was a devastating loss for the team."
C1.mistake: Positiv selten: auch "devastatingly beautiful" bedeutet "umwerfend schön".

C1.def: the process of growing or improving
C1.example: Child development begins before birth.
C1.ielts_writing: Economic development has lifted millions out of poverty.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; zählbar als "a development" (Ereignis).

C1.def: to move away from a standard or expected course
C1.example: Do not deviate from the plan.
C1.ielts_writing: Results that deviate from expectations require further investigation.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "deviate FROM sth"; "standard deviation" ist die Standardabweichung.

C1.def: the supreme evil spirit, or a mischievous person
C1.example: The play shows a pact with the devil.
C1.ielts_writing: Some cultures personify evil as the devil.
C1.mistake: "devil's advocate" ist jemand, der absichtlich dagegen argumentiert; "the Devil" groß.

C1.def: to invent or plan something carefully
C1.example: She devised a clever way to save money.
C1.ielts_writing: Engineers devised a new method to reduce emissions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We devised a plan to surprise him."
C1.mistake: Verb mit "s" (devise) und Nomen "device" mit "c"; nicht verwechseln.

C1.def: very loving or loyal
C1.example: She is a devoted mother.
C1.ielts_writing: Devoted fans waited overnight for tickets.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "devoted TO sb/sth"; Verb "devote yourself to sth".

C1.def: great love or loyalty, or religious zeal
C1.example: Her devotion to her family was unwavering.
C1.ielts_writing: Acts of devotion take many forms across religions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The nun lived a life of devotion."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "devotion TO sb/sth"; auch Plural "devotions" (Andacht).

C1.def: to identify an illness by examining the symptoms
C1.example: The doctor diagnosed her with asthma.
C1.ielts_writing: Early symptoms are often hard to diagnose accurately.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He was diagnosed with diabetes last year."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "diagnose sb WITH sth" oder "be diagnosed WITH"; Nomen "diagnosis".

C1.def: the identification of an illness from its symptoms
C1.example: The doctor confirmed the diagnosis.
C1.ielts_writing: An accurate diagnosis is essential for effective treatment.
C1.mistake: Plural "diagnoses" /-siːz/; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-NO-).

C1.def: a form of a language spoken in a particular region
C1.example: She speaks a regional dialect.
C1.ielts_writing: Dialects can vary widely within one country.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love hearing local dialects when I travel."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "accent" (Aussprache) gleichsetzen: dialect betrifft auch Wortschatz und Grammatik.

C1.def: a straight line through the center of a circle
C1.example: The pipe has a diameter of five centimeters.
C1.ielts_writing: The diameter of the earth is about twelve thousand kilometers.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (/daɪˈæ-/); Präposition: "ten inches IN diameter".

C1.def: a condition with frequent loose bowel movements
C1.example: The child had diarrhea and a fever.
C1.ielts_writing: Clean water prevents diseases such as diarrhea.
C1.mistake: Schreibweise "diarrhea" mit "rrh"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: to say words aloud for someone to write down, or to control what happens
C1.example: She dictated a letter to her assistant.
C1.ielts_writing: Market forces dictate prices.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Don't let others dictate how you live."
C1.mistake: "dictate TO sb" bedeutet "jemandem Vorschriften machen"; "be dictated by" heißt "bestimmt von".

C1.def: a ruler with absolute power
C1.example: The dictator controlled the media.
C1.ielts_writing: Dictators often suppress opposition to remain in power.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The country was ruled by a dictator."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Nomen "dictatorship".

C1.def: to become extinct or gradually disappear
C1.example: Many species could die out within decades.
C1.ielts_writing: Traditional crafts are in danger of dying out.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The old custom has almost died out."
C1.mistake: Partizip "died out"; nicht "die away" (verklingen).

C1.def: to recognize or show the difference between things
C1.example: It is hard to differentiate between the twins.
C1.ielts_writing: Marketers differentiate their products through branding.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "differentiate BETWEEN A and B" oder "differentiate A FROM B".

C1.def: to break down food in the body, or to absorb information
C1.example: The stomach digests food in several hours.
C1.ielts_writing: It took me weeks to digest the news.
C1.mistake: Betonung beim Verb auf der zweiten Silbe; Nomen "digest" (Zusammenfassung) auf der ersten.

C1.def: having or showing dignity
C1.example: He gave a dignified reply.
C1.ielts_writing: A dignified manner can earn respect even in defeat.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She left the room with a dignified air."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "undignified"; Nomen "dignity".

C1.def: the quality of being worthy of respect
C1.example: Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity.
C1.ielts_writing: Human dignity is a cornerstone of modern law.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Wendung: "beneath one's dignity" (unter seiner Würde).

C1.def: a situation requiring a difficult choice
C1.example: She faced a moral dilemma.
C1.ielts_writing: Policymakers face a dilemma between growth and sustainability.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Wendung: "on the horns of a dilemma".

C1.def: a US coin worth ten cents
C1.example: I found a dime on the sidewalk.
C1.ielts_writing: A dime is the smallest-value coin in American currency.
C1.mistake: "a dime a dozen" bedeutet "etwas Alltägliches"; "stop on a dime" heißt "sofort anhalten".

C1.def: a measurable extent, or an aspect of a situation
C1.example: The room's dimensions are ten by twelve feet.
C1.ielts_writing: Social media adds a new dimension to politics.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural bei Maßen: "dimensions"; bildlich "an added dimension".

C1.def: to become or make something smaller or less
C1.example: The pain began to diminish.
C1.ielts_writing: Funding for the program has diminished over the years.
C1.mistake: "diminishing returns" bedeutet "abnehmender Ertrag"; transitive und intransitive Verwendung.

C1.def: a small, informal restaurant, or a person eating a meal
C1.example: We stopped at a diner for breakfast.
C1.ielts_writing: A classic American diner serves pancakes and burgers all day.
C1.mistake: Als Person "a diner" (Gast); als Lokal meist mit Theke und einfacher Karte.

C1.def: to put something briefly into a liquid, or a slight drop
C1.example: She dipped the bread in the soup.
C1.ielts_writing: Sales dipped slightly in the third quarter.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We went for a quick dip in the pool."
C1.mistake: "dip into savings" bedeutet "Ersparnisse angreifen"; "a dip" kann Soße oder Bad sein.

C1.def: the work of managing relations between countries, or tactful skill in dealing with people
C1.example: The crisis was resolved through diplomacy.
C1.ielts_writing: Quiet diplomacy often achieves more than public confrontation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It took some diplomacy to calm him down."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-PLO-); unzählbar.

C1.def: an official who represents a country abroad
C1.example: The diplomat met with foreign ministers.
C1.ielts_writing: Diplomats negotiate treaties and manage international disputes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She works as a diplomat in Brussels."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe: DIP-lo-mat; Adjektiv "diplomatic" auf "-MAT-".

C1.def: relating to diplomacy, or tactful
C1.example: The two countries established diplomatic relations.
C1.ielts_writing: A diplomatic reply avoided offending anyone.
C1.mistake: Auch im Alltag: "be diplomatic" heißt "taktvoll sein".

C1.def: a list of names, addresses, or files
C1.example: I looked up his number in the directory.
C1.ielts_writing: The file is stored in a hidden directory.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We have a staff directory on our website."
C1.mistake: In der IT: Ordner; nicht mit "director" (Leiter) verwechseln.

C1.def: (slang) a despicable or untrustworthy person
C1.example: He's a dirtbag who cheats his customers.
C1.ielts_writing: The word "dirtbag" is considered offensive and should be avoided in formal contexts.
C1.mistake: Derb; nur im Slang; in formellen Texten vermeiden.

C1.def: causing great damage or failure
C1.example: The decision had disastrous consequences.
C1.ielts_writing: A disastrous harvest led to widespread hunger.
C1.mistake: Nomen "disaster"; Schreibweise "disastrous" ohne zweites "e" (nicht "disasterous").

C1.def: to get rid of something that is no longer useful
C1.example: Discard the outer leaves before cooking.
C1.ielts_writing: Outdated hypotheses should be discarded in light of new data.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; als Nomen "discard" (ausgesonderte Karte).

C1.def: to officially allow someone to leave, or to release a substance
C1.example: The patient was discharged from the hospital.
C1.ielts_writing: The factory discharged waste into the river.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Patient entlassen, Soldat entlassen, Flüssigkeit ausstoßen; Nomen "discharge".

C1.def: to make secret information known
C1.example: The company refused to disclose the figures.
C1.ielts_writing: Employees must disclose any conflicts of interest.
C1.mistake: Nomen "disclosure"; Gegenteil: "withhold".

C1.def: the act of revealing information
C1.example: Full disclosure is required by law.
C1.ielts_writing: The disclosure of the report caused a scandal.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The disclosure of her identity surprised us."
C1.mistake: "full disclosure" heißt "vollständige Offenlegung"; auch als Redeeinleitung benutzt.

C1.def: to break the connection between things
C1.example: Please disconnect the power cable.
C1.ielts_writing: Rural areas were disconnected from the internet during the storm.
C1.mistake: Auch emotional: "feel disconnected" (abgekoppelt); Nomen "disconnection".

C1.def: written or spoken communication on a subject
C1.example: Political discourse has become more polarized.
C1.ielts_writing: Academic discourse often relies on specialized vocabulary.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The discourse around the issue is complex."
C1.mistake: Als Verb "to discourse on sth" (sich ausführlich äußern); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: the quality of being careful about what one says, or the freedom to decide
C1.example: The matter requires discretion.
C1.ielts_writing: The judge has the discretion to reduce the sentence.
C1.mistake: "at your discretion" heißt "nach Ihrem Ermessen"; nicht mit "discrete" (getrennt) verwechseln.

C1.def: unfair treatment of people based on group membership
C1.example: The law prohibits discrimination at work.
C1.ielts_writing: Discrimination against minorities remains a global problem.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She faced discrimination because of her accent."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "discrimination AGAINST sb"; "discriminate between" bedeutet "unterscheiden".

C1.def: disappointed and no longer believing in something
C1.example: Many voters feel disenchanted with politics.
C1.ielts_writing: Disenchanted employees often leave without warning.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "disenchanted WITH sth"; Nomen "disenchantment".

C1.def: feeling strong dislike or disapproval
C1.example: I was disgusted by the smell.
C1.ielts_writing: Readers were disgusted at the cruelty described in the report.
C1.mistake: Präpositionen: "disgusted AT/BY/WITH"; nicht mit "disgusting" (ekelhaft) verwechseln.

C1.def: disappointed after discovering something is not as good as believed
C1.example: She became disillusioned with her career.
C1.ielts_writing: Disillusioned voters stayed away from the polls.
C1.mistake: Nomen "disillusionment"; Präposition: "disillusioned WITH sth".

C1.def: the act of removing someone from a job, or rejecting an idea
C1.example: His dismissal came as a surprise.
C1.ielts_writing: The court ordered the dismissal of the case.
C1.mistake: "unfair dismissal" heißt "ungerechtfertigte Kündigung"; Verb "dismiss".

C1.def: to force someone to leave home, or to take the place of something
C1.example: The war displaced thousands of families.
C1.ielts_writing: Automation may displace many workers.
C1.mistake: "displaced persons" sind Vertriebene; Nomen "displacement".

C1.def: an arrangement of things for the public to see, or to show
C1.example: The shop window had a lovely display.
C1.ielts_writing: Digital displays show real-time flight information.
C1.mistake: "on display" bedeutet "ausgestellt"; Nomen und Verb gleich.

C1.def: the act of getting rid of something
C1.example: Waste disposal is a major issue in cities.
C1.ielts_writing: The land is at the disposal of the government.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have the car at my disposal."
C1.mistake: "at your disposal" heißt "zu Ihrer Verfügung"; nicht mit "Disposition" gleichsetzen.

C1.def: to get rid of something, or to make someone inclined to something
C1.example: Dispose of the batteries safely.
C1.ielts_writing: Parents are disposed to support their children.
C1.mistake: Fast immer "dispose OF sth"; "well disposed" bedeutet "wohlgesinnt".

C1.def: to show that something is false
C1.example: New evidence disproved the theory.
C1.ielts_writing: It is impossible to disprove a claim that cannot be tested.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "prove"; Nomen "disproof".

C1.def: a disagreement, or to argue against something
C1.example: The two countries are in a border dispute.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientists dispute the findings of the study.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen und Verb: "dispute sth" (bestreiten); "beyond dispute" heißt "unbestritten".

C1.def: to interrupt the normal course of something
C1.example: Heavy snow disrupted traffic.
C1.ielts_writing: New technology can disrupt traditional industries.
C1.mistake: Nomen "disruption"; "disruptive technology" heißt "disruptive Technologie".

C1.def: an interruption in the normal course of events
C1.example: Strikes caused major disruption to rail services.
C1.ielts_writing: Supply chain disruption affected many industries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There was a brief disruption in service."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "disruption TO sth"; unzählbar im Alltag.

C1.def: the spreading of information or ideas widely
C1.example: The dissemination of knowledge is a core mission of universities.
C1.ielts_writing: Rapid dissemination of misinformation can harm public health.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The dissemination of the report took weeks."
C1.mistake: Verb "disseminate"; Betonung auf der vierten Silbe.

C1.def: a long academic essay, usually for a doctoral degree
C1.example: She is writing her dissertation on medieval history.
C1.ielts_writing: A dissertation requires original research and critical analysis.
C1.mistake: Für den Doktor: "dissertation"; für den Master: "thesis".

C1.def: to mix into a liquid, or to officially end an organization
C1.example: Sugar dissolves in hot water.
C1.ielts_writing: Parliament was dissolved before the election.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "dissolve into tears" bedeutet "in Tränen ausbrechen".

C1.def: a difference, or special honor or excellence
C1.example: There is a clear distinction between the two terms.
C1.ielts_writing: She graduated with distinction.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "distinction BETWEEN A and B"; "graduate with distinction" heißt "mit Auszeichnung".

C1.def: having a quality that makes something easy to recognize
C1.example: The singer has a distinctive voice.
C1.ielts_writing: The building's distinctive design makes it a landmark.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There was a distinctive smell of smoke."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "distinct" (deutlich) gleichsetzen: distinctive = charakteristisch.

C1.def: successful and respected
C1.example: He is a distinguished professor of law.
C1.ielts_writing: The conference welcomed several distinguished guests.
C1.mistake: Auch "distinguished service" (verdienstvoll); Verb "distinguish".

C1.def: to change the shape or meaning of something
C1.example: The mirror distorted his face.
C1.ielts_writing: Media coverage can distort public perception.
C1.mistake: Nomen "distortion"; "distort the truth" bedeutet "die Wahrheit verdrehen".

C1.def: extreme anxiety, pain, or danger
C1.example: The child showed signs of distress.
C1.ielts_writing: The ship sent out a distress signal.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It distresses me to see them argue."
C1.mistake: Auch bei Möbeln: "distressed furniture" bedeutet "absichtlich auf alt getrimmt".

C1.def: upset or in difficulty
C1.example: She was distressed by the news.
C1.ielts_writing: Distressed borrowers struggled to repay their loans.
C1.mistake: Bei Kleidung heißt "distressed" absichtlich abgenutzt ("distressed jeans").

C1.def: emotionally upset, or mentally unwell
C1.example: He grew up in a disturbed family.
C1.ielts_writing: The report highlights mentally disturbed offenders.
C1.mistake: Auch "undisturbed" für "ungestört"; "disturbed" bei Menschen kann stigmatisierend wirken.

C1.def: causing worry or shock
C1.example: The film contains disturbing scenes.
C1.ielts_writing: A disturbing trend of rising prices continues.
C1.mistake: Gegensatz zu "disturbed": disturbing löst Unruhe aus, disturbed ist beunruhigt.

C1.def: to change the direction of something, or to distract attention
C1.example: Traffic was diverted around the accident.
C1.ielts_writing: Funds were diverted from health to defense.
C1.mistake: Nomen "diversion" (Umleitung, Ablenkung); Konstruktion: "divert sth FROM A TO B".

C1.def: a payment made to shareholders from company profits
C1.example: The company paid a quarterly dividend.
C1.ielts_writing: Dividends provide investors with a steady income stream.
C1.mistake: "pay dividends" bedeutet auch bildlich "sich auszahlen"; Plural "dividends".

C1.def: relating to God, or wonderful
C1.example: The queen claimed divine authority.
C1.ielts_writing: The scenery was simply divine.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich "divine" für "himmlisch" (Essen); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a number by which another number is divided
C1.example: Two is a divisor of ten.
C1.ielts_writing: The divisor must not be zero.
C1.mistake: Mathematischer Fachbegriff; Gegenstück: "dividend" in der Mathematik.

C1.def: feeling as if everything is spinning
C1.example: I felt dizzy after standing up too fast.
C1.ielts_writing: Dizzy spells may indicate low blood pressure.
C1.mistake: "dizzy heights" bedeutet "schwindelnde Höhen" (Erfolg); Nomen "dizziness".

C1.def: the system that translates website names into numerical addresses
C1.example: A DNS error prevented the site from loading.
C1.ielts_writing: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "domain name system"; als Buchstaben gesprochen.

C1.def: the activity of making or repairing things yourself
C1.example: He loves do-it-yourself projects.
C1.ielts_writing: The do-it-yourself movement encourages self-reliance.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I renovated the kitchen using do-it-yourself tips."
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "DIY"; als Adjektiv mit Bindestrichen.

C1.def: a structure where ships load and unload, or to bring a ship to a dock
C1.example: The ship docked at the harbor.
C1.ielts_writing: Dock workers went on strike for better wages.
C1.mistake: Auch "dock" in der IT (Docking-Station); "in the dock" heißt "auf der Anklagebank".

C1.def: the highest university degree
C1.example: She earned a doctorate in physics.
C1.ielts_writing: A doctorate usually involves several years of independent research.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "a doctorate IN physics"; "doctoral" ist das Adjektiv.

C1.def: a set of beliefs held by a church, party, or government
C1.example: The doctrine of free will is debated by philosophers.
C1.ielts_writing: Foreign policy doctrines shape international relations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The Monroe Doctrine guided US foreign policy."
C1.mistake: Verb "indoctrinate" (indoktrinieren); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: documents providing information or evidence
C1.example: Please submit the necessary documentation.
C1.ielts_writing: Clear documentation helps new developers understand the system.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "the documentation is"; nicht "documentations".

C1.def: a small tree with flowers and red berries
C1.example: A dogwood bloomed in our yard.
C1.ielts_writing: The dogwood is the state tree of Virginia.
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; der Baum, nicht "dog wood" getrennt.

C1.def: an area of knowledge or activity, or a website address
C1.example: Medicine is her domain of expertise.
C1.ielts_writing: Public domain works can be freely used.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I registered a new domain for my blog."
C1.mistake: "in the public domain" heißt "gemeinfrei"; "domain name" ist die Web-Adresse.

C1.def: a rounded roof or ceiling
C1.example: The dome of the cathedral can be seen from afar.
C1.ielts_writing: Domes allow architects to cover large spaces without interior columns.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We climbed to the top of the dome."
C1.mistake: "dome" ist die Kuppel, nicht der "Dom" (cathedral).

C1.def: the state of being more powerful or influential
C1.example: The team's dominance continued for years.
C1.ielts_writing: Economic dominance gives a nation considerable political leverage.
C1.ielts_speaking: "His dominance in the meeting was obvious."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "dominance OVER sb/sth"; Verb "dominate".

C1.def: a person who has not made up their mind in a survey or vote
C1.example: The poll showed a high number of don't-knows.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't-knows can decide the outcome of a close election.
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich als Nomen; in Umfragen: "don't know"-Antworten.

C1.def: a person who gives money or organs
C1.example: The donor gave a million dollars to the school.
C1.ielts_writing: Organ donors save thousands of lives each year.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Gegenstück: "recipient".

C1.def: to cause someone or something to certain failure or destruction
C1.example: The plan was doomed from the start.
C1.ielts_writing: Rising costs may doom the project.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt doomed when I saw the exam."
C1.mistake: Meist im Passiv: "be doomed to + Infinitiv"; Nomen "doom" (Verhängnis).

C1.def: rules about what to do and what not to do
C1.example: We prepared a list of dos and don'ts for visitors.
C1.ielts_writing: The brochure lists the dos and don'ts of food hygiene.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I read up on the dos and don'ts of etiquette."
C1.mistake: Immer Plural: "dos and don'ts"; nicht "do and don't".

C1.def: a measured amount of medicine
C1.example: Take a double dose if you miss one.
C1.ielts_writing: An overdose of the medication can be dangerous.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need a dose of fresh air."
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "a dose of reality" heißt "ein Stück Wirklichkeit"; Nomen "dosage" (Dosierung).

C1.def: to deceive someone who trusts you
C1.example: They double-crossed their partner.
C1.ielts_writing: A double-cross by an ally can destroy an alliance.
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich; Nomen "a double-cross" (Verrat).

C1.def: a bus or vehicle with two levels
C1.example: We rode a double-decker bus.
C1.ielts_writing: The double-decker bus has become a symbol of London.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I like sitting on the top deck of a double-decker."
C1.mistake: Kann auch ein Sandwich mit zwei Schichten sein; nicht nur Bus.

C1.def: having two possible effects, one good and one bad
C1.example: Social media is a double-edged sword.
C1.ielts_writing: The reform proved double-edged, bringing both benefits and risks.
C1.mistake: Häufige Wendung: "a double-edged sword" (zweischneidiges Schwert).

C1.def: uncertain or unlikely
C1.example: It is doubtful whether she will come.
C1.ielts_writing: The effectiveness of the treatment remains doubtful.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "doubtful whether/that"; nicht mit "dubious" (fragwürdig) verwechseln.

C1.def: a small bird often a symbol of peace
C1.example: A white dove flew over the square.
C1.ielts_writing: The dove is a universal symbol of peace.
C1.mistake: Im Politischen: "dove" bedeutet "Friedensbefürworter", Gegenteil "hawk".

C1.def: feeling sad, or (of a system) not working
C1.example: I've been feeling down lately.
C1.ielts_writing: The server is down, so we cannot access the files.
C1.mistake: "feel down" bedeutet "niedergeschlagen sein"; "the system is down" heißt "das System ist ausgefallen".

C1.def: a period when a machine is not working, or time for rest
C1.example: The network had two hours of downtime.
C1.ielts_writing: Downtime between projects allows employees to recharge.
C1.mistake: Zusammen geschrieben: "downtime"; Gegenteil in der IT: "uptime".

C1.def: a very heavy fall of rain
C1.example: We got caught in a downpour.
C1.ielts_writing: The downpour flooded several streets.
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; Plural "downpours".

C1.def: a decline in economic activity
C1.example: The economy suffered a sharp downturn.
C1.ielts_writing: A downturn in consumer spending hit the retail sector.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The company saw a downturn in profits."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "upturn"; Präposition: "downturn IN sth".

C1.def: a large insect with transparent wings that hovers over water
C1.example: A dragonfly hovered over the pond.
C1.ielts_writing: Dragonflies are an indicator of clean water.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I saw a dragonfly by the river."
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; Libelle ist nicht "dragon fly" getrennt.

C1.def: to remove liquid, or to exhaust someone's energy
C1.example: He drained the water from the pasta.
C1.ielts_writing: The long meeting drained my energy.
C1.mistake: "brain drain" bedeutet "Abwanderung Hochqualifizierter"; "down the drain" heißt "den Bach runter".

C1.def: a person who writes plays
C1.example: Shakespeare is the most famous dramatist in English.
C1.ielts_writing: The dramatist explores themes of power and betrayal.
C1.mistake: Synonym "playwright" ist üblicher; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to make something more exciting, or to adapt a story for stage or screen
C1.example: The novel was dramatized for television.
C1.ielts_writing: Media outlets often dramatize ordinary events.
C1.mistake: Nomen "dramatization"; "dramatize" wird auch abwertend für "übertreiben" benutzt.

C1.def: a style of horse riding in which the horse performs precise movements
C1.example: She competes in dressage at national level.
C1.ielts_writing: Dressage requires precise communication between rider and horse.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I watched a dressage event on TV."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; das Wort stammt aus dem Französischen.

C1.def: a chest of drawers, or a person who helps actors dress
C1.example: I keep my sweaters in the dresser.
C1.ielts_writing: A theater dresser helps actors change quickly between scenes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She has a mirror on her dresser."
C1.mistake: "dresser" ist ein Möbelstück; "to dress" heißt anziehen.

C1.def: a room for changing clothes, especially in a theater
C1.example: The actor waited in his dressing room.
C1.ielts_writing: Dressing rooms at stadiums are used by both teams.
C1.mistake: Plural "dressing rooms"; in Läden "fitting room" (Anprobe).

C1.def: to move slowly with no direction, or to gradually move away
C1.example: The boat drifted down the river.
C1.ielts_writing: Many students drift through university without clear goals.
C1.mistake: "drift apart" bedeutet "sich auseinanderleben"; "get the drift" heißt "den Sinn verstehen".

C1.def: a strong determination, or a journey in a vehicle
C1.example: She has the drive to succeed.
C1.ielts_writing: The charity launched a drive for donations.
C1.mistake: Viele Bedeutungen: Motivation, Fahrt, Spendenaktion, Festplatte ("hard drive").

C1.def: a restaurant or shop where customers are served in their cars
C1.example: We ordered food at the drive-through.
C1.ielts_writing: Drive-through restaurants have become common worldwide.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I stopped at a drive-through for coffee."
C1.mistake: Auch "drive-thru" geschrieben; im Deutschen "Drive-in" für das Kino.

C1.def: powerful, strong, or forceful
C1.example: A driving rain beat against the windows.
C1.ielts_writing: Competition is the driving force behind innovation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's a driving force on the team."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "driving force" (treibende Kraft); nicht nur "fahren".

C1.def: an unmanned aircraft, or a low humming sound
C1.example: A drone filmed the landscape from above.
C1.ielts_writing: The drone of the engine put him to sleep.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The teacher droned on for an hour."
C1.mistake: "drone on" bedeutet "monoton weiterreden"; Männliche Biene: "drone".

C1.def: a menu that opens downward when clicked
C1.example: Select your country from the drop-down menu.
C1.ielts_writing: A drop-down menu keeps the interface uncluttered.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I couldn't find the option in the drop-down menu."
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich oder zusammen: "drop-down"; Plural "menus".

C1.def: a person who leaves school or a course before finishing
C1.example: He is a high school dropout.
C1.ielts_writing: The dropout rate has fallen thanks to new support programs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Many dropouts return later to complete their studies."
