C1.mistake: Verb getrennt: "drop out"; Nomen "dropout" zusammen.

C1.def: to die in water, or to cover a sound with a louder one
C1.example: Two swimmers nearly drowned.
C1.ielts_writing: The music drowned out the conversation.
C1.mistake: "drown out" bedeutet "übertönen"; "drown in" kann auch "überhäuft sein mit" bedeuten.

C1.def: having two parts or aspects
C1.example: She holds dual citizenship.
C1.ielts_writing: The tool serves a dual purpose.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "duel" (Duell) verwechseln; gleiche Aussprache.

C1.def: to replace the original language in a film, or to give a nickname
C1.example: The film was dubbed into German.
C1.ielts_writing: The press dubbed him "the iron chancellor."
C1.ielts_speaking: "She dubbed me the queen of procrastination."
C1.mistake: Gegensatz: "subtitled" (untertitelt); auch für Spitznamen.

C1.def: doubtful or suspicious
C1.example: He has a dubious reputation.
C1.ielts_writing: Dubious claims should be checked against reliable sources.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "dubious ABOUT sth"; "dubious honor" ist "zweifelhafte Ehre".

C1.def: not interesting or lively, or not sharp
C1.example: The lecture was dull.
C1.ielts_writing: A dull knife is dangerous because it slips.
C1.mistake: Auch "dull pain" (dumpfer Schmerz); "dull" ist das Gegenteil von "sharp" oder "bright".

C1.def: (informal) stupid, or unable to speak
C1.example: That was a dumb mistake.
C1.ielts_writing: Calling people dumb can be offensive and inaccurate.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt dumb for forgetting my keys."
C1.mistake: "dumb" für "stumm" gilt als beleidigend; heute "speech-impaired"; "dumb luck" heißt "reines Glück".

C1.def: to throw away carelessly, or to end a relationship
C1.example: Don't dump your trash here.
C1.ielts_writing: Illegal dumping of waste harms the environment.
C1.mistake: Auch IT: "data dump"; "dump" ist als Nomen die Müllkippe.

C1.def: (informal) someone who ends a relationship
C1.example: She was the dumper, not the dumpee.
C1.ielts_writing: Studies show that both the dumper and the dumpee experience stress.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I don't want to be the dumper."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen selten; "dump truck" (Kipplaster) ist die Hauptbedeutung.

C1.def: an underground prison in a castle
C1.example: The prisoner was locked in the dungeon.
C1.ielts_writing: Medieval castles had dungeons beneath the main hall.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We played a game called Dungeons and Dragons."
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈdʌndʒən/ mit "dsch"; "Dungeon master" im Rollenspiel.

C1.def: a pair of people performing together
C1.example: The singing duo released a new album.
C1.ielts_writing: A dynamic duo of scientists made the discovery.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We were a comedy duo in college."
C1.mistake: Plural "duos"; "dynamic duo" bezeichnet ein erfolgreiches Paar.

C1.def: deceitful in a way that involves saying one thing and doing another
C1.example: The duplicitous minister lied to the public.
C1.ielts_writing: A duplicitous strategy eventually damages trust.
C1.mistake: Nomen "duplicity"; stärker als "dishonest".

C1.def: the time just after sunset when it's not yet dark
C1.example: We arrived at the cabin at dusk.
C1.ielts_writing: Bats emerge at dusk to feed.
C1.ielts_speaking: "From dawn to dusk, the farm was busy."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "dawn"; Wendung: "from dawn till dusk".

C1.def: (of goods) sold without paying customs tax
C1.example: We bought perfume at the duty-free shop.
C1.ielts_writing: Duty-free allowances limit how much alcohol travelers may bring.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I picked up some chocolates at duty-free."
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich; Steuer heißt hier "duty", nicht "tax".

C1.def: a very small person or animal, or (of plants) smaller than normal
C1.example: The garden had a dwarf apple tree.
C1.ielts_writing: A dwarf planet like Pluto is smaller than a normal planet.
C1.mistake: Als Bezeichnung für Menschen kann das Wort verletzen; Fachbegriff: "dwarf planet".

C1.def: energetic and constantly changing
C1.example: She's a dynamic leader.
C1.ielts_writing: The dynamic nature of markets requires constant adaptation.
C1.mistake: Nomen "dynamics" (Plural) bedeutet "Dynamik, Kräfteverhältnis".

C1.def: an explosive used in mining and demolition
C1.example: Workers used dynamite to blast the rock.
C1.ielts_writing: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite in 1867.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich als Adjektiv "dynamite" für "großartig"; "politically dynamite" heißt "politischer Sprengstoff".

C1.def: buying and selling goods over the internet
C1.example: E-commerce has transformed retail.
C1.ielts_writing: Many small businesses moved to e-commerce during the pandemic.
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich; "brick-and-mortar" bezeichnet den stationären Handel.

C1.def: for example, from Latin "exempli gratia"
C1.example: Use tools, e.g. a hammer or a saw.
C1.ielts_writing: Many fruits, e.g. apples and oranges, are rich in vitamin C.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "i.e." (das heißt) verwechseln: "e.g." gibt Beispiele.

C1.def: wanting to do or have something very much
C1.example: The students were eager to learn.
C1.ielts_writing: Eager investors rushed to buy the new stock.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "eager TO do sth" oder "eager FOR sth"; "eager beaver" heißt Streber.

C1.def: a nobleman of high rank
C1.example: The Earl of Warwick owned the castle.
C1.ielts_writing: Earls were important figures in medieval politics.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "early" (früh) verwechseln; Aussprache /ɜːrl/ wie "Pearl".

C1.def: money earned from work or profits made by a company
C1.example: The company reported strong quarterly earnings.
C1.ielts_writing: Rising earnings often lead to higher share prices.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "earnings"; bei Firmen "earnings report" (Gewinnbericht).

C1.def: freedom from difficulty, or to reduce pain or pressure
C1.example: She completed the task with ease.
C1.ielts_writing: Medication can ease the pain.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I feel ill at ease in large crowds."
C1.mistake: "at ease" heißt "entspannt"; "ill at ease" bedeutet "unwohl".

C1.def: without difficulty, or by a large margin
C1.example: She solved the puzzle easily.
C1.ielts_writing: It is easily the best result of the year.
C1.mistake: Auch zur Verstärkung: "easily the best" heißt "mit Abstand der beste".

C1.def: a hard black wood, or a deep black color
C1.example: She had ebony hair.
C1.ielts_writing: Ebony is prized for its dense, dark wood.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The piano keys are made of ebony."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen auch Holz; "ebony" wird als Farbe literarisch benutzt.

C1.def: unconventional and slightly strange
C1.example: The scientist was known for his eccentric habits.
C1.ielts_writing: Eccentric behavior is often tolerated in talented artists.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; nicht negativ, eher "schrullig".

C1.def: to repeat or reflect a sound, or to repeat someone's opinion
C1.example: Her voice echoed in the empty hall.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics echoed his concerns about the new law.
C1.mistake: "echo chamber" bedeutet "Echokammer" in Medien; Plural "echoes".

C1.def: drawing from a wide range of sources
C1.example: He has an eclectic taste in music.
C1.ielts_writing: The library has an eclectic collection of books.
C1.mistake: Nicht "elektrisch" (electric); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: worry about the effects of climate change on the environment
C1.example: Many young people suffer from eco-anxiety.
C1.ielts_writing: Eco-anxiety is increasingly recognized as a mental health concern.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I feel eco-anxiety when I read the news."
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich; auch "climate anxiety" gebräuchlich.

C1.def: relating to ecosystems and the environment
C1.example: The oil spill caused an ecological disaster.
C1.ielts_writing: Ecological balance is essential for healthy ecosystems.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We take an ecological approach to farming."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "economical" (sparsam) verwechseln; Nomen "ecology".

C1.def: an unequal distribution of wealth or income
C1.example: Economic disparity between regions has widened.
C1.ielts_writing: Economic disparity can fuel social unrest.
C1.mistake: Meist Singular; "disparity BETWEEN groups".

C1.def: feeling overwhelming happiness
C1.example: She was ecstatic about the news.
C1.ielts_writing: Ecstatic fans greeted the team at the airport.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "ecstatic ABOUT sth"; Nomen "ecstasy" (auch Droge).

C1.def: a person who teaches or provides education
C1.example: Educators emphasize critical thinking.
C1.ielts_writing: Teachers and educators play a crucial role in child development.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She works as an educator at a museum."
C1.mistake: Wird oft als Oberbegriff für Lehrkräfte verwendet; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: the degree to which something produces a desired result
C1.example: The study assessed the effectiveness of the vaccine.
C1.ielts_writing: Effectiveness of teaching methods varies by context.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I doubt the effectiveness of this approach."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "effectiveness OF sth"; nicht mit "efficiency" gleichsetzen.

C1.def: the ability to do something well with little waste
C1.example: New machines improved efficiency.
C1.ielts_writing: Energy efficiency can lower household bills.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "effectiveness" verwechseln: efficiency = mit wenig Aufwand.

C1.def: a person's sense of self-importance
C1.example: His ego was hurt by the criticism.
C1.ielts_writing: A large ego can make teamwork difficult.
C1.mistake: Im Alltag eher "Selbstüberschätzung" als psychologisches Ich.

C1.def: detailed and complicated, or to explain in detail
C1.example: She wore an elaborate costume.
C1.ielts_writing: Could you elaborate on your last point?
C1.mistake: Betonung wechselt: Adjektiv -rət, Verb -reɪt; "elaborate ON sth" bedeutet "näher ausführen".

C1.def: older (especially within a family), or a respected older person
C1.example: My elder sister lives in Texas.
C1.ielts_writing: Elders in the community guide younger generations.
C1.mistake: "elder" nur attributiv und für Familienmitglieder, nicht "elder than".

C1.def: relating to elections
C1.example: The country is reforming its electoral system.
C1.ielts_writing: Electoral turnout was the highest in years.
C1.mistake: "Electoral College" ist das Wahlmännergremium in den USA; Nomen "electorate".

C1.def: graceful and stylish
C1.example: She wore an elegant dress.
C1.ielts_writing: The solution is elegant in its simplicity.
C1.mistake: Auch für Lösungen oder Beweise: "an elegant solution".

C1.def: to raise to a higher position or level
C1.example: The chef elevated simple ingredients into a masterpiece.
C1.ielts_writing: She was elevated to the rank of general.
C1.mistake: Nomen "elevation" (Höhe); "elevated" kann auch "erhöht" heißen ("elevated blood pressure").

C1.def: to draw out a reaction or information
C1.example: The question elicited a strong response.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers use surveys to elicit opinions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I couldn't elicit any information from him."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "illicit" (unerlaubt) verwechseln; Konstruktion: "elicit sth FROM sb".

C1.def: qualified to participate or be chosen
C1.example: You are eligible for a refund.
C1.ielts_writing: Only citizens are eligible to vote.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "eligible FOR sth" oder "eligible TO do sth"; Gegenteil: "ineligible".

C1.def: to remove something completely
C1.example: The team eliminated errors from the process.
C1.ielts_writing: Police eliminated three suspects from the inquiry.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We were eliminated in the second round."
C1.mistake: "process of elimination" bedeutet "Ausschlussverfahren"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: the best or most privileged group in society
C1.example: The elite enjoy considerable power.
C1.ielts_writing: Educational elites tend to reproduce their advantage.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /eɪˈliːt/ (nicht /ɪˈlaɪt/); Adjektiv "elitist" ist abwertend.

C1.def: speaking fluently and persuasively
C1.example: He gave an eloquent speech.
C1.ielts_writing: An eloquent speaker can inspire an audience.
C1.mistake: Nomen "eloquence"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: difficult to find, catch, or achieve
C1.example: The thief remained elusive.
C1.ielts_writing: Success proved elusive for the young team.
C1.mistake: Verb "elude" (entgehen); nicht mit "illusive" verwechseln.

C1.def: to begin a journey or a new venture
C1.example: They embarked on a long voyage.
C1.ielts_writing: Students embark on a career with high expectations.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "embark ON/UPON sth"; Gegenteil: "disembark".

C1.def: a feeling of shame or discomfort
C1.example: He blushed with embarrassment.
C1.ielts_writing: The scandal was a major embarrassment for the government.
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit "rr" und "ss": "embarrassment"; häufig falsch geschrieben.

C1.def: the offices of an ambassador in a foreign country
C1.example: He visited the US embassy to renew his passport.
C1.ielts_writing: Embassies provide assistance to citizens abroad.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "consulate" (Konsulat) verwechseln; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to fix firmly into a surface, or to include as an integral part
C1.example: The video is embedded in the web page.
C1.ielts_writing: Values are embedded in the school's culture.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The bullet was embedded in the wall."
C1.mistake: Auch "embedded journalist" (Journalist, der Truppen begleitet).

C1.def: to make something more attractive or interesting, often with added details
C1.example: He embellished the story with funny details.
C1.ielts_writing: Writers often embellish facts to create drama.
C1.mistake: Auch "übertreiben": "embellish the truth"; Nomen "embellishment".

C1.def: to represent an idea or quality in a clear form
C1.example: She embodies the spirit of the team.
C1.ielts_writing: The constitution embodies the nation's core values.
C1.mistake: Nomen "embodiment"; kein "to" nach dem Verb: "embody sth".

C1.def: an unborn offspring at an early stage of development
C1.example: The embryo develops in the womb.
C1.ielts_writing: Research on embryos raises ethical questions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Doctors examined the embryo under the microscope."
C1.mistake: Das "y" wird nicht gesprochen wie in "bryo"; Adjektiv "embryonic" (im Anfangsstadium).

C1.def: bright green, or a precious green gemstone
C1.example: She wore an emerald necklace.
C1.ielts_writing: The emerald hills of Ireland attract visitors.
C1.mistake: "Emerald Isle" ist ein Beiname für Irland.

C1.def: the process of coming into existence or becoming noticeable
C1.example: The emergence of social media changed communication.
C1.ielts_writing: The emergence of new variants complicates vaccination efforts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm curious about the emergence of this trend."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "emergency" (Notfall) verwechseln; Verb "emerge".

C1.def: to send out gas, light, or sound
C1.example: The factory emits harmful gases.
C1.ielts_writing: Cars emit carbon dioxide that contributes to climate change.
C1.mistake: Nomen "emission" (meist Plural: emissions); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a small digital image used to express emotion
C1.example: She ended her message with a smiling emoji.
C1.ielts_writing: Emojis can make written communication feel more personal.
C1.mistake: Plural "emojis" oder "emoji"; nicht dasselbe wie "emoticon" (Zeichenfolge wie :-)).

C1.def: a combination of characters representing a facial expression
C1.example: He added a smiley emoticon to the message.
C1.ielts_writing: Emoticons predate the emoji and rely on punctuation.
C1.mistake: Besteht aus Zeichen wie ":)" im Unterschied zum Bild-Symbol "emoji".

C1.def: based on observation or experience rather than theory
C1.example: The study provided empirical evidence.
C1.ielts_writing: Empirical research tests hypotheses through observation.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "theoretical"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe (-PIR-).

C1.def: a person who works for someone for pay
C1.example: The company has two hundred employees.
C1.ielts_writing: Employees are entitled to paid leave.
C1.mistake: Gegenstück: "employer"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-EE).

C1.def: a person or company that employs people
C1.example: The employer provides health insurance.
C1.ielts_writing: Large employers often offer training programs.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My employer is flexible about working hours."
C1.mistake: Gegenstück: "employee"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to give someone more control over their life or authority
C1.example: The program empowers women to start businesses.
C1.ielts_writing: Education empowers individuals to make informed choices.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I feel empowered when I take action."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "empower sb TO do sth"; Nomen "empowerment".

C1.def: to try to equal or surpass someone by imitation
C1.example: Young athletes try to emulate their heroes.
C1.ielts_writing: Companies emulate successful business models.
C1.mistake: Nicht "emulieren" im Sinn von "nachbilden" nur in der IT; sonst "nacheifern".

C1.def: to make a bill into law, or to act out
C1.example: Parliament enacted new legislation.
C1.ielts_writing: The actors enacted a scene from history.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The government enacted a ban on smoking."
C1.mistake: Nomen "enactment"; Konstruktion ohne Präposition: "enact a law".

C1.def: to convert information into a code
C1.example: Data is encoded before transmission.
C1.ielts_writing: The software encodes video into smaller files.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The message was encoded in secret symbols."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "decode"; im Gehirn auch "memory encoding".

C1.def: to include a wide range of things
C1.example: The course encompasses history and literature.
C1.ielts_writing: The term "sustainability" encompasses environmental, social, and economic aspects.
C1.mistake: Ohne Präposition: "encompass sth"; sehr formell.

C1.def: support or praise that gives someone confidence
C1.example: She needed words of encouragement.
C1.ielts_writing: Positive encouragement boosts students' confidence.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "a lot of encouragement"; Verb "encourage".

C1.def: giving hope or confidence
C1.example: The results are encouraging.
C1.ielts_writing: Encouraging signs suggest the economy is recovering.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's encouraging to see so many volunteers."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "discouraging"; "It is encouraging TO + Infinitiv".

C1.def: at risk of extinction
C1.example: The panda is an endangered species.
C1.ielts_writing: Endangered habitats require urgent protection.
C1.mistake: Nomen "endangerment"; Gegenteil: "thriving".

C1.def: an earnest attempt to achieve something
C1.example: It was a joint endeavor between two universities.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientific endeavor depends on curiosity and perseverance.
C1.mistake: Als Verb: "endeavor TO do sth" (sich bemühen); sehr formell.

C1.def: regularly found in a particular region or group
C1.example: Malaria is endemic in parts of Africa.
C1.ielts_writing: Corruption is endemic in some institutions.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The species is endemic to the island."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "endemic TO a region"; nicht mit "epidemic" (Epidemie) verwechseln.

C1.def: having or seeming to have no end
C1.example: The desert stretched endlessly before us.
C1.ielts_writing: Endless debates delayed the decision.
C1.mistake: Adverb "endlessly"; nicht mit "ending" verwechseln.

C1.def: to publicly declare support for someone or something
C1.example: The union endorsed the candidate.
C1.ielts_writing: Celebrities often endorse products for large fees.
C1.mistake: Auch "ein Scheck gegenzeichnen"; Nomen "endorsement".

C1.def: public support or approval
C1.example: The singer signed an endorsement deal with a sports brand.
C1.ielts_writing: Endorsement by a leading scientist lent credibility to the study.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I got her endorsement for the project."
C1.mistake: Auch Werbevertrag: "endorsement deal"; Verb "endorse".

C1.def: to suffer something painful over a long time, or to last
C1.example: They endured years of hardship.
C1.ielts_writing: Great works of literature endure for centuries.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I can't endure this noise any longer."
C1.mistake: Nomen "endurance" (Ausdauer); Adjektiv "enduring" (dauerhaft).

C1.def: to make people obey a law or rule
C1.example: Police enforce traffic laws.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments must enforce environmental regulations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The school strictly enforces its dress code."
C1.mistake: Nomen "enforcement"; "law enforcement" ist die Strafverfolgung.

C1.def: the act of making sure that laws or rules are obeyed
C1.example: Weak enforcement undermines the rule of law.
C1.ielts_writing: Law enforcement agencies cooperate across borders.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "enforcement OF sth"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: an agreement to marry, involvement in an activity, or an appointment
C1.example: They announced their engagement in June.
C1.ielts_writing: Employee engagement strongly influences productivity.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Verlobung, Beteiligung, Verpflichtung ("a prior engagement"); Verb "engage".

C1.def: charming, interesting, and attracting attention
C1.example: The author has an engaging style.
C1.ielts_writing: Engaging lessons help students stay focused.
C1.mistake: Verb "engage" (fesseln, einstellen); nicht mit "engaged" (verlobt) verwechseln.

C1.def: to cause a feeling or situation to exist
C1.example: Injustice engenders resentment.
C1.ielts_writing: Distrust engenders conflict between neighbors.
C1.mistake: Ohne Präposition: "engender sth"; selten und sehr formell.

C1.def: the application of science to design and build things
C1.example: She studied electrical engineering.
C1.ielts_writing: Civil engineering involves building roads and bridges.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-NEER-); unzählbar.

C1.def: a period of reason in 18th-century Europe, or spiritual insight
C1.example: The Enlightenment shaped modern ideas of liberty.
C1.ielts_writing: Thinkers of the Enlightenment promoted reason over tradition.
C1.mistake: Mit großem "E" für die Epoche: "the Enlightenment"; Verb "enlighten".

C1.def: to ask for information
C1.example: I called to inquire about the opening hours.
C1.ielts_writing: Journalists inquire into the causes of the accident.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She inquired whether the room was available."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inquire ABOUT sth" oder "inquire INTO sth" (untersuchen); Nomen "inquiry".

C1.def: to improve the quality or value of something
C1.example: Reading enriches your vocabulary.
C1.ielts_writing: Travel can enrich one's understanding of other cultures.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "enrich sth WITH sth"; Nomen "enrichment".

C1.def: to officially register for a course or institution
C1.example: She enrolled in a design course.
C1.ielts_writing: Over five thousand students enroll each year.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I enrolled my son in a swimming class."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "enroll IN a course" oder "enroll AT a school"; Nomen "enrollment".

C1.def: to happen afterward as a result
C1.example: A heated argument ensued.
C1.ielts_writing: Chaos ensued after the announcement.
C1.mistake: Meist im Präteritum und ohne Objekt: "chaos ensued"; Adjektiv "ensuing".

C1.def: a business or a bold project, or initiative
C1.example: The family runs a small enterprise.
C1.ielts_writing: Private enterprise drives innovation.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Nomen "entrepreneur" (Unternehmer).

C1.def: a person who is very interested in a particular activity
C1.example: He's a film enthusiast.
C1.ielts_writing: Car enthusiasts gather at the annual show.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Nomen "enthusiasm".

C1.def: to give someone a right or a name
C1.example: You are entitled to a refund.
C1.ielts_writing: The book is entitled "A Short History of Time."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "be entitled TO sth"; Nomen "entitlement" (Anspruch).

C1.def: something that exists as a separate unit
C1.example: The company is a separate legal entity.
C1.ielts_writing: A government is a distinct political entity.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt as if I was an entity apart."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; "legal entity" bedeutet "juristische Person".

C1.def: a group of people who accompany a famous person
C1.example: The singer arrived with a large entourage.
C1.ielts_writing: A president's entourage includes security and advisers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She travels with an entourage of assistants."
C1.mistake: Aussprache französisch: /ˌɑːntʊˈrɑːʒ/; Betonung auf der letzten Silbe.

C1.def: the main course of a meal
C1.example: I ordered the steak as my entree.
C1.ielts_writing: Entrees are typically served after appetizers.
C1.mistake: "entree" heißt Hauptgericht, nicht Vorspeise; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a protein that speeds up chemical reactions
C1.example: Enzymes help digest food.
C1.ielts_writing: Enzyme activity depends on temperature and acidity.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Plural "enzymes".

C1.def: a long poem about heroes, or a grand film or story
C1.example: The Odyssey is an ancient epic.
C1.ielts_writing: The film is an epic of love and war.
C1.mistake: Im Slang "epic" für "großartig"; Nomen "epic" (Epos), Adjektiv "epic".

C1.def: a widespread outbreak of an infectious disease
C1.example: A flu epidemic swept the city.
C1.ielts_writing: Obesity has been described as an epidemic in many countries.
C1.mistake: Größer als "outbreak", kleiner als "pandemic"; auch bildlich: "an epidemic of crime".

C1.def: the state of being equal in rights and status
C1.example: The law promotes gender equality.
C1.ielts_writing: Equality before the law is a basic principle of democracy.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "inequality"; Präposition: "equality BETWEEN" oder "equality OF".

C1.def: a mathematical statement that two expressions are equal
C1.example: Solve the equation for x.
C1.ielts_writing: The equation describes the relationship between mass and energy.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "factor into the equation"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a state of balance between forces
C1.example: The market reached equilibrium.
C1.ielts_writing: Chemical equilibrium occurs when reaction rates are equal.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I lost my equilibrium on the ice."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-LIB-); Plural "equilibria".

C1.def: the value of ownership in a company or property, or fairness
C1.example: He invested in private equity.
C1.ielts_writing: Equity in education should be a national priority.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They sold their equity in the home."
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Finanzen und Fairness; Adjektiv "equitable".

C1.def: to build something, or standing upright
C1.example: They erected a monument to the heroes.
C1.ielts_writing: The tent was erected in minutes.
C1.mistake: Auch Adjektiv "erect" (aufrecht); Nomen "erection" kann missverständlich sein.

C1.def: to wear away gradually, or to weaken slowly
C1.example: The river eroded the soil.
C1.ielts_writing: Trust in institutions is eroding.
C1.mistake: Nomen "erosion"; bildlich "erode support".

C1.def: to increase in intensity
C1.example: The conflict escalated quickly.
C1.ielts_writing: Tensions escalated after the incident.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "de-escalate"; Nomen "escalation".

C1.def: a moving staircase
C1.example: We took the escalator to the second floor.
C1.ielts_writing: Escalators carry thousands of shoppers daily.
C1.mistake: Auf der Rolltreppe: "on the escalator"; nicht mit "elevator" (Aufzug) verwechseln.

C1.def: the central quality of something
C1.example: The essence of the argument is simple.
C1.ielts_writing: Time is of the essence in an emergency.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She captured the essence of the city in her photographs."
C1.mistake: "in essence" bedeutet "im Kern"; "of the essence" heißt "von entscheidender Bedeutung".

C1.def: the act of creating something, or the ruling group in society
C1.example: The establishment of the museum took three years.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics accused the establishment of ignoring ordinary citizens.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Gründung und etablierte Machtstruktur ("the Establishment").

C1.def: the wide mouth of a river where it meets the sea
C1.example: The estuary is rich in birdlife.
C1.ielts_writing: Estuaries are important nursery areas for fish.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Plural "estuaries".

C1.def: lasting forever, without end
C1.example: They pledged eternal love.
C1.ielts_writing: Philosophers have long debated eternal truths.
C1.mistake: Auch umgangssprachlich: "an eternal wait" für "ewiges Warten".

C1.def: infinite time, or a very long time
C1.example: The wait felt like an eternity.
C1.ielts_writing: Many religions promise life after death in eternity.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It took an eternity to get served."
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich: "an eternity" für "eine gefühlte Ewigkeit".

C1.def: membership in a group with shared culture and ancestry
C1.example: Forms often ask for your ethnicity.
C1.ielts_writing: Ethnicity and nationality are not the same thing.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "race" oder "nationality" gleichsetzen; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a mild expression used instead of one that is harsh
C1.example: "Passed away" is a euphemism for "died."
C1.ielts_writing: Euphemisms soften unpleasant realities.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He used a euphemism to avoid offending anyone."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "euphemism FOR sth"; Adjektiv "euphemistic".

C1.def: to move people away from a dangerous place
C1.example: Residents were evacuated before the flood.
C1.ielts_writing: The building was evacuated after the fire alarm.
C1.mistake: Nomen "evacuation"; Person: "evacuee".

C1.def: the removal of people from a dangerous place
C1.example: The evacuation was orderly and calm.
C1.ielts_writing: Evacuation plans should be tested regularly.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der vierten Silbe (-AY-); Plural "evacuations".

C1.def: to turn from liquid to vapor, or to disappear
C1.example: Water evaporates in the sun.
C1.ielts_writing: Hopes of a quick deal evaporated.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "evaporate" heißt "sich in Luft auflösen"; Nomen "evaporation".

C1.def: full of notable events
C1.example: It was an eventful year for the company.
C1.ielts_writing: The eventful journey lasted three months.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "uneventful"; "eventful" ist immer positiv oder neutral beschreibend.

C1.def: happening at the end of a process
C1.example: The eventual winner received a trophy.
C1.ielts_writing: The eventual outcome was uncertain.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm sure the eventual result will be positive."
C1.mistake: Nicht "eventuell" (possibly); "eventual" heißt "schließlich eintretend".

C1.def: to bring a feeling or memory to mind
C1.example: The smell evoked memories of childhood.
C1.ielts_writing: The poem evokes the beauty of the countryside.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "evocative" (stimmungsvoll); nicht "provoke" (provozieren).

C1.def: gradual development, especially of living things
C1.example: The theory of evolution explains biodiversity.
C1.ielts_writing: The evolution of technology has accelerated in recent decades.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I've noticed a gradual evolution in his style."
C1.mistake: Verb "evolve"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-LOO-).

C1.def: relating to evolution
C1.example: Evolutionary biology studies how species change.
C1.ielts_writing: An evolutionary approach to reform avoids sudden disruption.
C1.mistake: Nicht "revolutionary" (revolutionär) verwechseln: evolutionary = schrittweise.

C1.def: to describe something as larger or better than it is
C1.example: He tends to exaggerate his achievements.
C1.ielts_writing: Media reports exaggerated the scale of the problem.
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit Doppel-"g" im Wort "exaggerate"; nicht "exagerate".

C1.def: the quality of being outstanding
C1.example: The school is known for academic excellence.
C1.ielts_writing: Excellence requires consistent effort.
C1.mistake: Verb "excel" (sich auszeichnen); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: unusually good, or rare
C1.example: She showed exceptional talent.
C1.ielts_writing: Only in exceptional circumstances will the rule be waived.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "exceptionell" im Deutschen gleichsetzen; Nomen "exception".

C1.def: an amount greater than needed
C1.example: Excess baggage costs extra.
C1.ielts_writing: An excess of nutrients can harm lakes.
C1.mistake: "in excess OF" heißt "über ... hinaus"; "to excess" bedeutet "im Übermaß".

C1.def: the act of not allowing someone to take part
C1.example: Social exclusion affects many young people.
C1.ielts_writing: The exclusion of minorities from decision-making erodes legitimacy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt a sense of exclusion at school."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "exclusion FROM sth"; Gegenteil: "inclusion".

C1.def: available only to a select group, or not shared
C1.example: It's an exclusive club for members only.
C1.ielts_writing: The newspaper secured an exclusive interview.
C1.mistake: "mutually exclusive" bedeutet "sich gegenseitig ausschließend".

C1.def: only, and not including anything else
C1.example: The shop sells exclusively organic food.
C1.ielts_writing: The service is exclusively for members.
C1.mistake: Nicht verwechseln mit "exklusiv" im Sinn von "luxuriös"; hier "nur".

C1.def: to carry out a plan or order, or to put someone to death
C1.example: The team executed the plan flawlessly.
C1.ielts_writing: The prisoner was executed in 1990.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; zwei Bedeutungen: ausführen und hinrichten.

C1.def: the carrying out of a plan, or the putting to death of a person
C1.example: The execution of the project was flawless.
C1.ielts_writing: The execution drew widespread protests.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The execution of the dance was impressive."
C1.mistake: "stay of execution" heißt "Aufschub der Vollstreckung"; nicht mit "Exekution" verwechseln.

C1.def: to apply force, influence, or effort
C1.example: The sun exerts a strong gravitational pull.
C1.ielts_writing: Parents exert considerable influence on children's choices.
C1.mistake: "exert yourself" bedeutet "sich anstrengen"; Nomen "exertion" (Anstrengung).

C1.def: to breathe out
C1.example: She exhaled slowly.
C1.ielts_writing: Plants absorb carbon dioxide and exhale oxygen.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "inhale"; das "h" bleibt stumm.

C1.def: forced absence from one's country
C1.example: The poet lived in exile for twenty years.
C1.ielts_writing: The king was exiled after the revolution.
C1.mistake: "in exile" ohne Artikel; Verb "exile sb" (verbannen).

C1.def: a planet outside our solar system
C1.example: Astronomers discovered a new exoplanet.
C1.ielts_writing: Thousands of exoplanets have been detected by telescopes.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I read about an exoplanet that may support life."
C1.mistake: Plural "exoplanets"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: attractively unusual, especially from another country
C1.example: We ate exotic fruit at the market.
C1.ielts_writing: Exotic species can threaten native wildlife.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; "exotic" kann bei Menschen unangenehm klingen.

C1.def: a journey made for a purpose such as exploration
C1.example: The expedition reached the summit in five days.
C1.ielts_writing: Polar expeditions require careful planning.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "expedition TO + Ort"; "fishing expedition" kann auch "Suche nach Belastendem" heißen.

C1.def: to force someone to leave an institution or country
C1.example: The student was expelled from school.
C1.ielts_writing: The country expelled several foreign diplomats.
C1.mistake: Nomen "expulsion"; Konstruktion: "expel sb FROM sth".

C1.def: the amount of money spent
C1.example: Government expenditure rose sharply.
C1.ielts_writing: Capital expenditure on infrastructure boosts growth.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "expenditure ON sth"; Gegenteil: "income".

C1.def: based on trying new methods or ideas
C1.example: The drug is still at the experimental stage.
C1.ielts_writing: Experimental music challenges traditional forms.
C1.mistake: Nomen "experiment"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe (-MEN-).

C1.def: to come to an end, or to become invalid
C1.example: My passport expires next month.
C1.ielts_writing: The contract expires at the end of the year.
C1.mistake: Nomen "expiration" (Ablauf); "expiration date" ist das Verfallsdatum.

C1.def: stated clearly and in detail
C1.example: She gave explicit instructions.
C1.ielts_writing: The report is explicit about the risks.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "implicit"; "explicit content" bedeutet auch "nicht jugendfrei".

C1.def: in a clear and detailed way
C1.example: The contract explicitly forbids subletting.
C1.ielts_writing: He explicitly asked not to be disturbed.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "implicitly"; steht oft vor Verben wie "state, mention, forbid".

C1.def: unfair treatment for profit, or the use of resources
C1.example: Labor exploitation remains a global problem.
C1.ielts_writing: Exploitation of natural resources must be sustainable.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Ausbeutung und wirtschaftliche Nutzung; Verb "exploit".

C1.def: likely to explode, or very sudden and intense
C1.example: The situation is explosive.
C1.ielts_writing: Explosive growth strained the city's infrastructure.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen: "explosives" (Sprengstoffe); "explosive growth" bedeutet "sprunghaftes Wachstum".

C1.def: to show a feeling or opinion, or fast and direct
C1.example: She expressed her gratitude.
C1.ielts_writing: Express trains skip small stations.
C1.mistake: Auch "express delivery" (Eilzustellung); "express yourself" heißt "sich ausdrücken".

C1.def: extremely beautiful and delicate
C1.example: The lace was exquisite.
C1.ielts_writing: The restaurant serves exquisite cuisine.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe: EX-qui-site.

C1.def: the act of extending, or a phone line in an office
C1.example: We built an extension on the house.
C1.ielts_writing: She requested an extension on the deadline.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Anbau, Fristverlängerung, Telefonnebenstelle; Verb "extend".

C1.def: on the outside, or the outer part of something
C1.example: The exterior walls were painted white.
C1.ielts_writing: The exterior of the building appeared unchanged.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "interior"; auch Nomen "the exterior".

C1.def: a substance taken from something, or a short piece from a text
C1.example: The recipe calls for vanilla extract.
C1.ielts_writing: The company extracts oil from the seabed.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She read an extract from the novel."
C1.mistake: Betonung wechselt: Nomen EXtract, Verb exTRACT.

C1.def: activities outside the regular curriculum
C1.example: She does many extracurricular activities.
C1.ielts_writing: Extracurricular activities build leadership skills.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "extracurricular activities"; auch "extracurriculars".

C1.def: spending more than necessary, or excessive
C1.example: He leads an extravagant lifestyle.
C1.ielts_writing: Extravagant claims require strong evidence.
C1.mistake: Nomen "extravagance"; betont auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: very great, or at the furthest limit
C1.example: They live in extreme poverty.
C1.ielts_writing: Extreme weather events are becoming more frequent.
C1.mistake: Adverb "extremely"; "in the extreme" bedeutet "äußerst".

C1.def: sports involving a high degree of risk
C1.example: Extreme sports attract thrill seekers.
C1.ielts_writing: Extreme sports have grown in popularity among young adults.
C1.mistake: Plural "extreme sports"; Beispiel: Fallschirmspringen.

C1.def: the holding of radical political views
C1.example: The government fights extremism.
C1.ielts_writing: Online platforms have become a breeding ground for extremism.
C1.mistake: Nomen "extremist" für die Person; unzählbar.

C1.def: a person with radical views, especially in politics or religion
C1.example: The extremist group claimed responsibility.
C1.ielts_writing: Extremists often exploit economic hardship.
C1.mistake: Plural "extremists"; Adjektiv "extremist" (extremistisch).

C1.def: a short story that teaches a moral lesson
C1.example: Aesop's fable teaches the value of patience.
C1.ielts_writing: Fables often feature animals with human traits.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "fabel" im Deutschen als Märchen gleichsetzen; "fabled" bedeutet "legendär".

C1.def: to make a process easier
C1.example: The software facilitates communication.
C1.ielts_writing: Teachers facilitate discussion among students.
C1.mistake: Nomen "facilitator" (Moderator); nicht "erleichtern" im emotionalen Sinn.

C1.def: a small organized group within a larger one
C1.example: Rival factions fought for control.
C1.ielts_writing: Party factions disagreed on the budget.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There are two factions in our department."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "fraction" (Bruchteil) verwechseln; Adjektiv "factional".

C1.def: a circumstance that contributes to a result
C1.example: Weather is a factor in the outcome.
C1.ielts_writing: Risk factors for disease include age and lifestyle.
C1.mistake: Mathematisch "factor" (Teiler); Konstruktion: "a factor IN sth".

C1.def: a department of a university, its staff, or a mental ability
C1.example: She is a member of the faculty.
C1.ielts_writing: The faculty of law is highly ranked.
C1.mistake: Im US-Bereich auch: Lehrpersonal einer Hochschule; nicht nur "Fakultät".

C1.def: to lose color, strength, or brightness gradually
C1.example: The curtains faded in the sun.
C1.ielts_writing: Public interest in the scandal began to fade.
C1.mistake: "fade away" bedeutet "allmählich verschwinden"; "fade out" für Musik oder Film.

C1.def: the act of failing a test, or to be unsuccessful
C1.example: He got a fail on the exam.
C1.ielts_writing: Businesses that fail to adapt may close.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "fail TO do sth"; Nomen meist "failure"; "an epic fail" ist Umgangssprache.

C1.def: to lose consciousness briefly, or weak and barely noticeable
C1.example: She fainted in the heat.
C1.ielts_writing: A faint smell of smoke lingered.
C1.mistake: "faint" ist auch Adjektiv: "a faint noise" (leises Geräusch).

C1.def: the quality of treating people equally and justly
C1.example: Everyone expects fairness in the workplace.
C1.ielts_writing: Fairness in sentencing is a key concern for legal reformers.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Präposition: "fairness TO sb" oder "fairness IN sth".

C1.def: loyal and trustworthy, or accurate
C1.example: He was a faithful friend.
C1.ielts_writing: The film is a faithful adaptation of the book.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "unfaithful"; "Yours faithfully" ist eine formelle Briefschlussformel.

C1.def: a bird of prey with narrow wings
C1.example: A falcon circled above us.
C1.ielts_writing: Falcons are known for their speed in flight.
C1.mistake: Das "l" wird in /ˈfɔːlkən/ gesprochen oder stumm; beides üblich.

C1.def: the act of dropping, the season after summer, or a decline
C1.example: The fall in prices helped consumers.
C1.ielts_writing: The fall of the empire changed history.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Herbst und Sturz; Verb unregelmäßig: fall, fell, fallen.

C1.def: to begin to love someone
C1.example: They fell in love at first sight.
C1.ielts_writing: Many couples fall in love during university.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I fell in love with the city."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "fall in love WITH sb"; nicht "fall in love to".

C1.def: to have an argument, or to leave a position
C1.example: They fell out over money.
C1.ielts_writing: Several players fell out of the team.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Friends sometimes fall out over silly things."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "fall out WITH sb OVER sth"; Nomen "falling-out" (Streit).

C1.def: the patterns of relationships within a family
C1.example: Family dynamics shape a child's development.
C1.ielts_writing: Complex family dynamics can affect adult relationships.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "family dynamics" mit Pluralverb.

C1.def: extreme scarcity of food
C1.example: A severe famine struck the region.
C1.ielts_writing: Famine often follows prolonged drought and conflict.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The Great Famine killed millions in Ireland."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "famished" (ausgehungert); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: an authoritarian nationalist ideology
C1.example: The rise of fascism devastated Europe.
C1.ielts_writing: Historians study the conditions that enabled fascism.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We learned about fascism in history class."
C1.mistake: Person: "fascist"; Aussprache /ˈfæʃɪzəm/ mit "sch".

C1.def: something that holds things together, such as a zipper
C1.example: The bag has a metal fastener.
C1.ielts_writing: Fasteners such as screws and bolts are essential in construction.
C1.mistake: Das "t" wird nicht gesprochen: /ˈfæsnər/; Verb "fasten".

C1.def: very careful about details or cleanliness
C1.example: He is fastidious about his appearance.
C1.ielts_writing: A fastidious editor checks every comma.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "fastidious ABOUT sth"; kann abwertend "übergenau" wirken.

C1.def: causing death, or having disastrous results
C1.example: The accident was fatal.
C1.ielts_writing: A fatal error crashed the system.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It was a fatal mistake to trust him."
C1.mistake: Nomen "fatality" (Todesopfer); "fatal" auch "verhängnisvoll" ohne Tod.

C1.def: the power that is believed to control events
C1.example: Fate brought them together.
C1.ielts_writing: The fate of the project depends on funding.
C1.mistake: "tempt fate" heißt "das Schicksal herausfordern"; Adjektiv "fateful" (folgenschwer).

C1.def: a male parent, or a priest
C1.example: He became a father last year.
C1.ielts_writing: The father of modern physics is often considered to be Newton.
C1.mistake: "founding fathers" sind die Gründerväter der USA; als Verb "father a child" (zeugen).

C1.def: extreme tiredness
C1.example: Fatigue made it hard to concentrate.
C1.ielts_writing: Metal fatigue can cause structural failures.
C1.mistake: Das "gue" wird /ɡ/ gesprochen; "metal fatigue" ist Materialermüdung.

C1.def: responsibility for a mistake, or a defect
C1.example: It's not your fault.
C1.ielts_writing: A technical fault delayed the train.
C1.mistake: "at fault" heißt "schuld"; "find fault with" bedeutet "etwas bemängeln".

C1.def: showing approval, or advantageous
C1.example: The reviews were favorable.
C1.ielts_writing: Favorable weather conditions boosted the harvest.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "unfavorable"; Präposition: "favorable TO/FOR sth".

C1.def: in a way that shows approval
C1.example: She was favorably impressed.
C1.ielts_writing: The plan was favorably received by the committee.
C1.mistake: "compare favorably with sth" bedeutet "den Vergleich bestehen".

C1.def: a machine or message sent via telephone lines
C1.example: Please send the contract by fax.
C1.ielts_writing: Fax machines were once common in every office.
C1.mistake: Heute veraltet; als Verb "to fax sth TO sb".

C1.def: a US federal agency for domestic security and investigations
C1.example: The FBI is investigating the case.
C1.ielts_writing: The FBI works with local police to track suspects.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He joined the FBI after law school."
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "Federal Bureau of Investigation"; als Buchstaben gesprochen.

C1.def: to be afraid of something
C1.example: Many people fear spiders.
C1.ielts_writing: Experts fear that the outbreak could spread.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "fear FOR sb" (sich Sorgen machen um) oder "fear sth".

C1.def: possible to do easily or conveniently
C1.example: The plan is technically feasible.
C1.ielts_writing: A feasible solution must be both affordable and effective.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Is it feasible to finish by Friday?"
C1.mistake: Nomen "feasibility"; "feasibility study" ist eine Machbarkeitsstudie.

C1.def: a large elaborate meal, or to eat with enjoyment
C1.example: The wedding feast lasted all night.
C1.ielts_writing: The festival is a feast for the senses.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "fast" (Fasten); "feast on" bedeutet "schlemmen".

C1.def: a full-length film intended as the main item in a cinema
C1.example: The director's first feature film premiered at Cannes.
C1.ielts_writing: Feature films usually run between ninety and one hundred twenty minutes.
C1.mistake: Unterscheidet sich von "short film"; Plural "feature films".

C1.def: a system in which power is shared between central and regional governments
C1.example: Federalism divides authority between levels of government.
C1.ielts_writing: Debates over federalism shape American politics.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "federal"; Gegenteil: "unitary system".

C1.def: used to give permission or encourage someone to do something
C1.example: Feel free to ask any questions.
C1.ielts_writing: Participants should feel free to share their opinions.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "feel free TO + Infinitiv"; höfliche Aufforderung.

C1.def: a pen with a tip made of felt
C1.example: She drew a picture with a felt tip.
C1.ielts_writing: Felt tips are popular among children.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I bought a pack of felt tips."
C1.mistake: Auch "felt-tip pen" mit Bindestrich; Plural "felt tips".

C1.def: having qualities traditionally associated with women
C1.example: The room had a feminine touch.
C1.ielts_writing: Gender roles define what is considered masculine or feminine.
C1.mistake: Nicht dasselbe wie "female" (biologisch); Nomen "femininity".

C1.def: supporting equal rights for women
C1.example: She wrote a feminist novel.
C1.ielts_writing: Feminist theory examines the role of gender in society.
C1.mistake: Nomen "feminism"; als Person "a feminist".

C1.def: a plant with an aromatic bulb and feathery leaves
C1.example: She roasted fennel with olive oil.
C1.ielts_writing: Fennel seeds are used to flavor sausages and breads.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "fennel seeds" sind Fenchelsamen.

C1.def: able to produce crops or offspring
C1.example: The valley has fertile soil.
C1.ielts_writing: Fertile ground for new ideas exists in universities.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "infertile"; bildlich: "a fertile imagination" (rege Fantasie).

C1.def: having or showing intense belief or enthusiasm
C1.example: He is a fervent supporter of the team.
C1.ielts_writing: Fervent prayers filled the church.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She has a fervent wish for peace."
C1.mistake: Nomen "fervor"; selten im Alltag, eher gehoben.

C1.def: relating to a celebration
C1.example: The town has a festive atmosphere.
C1.ielts_writing: Festive decorations brightened the streets.
C1.mistake: Nomen "festivities" (Festlichkeiten); "festive season" meint Weihnachtszeit.

C1.def: having a fever, or restless and excited
C1.example: The child was feverish and weak.
C1.ielts_writing: Feverish activity surrounded the opening of the exhibition.
C1.mistake: Bei Aktivitäten: "feverish" bedeutet "hektisch"; Nomen "fever".

C1.def: a substance in food that aids digestion, or a thread-like material
C1.example: Whole grains are rich in fiber.
C1.ielts_writing: Fiber optic cables transmit data at high speed.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need more fiber in my diet."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar bei Ernährung; "fiber optic" heißt Glasfaser.

C1.def: an opportunity to do something with great success, or a day of outdoor sports at school
C1.example: The press had a field day with the scandal.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics had a field day after the failed launch.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The kids loved field day at school."
C1.mistake: Redewendung: "have a field day" bedeutet "sich genüsslich austoben".

C1.def: an educational outing to a place outside school
C1.example: The class went on a field trip to the museum.
C1.ielts_writing: Field trips enhance learning by providing hands-on experience.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "go on a field trip TO + Ort".

C1.def: violent or intense
C1.example: The lion is a fierce predator.
C1.ielts_writing: Fierce competition drove prices down.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She has a fierce loyalty to her friends."
C1.mistake: Aussprache /fɪrs/, nicht "fiers"; Adverb "fiercely".

C1.def: to settle a dispute by fighting or arguing
C1.example: They had to fight it out in court.
C1.ielts_writing: The rival parties fought out the dispute in public.
C1.mistake: Meist mit Objekt: "fight it out"; Partizip "fought out".

C1.def: a piece of office furniture for storing documents
C1.example: She put the folder in the file cabinet.
C1.ielts_writing: A file cabinet keeps documents organized and secure.
C1.mistake: Plural "file cabinets"; im Büro oft auch "filing cabinet".

C1.def: a person who makes films
C1.example: The film-maker won a prize at the festival.
C1.ielts_writing: Independent film-makers often struggle for funding.
C1.mistake: Auch "filmmaker" zusammengeschrieben; Nomen "film-making".

C1.def: a device that removes unwanted material, or to remove impurities
C1.example: Use a coffee filter.
C1.ielts_writing: The app lets you filter results by price.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We filter the water before drinking it."
C1.mistake: "filter out" bedeutet "aussortieren"; Nomen "filtration".

C1.def: to discover something or judge it to be true
C1.example: I found my keys under the sofa.
C1.ielts_writing: The court found him guilty.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: find, found, found; "find out" bedeutet "herausfinden".

C1.def: the result of an investigation
C1.example: The key finding was surprising.
C1.ielts_writing: Research findings suggest a link between sleep and memory.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "findings"; nicht "Fund" im Sinn von Fundstück.

C1.def: money paid as a punishment
C1.example: She got a parking fine.
C1.ielts_writing: The company was fined five million dollars.
C1.mistake: Auch Adjektiv "fine" (fein, gut); Konstruktion: "fine sb FOR sth".

C1.def: to touch or handle something with the fingers, or to point out someone
C1.example: He fingered the old coin curiously.
C1.ielts_writing: Police fingered him as the main suspect.
C1.mistake: Als Verb weniger üblich; "finger sb" heißt "jemanden verpfeifen" (Slang).

C1.def: a mark left by the ridges of a finger
C1.example: Police found a fingerprint at the scene.
C1.ielts_writing: Fingerprint analysis helped solve the case.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I left a fingerprint on the glass."
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "digital fingerprint" (digitaler Fingerabdruck).

C1.def: the end of a finger
C1.example: He touched the screen with his fingertip.
C1.ielts_writing: Fingertip sensitivity is essential for surgeons.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt a tingle in my fingertips."
C1.mistake: "at your fingertips" bedeutet "griffbereit".

C1.def: the end of something, or the surface appearance of a product
C1.example: The race had an exciting finish.
C1.ielts_writing: The furniture has a glossy finish.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "finish doing sth", nicht "finish to do".

C1.def: the head of a fire department
C1.example: The fire chief praised the crew.
C1.ielts_writing: The fire chief explained the new safety rules.
C1.mistake: Kurzform "chief"; Feuerwehr: "fire department".

C1.def: a gun that can be carried and used by one person
C1.example: He was charged with possessing an unlicensed firearm.
C1.ielts_writing: Strict regulations govern the sale of firearms.
C1.mistake: Plural "firearms"; formeller Ausdruck für "gun".

C1.def: written or told from the perspective of "I"
C1.example: The novel uses a first-person narrator.
C1.ielts_writing: First-person narratives create a sense of intimacy.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "third-person"; auch "first-person shooter" (Videospielgenre).

C1.def: a small breaded piece of fish
C1.example: The kids love fish sticks with ketchup.
C1.ielts_writing: Fish sticks are an easy frozen meal.
C1.mistake: Plural "fish sticks"; meist tiefgekühlt.

C1.def: a closed hand with the fingers bent
C1.example: He clenched his fist in anger.
C1.ielts_writing: The protesters raised their fists in the air.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She slammed her fist on the table."
C1.mistake: Redewendung: "with an iron fist" heißt "mit eiserner Hand".

C1.def: a sudden attack, a good match, or to be the right size
C1.example: She had a coughing fit.
C1.ielts_writing: The shirt fits perfectly.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He threw a fit when he lost."
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig im US-Englisch: fit, fit, fit; "fit in" bedeutet "dazupassen".

C1.def: popular new approaches to exercise and wellness
C1.example: Fitness trends change every few years.
C1.ielts_writing: Wearable devices are among the latest fitness trends.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural: "fitness trends"; nicht mit "fitness" im Sinn von Gesundheitszustand gleichsetzen.

C1.def: made to fit exactly, or installed permanently
C1.example: They bought fitted wardrobes.
C1.ielts_writing: A fitted sheet stays in place on the mattress.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: eng anliegend ("fitted dress") und fest eingebaut ("fitted wardrobe").

C1.def: something permanently attached to a building, or a scheduled event
C1.example: The bathroom fixtures were replaced.
C1.ielts_writing: The annual festival has become a regular fixture in the town's calendar.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's a fixture at the local pub."
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "a fixture" für etwas Dauerhaftes; "fixture" im Sport ist ein Spieltermin.

C1.def: to mark something for attention, or a piece of cloth with a design
C1.example: The system flagged the transaction as suspicious.
C1.ielts_writing: Several countries lowered their flags to half-mast.
C1.mistake: "flag down" bedeutet "anhalten (Taxi)"; "red flag" heißt "Warnsignal".

C1.def: a small portable device for storing data
C1.example: Save the file on a flash drive.
C1.ielts_writing: Flash drives have largely replaced floppy disks.
C1.mistake: Auch "thumb drive" oder "USB stick"; nicht "memory stick" für Sony-Produkte.

C1.def: a mistake or imperfection
C1.example: The report contained a serious flaw.
C1.ielts_writing: A fatal flaw in the design caused the collapse.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "flawed" (fehlerhaft), "flawless" (makellos); nicht "flow" verwechseln.

C1.def: having a mistake or weakness
C1.example: The study was fundamentally flawed.
C1.ielts_writing: Flawed logic leads to false conclusions.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "flawless"; Aussprache /flɔːd/ wie "flawed" ≈ "floored".

C1.def: to run away from danger
C1.example: Thousands of people had to flee the war.
C1.ielts_writing: The suspect fled the scene.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: flee, fled, fled; nicht mit "fly" verwechseln.

C1.def: a group of ships, or a group of vehicles
C1.example: The fleet left the harbor at dawn.
C1.ielts_writing: The company manages a fleet of delivery vans.
C1.mistake: Auch Adjektiv: "fleet of foot" (flink); Plural "fleets".

C1.def: the soft substance of a body, or the pulp of fruit
C1.example: The knife cut deep into his flesh.
C1.ielts_writing: The film explores the conflict between spirit and flesh.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Fleisch" als Speise (das heißt "meat"); "in the flesh" bedeutet "persönlich".

C1.def: the ability to change or adapt easily
C1.example: The job offers flexibility in working hours.
C1.ielts_writing: Flexibility is key to coping with change.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I appreciate the flexibility of remote work."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "flexible"; Präposition: "flexibility IN sth".

C1.def: a group of birds or sheep, or a congregation
C1.example: A flock of birds flew overhead.
C1.ielts_writing: The pastor addressed his flock.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "flock TO" (strömen); "birds of a feather flock together" ist ein Sprichwort.

C1.def: a powerful lamp used to light large outdoor areas
C1.example: The stadium was lit by floodlights.
C1.ielts_writing: Floodlights allow evening matches to be played.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We installed a floodlight in the yard."
C1.mistake: Als Verb "floodlight sth" (anstrahlen); Plural "floodlights".

C1.def: material used for covering floors
C1.example: We chose wooden flooring for the living room.
C1.ielts_writing: Laminate flooring is a cheaper alternative to hardwood.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some flooring"; nicht "floors".

C1.def: a person who sells and arranges flowers
C1.example: The florist arranged a bouquet of roses.
C1.ielts_writing: Florists often work long hours before holidays.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Geschäft: "flower shop" oder "florist".

C1.def: to grow or develop successfully
C1.example: Small businesses flourish in supportive environments.
C1.ielts_writing: Art and culture flourished during the Renaissance.
C1.mistake: Nomen "flourish" (Schnörkel, schwungvolle Bewegung); Aussprache /ˈflɜːrɪʃ/.

C1.def: a steady, continuous movement, or to move steadily
C1.example: The flow of traffic slowed.
C1.ielts_writing: Conversations flow more easily when people are relaxed.
C1.mistake: "go with the flow" bedeutet "sich treiben lassen"; "cash flow" ist der Geldfluss.

C1.def: the art of arranging cut flowers
C1.example: She took a class in flower arranging.
C1.ielts_writing: Flower arranging is a traditional art in Japan.
C1.mistake: Im Japanischen "ikebana"; unzählbar.

C1.def: to rise and fall irregularly
C1.example: Prices fluctuate throughout the year.
C1.ielts_writing: Body temperature can fluctuate during illness.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "fluctuate BETWEEN A and B"; Nomen "fluctuation".

C1.def: a substance that flows, such as a liquid or gas
C1.example: Drink plenty of fluids.
C1.ielts_writing: Fluid dynamics describes how liquids and gases move.
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv auch "unklar, im Wandel": "a fluid situation".

C1.def: to be very successful
C1.example: She's flying high after the promotion.
C1.ielts_writing: Young entrepreneurs are flying high after the product launch.
C1.mistake: Meist in der Verlaufsform: "She's flying high".

C1.def: a radio broadcasting system using frequency modulation
C1.example: I listen to music on FM radio.
C1.ielts_writing: FM signals offer better sound quality than AM.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "frequency modulation"; als Buchstaben gesprochen.

C1.def: a container for papers, or a directory on a computer
C1.example: Put the documents in a folder.
C1.ielts_writing: Create a separate folder for each project.
C1.mistake: Auch Ordner am Computer; nicht mit "folder" im Sinn von Flyer verwechseln.

C1.def: to take further action on something
C1.example: I'll follow up with the client tomorrow.
C1.ielts_writing: We need to follow up on the survey results.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "follow up ON sth" oder "WITH sb"; Nomen "follow-up".

C1.def: something that follows an earlier action
C1.example: A follow-up meeting is scheduled for Monday.
C1.ielts_writing: The follow-up study confirmed the initial results.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I got a follow-up call from the clinic."
C1.mistake: Nomen/Adjektiv mit Bindestrich; Verb getrennt: "follow up".

C1.def: a person who supports a leader or belief, or who follows an account
C1.example: She has thousands of followers on social media.
C1.ielts_writing: Followers of the movement gathered in the square.
C1.mistake: Plural "followers"; "follow" auch in sozialen Medien.

C1.def: having affection for someone or enjoying something
C1.example: I'm fond of my grandmother.
C1.ielts_writing: The professor is fond of quoting poetry.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm not very fond of spicy food."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "fond OF sb/sth"; nicht mit "fund" (Geld) verwechseln.

C1.def: an area in a mall with several food vendors
C1.example: We had lunch at the food court.
C1.ielts_writing: Food courts offer a variety of cuisines in one place.
C1.mistake: Plural "food courts"; meist in Einkaufszentren.

C1.def: bold in a reckless or stupid way
C1.example: It was foolhardy to swim in the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: Foolhardy investors lost their savings.
C1.mistake: Wird zusammengeschrieben; nicht schmeichelhaft gemeint.

C1.def: the number of people walking past or into a shop
C1.example: The store depends on foot traffic.
C1.ielts_writing: Foot traffic dropped sharply during the lockdown.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; im Einzelhandel ein Kennwert.

C1.def: film or video recordings of an event
C1.example: Security footage showed the thief.
C1.ielts_writing: Archive footage was used in the documentary.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some footage", nicht "a footage".

C1.def: a note at the bottom of a page
C1.example: The footnote explains the term.
C1.ielts_writing: Footnotes provide sources and extra information.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I added a footnote to the page."
C1.mistake: "a footnote in history" bedeutet "eine Randnotiz der Geschichte".

C1.def: shoes, boots, and other items worn on the feet
C1.example: The store sells sportswear and footwear.
C1.ielts_writing: Appropriate footwear is essential for hiking.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; kein Plural "footwears".

C1.def: permanently
C1.example: She left the country for good.
C1.ielts_writing: The company closed for good after twenty years.
C1.mistake: Nicht "für gut"; Gegenteil: "temporarily".

C1.def: used to add that what you said also applies to something else
C1.example: I don't like jazz, or music at all for that matter.
C1.ielts_writing: He's never been there, nor have I for that matter.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Nobody, myself included for that matter, knew."
C1.mistake: Steht meist am Ende eines Satzes; verallgemeinert eine Aussage.

C1.def: for now, until something changes
C1.example: We'll stay here for the time being.
C1.ielts_writing: The policy will remain in place for the time being.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm using this laptop for the time being."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung ohne Änderung; nicht "for the time being time".

C1.def: relating to scientific methods used in solving crimes
C1.example: Forensic experts examined the evidence.
C1.ielts_writing: Forensic science plays a vital role in modern criminal justice.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen "forensics" (Kriminaltechnik); nicht mit "foreign" verwechseln.

C1.def: to shape metal by heating, or to create something illegally
C1.example: He forged a sword from steel.
C1.ielts_writing: They forged a strong partnership.
C1.mistake: "forge ahead" bedeutet "vorankommen"; "forge links" heißt "Beziehungen aufbauen".

C1.def: the crime of making fake copies
C1.example: The painting turned out to be a forgery.
C1.ielts_writing: Forgery of documents is punishable by law.
C1.mistake: Täter: "forger"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: the way something is arranged, or to prepare a disk for use
C1.example: The file format is not supported.
C1.ielts_writing: The event follows a debate format.
C1.mistake: Verb "format" (formatiert); "formatting" ist die Formatierung.

C1.def: inspiring fear or respect because of size or ability
C1.example: The team faced a formidable opponent.
C1.ielts_writing: Formidable obstacles stand in the way of reform.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; "formidable" bedeutet nicht "großartig" wie im Französischen.

C1.def: a rule written with symbols, or a method for achieving something
C1.example: The formula for the area of a circle is πr².
C1.ielts_writing: There is no secret formula for success.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We switched to a different baby formula."
C1.mistake: Plural "formulas" oder "formulae"; "baby formula" ist Säuglingsnahrung.

C1.def: to create or express something carefully
C1.example: She formulated a plan to cut costs.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers formulate hypotheses based on observations.
C1.mistake: Nomen "formulation"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a strong building used for defense
C1.example: Soldiers defended the fort.
C1.ielts_writing: The old fort overlooks the harbor.
C1.mistake: "hold the fort" bedeutet "die Stellung halten"; Nomen "fortress".

C1.def: forward or out into view
C1.example: He ventured forth into the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: The committee put forth several proposals.
C1.mistake: "back and forth" heißt "hin und her"; "forth" nicht mit "fourth" (vierte) verwechseln.

C1.def: about to happen, or willing to provide information
C1.example: The forthcoming election is the focus of debate.
C1.ielts_writing: The author's forthcoming book is eagerly anticipated.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: "bevorstehend" und "auskunftsfreudig" (meist verneint: "not forthcoming").

C1.def: to encourage development, or to care for a child temporarily
C1.example: Good teachers foster curiosity.
C1.ielts_writing: Schools should foster cooperation among students.
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv "foster" (Pflege-): "foster parents" sind Pflegeeltern.

C1.def: the base of a structure, or an organization that provides funds
C1.example: The house is built on a solid foundation.
C1.ielts_writing: The foundation awards scholarships to students.
C1.ielts_speaking: "This book laid the foundation for the field."
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Grundlage, Stiftung, Make-up ("foundation cream").

C1.def: a pen with a refillable ink reservoir
C1.example: He signed with a fountain pen.
C1.ielts_writing: Fountain pens have become a collector's item.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I got a fountain pen as a graduation gift."
C1.mistake: Plural "fountain pens"; Tinte: "ink cartridge".

C1.def: an entrance hall in a building
C1.example: We waited in the theater foyer.
C1.ielts_writing: The hotel foyer was decorated with flowers.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈfɔɪər/; im Hotel oft "lobby".

C1.def: a break in a bone, or to break something
C1.example: He suffered a fracture in his arm.
C1.ielts_writing: The earthquake caused a fracture in the rock.
C1.mistake: "fracture" ist der Knochenbruch; Plural "fractures".

C1.def: easily broken or damaged
C1.example: The glass is fragile.
C1.ielts_writing: Ecosystems are fragile and sensitive to change.
C1.mistake: Nomen "fragility"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; "fragile" steht auf Paketen.

C1.def: a structure that surrounds or supports something, or to express in a particular way
C1.example: She put the photo in a silver frame.
C1.ielts_writing: The article frames the debate as a conflict between generations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The issue was framed as a question of fairness."
C1.mistake: "frame of mind" bedeutet "Stimmung"; Verb: "frame sth AS sth".

C1.def: a license to sell a company's products, or the right to vote
C1.example: She bought a coffee shop franchise.
C1.ielts_writing: Women gained the franchise in the early twentieth century.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The restaurant is part of a national franchise."
C1.mistake: Auch Sport-/Filmreihe: "a film franchise"; Verb "franchise sth".

C1.def: honest and direct in speech
C1.example: She gave a frank answer.
C1.ielts_writing: A frank discussion cleared the air between the partners.
C1.mistake: Nicht "frank" als Name; "to be frank" bedeutet "ehrlich gesagt".

C1.def: in an honest and direct way
C1.example: Frankly, I don't care.
C1.ielts_writing: He spoke frankly about his mistakes.
C1.mistake: Oft als Satzadverb am Anfang: "Frankly, ...".

C1.def: done in a hurried, anxious way
C1.example: She made frantic phone calls.
C1.ielts_writing: Rescuers made a frantic search for survivors.
C1.mistake: Adverb "frantically"; nicht mit "frenetic" (rastlos) verwechseln.

C1.def: a cold drink of blended ice, coffee, or fruit
C1.example: He ordered a mocha frappe.
C1.ielts_writing: Cafés sell frappes during the summer.
C1.mistake: Aussprache mit Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; das "e" wird nicht stumm.

C1.def: an economic system with little government control
C1.example: Supporters of the free market oppose strict regulation.
C1.ielts_writing: A free market allows prices to be set by supply and demand.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "planned economy"; "free market economy" meint Marktwirtschaft.

C1.def: trade between countries without tariffs or restrictions
C1.example: The countries signed a free trade agreement.
C1.ielts_writing: Free trade can reduce prices but threaten local industries.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "protectionism"; kein Plural.

C1.def: raised outdoors, not in cages
C1.example: We buy free-range eggs.
C1.ielts_writing: Free-range chickens are allowed to roam outside.
C1.mistake: Bei Eiern "Freilandhaltung"; auch bildlich: "free-range kids".

C1.def: a person who takes advantage of others without giving anything back
C1.example: Nobody likes a freeloader.
C1.ielts_writing: The roommate was a freeloader who never paid rent.
C1.mistake: Verb "freeload"; abwertend gemeint.

C1.def: without restriction or limit
C1.example: Water flows freely through the pipe.
C1.ielts_writing: He freely admitted his mistake.
C1.mistake: Nicht "free" als Adverb für "gratis" verwechseln; "freely" bedeutet "ungehindert".

C1.def: to turn into ice, or to stop moving
C1.example: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
C1.ielts_writing: The company decided to freeze hiring.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: freeze, froze, frozen; "freeze up" bedeutet "einfrieren/stocken".

C1.def: extremely cold
C1.example: It was freezing cold outside.
C1.ielts_writing: The room was freezing cold because the heating had failed.
C1.mistake: Auch kurz "freezing"; Steigerung "absolutely freezing".

C1.def: a railroad car for carrying goods
C1.example: A freight car was derailed.
C1.ielts_writing: Freight cars carry grain across the country.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The freight car was loaded with coal."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "passenger car"; Plural "freight cars".

C1.def: a train that carries goods
C1.example: The freight train passed slowly through town.
C1.ielts_writing: Freight trains move bulk goods over long distances.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We waited for the freight train to pass."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "passenger train"; "freight" ist unzählbar.

C1.def: how often something happens, or the number of waves per second
C1.example: The frequency of earthquakes has increased.
C1.ielts_writing: Radio stations broadcast at different frequencies.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The frequency of her visits surprised me."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "frequent" (häufig); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: occasionally
C1.example: We meet from time to time.
C1.ielts_writing: He visits his hometown from time to time.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I call her from time to time."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung; nicht "from time to times".

C1.def: the forward-facing part, or a line of conflict
C1.example: He sat in the front of the class.
C1.ielts_writing: The company is a front for illegal activities.
C1.mistake: "in front of" bedeutet "vor" (örtlich); "front" auch Wetterfront.

C1.def: a border between countries, or the limit of knowledge
C1.example: The army patrolled the frontier.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientists are pushing the frontiers of medicine.
C1.mistake: In den USA meist die "frontier" des Wilden Westens; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: turned into ice, or preserved by freezing
C1.example: The lake is frozen.
C1.ielts_writing: Frozen vegetables are convenient and nutritious.
C1.mistake: Partizip von "freeze"; "frozen assets" sind eingefrorene Vermögenswerte.

C1.def: careful about spending money or using resources
C1.example: She lives a frugal life.
C1.ielts_writing: The family was frugal and saved every dollar.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I try to be frugal with my money."
C1.mistake: Positiver als "stingy"; Nomen "frugality".

C1.def: feeling annoyed because you cannot achieve something
C1.example: She felt frustrated by the delays.
C1.ielts_writing: Frustrated employees often seek jobs elsewhere.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "frustrated WITH/BY sth"; "frustrating" beschreibt die Ursache.

C1.def: causing annoyance because of difficulty
C1.example: It's frustrating to wait so long.
C1.ielts_writing: The slow internet connection was frustrating.
C1.mistake: Nicht "frustriert": "frustrating" ist die Sache, "frustrated" die Person.

C1.def: a feeling of annoyance at being unable to do something
C1.example: He threw the book in frustration.
C1.ielts_writing: Growing frustration with the government led to protests.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I could hear the frustration in her voice."
C1.mistake: Auch Plural "frustrations" (Ärgernisse); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: feeling satisfied because of using your abilities
C1.example: She feels fulfilled in her career.
C1.ielts_writing: People who feel fulfilled are generally more resilient.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I want to lead a fulfilled life."
C1.mistake: US-Schreibweise "fulfill" mit einem "l" im Verb; Nomen "fulfillment".

C1.def: the moon when it appears as a complete circle
C1.example: The full moon lit the path.
C1.ielts_writing: Many legends are connected with the full moon.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We hiked by the light of the full moon."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "new moon"; Plural "full moons".

C1.def: a university teacher of the highest academic rank
C1.example: She was promoted to full professor.
C1.ielts_writing: Full professors usually hold tenure and lead research groups.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He became a full professor at forty."
C1.mistake: Im US-System: assistant, associate, full professor; entspricht etwa deutscher W3-Professur.

C1.def: the purpose of something, or to work properly
C1.example: The function of the heart is to pump blood.
C1.ielts_writing: The machine functions without electricity.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She has to attend a social function."
C1.mistake: Auch "Veranstaltung"; Verb: "function AS sth" (als etwas dienen).

C1.def: designed to be practical, or working properly
C1.example: The kitchen is small but functional.
C1.ielts_writing: Functional design prioritizes usability over appearance.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "dysfunctional"; Nomen "functionality" (Funktionsumfang).

C1.def: the activity of raising money for a cause
C1.example: The school organized a fundraising event.
C1.ielts_writing: Online fundraising has transformed charity work.
C1.mistake: Nomen "fundraiser" (Veranstaltung oder Person); unzählbar.

C1.def: a ceremony held after someone's death
C1.example: Hundreds attended the funeral.
C1.ielts_writing: The funeral was held in a small chapel.
C1.mistake: "funeral" meint die Feier, nicht den Tod ("death"); "funeral home" ist ein Bestattungsinstitut.

C1.def: an organism such as mold or a mushroom
C1.example: Fungus grew on the damp wall.
C1.ielts_writing: Fungi play an important role in decomposing organic matter.
C1.mistake: Plural "fungi" (/ˈfʌndʒaɪ/); Adjektiv "fungal".

C1.def: a style of rhythmic music, or a state of depression
C1.example: They danced to funk music.
C1.ielts_writing: After the loss, he fell into a deep funk.
C1.mistake: "in a funk" bedeutet "niedergeschlagen"; "funky" bedeutet "cool, abgefahren".

C1.def: unnecessary excitement or attention
C1.example: There was a lot of fuss about the new policy.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't make a fuss over small mistakes.
C1.mistake: "make a fuss" bedeutet "viel Aufhebens machen"; Adjektiv "fussy" (wählerisch).

C1.def: a very strong wind
C1.example: A gale damaged the roofs.
C1.ielts_writing: Gale-force winds disrupted ferry services.
C1.mistake: "gales of laughter" bedeutet "Lachsalven"; Aussprache /ɡeɪl/.

C1.def: a unit of liquid measure equal to about 3.8 liters
C1.example: We bought a gallon of milk.
C1.ielts_writing: A gallon of paint covers about four hundred square feet.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The car gets thirty miles per gallon."
C1.mistake: Eine US-Gallone entspricht etwa 3,8 Litern; "per gallon" im Verbrauch.

C1.def: a risky action taken in hope of success, or to bet
C1.example: The investment was a big gamble.
C1.ielts_writing: Entrepreneurs often gamble on new technology.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's a gamble, but it might pay off."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "gamble ON sth"; "gamble with sth" heißt "etwas aufs Spiel setzen".

C1.def: the activity of betting money on uncertain outcomes
C1.example: Gambling is illegal in some states.
C1.ielts_writing: Gambling addiction can ruin families financially.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "gamble" ist das einzelne Wagnis.
