C1.def: to play video games, or to be willing and ready
C1.example: He games for hours every night.
C1.ielts_writing: She was game for anything on the trip.
C1.mistake: "game for sth" bedeutet "zu allem bereit"; "game the system" heißt "das System austricksen".

C1.def: a member of a violent criminal gang
C1.example: The movie is about a notorious gangster.
C1.ielts_writing: Gangsters controlled the city during Prohibition.
C1.mistake: Nomen "gang" ist die Bande; Genre: "gangster film".

C1.def: a vehicle that collects household waste
C1.example: The garbage truck comes on Tuesday.
C1.ielts_writing: Garbage trucks start work very early in the morning.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar "garbage"; Plural "garbage trucks".

C1.def: an item of clothing
C1.example: She hung the garment in the closet.
C1.ielts_writing: Garment factories employ millions of workers worldwide.
C1.mistake: Eher formell; "clothes" ist Plural und unzählbar.

C1.def: the art and science of good eating
C1.example: The city is famous for its gastronomy.
C1.ielts_writing: Molecular gastronomy applies science to cooking.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Gastronomie" im Sinn von Gastgewerbe ("restaurant industry").

C1.def: a meeting of people
C1.example: The family gathering lasted all afternoon.
C1.ielts_writing: Large public gatherings were banned.
C1.mistake: Verb "gather" (sich versammeln); nicht "Gathering" als Konzert.

C1.def: attracted to people of the same sex
C1.example: The city has a vibrant gay community.
C1.ielts_writing: Gay rights have advanced in many countries.
C1.mistake: Sensibel im Gebrauch; neutral als Selbstbezeichnung; nicht "gay" im Sinn von "fröhlich" (veraltet).

C1.def: a long, steady look
C1.example: She felt his gaze on her.
C1.ielts_writing: They gazed at the stars for hours.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "gaze AT sth"; länger als "glance".

C1.def: equipment for a particular activity, or part of a vehicle
C1.example: He packed his camping gear.
C1.ielts_writing: She shifted into fourth gear.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some gear"; "gear up" bedeutet "sich vorbereiten".

C1.def: the social and cultural identity of being male, female, or neither
C1.example: The study examines gender and pay.
C1.ielts_writing: Gender roles vary across cultures.
C1.mistake: Unterschied zu "sex" (biologisch); im Deutschen oft "Gender" übernommen.

C1.def: not specific to men or women
C1.example: The company introduced gender-neutral restrooms.
C1.ielts_writing: Gender-neutral language avoids assuming a person's sex.
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich geschrieben; Gegenteil: "gender-specific".

C1.def: a high-ranking army officer, or relating to most people
C1.example: The general ordered the troops forward.
C1.ielts_writing: There is general agreement on the issue.
C1.mistake: "in general" bedeutet "im Allgemeinen"; "general" als Adjektiv ist nicht "Generalist".

C1.def: to make a general statement from specific cases
C1.example: It's unfair to generalize about a whole group.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers cannot generalize results from a small sample.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "generalize ABOUT/FROM"; Nomen "generalization".

C1.def: a machine that produces electricity
C1.example: The hospital has a backup generator.
C1.ielts_writing: A random number generator is used in the experiment.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We used a generator during the blackout."
C1.mistake: Verb "generate"; nicht mit "generation" (Generation) verwechseln.

C1.def: not specific to a brand, or relating to a whole group
C1.example: She bought a generic version of the drug.
C1.ielts_writing: The email used a generic greeting.
C1.mistake: "generic drug" ist ein Generikum; nicht mit "genetic" verwechseln.

C1.def: relating to genes and heredity
C1.example: The disease has a genetic cause.
C1.ielts_writing: Genetic testing can reveal inherited risks.
C1.mistake: Nomen "genetics" (Genetik); Aussprache mit zweiter Silbe betont.

C1.def: friendly and cheerful
C1.example: He is a genial host.
C1.ielts_writing: Her genial manner put everyone at ease.
C1.mistake: Nicht "genial" im Sinn von "brilliant" (das heißt "brilliant"); falscher Freund.

C1.def: the external sex organs
C1.example: The doctor examined the genitals for signs of infection.
C1.ielts_writing: Medical textbooks use the term genitals neutrally.
C1.mistake: Meist im Plural; medizinische Fachsprache; Adjektiv "genital".

C1.def: the deliberate killing of a large group of people
C1.example: The world condemned the genocide.
C1.ielts_writing: Genocide is considered the gravest crime against humanity.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "genocidal"; unzählbar.

C1.def: the complete set of genetic material in an organism
C1.example: Scientists sequenced the human genome.
C1.ielts_writing: Mapping the genome opened new paths in medicine.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The genome contains billions of base pairs."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Plural "genomes".

C1.def: a group of related species in biology
C1.example: The lion belongs to the genus Panthera.
C1.ielts_writing: Taxonomists place closely related species in one genus.
C1.ielts_speaking: "This plant is a member of the rose genus."
C1.mistake: Plural "genera"; ranghöher als "species".

C1.def: a verb form ending in -ing used as a noun
C1.example: "Swimming" in "I like swimming" is a gerund.
C1.ielts_writing: After "enjoy," a gerund is used instead of an infinitive.
C1.mistake: Im Englischen die -ing-Form als Nomen; nicht dasselbe wie das deutsche Gerundium.

C1.def: to contact someone
C1.example: Please get in touch if you need help.
C1.ielts_writing: We will get in touch with the successful candidates next week.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "get in touch WITH sb"; Gegenteil: "lose touch".

C1.def: to have a friendly relationship
C1.example: They get on well with their neighbors.
C1.ielts_writing: Colleagues who get on well tend to work better together.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Do you get on well with your sister?"
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "get on well WITH sb"; auch "get along".

C1.def: the very beginning of something
C1.example: He opposed the plan from the get-go.
C1.ielts_writing: The project was in trouble from the get-go.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung "from the get-go" (von Anfang an); umgangssprachlich.

C1.def: a live performance by a musician, or a short-term job
C1.example: The band had a gig on Friday.
C1.ielts_writing: Many freelancers rely on gig work.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I landed a new gig as a DJ."
C1.mistake: "gig economy" meint Kurzzeitjobs; Plural "gigs".

C1.def: a unit of computer memory equal to one billion bytes
C1.example: The phone has sixty-four gigabytes of storage.
C1.ielts_writing: One gigabyte of data holds hundreds of photos.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I used up my data allowance of two gigabytes."
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "GB"; Aussprache mit hartem "g".

C1.def: a spicy root used in cooking, or reddish-orange in color
C1.example: She added fresh ginger to the soup.
C1.ielts_writing: Ginger tea helps relieve nausea.
C1.mistake: Auch "ginger ale" (Getränk); "ginger hair" ist rothaarig.

C1.def: to cause difficulty for someone
C1.example: The old printer will give us trouble again.
C1.ielts_writing: His knee has been giving him trouble since the accident.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The kids gave me trouble at bedtime."
C1.mistake: Struktur: "give sb trouble" mit Objekt; nicht "give trouble to me".

C1.def: considering that something is true
C1.example: Given that it's raining, we'll stay home.
C1.ielts_writing: Given that resources are limited, the committee must prioritize.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Given that he's new, he did well."
C1.mistake: Gleichbedeutend mit "considering that"; folgt ein Satz mit Verb.

C1.def: the attractive and exciting quality of a person or place
C1.example: The glamor of Hollywood attracts many young actors.
C1.ielts_writing: The glamor of the red carpet hides the hard work behind it.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "glamorous"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to look quickly, or a brief look
C1.example: She glanced at her watch.
C1.ielts_writing: At first glance, the proposal seems reasonable.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He cast a glance at the clock."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "glance AT sth"; "at a glance" heißt "auf einen Blick".

C1.def: an organ that produces a substance such as hormones
C1.example: The thyroid gland controls metabolism.
C1.ielts_writing: Sweat glands help regulate body temperature.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "glandular"; Plural "glands".

C1.def: items made of glass, such as cups and bowls
C1.example: The shop sells beautiful glassware.
C1.ielts_writing: Fine glassware should be washed by hand.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some glassware", nicht "glasswares".

C1.def: a brief look at something
C1.example: I caught a glimpse of the star.
C1.ielts_writing: The documentary offers a glimpse into daily life in rural Japan.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We got a glimpse of the sea."
C1.mistake: Typisch: "catch a glimpse OF sth"; auch als Verb "glimpse".

C1.def: a policy or belief in international rather than national interests
C1.example: Critics blame globalism for job losses.
C1.ielts_writing: Debates over globalism divide voters in many countries.
C1.mistake: Politisch aufgeladen; nicht dasselbe wie "globalization" (Prozess).

C1.def: dark or depressing
C1.example: It was a gloomy day.
C1.ielts_writing: The economic outlook remains gloomy.
C1.mistake: Nomen "gloom"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: wonderful or deserving great praise
C1.example: We had a glorious day at the beach.
C1.ielts_writing: The team celebrated a glorious victory.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Adverb "gloriously".

C1.def: great fame or honor
C1.example: The soldiers returned covered in glory.
C1.ielts_writing: The old stadium has lost its former glory.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She reveled in the glory of success."
C1.mistake: "in all its glory" bedeutet "in voller Pracht"; Verb "glorify".

C1.def: to shine with a soft light
C1.example: The embers glowed in the dark.
C1.ielts_writing: She glowed with pride at her son's graduation.
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "glow with pride/health"; "glowing review" ist eine begeisterte Kritik.

C1.def: to oppose or conflict with something
C1.example: His actions go against company policy.
C1.ielts_writing: Voters went against the party's recommendation.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion mit Objekt: "go against sb/sth"; "against the grain" heißt "gegen den Strich".

C1.def: to decrease, sink, or be received in a certain way
C1.example: Prices should go down next month.
C1.ielts_writing: The ship went down in the storm.
C1.mistake: "go down in history" bedeutet "in die Geschichte eingehen"; "go down with" heißt "an etwas erkranken".

C1.def: having a deep respect for God
C1.example: She comes from a God-fearing family.
C1.ielts_writing: God-fearing citizens attended church every Sunday.
C1.mistake: "God" wird großgeschrieben; Bindestrich; leicht altmodisch.

C1.def: used to express anger or annoyance
C1.example: He couldn't find the goddamn keys.
C1.ielts_writing: The goddamn printer broke again.
C1.mistake: Sehr stark umgangssprachlich und für manche anstößig; im formellen Kontext meiden.

C1.def: remote, dreary, and unpleasant
C1.example: They lived in a godforsaken village.
C1.ielts_writing: The expedition crossed a godforsaken stretch of desert.
C1.mistake: Zusammengeschrieben; Verb "forsake" (verlassen).

C1.def: not believing in God, or wicked
C1.example: Critics called the regime godless.
C1.ielts_writing: A godless society, he argued, has no moral foundation.
C1.mistake: Nomen "godlessness"; kann abwertend wirken.

C1.def: having the qualities of a god
C1.example: He had a godlike presence.
C1.ielts_writing: Fans treated the singer with godlike reverence.
C1.mistake: Zusammengeschrieben; nicht "godly" (fromm).

C1.def: a period of great prosperity or achievement
C1.example: The 1950s were the golden age of television.
C1.ielts_writing: Scholars debate when the golden age of cinema ended.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We live in a golden age of technology."
C1.mistake: Präposition: "golden age OF + Bereich"; Plural "golden ages".

C1.def: a thug or hired criminal
C1.example: The boss sent his goons to collect the money.
C1.ielts_writing: Political goons intimidated voters.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A couple of goons blocked the door."
C1.mistake: Abwertend; auch im Plural "goons"; Slang-Register.

C1.def: a small green berry with a sour taste
C1.example: She made gooseberry jam.
C1.ielts_writing: Gooseberries are popular in desserts.
C1.mistake: Wörtlich "Gänsebeere"; Aussprache mit /ɡuːs-/.

C1.def: the teachings of Jesus, or a style of religious music
C1.example: The preacher read from the gospel.
C1.ielts_writing: Gospel music has deep roots in African American churches.
C1.mistake: "take sth as gospel" heißt "etwas für bare Münze nehmen"; "gospel truth" bedeutet "reine Wahrheit".

C1.def: a person with refined taste in food
C1.example: The restaurant serves gourmet meals.
C1.ielts_writing: Gourmet coffee shops have multiplied in recent years.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "gourmand" (Genießer, Vielesser) verwechseln; Aussprache /ˈɡʊrmeɪ/.

C1.def: the way an organization or country is managed
C1.example: Good governance builds public trust.
C1.ielts_writing: Corporate governance rules require transparency.
C1.mistake: Nicht "government" (Regierung als Institution); unzählbar.

C1.def: elegant movement, or a short prayer, or kindness
C1.example: She moved with grace.
C1.ielts_writing: They said grace before the meal.
C1.mistake: "grace period" ist eine Karenzzeit; "saving grace" eine rettende Eigenschaft.

C1.def: moving or shaped in an elegant way
C1.example: The dancer was graceful.
C1.ielts_writing: A graceful curve marks the bridge's design.
C1.mistake: Adverb "gracefully"; Gegenteil: "ungraceful".

C1.def: to understand fully, or to grab firmly
C1.example: It took time to grasp the concept.
C1.ielts_writing: He grasped the rope tightly.
C1.mistake: Nomen "grasp"; "beyond my grasp" bedeutet "außerhalb meiner Reichweite/Verständnisses".

C1.def: a jumping insect that makes a chirping sound
C1.example: A grasshopper jumped onto the leaf.
C1.ielts_writing: Grasshoppers can damage crops in large swarms.
C1.mistake: "knee-high to a grasshopper" bedeutet "sehr klein"; Plural "grasshoppers".

C1.def: to shred food, or to irritate
C1.example: Grate the cheese over the pasta.
C1.ielts_writing: His constant humming grates on my nerves.
C1.mistake: "grate on sb's nerves" bedeutet "jdm. auf die Nerven gehen"; Nomen "grater" (Reibe).

C1.def: done without good reason, and often harmful
C1.example: The film contains gratuitous violence.
C1.ielts_writing: Gratuitous insults did nothing to help the debate.
C1.mistake: Nicht "gratuity" (Trinkgeld) verwechseln; meist negativ: "gratuitous violence".

C1.def: a place where a dead person is buried, or serious
C1.example: They visited her grave.
C1.ielts_writing: The situation is grave.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb "engrave"; "grave" (ernst) im Gegensatz zu "gravity" (Schwerkraft).

C1.def: the force that pulls objects toward the earth, or seriousness
C1.example: Gravity keeps us on the ground.
C1.ielts_writing: The gravity of the crime shocked the court.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He understood the gravity of the situation."
C1.mistake: "zero gravity" ist Schwerelosigkeit; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a standardized test for admission to graduate school
C1.example: She prepared for the GRE for six months.
C1.ielts_writing: High GRE scores can strengthen a graduate application.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "Graduate Record Examination"; als Buchstaben gesprochen.

C1.def: covered with or containing grease
C1.example: The pizza was too greasy.
C1.ielts_writing: Greasy fingers left marks on the keyboard.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈɡriːsi/ mit stimmlosem "s"; "greasy spoon" ist eine einfache Imbissbude.

C1.def: permission to go ahead with something
C1.example: The board gave the project the green light.
C1.ielts_writing: Investors are waiting for a green light from regulators.
C1.mistake: Typisch: "give sth the green light"; auch wörtlich Ampel.

C1.def: the warming of the earth caused by trapped heat
C1.example: The greenhouse effect warms the planet.
C1.ielts_writing: Burning fossil fuels intensifies the greenhouse effect.
C1.mistake: Mit "greenhouse gases" (Treibhausgase) verbunden; unzählbar.

C1.def: fond of company and social
C1.example: She is a gregarious person who loves parties.
C1.ielts_writing: Wolves are gregarious animals that live in packs.
C1.mistake: Auch für Tiere: "gregarious animals" leben in Gruppen.

C1.def: a pattern of crossing lines, or a network of electric wires
C1.example: The map is divided into a grid.
C1.ielts_writing: A storm knocked out the power grid.
C1.mistake: "off the grid" bedeutet "autark/ohne Anschluss"; "gridlock" ist Verkehrsstillstand.

C1.def: deep sorrow caused by loss
C1.example: She was overcome with grief.
C1.ielts_writing: Support groups help people cope with grief.
C1.mistake: "come to grief" bedeutet "scheitern"; Verb "grieve" (trauern).

C1.def: to crush into small pieces, or to rub together
C1.example: He grinds coffee beans each morning.
C1.ielts_writing: The economy came to a grinding halt.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: grind, ground, ground; "grind to a halt" heißt "zum Erliegen kommen".

C1.def: a firm hold, or to hold something tightly
C1.example: He lost his grip on the rope.
C1.ielts_writing: The story grips readers from the first page.
C1.mistake: "get a grip" bedeutet "sich zusammenreißen"; "in the grip of" heißt "im Griff von".

C1.def: holding your attention completely
C1.example: The film was gripping from start to finish.
C1.ielts_writing: A gripping thriller kept the audience on the edge of their seats.
C1.mistake: Von "grip" (packen); nicht "gripping" im Sinn von Griffigkeit.

C1.def: a person who sells food and household goods
C1.example: The grocer delivers fresh vegetables.
C1.ielts_writing: The local grocer knows all his customers by name.
C1.mistake: Nomen "groceries" (Lebensmittel, Plural); "grocery store" ist das Geschäft.

C1.def: the area where the legs join the abdomen
C1.example: He pulled a muscle in his groin.
C1.ielts_writing: Groin injuries are common among soccer players.
C1.mistake: Vor allem medizinisch und im Sport; unzählbar im Singular.

C1.def: total before deductions, or disgusting
C1.example: Her gross income is fifty thousand dollars.
C1.ielts_writing: It was a gross violation of human rights.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "net"; umgangssprachlich "gross" = eklig; "gross domestic product" ist das BIP.

C1.def: strangely distorted or ugly
C1.example: The statue had grotesque features.
C1.ielts_writing: The grotesque violence of the scene shocked viewers.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Adverb "grotesquely".

C1.def: the point of a bomb blast, or the center of an event
C1.example: Ground zero of the outbreak was a small village.
C1.ielts_writing: The memorial stands at ground zero in New York.
C1.mistake: In den USA oft der Ort der Anschläge vom 11. September; bildlich "Ausgangspunkt".

C1.def: to increase in size, or to cultivate plants
C1.example: Children grow quickly.
C1.ielts_writing: The company plans to grow its customer base.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: grow, grew, grown; "grow up" bedeutet "erwachsen werden".

C1.def: to make a low threatening sound
C1.example: The dog growled at the stranger.
C1.ielts_writing: The boss growled his disapproval.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "growl AT sb"; auch vom Magen.

C1.def: cautious and not revealing much
C1.example: She gave a guarded answer.
C1.ielts_writing: His guarded optimism reflects the uncertain situation.
C1.mistake: Nicht "bewacht" im Sinn von Wache; Adverb "guardedly".

C1.def: a tropical fruit with pink flesh
C1.example: She drank guava juice with breakfast.
C1.ielts_writing: Guava trees grow in warm climates.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈɡwɑːvə/; unzählbar bei Saft.

C1.def: a member of an irregular military group
C1.example: Guerrillas attacked the convoy.
C1.ielts_writing: Guerrilla warfare relies on surprise and mobility.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They fought as guerrillas in the jungle."
C1.mistake: Aussprache wie "gorilla"; "guerrilla marketing" ist unkonventionelles Marketing.

C1.def: conclusions made without enough evidence
C1.example: The plan was based on guesswork.
C1.ielts_writing: Accurate data eliminates guesswork.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; nicht "a guesswork".

C1.def: help or advice given to someone
C1.example: Students receive guidance from teachers.
C1.ielts_writing: The agency issued new guidance on data protection.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some guidance"; "under the guidance of" heißt "unter der Anleitung von".

C1.def: helping to direct a decision or action
C1.example: Honesty is her guiding principle.
C1.ielts_writing: The guiding idea behind the reform is fairness.
C1.mistake: Meist vor Nomen: "guiding principle"; nicht "Führer" als Person ("guide").

C1.def: a feeling of responsibility for wrongdoing
C1.example: He felt guilt about lying.
C1.ielts_writing: The jury found no evidence of guilt.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Schuld" im Sinn von Geldschuld (das ist "debt"); "guilt trip" bedeutet "Schuldgefühle machen".

C1.def: a person used in an experiment
C1.example: He volunteered to be the guinea pig.
C1.ielts_writing: The students were guinea pigs for the new curriculum.
C1.mistake: Wörtlich "Meerschweinchen"; bildlich Versuchskaninchen.

C1.def: a large area of sea partly enclosed by land, or a wide gap
C1.example: The Gulf of Mexico is warm.
C1.ielts_writing: A gulf exists between the rich and the poor.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "golf" (Sport) verwechseln; "gulf between A and B" bedeutet "Kluft".

C1.def: a person hired to do a violent job
C1.example: He worked as a gun for hire.
C1.ielts_writing: Mercenaries have long been described as guns for hire.
collocations: gun for hire in the Wild West
C1.mistake: Plural "guns for hire"; bildlich "Auftragsarbeiter".

C1.def: a soldier who operates a large gun
C1.example: The gunner aimed at the target.
C1.ielts_writing: Each gunner on the ship had a specific role.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Gunner" als Spitzname von Arsenal; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: an explosive powder used in guns
C1.example: Gunpowder was invented in China.
C1.ielts_writing: The smell of gunpowder hung in the air.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "Gunpowder Plot" ist eine bekannte historische Verschwörung in England.

C1.def: a skilled gunfighter in the Old West
C1.example: The gunslinger drew his pistol.
C1.ielts_writing: Westerns often feature a lone gunslinger.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He walked into town like a gunslinger."
C1.mistake: Typische Figur im Western; bildlich "Draufgänger".

C1.def: the intestine, or an instinctive feeling
C1.example: Gut bacteria affect digestion.
C1.ielts_writing: Her gut feeling told her something was wrong.
C1.mistake: "gut feeling" bedeutet "Bauchgefühl"; Plural "guts" auch "Mut".

C1.def: the natural home of an animal or plant
C1.example: The forest is the animal's natural habitat.
C1.ielts_writing: Habitat loss threatens many species.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Plural "habitats".

C1.def: to break into computer systems, or a cutting blow
C1.example: Criminals hacked the company's database.
C1.ielts_writing: A life hack can make daily tasks easier.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "hack INTO sth"; "life hack" ist ein Alltagstrick.

C1.def: a person who gains unauthorized access to computers
C1.example: A hacker stole thousands of passwords.
C1.ielts_writing: Ethical hackers test systems for weaknesses.
C1.mistake: Positive Variante: "ethical hacker"; Nomen "hacking".

C1.def: to praise publicly, or to call out to
C1.example: Critics hailed the film as a masterpiece.
C1.ielts_writing: He hailed a taxi on the corner.
C1.mistake: "hail from" bedeutet "stammen aus"; Nomen "hail" (Hagel).

C1.def: a brother who shares only one parent
C1.example: He lives with his half-brother.
C1.ielts_writing: My half-brother and I share the same father.
C1.mistake: Nicht "stepbrother" (Stiefbruder, nicht blutsverwandt); Bindestrich.

C1.def: the moon when only half of it is visible
C1.example: A half-moon hung in the sky.
C1.ielts_writing: The half-moon provided just enough light to walk by.
C1.mistake: Mit Bindestrich; Form: "half-moon shaped".

C1.def: costing half the usual amount
C1.example: Half-price tickets are available after six.
C1.ielts_writing: The store offered half-price shoes on weekends.
C1.mistake: Adverbial: "at half price"; Bindestrich bei Adjektiv.

C1.def: a sister who shares only one parent
C1.example: I visited my half-sister in Boston.
C1.ielts_writing: Her half-sister is a doctor.
C1.mistake: Nicht "stepsister" (Stiefschwester); Bindestrich.

C1.def: at a point midway between two places
C1.example: We stopped halfway to the city.
C1.ielts_writing: The project is only halfway done.
C1.mistake: "meet sb halfway" bedeutet "jemandem entgegenkommen"; "halfway house" ist eine Übergangseinrichtung.

C1.def: to stop or make something stop
C1.example: The government halted the program.
C1.ielts_writing: Production was halted by a strike.
C1.mistake: Nomen "halt" (Halt); "come to a halt" heißt "zum Stillstand kommen".

C1.def: a tool for hitting nails, or to strike repeatedly
C1.example: He hit the nail with a hammer.
C1.ielts_writing: She hammered out a compromise after hours of talks.
C1.mistake: "hammer out" bedeutet "aushandeln"; "hammer home" heißt "einhämmern".

C1.def: a large basket with a lid, or to hinder
C1.example: She packed a picnic hamper.
C1.ielts_writing: Bad weather hampered rescue efforts.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen: US "laundry hamper" (Wäschekorb), als Verb "behindern".

C1.def: to distribute something to people
C1.example: The teacher handed out the worksheets.
C1.ielts_writing: Volunteers hand out food at the shelter.
C1.mistake: Nomen "handout" (Skript, Handzettel); getrennt als Verb.

C1.def: a metal ring used to restrain a prisoner's wrist
C1.example: The officer put handcuffs on the suspect.
C1.ielts_writing: He was handcuffed and led away.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural "handcuffs"; Verb "handcuff sb".

C1.def: a small number or amount
C1.example: A handful of people attended.
C1.ielts_writing: Only a handful of countries have signed the treaty.
C1.mistake: "a handful" bedeutet auch "ein anstrengendes Kind".

C1.def: the way something is dealt with or controlled
C1.example: Careful handling of data is important.
C1.ielts_writing: The company's handling of the crisis was criticized.
C1.mistake: Nomen zu "handle"; "handling fee" ist eine Bearbeitungsgebühr.

C1.def: convenient or useful
C1.example: A flashlight is handy in a power outage.
C1.ielts_writing: He is handy with tools.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's handy to have a spare key."
C1.mistake: "come in handy" bedeutet "nützlich sein"; "handy" ist kein Handy (das ist "cell phone").

C1.def: a person who does repairs in a home
C1.example: We called a handyman to fix the sink.
C1.ielts_writing: A handyman can tackle small repairs around the house.
C1.mistake: Plural "handymen"; nicht mit "Handy" (Mobiltelefon).

C1.def: lacking order or planning
C1.example: The books were stored in a haphazard manner.
C1.ielts_writing: A haphazard approach rarely produces reliable results.
C1.mistake: Adverb "haphazardly"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: aggressive pressure or intimidation
C1.example: She reported the harassment to HR.
C1.ielts_writing: Workplace harassment is illegal in many countries.
C1.mistake: Betonung kann auf der zweiten Silbe liegen (/həˈræsmənt/); Verb "harass".

C1.def: a device that stores computer data permanently
C1.example: The hard disk drive failed without warning.
C1.ielts_writing: Hard disk drives are slower than solid-state drives.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I backed up everything to an external hard disk drive."
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "HDD"; im US-Alltag oft "hard drive".

C1.def: a book with a stiff cover
C1.example: The novel is available in hardcover.
C1.ielts_writing: Hardcover editions cost more than paperbacks.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "paperback"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: physical parts of a computer, or tools and metal goods
C1.example: The computer hardware needs an upgrade.
C1.ielts_writing: The hardware store sells nails and screws.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I bought some hardware for the shelf."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "software"; unzählbar; auch Baumarkt: "hardware store".

C1.def: a fast animal like a large rabbit
C1.example: A hare ran across the field.
C1.ielts_writing: The fable of the tortoise and the hare teaches patience.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw a hare in the meadow."
C1.mistake: Nicht "hair" (Haar); gleiche Aussprache wie "hair".

C1.def: a state of peaceful agreement, or pleasing sounds together
C1.example: The neighbors live in harmony.
C1.ielts_writing: The choir sang in perfect harmony.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "in harmony WITH sb/sth"; Adjektiv "harmonious".

C1.def: a large stringed instrument played with the fingers
C1.example: She plays the harp in the orchestra.
C1.ielts_writing: The sound of the harp filled the hall.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "harp on" (immer wieder darauf herumreiten).

C1.def: unpleasantly severe or cruel
C1.example: The harsh winter killed many animals.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics were harsh in their judgment.
C1.mistake: Nicht "harsch" im Deutschen (Schnee); "harsh" bedeutet "rau/hart".

C1.def: the gathering of crops, or to gather crops
C1.example: The harvest was poor this year.
C1.ielts_writing: Farmers harvest wheat in late summer.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; "Thanksgiving" ist ein Erntedank.

C1.def: an intense feeling of dislike
C1.example: He felt deep hatred for his enemies.
C1.ielts_writing: Hatred and prejudice often grow from fear.
C1.mistake: Nomen zu "hate"; Präposition: "hatred OF/FOR sb".

C1.def: to appear as a ghost, or to continually trouble
C1.example: Legends say a ghost haunts the castle.
C1.ielts_writing: The memory of the accident haunted him for years.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "haunted" (verwunschen); "haunting" (eindringlich).

C1.def: to think about something
C1.example: I'll have a think and call you back.
C1.ielts_writing: Let's have a think about our options.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Give me a moment to have a think."
collocations: have a bit of a think
C1.mistake: Alltagswendung; entspricht "think about sth".

C1.def: used to introduce a contrasting point
C1.example: The results are good; having said that, there is room to improve.
C1.ielts_writing: Having said that, the plan has risks.
C1.mistake: Verbindet zwei Gegensätze; Synonym "that said".

C1.def: an allergy to pollen causing sneezing
C1.example: She suffers from hay fever each spring.
C1.ielts_writing: Hay fever can cause itchy eyes and a runny nose.
C1.mistake: Hat kein "Fieber"; ist eine Pollenallergie; unzählbar.

C1.def: something that could cause harm
C1.example: Loose cables are a safety hazard.
C1.ielts_writing: Toxic waste poses a health hazard.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Smoking is a hazard to your health."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "hazardous"; "occupational hazard" ist ein Berufsrisiko.

C1.def: light brown with a green or yellow tinge
C1.example: She has hazel eyes.
C1.ielts_writing: Hazel eyes can appear green in some light.
C1.mistake: Häufig für Augenfarbe; Nomen "hazelnut" (Haselnuss).

C1.def: not clear because of mist, or unclear
C1.example: The morning was hazy.
C1.ielts_writing: My memories of that day are hazy.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "hazy ABOUT/ON sth"; Nomen "haze".

C1.def: the process of becoming healthy again
C1.example: The wound is slowly healing.
C1.ielts_writing: Time is essential for emotional healing.
C1.mistake: Verb "heal"; "healing process" (Heilungsprozess).

C1.def: a legal or official session, or the sense of listening
C1.example: The court scheduled a hearing for Monday.
C1.ielts_writing: Her hearing is excellent.
C1.mistake: "hearing aid" ist ein Hörgerät; "hearing" auch Gerichtstermin.

C1.def: information that is repeated but not confirmed
C1.example: The evidence is mere hearsay.
C1.ielts_writing: Hearsay is generally not admissible in court.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; im Recht: "hearsay evidence" (Beweis vom Hörensagen).

C1.def: great sadness caused by loss, especially in love
C1.example: The film is about love and heartbreak.
C1.ielts_writing: She never fully recovered from the heartbreak.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "heartbroken" (untröstlich); unzählbar.

C1.def: having great weight, or large in amount
C1.example: The box is heavy.
C1.ielts_writing: Heavy rain flooded the roads.
C1.mistake: Nicht nur "schwer": "heavy traffic" bedeutet starker Verkehr; Adverb "heavily".

C1.def: a unit of area equal to ten thousand square meters
C1.example: The farm covers fifty hectares.
C1.ielts_writing: The forest area shrank by a thousand hectares last year.
C1.mistake: Metrische Fläche: 1 Hektar = 10.000 Quadratmeter.

C1.def: full of frantic activity
C1.example: It was a hectic week.
C1.ielts_writing: The airport is hectic during the holidays.
C1.mistake: Bedeutet "hektisch" im Alltagssinn; im Medizinischen auch "hektisches Fieber".

C1.def: the back part of the foot, or raised shoes
C1.example: She wore high heels.
C1.ielts_writing: The dog followed at his heels.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural; "head over heels" bedeutet "Hals über Kopf (verliebt)".

C1.def: to increase in intensity or degree
C1.example: The news heightened our fears.
C1.ielts_writing: Heightened security followed the attack.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "heightened"; das "gh" ist stumm; /ˈhaɪtn/.

C1.def: a person who inherits property or a title
C1.example: The heir to the throne visited the school.
C1.ielts_writing: She was the sole heir to the fortune.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He is heir to a large estate."
C1.mistake: "h" ist stumm: /er/ wie "air"; weiblich "heiress".

C1.def: a service that provides technical assistance
C1.example: Call the help desk for assistance.
C1.ielts_writing: The help desk resolved my login problem.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The help desk is open on weekdays."
C1.mistake: Plural "help desks"; im Unternehmen für IT-Support.

C1.def: a loyal follower of a powerful, often criminal person
C1.example: The boss sent his henchman to threaten them.
C1.ielts_writing: The villain's henchmen guard the entrance.
C1.mistake: Plural "henchmen"; meist abwertend, oft in Filmen.

C1.def: a chemical used to kill unwanted plants
C1.example: The farmer sprayed herbicide on the field.
C1.ielts_writing: Herbicides can contaminate groundwater.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Pestizid" allgemein; Endung "-cide" bedeutet "töten".

C1.def: traditions and values passed down through generations
C1.example: The city has a rich cultural heritage.
C1.ielts_writing: Protecting our heritage is a shared responsibility.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "inheritance" (Erbschaft, Vermögen) gleichsetzen; unzählbar.

C1.def: showing great courage
C1.example: The firefighter made a heroic rescue.
C1.ielts_writing: Her heroic efforts saved many lives.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Nomen "heroism".

C1.def: a pause before doing something because of doubt
C1.example: He agreed without hesitation.
C1.ielts_writing: Her hesitation suggested she had doubts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have no hesitation in recommending him."
C1.mistake: Verb "hesitate"; "without hesitation" heißt "ohne Zögern".

C1.def: attracted to people of the opposite sex
C1.example: The survey included heterosexual couples.
C1.ielts_writing: Heterosexual and same-sex couples have equal rights.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich "straight"; Nomen "heterosexuality".

C1.def: a pause in activity
C1.example: The band is on hiatus.
C1.ielts_writing: The series returned after a two-year hiatus.
C1.mistake: Plural "hiatuses"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: extremely ugly or unpleasant
C1.example: The monster looked hideous.
C1.ielts_writing: The hideous crime shocked the nation.
C1.mistake: Adverb "hideously"; nicht mit "hide" (verstecken) verwechseln.

C1.def: a system with ranked levels of authority
C1.example: The company has a strict hierarchy.
C1.ielts_writing: Social hierarchy shapes access to resources.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "hierarchical"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: attracting a lot of public attention
C1.example: He is defending a high-profile client.
C1.ielts_writing: The high-profile case drew media attention.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "low-profile"; Bindestrich vor Nomen.

C1.def: a tall building with many floors
C1.example: They live in a high-rise downtown.
C1.ielts_writing: High-rise buildings dominate the skyline.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "low-rise"; Plural "high-rises".

C1.def: intellectual and cultured
C1.example: The magazine is highbrow.
C1.ielts_writing: Highbrow literature appeals to a smaller audience.
C1.mistake: Oft leicht abwertend (snobistisch); Gegenteil: "lowbrow".

C1.def: a pen with bright ink for marking text
C1.example: She underlined the key points with a highlighter.
C1.ielts_writing: Students use highlighters to review notes.
C1.mistake: Verb "highlight" (hervorheben); Plural "highlighters".

C1.def: to seize a vehicle or plane by force
C1.example: Terrorists hijacked the plane.
C1.ielts_writing: Hackers hijacked the website's homepage.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "hijack the debate" (an sich reißen); Nomen "hijacker".

C1.def: the activity of walking in nature
C1.example: Hiking is popular in the mountains.
C1.ielts_writing: Hiking boots protect your ankles on rough trails.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "hike" ist die einzelne Wanderung; "hiking" ist nicht "Hitching".

C1.def: a person from a remote rural area, often seen as unsophisticated
C1.example: He grew up as a hillbilly in the mountains.
C1.ielts_writing: The stereotype of the hillbilly appears in many comedies.
C1.mistake: Oft abwertend; Vorsicht im Gebrauch; typisch für Appalachen-Klischee.

C1.def: a slight indication, or to suggest indirectly
C1.example: She dropped a hint about the surprise.
C1.ielts_writing: He hinted that he might resign.
C1.mistake: "take the hint" bedeutet "den Wink verstehen"; Konstruktion: "hint AT sth".

C1.def: a bone in the pelvis
C1.example: The doctor found a crack in her hipbone.
C1.ielts_writing: A fall can cause a fracture of the hipbone.
C1.mistake: Auch "hip bone" getrennt; medizinisch "ilium".

C1.def: a large African river mammal
C1.example: The hippo wallowed in the mud.
C1.ielts_writing: Hippos spend most of the day in water.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw a hippo at the zoo."
C1.mistake: Kurzform von "hippopotamus"; Plural "hippos".

C1.def: a person hired to do a particular job, often violent
C1.example: The company brought in a hired gun to fix the system.
C1.ielts_writing: A hired gun handled the dangerous mission.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich für externe Spezialisten; ähnlich "gun for hire".

C1.def: a virus that attacks the immune system
C1.example: The test came back negative for HIV.
C1.ielts_writing: HIV treatment has advanced dramatically over the past decades.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "human immunodeficiency virus"; als Buchstaben gesprochen.

C1.def: to store or collect large amounts secretly
C1.example: He hoards old newspapers.
C1.ielts_writing: Shoppers hoarded toilet paper during the crisis.
C1.mistake: Nomen "hoard" (Hort); Person: "hoarder".

C1.def: memories or events from a vacation
C1.example: She shared her holiday experiences with us.
C1.ielts_writing: Holiday experiences vary widely between travelers.
C1.mistake: "holiday" bedeutet nicht nur Urlaub, sondern auch Feiertag.

C1.def: a close male friend from your neighborhood
C1.example: He greeted his homeboy at the door.
C1.ielts_writing: Two homeboys from the old block opened a restaurant together.
C1.mistake: Slang; weibliche Form "homegirl"; im formellen Kontext meiden.

C1.def: the country where someone was born or feels they belong
C1.example: Refugees dream of returning to their homeland.
C1.ielts_writing: The government pledged to defend the homeland.
C1.mistake: "Homeland Security" ist das US-Heimatschutzministerium; nicht "Heimat" im emotionalen Sinn allein.

C1.def: simple and comfortable, or plain in appearance
C1.example: The cabin has a homely atmosphere.
C1.ielts_writing: The restaurant serves homely, hearty meals.
C1.mistake: Falscher Freund: "homely" kann auch "unattraktiv" bedeuten, also vorsichtig verwenden.

C1.def: an arrangement to stay in a local family's home
C1.example: Students arranged a homestay abroad.
C1.ielts_writing: A homestay offers cultural immersion and language practice.
C1.mistake: Plural "homestays"; Gastfamilie: "host family".

C1.def: attracted to people of the same sex
C1.example: The study included homosexual couples.
C1.ielts_writing: Laws on homosexual rights differ across countries.
C1.mistake: Als Substantiv heute oft als veraltet empfunden; neutral "gay" oder "lesbian".

C1.def: used to emphasize honesty or sincerity
C1.example: It was an honest to God miracle.
C1.ielts_writing: Honest to God, I had no idea.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Honest to God, I didn't do it."
C1.mistake: Auch "honest to goodness"; verstärkt Aussagen; "God" großschreiben.

C1.def: a climbing plant with sweet-smelling flowers
C1.example: Honeysuckle covers the garden fence.
C1.ielts_writing: The scent of honeysuckle drifted through the window.
C1.mistake: Wörtlich "Honigsauger"; unzählbar.

C1.def: a curved piece of metal for hanging things, or to catch
C1.example: Hang your coat on the hook.
C1.ielts_writing: The movie hooked me from the first scene.
C1.mistake: "get hooked on sth" bedeutet "süchtig werden"; "off the hook" heißt "aus dem Schneider".

C1.def: feeling optimistic about the future
C1.example: She remains hopeful about the results.
C1.ielts_writing: Hopeful applicants lined up outside.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "hopeful ABOUT sth" oder "hopeful THAT"; Nomen auch "a hopeful" (Anwärter).

C1.def: the line where earth and sky appear to meet
C1.example: The sun dipped below the horizon.
C1.ielts_writing: Travel broadens your horizons.
C1.mistake: "on the horizon" bedeutet "in Sicht"; Adjektiv "horizontal".

C1.def: a hard growth on an animal's head, or a signal device
C1.example: The driver sounded the horn.
C1.ielts_writing: He plays the French horn in the orchestra.
C1.mistake: "honk the horn" bedeutet "hupen"; "horn" auch Blasinstrument.

C1.def: feeling shock and fear
C1.example: She was horrified by the news.
C1.ielts_writing: Horrified onlookers watched the accident unfold.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I was horrified to learn the truth."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "horrified AT/BY sth"; Verb "horrify".

C1.def: a unit of engine power
C1.example: The engine produces three hundred horsepower.
C1.ielts_writing: Horsepower measures the strength of motors.
C1.ielts_speaking: "This car has a lot of horsepower."
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "hp"; unzählbar im Plural unverändert: "three hundred horsepower".

C1.def: welcoming and generous toward guests
C1.example: The villagers were hospitable.
C1.ielts_writing: A hospitable climate encourages growth.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "inhospitable"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; auch "hospitable to sth".

C1.def: friendly treatment of guests, or the hotel and restaurant industry
C1.example: We thanked them for their hospitality.
C1.ielts_writing: She works in the hospitality industry.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "Hospitalität"; "hospitality industry" ist das Gastgewerbe.

C1.def: the admission of a patient to a hospital
C1.example: The illness required hospitalization.
C1.ielts_writing: Hospitalization rates rose during the winter.
C1.mistake: Verb "hospitalize"; Betonung auf der vierten Silbe.

C1.def: a person held captive to force demands
C1.example: The hostages were freed.
C1.ielts_writing: Terrorists took several people hostage.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendungen: "take sb hostage", "be held hostage"; Aussprache /ˈhɑːstɪdʒ/.

C1.def: unfriendly or opposed
C1.example: The crowd turned hostile.
C1.ielts_writing: A hostile takeover can damage a company's culture.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "hostile TO sb/sth"; "hostile takeover" ist eine feindliche Übernahme.

C1.def: unfriendly or aggressive behavior
C1.example: He met her proposal with hostility.
C1.ielts_writing: Hostilities between the countries ended with a ceasefire.
C1.mistake: Plural "hostilities" bedeutet Kampfhandlungen; Präposition: "hostility TO/TOWARD".

C1.def: a person employed to clean and manage a household
C1.example: The housekeeper tidied the rooms.
C1.ielts_writing: Hotels employ housekeepers to maintain cleanliness.
C1.mistake: Nomen "housekeeping" (Haushaltsführung); "good housekeeping" ist gutes Wirtschaften.

C1.def: a vehicle that travels on a cushion of air
C1.example: The hovercraft glided over the water.
C1.ielts_writing: Hovercraft services connect the island with the mainland.
C1.mistake: Unveränderlicher Plural "hovercraft"; Verb "hover" (schweben).

C1.def: giving practical instructions
C1.example: She bought a how-to book on gardening.
C1.ielts_writing: How-to videos are popular on social media.
C1.mistake: Bindestrich; als Nomen "a how-to" (Anleitung).

C1.def: a central point of activity or connection
C1.example: The airport is a major hub.
C1.ielts_writing: The city is a financial hub.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The library is the hub of the community."
C1.mistake: Im Netzwerk: Hub verbindet mehrere Geräte; "hub and spoke" ist Sternstruktur.

C1.def: to make a low continuous sound
C1.example: She hummed a tune while cooking.
C1.ielts_writing: The refrigerator hums softly all night.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig nicht: hum, hummed, hummed; auch bildlich "hum with energy".

C1.def: concerned with improving human welfare
C1.example: The country faces a humanitarian crisis.
C1.ielts_writing: Humanitarian organizations deliver food to war zones.
C1.mistake: Auch Nomen "humanitarian" (Menschenfreund); Betonung auf der vierten Silbe.

C1.def: help given to people in need after disasters
C1.example: Humanitarian aid reached the flooded region.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments pledged humanitarian aid for refugees.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some humanitarian aid"; nicht Plural.

C1.def: academic subjects such as literature, history, and philosophy
C1.example: She majored in the humanities.
C1.ielts_writing: Funding for the humanities has declined.
C1.mistake: Nur Plural; nicht mit "humanity" (Menschlichkeit) verwechseln.

C1.def: all human beings, or kindness
C1.example: The disaster tested humanity's resilience.
C1.ielts_writing: She treated every patient with humanity.
C1.mistake: "Crimes against humanity" sind Verbrechen gegen die Menschlichkeit; unzählbar.

C1.def: not proud or arrogant
C1.example: He remained humble despite his fame.
C1.ielts_writing: She comes from a humble background.
C1.mistake: Nomen "humility"; "eat humble pie" bedeutet "klein beigeben".

C1.def: an obstacle to overcome
C1.example: The final hurdle is funding.
C1.ielts_writing: Runners cleared each hurdle in the race.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb "hurdle" (überspringen); bildlich "jump the final hurdle".

C1.def: made by combining two different things
C1.example: He drives a hybrid car.
C1.ielts_writing: The new species is a hybrid of two plants.
C1.mistake: "hybrid work" ist Mischung aus Homeoffice und Büro; Verb "hybridize".

C1.def: electricity produced from moving water
C1.example: The country relies on hydroelectricity.
C1.ielts_writing: Hydroelectricity provides clean energy without carbon emissions.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "hydroelectric"; auch "hydropower" (Wasserkraft).

C1.def: the lightest chemical element, symbol H
C1.example: Water contains hydrogen and oxygen.
C1.ielts_writing: Hydrogen is considered a promising fuel for the future.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "hydrogen peroxide" ist Wasserstoffperoxid.

C1.def: practices that keep people healthy and clean
C1.example: Good hygiene prevents infection.
C1.ielts_writing: Poor hygiene caused the outbreak.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "hygienic"; unzählbar; Aussprache /ˈhaɪdʒiːn/.

C1.def: a short line used to join words
C1.example: Use a hyphen in "well-known".
C1.ielts_writing: A hyphen connects the two parts of the compound.
C1.mistake: Unterschied zu "dash" (Gedankenstrich); Verb "hyphenate".

C1.def: a long period when much of the earth was covered in ice
C1.example: Mammoths lived during the last ice age.
C1.ielts_writing: The ice age shaped many of today's valleys.
C1.mistake: Groß: "Ice Age" als Epochenname; unzählbar: "an ice age" für eine einzelne Epoche.

C1.def: a huge mass of ice floating in the sea
C1.example: The ship hit an iceberg.
C1.ielts_writing: Only the tip of the iceberg is visible above water.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It's just the tip of the iceberg."
C1.mistake: "the tip of the iceberg" bedeutet "nur die Spitze des Eisbergs"; Kopfsalat: "iceberg lettuce".

C1.def: proof of who someone is, or the act of recognizing something
C1.example: Please show some identification.
C1.ielts_writing: Accurate identification of the suspect took days.
C1.mistake: Kurz "ID"; "identification card" ist der Ausweis.

C1.def: based on a set of political or social beliefs
C1.example: They had an ideological disagreement.
C1.ielts_writing: Ideological differences divided the party.
C1.mistake: Nomen "ideology"; Gegenteil: "pragmatic".

C1.def: a system of ideas that guides political or social action
C1.example: The party's ideology is conservative.
C1.ielts_writing: Different ideologies compete for public support.
C1.mistake: Plural "ideologies"; Adjektiv "ideological".

C1.def: a fixed expression whose meaning isn't obvious from its words
C1.example: "Kick the bucket" is an idiom.
C1.ielts_writing: Learning idioms helps students sound more fluent.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "idiomatic" (idiomatisch); Plural "idioms".

C1.def: used to add a point that is the opposite of what was expected
C1.example: If anything, the problem has gotten worse.
C1.ielts_writing: If anything, the new rules made things harder.
C1.ielts_speaking: "If anything, I like him more now."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung; verstärkt eine Gegenthese.

C1.def: used to give advice
C1.example: If I were you, I'd apologize.
C1.ielts_writing: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
C1.ielts_speaking: "If I were you, I'd call her."
collocations: what I'd do if I were you
C1.mistake: Konjunktiv mit "were", nicht "was": "if I were you".

C1.def: a dome-shaped shelter made of snow blocks
C1.example: They built an igloo.
C1.ielts_writing: Igloos are traditional dwellings of some Arctic peoples.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈɪɡluː/; auch "iglu" nicht verwenden.

C1.def: lack of knowledge or information
C1.example: Ignorance of the law is no excuse.
C1.ielts_writing: Their ignorance of local customs caused offense.
C1.mistake: "Ignorance is bliss" ist ein Sprichwort; nicht mit "ignoring" (Ignorieren).

C1.def: forbidden by law or social rules
C1.example: They had an illicit affair.
C1.ielts_writing: Police seized illicit drugs.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "elicit" (hervorlocken) verwechseln; Aussprache gleich.

C1.def: language that creates mental pictures
C1.example: The poem is full of vivid imagery.
C1.ielts_writing: Religious imagery appears throughout the novel.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I love the imagery in this story."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "much imagery", nicht "imageries".

C1.def: extremely large
C1.example: The project requires immense effort.
C1.ielts_writing: She felt immense pride.
C1.mistake: Adverb "immensely"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to put something completely in liquid, or to involve deeply
C1.example: Immerse the vegetables in boiling water.
C1.ielts_writing: She immersed herself in her studies.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I want to immerse myself in the culture."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "immerse oneself IN sth"; Nomen "immersion".

C1.def: about to happen
C1.example: Danger is imminent.
C1.ielts_writing: The company faces imminent collapse.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "eminent" (bedeutend) oder "immanent" (innewohnend) verwechseln.

C1.def: protection against disease or legal action
C1.example: The vaccine provides immunity to the virus.
C1.ielts_writing: Diplomats enjoy immunity from prosecution.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "immunity TO a disease", "immunity FROM prosecution".

C1.def: to protect someone against disease, usually by vaccination
C1.example: Doctors immunize children against measles.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments aim to immunize the whole population.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "immunize sb AGAINST sth"; Nomen "immunization".

C1.def: to weaken or damage something
C1.example: Alcohol can impair your judgment.
C1.ielts_writing: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "impaired" (z. B. "hearing-impaired"); Nomen "impairment".

C1.def: treating all sides equally
C1.example: A judge must remain impartial.
C1.ielts_writing: An impartial investigation is essential.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "partial" oder "biased"; Nomen "impartiality".

C1.def: to slow or prevent progress
C1.example: Fallen trees impeded rescue efforts.
C1.ielts_writing: Poor infrastructure impedes economic growth.
C1.mistake: Nomen "impediment" (Hindernis); "speech impediment" ist eine Sprachstörung.

C1.def: relating to an empire or emperor
C1.example: The imperial palace was built in 1700.
C1.ielts_writing: Imperial powers once controlled much of Africa.
C1.mistake: Nomen "imperialism"; auch Maßsystem: "imperial units" (Zoll, Pfund).

C1.def: the process of putting a plan into action
C1.example: The implementation of the policy began in May.
C1.ielts_writing: Poor implementation led to the project's failure.
C1.mistake: Verb "implement"; "implementation OF sth".

C1.def: suggested but not stated directly
C1.example: There was an implicit threat in his tone.
C1.ielts_writing: Implicit bias can affect hiring decisions.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "explicit"; "implicit trust" bedeutet "uneingeschränktes Vertrauen".

C1.def: a nineteenth-century art movement focused on light and impression
C1.example: Monet is a leading figure of impressionism.
C1.ielts_writing: Impressionism changed the way artists painted light.
C1.mistake: Person: "impressionist"; unzählbar; auch in der Musik (Debussy).

C1.def: to put someone in prison
C1.example: The regime imprisoned its critics.
C1.ielts_writing: He was imprisoned for ten years.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "imprison sb FOR + Zeit/Grund"; Nomen "imprisonment".

C1.def: the state of being in prison
C1.example: She faces life imprisonment.
C1.ielts_writing: Imprisonment is the penalty for this crime.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "life imprisonment" ist lebenslange Haft.

C1.def: to create something without preparation
C1.example: The cook improvised a sauce from leftovers.
C1.ielts_writing: Jazz musicians improvise solos on stage.
C1.mistake: Nicht "improve" (verbessern); Kurzform "improv" (Stegreiftheater).

C1.def: following a rule or instruction
C1.example: We acted in accordance with the law.
C1.ielts_writing: The report was prepared in accordance with company guidelines.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Everything was done in accordance with the rules."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung mit "with"; Gegenteil: "in violation of".

C1.def: at the appropriate time in the future
C1.example: You will be notified in due course.
C1.ielts_writing: The results will be published in due course.
collocations: will be informed in due course
C1.mistake: Typisch für Geschäftsbriefe; bedeutet nicht "zeitnah", sondern "später".

C1.def: despite a difficulty or danger
C1.example: She stayed calm in the face of danger.
C1.ielts_writing: In the face of opposition, the plan was revised.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He showed courage in the face of adversity."
C1.mistake: Nicht wörtlich "im Gesicht von"; bedeutet "angesichts".

C1.def: at almost the same moment, often saying opposite things
C1.example: He praised her and in the same breath criticized her work.
C1.ielts_writing: You can't claim to value honesty and in the same breath lie.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They said yes and no in the same breath."
C1.mistake: Oft bei Widersprüchen: "in the same breath" bedeutet "im selben Atemzug".

C1.def: at the correct musical pitch, or in harmony with others
C1.example: The piano is not in tune.
C1.ielts_writing: The manager is in tune with her employees' needs.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "out of tune"; bildlich "in tune WITH sb/sth".

C1.def: without success
C1.example: They searched in vain for survivors.
C1.ielts_writing: His efforts were in vain.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I tried in vain to reach her."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "vain" (eitel) verwechseln; "take someone's name in vain" ist eine Redewendung.

C1.def: a tray for incoming documents
C1.example: She cleared her in-basket.
C1.ielts_writing: The in-basket was overflowing with unopened mail.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "out-basket"; "in-basket exercise" ist ein Assessment-Verfahren.

C1.def: lack of ability to do something
C1.example: His inability to focus worried the teacher.
C1.ielts_writing: The inability to pay led to bankruptcy.
C1.mistake: Präposition: "inability TO + Infinitiv"; Adjektiv "unable".

C1.def: not enough in quality or amount
C1.example: The supplies were inadequate.
C1.ielts_writing: Inadequate funding hindered the research.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inadequate FOR/TO sth"; Nomen "inadequacy".

C1.def: done without intention
C1.example: An inadvertent error caused the delay.
C1.ielts_writing: He made an inadvertent remark.
C1.mistake: Meist Adverb "inadvertently"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: not suitable for a situation
C1.example: His comment was inappropriate.
C1.ielts_writing: Inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "appropriate"; Präposition: "inappropriate FOR sb".

C1.def: something that motivates people to act
C1.example: The tax cut gives companies an incentive to invest.
C1.ielts_writing: Financial incentives encourage employees to work harder.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "incentive TO do sth"; Verb "incentivize".

C1.def: continuing without pause
C1.example: The incessant noise kept me awake.
C1.ielts_writing: Incessant rain delayed the harvest.
C1.mistake: Adverb "incessantly"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: the rate at which something occurs
C1.example: The incidence of the disease has dropped.
C1.ielts_writing: A higher incidence of crime was reported in the area.
C1.mistake: Nicht "incident" (Vorfall); "incidence OF + Ereignis".

C1.def: having a tendency or preference
C1.example: I'm inclined to agree.
C1.ielts_writing: She is inclined to trust people.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "be inclined TO + Infinitiv"; Nomen "inclination".

C1.def: the act of including someone or something
C1.example: The inclusion of all students is a priority.
C1.ielts_writing: Social inclusion improves community well-being.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We support the inclusion of women in leadership."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "exclusion"; Verb "include".

C1.def: including everyone or everything
C1.example: The school promotes an inclusive environment.
C1.ielts_writing: Prices are inclusive of tax.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inclusive OF sth"; Gegenteil: "exclusive".

C1.def: not leading to a clear result
C1.example: The evidence was inconclusive.
C1.ielts_writing: Inconclusive test results required further analysis.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "conclusive"; Adverb "inconclusively".

C1.def: not staying the same, or contradictory
C1.example: His statements were inconsistent.
C1.ielts_writing: Inconsistent results undermined the study's credibility.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inconsistent WITH sth"; Nomen "inconsistency".

C1.def: trouble or discomfort
C1.example: We apologize for any inconvenience.
C1.ielts_writing: The delay caused great inconvenience to passengers.
C1.mistake: Verb "inconvenience sb"; Adjektiv "inconvenient".

C1.def: formed as a legal company, or combined into a whole
C1.example: The firm is incorporated in Delaware.
C1.ielts_writing: The updated terms are incorporated in the contract.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "Inc."; Gegenteil: "unincorporated".

C1.def: a small increase in amount
C1.example: Salaries rise in annual increments.
C1.ielts_writing: Each increment adds five dollars to the fee.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "incremental" (schrittweise); gegen "decrement".

C1.def: to experience something unpleasant as a result of your actions
C1.example: The company incurred heavy losses.
C1.ielts_writing: Late payments incur a penalty fee.
C1.mistake: Meist mit Kosten oder Verlusten: "incur costs/debts"; nicht für positive Dinge.

C1.def: unable to make decisions quickly
C1.example: He was indecisive about the job offer.
C1.ielts_writing: Indecisive leadership can damage a team.
C1.mistake: Nomen "indecision"; Gegenteil: "decisive".

C1.def: for an unlimited period
C1.example: The meeting was postponed indefinitely.
C1.ielts_writing: The flight was delayed indefinitely.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "indefinite"; "indefinitely" bedeutet nicht "unendlich lang", sondern "ohne festes Ende".

C1.def: an alphabetical list, or a measure of change
C1.example: Look up the term in the index.
C1.ielts_writing: The consumer price index rose by two percent.
C1.mistake: Plural "indexes" oder "indices"; "index finger" ist der Zeigefinger.

C1.def: a sign that something exists or is likely
C1.example: There is no indication of improvement.
C1.ielts_writing: Early indications suggest the plan is working.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Give me an indication of the cost."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "indication OF sth" oder "indication THAT"; Verb "indicate".

C1.def: something that shows the state of a situation
C1.example: Unemployment is a key economic indicator.
C1.ielts_writing: The car's indicator shows when the tank is nearly empty.
C1.ielts_speaking: "This is a good indicator of progress."
C1.mistake: Plural "indicators"; auch Warnleuchte im Auto.

C1.def: a formal charge of a crime, or a sign of failure
C1.example: The grand jury issued an indictment.
C1.ielts_writing: The report is a damning indictment of the system.
C1.mistake: "c" ist stumm: /ɪnˈdaɪtmənt/; Verb "indict".

C1.def: originating naturally in a particular place
C1.example: Indigenous peoples have lived here for centuries.
C1.ielts_writing: The plant is indigenous to Africa.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "indigenous TO a region"; Plural "indigenous peoples".

C1.def: to cause something or persuade someone
C1.example: The drug can induce sleep.
C1.ielts_writing: Nothing could induce him to sign.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "induce sb TO do sth"; "induce labor" bedeutet "Geburt einleiten".

C1.def: to allow yourself to enjoy something
C1.example: She indulged in a bubble bath.
C1.ielts_writing: Parents often indulge their grandchildren.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "indulge IN sth"; Nomen "indulgence".

C1.def: not producing the desired result
C1.example: The medicine was ineffective.
C1.ielts_writing: Ineffective policies waste public money.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "inefficient" (verschwenderisch) verwechseln; Gegenteil: "effective".

C1.def: wasting time, money, or energy
C1.example: The old system was inefficient.
C1.ielts_writing: Inefficient processes cost the company millions.
C1.mistake: Nomen "inefficiency"; "ineffective" = wirkungslos, "inefficient" = unwirtschaftlich.

C1.def: an unfair difference between groups
C1.example: Income inequality is rising.
C1.ielts_writing: Gender inequality persists in many fields.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "equality"; Plural "inequalities".

C1.def: well known for something bad
C1.example: The infamous dictator ruled for decades.
C1.ielts_writing: She is infamous for her bad temper.
C1.mistake: Nicht "famous" (berühmt): "infamous" ist negativ; Nomen "infamy".

C1.def: a very young child
C1.example: The infant slept peacefully.
C1.ielts_writing: Infant mortality has declined significantly.
C1.mistake: "in its infancy" bedeutet "in den Kinderschuhen"; Adjektiv "infantile" (kindisch).

C1.def: to pass a disease to someone
C1.example: The virus infected thousands.
C1.ielts_writing: Her enthusiasm infected the whole team.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "infect sb WITH sth"; "infected" auch bei Computern.

C1.def: able to spread easily
C1.example: Measles is highly infectious.
C1.ielts_writing: Her infectious laugh made everyone smile.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich "infectious enthusiasm"; "contagious" ist durch Kontakt, "infectious" allgemein.

C1.def: to conclude from evidence
C1.example: We can infer from the data that sales rose.
C1.ielts_writing: Readers must infer the author's intent.
C1.ielts_speaking: "What can you infer from his silence?"
C1.mistake: Nicht "imply" (andeuten): wer folgert, "infers"; wer andeutet, "implies".

C1.def: without limits or end
C1.example: The universe may be infinite.
C1.ielts_writing: She has infinite patience with children.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "finite"; Nomen "infinity".

C1.def: the basic form of a verb, often with "to"
C1.example: "To run" is an infinitive.
C1.ielts_writing: After "want," the infinitive follows.
C1.mistake: "split infinitive" bedeutet "to boldly go"; "bare infinitive" ist der Infinitiv ohne "to".

C1.def: a general rise in prices
C1.example: Inflation reached seven percent.
C1.ielts_writing: High inflation reduces consumers' purchasing power.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "deflation"; Verb "inflate" (aufblasen).

C1.def: unwilling to change, or unable to bend
C1.example: The manager was inflexible about the schedule.
C1.ielts_writing: Inflexible rules make adapting difficult.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inflexible ABOUT sth"; Gegenteil: "flexible".

C1.def: to cause something unpleasant to be suffered
C1.example: The storm inflicted heavy damage.
C1.ielts_writing: He inflicted injuries on his opponent.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inflict sth ON sb"; negativer Sinn.

C1.def: having great effect on people or events
C1.example: She is an influential writer.
C1.ielts_writing: Influential people shape public opinion.
C1.mistake: Nomen "influence"; Konstruktion: "influential IN doing sth".

C1.def: permission given after being told all relevant facts
C1.example: Patients must give informed consent.
C1.ielts_writing: Informed consent is central to medical ethics.
C1.mistake: Wichtig in Medizin und Forschung; unzählbar.

C1.def: to breathe in
C1.example: Inhale deeply and then exhale slowly.
C1.ielts_writing: Workers inhaled toxic fumes.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "exhale"; Nomen "inhaler" (Inhalator).

C1.def: existing as a basic part of something
C1.example: Risk is inherent in any investment.
C1.ielts_writing: The system has inherent weaknesses.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inherent IN sth"; Adverb "inherently".

C1.def: money or property received from someone who died
C1.example: She received a large inheritance.
C1.ielts_writing: The inheritance was divided among three siblings.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "heritage" (Kulturerbe) verwechseln; "inheritance tax" ist die Erbschaftsteuer.

C1.def: to prevent or slow something
C1.example: Fear can inhibit creativity.
C1.ielts_writing: Certain drugs inhibit growth.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inhibit sb FROM doing sth"; Nomen "inhibition" (Hemmung).

C1.def: to cause something to begin
C1.example: The council initiated a review.
C1.ielts_writing: She initiated the conversation.
C1.mistake: Nomen "initiative" (Initiative); "initiate" auch "einweihen" (Person).

C1.def: to put liquid into the body with a needle
C1.example: The nurse injected the vaccine.
C1.ielts_writing: Investors injected millions into the startup.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "inject money INTO sth"; Nomen "injection".

C1.def: a shot of liquid into the body, or a large input of money
C1.example: She received an injection of antibiotics.
C1.ielts_writing: The company received a cash injection from investors.
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "cash injection" (Finanzspritze); Verb "inject".

C1.def: a lack of fairness
C1.example: They protested against the injustice.
C1.ielts_writing: Racial injustice remains a global issue.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "justice"; Adjektiv "unjust".

C1.def: located away from the coast
C1.example: The inland regions are drier.
C1.ielts_writing: Inland areas experienced severe flooding.
C1.mistake: Als Adverb "inland" ohne "to"; Gegenteil: "coastal".

C1.def: a person living in a prison or institution
C1.example: The inmate escaped from custody.
C1.ielts_writing: Inmates are given access to educational programs.
C1.mistake: Auch für Heim- oder Klinikbewohner; Plural "inmates".

C1.def: the state of being not guilty or free from harm
C1.example: He proclaimed his innocence.
C1.ielts_writing: The film captures the innocence of childhood.
C1.mistake: "presumption of innocence" ist die Unschuldsvermutung; Adjektiv "innocent".

C1.def: not harmful or offensive
C1.example: It was an innocuous comment.
C1.ielts_writing: The innocuous-looking email contained a virus.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; nicht mit "innocent" (unschuldig).

C1.def: eager to learn, or too curious about others
C1.example: The inquisitive child asked endless questions.
C1.ielts_writing: Inquisitive reporters crowded around her.
C1.mistake: Kann positiv (wissbegierig) oder negativ (neugierig im Sinne von aufdringlich) sein.

C1.def: not caring about other people's feelings
C1.example: That was an insensitive remark.
C1.ielts_writing: Insensitive handling of the case upset the family.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "insensitive TO sth"; nicht mit "insensible" (bewusstlos).

C1.def: a person with special knowledge from inside an organization
C1.example: An insider leaked the documents.
C1.ielts_writing: Industry insiders predicted the merger.
C1.mistake: "insider trading" ist Insiderhandel; Gegenteil: "outsider".

C1.def: to examine something carefully
C1.example: The officer inspected the vehicle.
C1.ielts_writing: Engineers inspect bridges regularly.
C1.mistake: Nomen "inspector" (Prüfer); "inspect sth FOR sth" prüft auf Mängel.

C1.def: a careful check of something
C1.example: The restaurant passed the health inspection.
C1.ielts_writing: A thorough inspection revealed several defects.
C1.mistake: Ähnlich "TÜV" im Alltag: "annual inspection"; Verb "inspect".

C1.def: something that inspires creativity or action
C1.example: The landscape was her inspiration.
C1.ielts_writing: He draws inspiration from nature.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "inspiration FROM sb/sth"; Verb "inspire".

C1.def: happening immediately, or a very short moment
C1.example: The coffee was an instant success.
C1.ielts_writing: In an instant, the lights went out.
C1.mistake: "instant" kann auch "Sofort-" vor Nomen sein; Adverb "instantly".

C1.def: to cause something bad to start
C1.example: He instigated the riot.
C1.ielts_writing: Police instigated an investigation into the fraud.
C1.mistake: Nomen "instigator" (Anstifter); meist negativ.

C1.def: a natural tendency to behave in a particular way
C1.example: Animals act on instinct.
C1.ielts_writing: My instinct told me to leave.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "instinctive"; Aussprache /ˈɪnstɪŋkt/ mit "ng".

C1.def: relating to an organization or establishment
C1.example: Institutional racism is deeply rooted.
C1.ielts_writing: Institutional reforms improved transparency.
C1.mistake: Nomen "institution"; "institutional investors" sind institutionelle Anleger.

C1.def: to order or teach someone
C1.example: The manager instructed staff to leave.
C1.ielts_writing: She instructs students in French.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "instruct sb TO do sth"; Nomen "instruction" (Anweisung).

C1.def: important in making something happen, or relating to musical instruments
C1.example: He was instrumental in the deal.
C1.ielts_writing: The piece is purely instrumental.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Her research was instrumental in finding a cure."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "instrumental IN doing sth"; auch Musik ohne Gesang.

C1.def: not enough
C1.example: The evidence is insufficient.
C1.ielts_writing: Insufficient funding halted the program.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "sufficient"; "insufficient funds" erscheint auf Banküberweisungen.

C1.def: covered with material to reduce heat or electricity loss
C1.example: The attic is well insulated.
C1.ielts_writing: Insulated wires reduce the risk of shocks.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "insulated FROM sth"; Nomen "insulation".

C1.def: a rude remark, or to speak rudely to someone
C1.example: He took her comment as an insult.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't insult my intelligence.
C1.mistake: Nomen betont auf der ersten Silbe, Verb auf der zweiten: /ˈɪnsʌlt/ vs. /ɪnˈsʌlt/.

C1.def: not damaged or changed
C1.example: The painting remained intact.
C1.ielts_writing: Most of the building was left intact.
C1.mistake: Prädikativ: "remain intact"; kein Adverb.

C1.def: the amount taken into the body or a group
C1.example: Limit your sugar intake.
C1.ielts_writing: The college's annual intake is five hundred students.
C1.mistake: "intake" auch Anzahl neuer Studierender; kein Plural.

C1.def: necessary as a basic part
C1.example: Music is integral to the film.
C1.ielts_writing: Trust is an integral part of any relationship.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "integral TO sth"; "integral part" bedeutet "wesentlicher Bestandteil".

C1.def: to combine into a whole, or to become part of a group
C1.example: Schools help immigrants integrate.
C1.ielts_writing: The software integrates with other tools.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "integrate INTO/WITH sth"; Nomen "integration".

C1.def: combined into a unified whole
C1.example: The app has an integrated camera.
C1.ielts_writing: Integrated systems simplify management.
C1.mistake: Oft in der Technik: "integrated circuit" (integrierter Schaltkreis).

C1.def: the process of combining or joining groups or systems
C1.example: Integration of newcomers requires effort.
C1.ielts_writing: Economic integration has deepened across Europe.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "segregation"; Verb "integrate".

C1.def: honesty and strong moral principles, or being whole
C1.example: She is known for her integrity.
C1.ielts_writing: The structural integrity of the bridge was in doubt.
C1.mistake: "structural integrity" bedeutet "bauliche Stabilität"; nicht nur moralisch.

C1.def: relating to the mind and reasoning, or a person who values ideas
C1.example: She enjoys intellectual discussions.
C1.ielts_writing: The intellectual left a mark on the debate.
C1.mistake: "intellectual property" ist geistiges Eigentum; Nomen "intellect" (Verstand).

C1.def: to become or make greater in degree
C1.example: The storm is expected to intensify.
C1.ielts_writing: Efforts to find survivors have intensified.
C1.mistake: Auch intransitiv: "The conflict intensified"; Adjektiv "intense".

C1.def: the quality of being strong or extreme
C1.example: The intensity of the storm surprised us.
C1.ielts_writing: She is known for her intensity on stage.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The intensity of the light was blinding."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "intense"; "high-intensity" bei Training.

C1.def: concentrated on a particular area, or very thorough
C1.example: She took an intensive course in Spanish.
C1.ielts_writing: Intensive care units treat critically ill patients.
C1.mistake: "intensive care" ist die Intensivstation; Endung "-intensive" (z. B. "labor-intensive").

C1.def: the aim or purpose of an action
C1.example: He denied any intent to harm.
C1.ielts_writing: The contract's intent is clear.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She entered with the intent to steal."
C1.mistake: Im Recht: "with intent to"; "letter of intent" ist eine Absichtserklärung.

C1.def: involving communication between user and system
C1.example: The museum has interactive exhibits.
C1.ielts_writing: Interactive lessons keep students engaged.
C1.mistake: Verb "interact"; Nomen "interaction".

C1.def: a device for speaking to people in another room
C1.example: She spoke through the intercom.
C1.ielts_writing: The receptionist announced the guest on the intercom.
C1.mistake: Kurzform von "intercommunication"; Plural "intercoms".

C1.def: a point where two systems meet, or the screen a user sees
C1.example: The app has a simple user interface.
C1.ielts_writing: The interface between hardware and software must be reliable.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "interface with sb/sth" (zusammenarbeiten); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to get involved in something that isn't your business, or to disrupt
C1.example: Don't interfere in their argument.
C1.ielts_writing: Loud music interferes with my concentration.
C1.mistake: Zwei Präpositionen: "interfere IN" (sich einmischen) und "interfere WITH" (stören).

C1.def: unwanted involvement, or noise disrupting a signal
C1.example: Political interference damaged the investigation.
C1.ielts_writing: Radio interference made the call hard to hear.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some interference"; Konstruktion: "interference IN sth".

C1.def: temporary until something permanent is arranged
C1.example: An interim manager took over.
C1.ielts_writing: The interim report outlines early results.
C1.mistake: Auch Nomen "in the interim" (inzwischen); "ad interim" ist lateinisch.

C1.def: inside, or the inner part of something
C1.example: The interior walls were painted white.
C1.ielts_writing: The interior of the car smelled new.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "exterior"; "Department of the Interior" ist das Innenministerium der USA.

C1.def: a word expressing a sudden emotion
C1.example: "Wow!" is an interjection.
C1.ielts_writing: Interjections often stand alone in a sentence.
C1.mistake: Verb "interject" (einwerfen); Wortart wie "Oh" oder "Ouch".

C1.def: between beginner and advanced level
C1.example: She is an intermediate learner of English.
C1.ielts_writing: The intermediate class meets on Tuesdays.
C1.mistake: Oft in Kurs- und Niveaustufen; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: a network of everyday objects connected to the internet
C1.example: The internet of things links sensors and appliances.
C1.ielts_writing: Smart homes rely on the internet of things.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Security is a concern for the internet of things."
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "IoT"; Singular, nicht "internets".

C1.def: a temporary position for gaining work experience
C1.example: She did a summer internship at a bank.
C1.ielts_writing: Internships provide valuable career experience.
C1.mistake: Person: "intern"; Plural "internships".

C1.def: an explanation of the meaning of something
C1.example: Her interpretation of the poem was original.
C1.ielts_writing: The interpretation of the data requires care.
C1.mistake: "open to interpretation" bedeutet "auslegungsfähig"; Dolmetscher: "interpreter".

C1.def: to become involved to change a situation
C1.example: Police intervened in the dispute.
C1.ielts_writing: The government will intervene if prices rise.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "intervene IN sth"; Nomen "intervention".

C1.def: action taken to change a situation
C1.example: Medical intervention saved his life.
C1.ielts_writing: Government intervention in the market is controversial.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "intervention IN sth"; "early intervention" ist Frühförderung.

C1.def: a person being interviewed
C1.example: The interviewee answered every question calmly.
C1.ielts_writing: Each interviewee was asked the same questions.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "interviewer"; Betonung auf der letzten Silbe.

C1.def: private and close, or very personal
C1.example: They had an intimate dinner.
C1.ielts_writing: She shared intimate details of her life.
C1.mistake: Nomen "intimacy"; "intimate knowledge" bedeutet "genaue Kenntnis".

C1.def: unwilling to accept different views or behavior
C1.example: He is intolerant of criticism.
C1.ielts_writing: Intolerant attitudes hinder dialogue.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "intolerant OF sth"; "lactose intolerant" ist Laktoseintoleranz.

C1.def: the rise and fall of the voice in speaking
C1.example: Rising intonation signals a question.
C1.ielts_writing: Intonation can change the meaning of a sentence.
C1.mistake: Verb "intone" (feierlich sprechen); wichtig für Aussprache.

C1.def: a verb that does not take a direct object
C1.example: "Sleep" is an intransitive verb.
