C1.ielts_writing: Intransitive verbs cannot be used in the passive voice.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "transitive verb"; ohne Akkusativobjekt.

C1.def: interested and curious
C1.example: I'm intrigued by her proposal.
C1.ielts_writing: Intrigued readers asked for more details.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "intrigued BY sth"; Nomen "intrigue" auch Intrige.

C1.def: arousing curiosity or interest
C1.example: It's an intriguing idea.
C1.ielts_writing: The story has an intriguing twist.
C1.mistake: Nicht "intrigant" im Deutschen; "intriguing" ist positiv.

C1.def: belonging naturally to something
C1.example: The painting has intrinsic value.
C1.ielts_writing: Intrinsic motivation comes from within.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "extrinsic"; Konstruktion: "intrinsic TO sth".

C1.def: to overwhelm with a large number of things
C1.example: The office was inundated with calls.
C1.ielts_writing: Residents were inundated by floodwater.
C1.mistake: Meist Passiv: "be inundated WITH sth"; bildlich für große Menge.

C1.def: not legally or officially acceptable
C1.example: The ticket is invalid.
C1.ielts_writing: An invalid password prevented access.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Nomen "invalid" (/ˈɪnvəlɪd/) bedeutet "Kranke(r)".

C1.def: something newly created, or the act of creating
C1.example: The telephone was a great invention.
C1.ielts_writing: The invention of the printing press changed history.
collocations: necessity is the mother of invention
C1.mistake: Sprichwort: "Necessity is the mother of invention"; Verb "invent".

C1.def: a person who examines something to discover facts
C1.example: Investigators examined the crime scene.
C1.ielts_writing: A private investigator was hired to find the missing man.
C1.mistake: Verb "investigate"; Nomen "investigation".

C1.def: impossible to see
C1.example: The virus is invisible to the naked eye.
C1.ielts_writing: Invisible barriers exist in many workplaces.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "visible"; "invisible hand" ist Adam Smiths "unsichtbare Hand".

C1.def: a document listing goods or services and their cost
C1.example: Please send the invoice by Friday.
C1.ielts_writing: The invoice must include the tax number.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb: "invoice sb FOR sth"; "bill" ist die Rechnung im Restaurant.

C1.def: to cite as authority, or to call forth
C1.example: The lawyer invoked the Fifth Amendment.
C1.ielts_writing: The song invokes memories of childhood.
C1.mistake: Nicht "evoke" (wachrufen) verwechseln; "invoke" ist rechtlich oder rituell.

C1.def: the act of taking part or being connected with something
C1.example: His involvement in the crime was proven.
C1.ielts_writing: Parental involvement improves student success.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "involvement IN sth"; Verb "involve".

C1.def: the colored part of the eye, or a flowering plant
C1.example: Her iris is a bright green.
C1.ielts_writing: Irises bloom in late spring.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Auge und Blume; "iris scan" ist ein Sicherheitsverfahren.

C1.def: the period when iron tools replaced bronze
C1.example: Iron Age tribes built hill forts.
C1.ielts_writing: The Iron Age followed the Bronze Age.
C1.mistake: Groß geschrieben als Epoche; folgt auf die "Bronze Age".

C1.def: using words to mean the opposite, or odd in outcome
C1.example: It's ironic that the fire station burned down.
C1.ielts_writing: Her ironic remark made everyone laugh.
C1.mistake: Nicht "ironisch" im harmlosen Sinn: "ironic" beschreibt oft eine Wendung des Schicksals.

C1.def: in a way that is the opposite of what is expected
C1.example: Ironically, the best meal was at the cheapest place.
C1.ielts_writing: He was, ironically, late for the punctuality award.
C1.mistake: Satzadverb am Satzanfang; "ironically enough" ist typisch.

C1.def: use of words to mean the opposite, or an odd twist of fate
C1.example: The irony of the situation was clear.
C1.ielts_writing: Dramatic irony is common in Shakespeare.
C1.mistake: "dramatic irony" ist dramatische Ironie; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: not connected with the subject
C1.example: Your age is irrelevant.
C1.ielts_writing: Irrelevant details distracted the audience.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "irrelevant TO sth"; Nomen "irrelevance".

C1.def: impossible to change back
C1.example: The damage is irreversible.
C1.ielts_writing: Irreversible decisions require careful thought.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "reversible"; Adverb "irreversibly".

C1.def: a monotheistic religion based on the teachings of Muhammad
C1.example: Islam is practiced by over a billion people.
C1.ielts_writing: The history of Islam spans more than fourteen centuries.
C1.mistake: Immer großgeschrieben; Gläubige: "Muslims"; Adjektiv "Islamic".

C1.def: the state of being separate from others
C1.example: The village lives in isolation.
C1.ielts_writing: Prolonged isolation can harm mental health.
C1.mistake: "in isolation" bedeutet "für sich allein"; Verb "isolate".

C1.def: an important topic or problem, or to officially provide
C1.example: Climate change is a pressing issue.
C1.ielts_writing: The agency issues passports to citizens.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The latest issue of the magazine arrived."
C1.mistake: Nicht "Issue" als Ausgabe: auch "magazine issue"; "issue a warning" bedeutet "eine Warnung aussprechen".

C1.def: a planned route or schedule for a journey
C1.example: The itinerary includes three cities.
C1.ielts_writing: Our itinerary changed because of the strike.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Plural "itineraries".

C1.def: a large spotted cat from Central and South America
C1.example: A jaguar prowled through the rainforest.
C1.ielts_writing: Jaguars are strong swimmers and excellent hunters.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈdʒæɡjuːər/; auch Automarke.

C1.def: a person employed to take care of a building
C1.example: The janitor locked the school.
C1.ielts_writing: Janitors clean and maintain public buildings.
C1.mistake: Plural "janitors"; Adjektiv "janitorial".

C1.def: specialized words used by a group
C1.example: Legal jargon confuses many people.
C1.ielts_writing: The report is full of technical jargon.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some jargon"; oft leicht abwertend.

C1.def: the bone that forms the lower jaw
C1.example: The boxer broke his jawbone.
C1.ielts_writing: A jawbone fragment was found at the dig site.
C1.mistake: Fachsprachlich "mandible"; Plural "jawbones".

C1.def: a feeling of resentment toward someone's success or relationship
C1.example: Jealousy ruined their friendship.
C1.ielts_writing: Professional jealousy is common in competitive fields.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "jealous OF sb"; "green with jealousy" bedeutet "grün vor Neid".

C1.def: a small rugged vehicle for rough terrain
C1.example: They drove a jeep across the desert.
C1.ielts_writing: The military used jeeps for reconnaissance.
C1.mistake: Ursprünglich Markenname, heute Alltagswort; Plural "jeeps".

C1.def: the central figure of Christianity
C1.example: Jesus is central to Christian belief.
C1.ielts_writing: Many artists have depicted the life of Jesus.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The church celebrates the birth of Jesus."
C1.mistake: Immer großgeschrieben; "Jesus Christ" ist Titel und Name.

C1.def: a person who makes or sells jewelry
C1.example: The jeweler repaired the necklace.
C1.ielts_writing: A local jeweler designed her engagement ring.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I took my watch to the jeweler."
C1.mistake: Nomen "jewelry" (Schmuck, unzählbar); Aussprache /ˈdʒuːələr/.

C1.def: running at a steady, gentle pace for exercise
C1.example: Jogging improves cardiovascular fitness.
C1.ielts_writing: She takes up jogging every morning in the park.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I go jogging three times a week."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "go jogging"; Verb "jog".

C1.def: shared by two or more people, or the place where bones meet
C1.example: They opened a joint account.
C1.ielts_writing: My knee joint hurts.
C1.mistake: Auch umgangssprachlich "Joint" (Lokal oder Zigarette); "joint venture" ist ein Gemeinschaftsunternehmen.

C1.def: happy and cheerful
C1.example: He was a jolly old man.
C1.ielts_writing: The party had a jolly atmosphere.
C1.mistake: Als Adverb in älteren Texten verstärkend; "jolly" ist heute eher altmodisch.

C1.def: to write something quickly
C1.example: Jot down my number before you forget.
C1.ielts_writing: She jotted down a few ideas during the meeting.
C1.mistake: Trennbar: "jot sth down" oder "jot down sth"; Nomen "jotting" (Notiz).

C1.def: feeling or causing great happiness
C1.example: The children sang a joyful song.
C1.ielts_writing: It was a joyful reunion after years apart.
C1.mistake: Nomen "joy"; Adverb "joyfully".

C1.def: feeling great happiness because of success
C1.example: The fans were jubilant after the win.
C1.ielts_writing: Jubilant crowds filled the streets.
C1.mistake: Nomen "jubilation"; "jubilee" ist ein Jubiläum.

C1.def: too quick to criticize others
C1.example: Don't be so judgmental.
C1.ielts_writing: A judgmental attitude can alienate friends.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt judged by her judgmental stare."
C1.mistake: Hat eine negative Konnotation; Nomen "judgment" (Urteil).

C1.def: relating to courts and justice
C1.example: The judicial branch interprets the law.
C1.ielts_writing: A judicial review overturned the decision.
C1.mistake: Nomen "judiciary" (Justizwesen); nicht mit "judicious" (klug) verwechseln.

C1.def: a machine that plays music when coins are inserted
C1.example: He put a coin in the jukebox.
C1.ielts_writing: The old diner has a working jukebox.
C1.mistake: Plural "jukeboxes"; typisch für ein Diner.

C1.def: a very large passenger aircraft
C1.example: A jumbo jet landed on the runway.
C1.ielts_writing: The jumbo jet carries over four hundred passengers.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich; bezieht sich oft auf die Boeing 747.

C1.def: a place where roads or railways meet
C1.example: Turn left at the junction.
C1.ielts_writing: The train stopped at a rail junction.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The accident happened at a busy junction."
C1.mistake: "junction" ist auch Fachbegriff; "at a critical junction" bedeutet "an einem kritischen Punkt".

C1.def: the official power to make legal decisions
C1.example: The case falls under federal jurisdiction.
C1.ielts_writing: Each state has jurisdiction over its own schools.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "jurisdiction OVER sb/sth"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: fair and morally right
C1.example: It was a just decision.
C1.ielts_writing: A just society protects the weak.
C1.mistake: Nicht das Adverb "just" (gerade); Adjektiv betont auf der ersten Silbe; Gegenteil "unjust".

C1.def: a reason that makes something acceptable
C1.example: There is no justification for violence.
C1.ielts_writing: He offered a weak justification for the delay.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "justification FOR sth"; Verb "justify".

C1.def: a young person, or relating to young people
C1.example: The juvenile was released to his parents.
C1.ielts_writing: Juvenile courts handle cases involving minors.
C1.mistake: Auch abwertend "kindisch": "juvenile behavior".

C1.def: a young person who commits crimes
C1.example: The juvenile delinquent was sent to a youth facility.
C1.ielts_writing: Programs aim to rehabilitate juvenile delinquents.
C1.mistake: Nomen "juvenile delinquency" (Jugendkriminalität); etwas veralteter Begriff.

C1.def: to place side by side to show contrast
C1.example: The artist juxtaposes old and new images.
C1.ielts_writing: The film juxtaposes wealth and poverty.
C1.mistake: Nomen "juxtaposition"; Konstruktion: "juxtapose A WITH B".

C1.def: a narrow, covered boat paddled with a double-bladed paddle
C1.example: They paddled a kayak across the lake.
C1.ielts_writing: Kayaks are popular for exploring coastal waters.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈkaɪæk/; Sportart "kayaking".

C1.def: having a strong interest or enthusiasm
C1.example: She's keen on tennis.
C1.ielts_writing: He has a keen sense of humor.
C1.mistake: "keen on sth" bedeutet "begeistert von"; "keen eye" heißt "scharfer Blick".

C1.def: to continue communicating with someone
C1.example: Let's keep in touch.
C1.ielts_writing: We kept in touch by email after graduation.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "keep in touch WITH sb"; Gegenteil: "lose touch".

C1.def: a device that opens a lock, or very important
C1.example: I lost my house key.
C1.ielts_writing: Communication is key to success.
C1.mistake: Als Adjektiv "key" vor Nomen: "key factor"; Musik: auch Tonart.

C1.def: a small set of buttons for entering numbers
C1.example: Enter the code on the keypad.
C1.ielts_writing: The door has a keypad lock.
C1.mistake: Plural "keypads"; nicht mit "keyboard" (Tastatur) verwechseln.

C1.def: a light brownish-green color, or fabric of that color
C1.example: He wore khaki pants.
C1.ielts_writing: The soldiers' khaki uniforms blended into the landscape.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈkæki/ mit hartem "k"; Plural "khakis" für Hosen.

C1.def: to take someone away illegally by force
C1.example: Armed men kidnapped the businessman.
C1.ielts_writing: The child was kidnapped from the park.
C1.mistake: Nomen "kidnapper" (Entführer).

C1.def: an organ that filters blood and produces urine
C1.example: She donated a kidney.
C1.ielts_writing: Kidney disease can lead to dialysis.
C1.mistake: Medizinisch Adjektiv "renal"; auch Speise: "kidney beans".

C1.def: a unit of data equal to about one thousand bytes
C1.example: The file is only fifty kilobytes.
C1.ielts_writing: A kilobyte is roughly one thousand characters of text.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "KB"; kleinste der gängigen Einheiten vor "megabyte".

C1.def: a country ruled by a king or queen, or a division in nature
C1.example: The kingdom was ruled by a wise queen.
C1.ielts_writing: The animal kingdom includes millions of species.
C1.mistake: Biologie: "animal kingdom" (Tierreich); "kingdom come" ist Jenseits.

C1.def: a small booth that sells goods or provides services
C1.example: She bought a newspaper at the kiosk.
C1.ielts_writing: Self-service kiosks reduced waiting times.
C1.mistake: Heute oft elektronisch: "digital kiosk"; Plural "kiosks".

C1.def: to make fabric by looping yarn together
C1.example: She knits sweaters for her grandchildren.
C1.ielts_writing: He knitted a scarf over the winter.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: knit, knit/knitted, knit/knitted; "knit one's brows" heißt "die Stirn runzeln".

C1.def: having a lot of knowledge
C1.example: The guide was very knowledgeable.
C1.ielts_writing: A knowledgeable teacher can inspire curiosity.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "knowledgeable ABOUT sth"; Stumm "k" im Nomen "knowledge".

C1.def: a small orange citrus fruit eaten whole
C1.example: She added kumquats to the salad.
C1.ielts_writing: Kumquats have an edible sweet rind and tart pulp.
C1.mistake: Wird mit Schale gegessen; Plural "kumquats".

C1.def: work, especially hard physical work, or workers as a group
C1.example: Labor costs are rising.
C1.ielts_writing: The union represents skilled labor.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The baby was born after twelve hours of labor."
C1.mistake: Auch Wehen bei Geburt: "in labor"; "Labor Day" ist der Tag der Arbeit in den USA.

C1.def: a person doing unskilled physical work
C1.example: The laborer carried bricks to the site.
C1.ielts_writing: Day laborers wait on street corners for work.
C1.mistake: Plural "laborers"; von "labor" (Arbeit).

C1.def: the supply and demand for workers
C1.example: The labor market is tightening.
C1.ielts_writing: A strong labor market lowers unemployment.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Young people face a tough labor market."
C1.mistake: "job market" ist umgangssprachlicher; kein Plural.

C1.def: a boy or young man
C1.example: The lad ran down the street.
C1.ielts_writing: The coach praised the young lad for his effort.
C1.mistake: Weiblich: "lass"; kommt vor allem in Erzählungen vor.

C1.def: to express sadness or regret about something
C1.example: Critics lament the loss of traditional skills.
C1.ielts_writing: She lamented her lost youth.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They lament the decline of local shops."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "lament THAT" oder "lament sth"; Adjektiv "lamentable" (beklagenswert).

C1.def: a person who rents property to others
C1.example: The landlord raised the rent.
C1.ielts_writing: Landlords must maintain safe living conditions.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "tenant"; weiblich "landlady".

C1.def: a recognizable building or a very important event
C1.example: The Eiffel Tower is a famous landmark.
C1.ielts_writing: The ruling was a landmark in civil rights.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw landmarks all over the city."
C1.mistake: "landmark decision/ruling" bedeutet "wegweisende Entscheidung".

C1.def: the flat area above the thighs when sitting, or one circuit of a track
C1.example: The cat curled up in her lap.
C1.ielts_writing: He completed ten laps around the track.
C1.mistake: "lap sth up" bedeutet "etwas genüsslich aufnehmen"; auch "laptop".

C1.def: involving a great number or wide range
C1.example: The city launched a large-scale cleanup.
C1.ielts_writing: Large-scale protests spread across the country.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "small-scale"; mit Bindestrich vor Nomen.

C1.def: an Italian dish of pasta layers, sauce, and cheese
C1.example: We had lasagna for dinner.
C1.ielts_writing: Lasagna is best served with a fresh salad.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar.

C1.def: a device producing an intense beam of light
C1.example: Doctors used a laser during surgery.
C1.ielts_writing: Laser technology is used in printers and scanners.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The laser beam cut through the metal."
C1.mistake: Akronym aus "light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation"; Aussprache /ˈleɪzər/.

C1.def: the distance north or south of the equator, or freedom of action
C1.example: The city lies at forty degrees north latitude.
C1.ielts_writing: The manager has wide latitude to make decisions.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "longitude"; bildlich "have latitude" (Handlungsspielraum).

C1.def: the second of two things mentioned, or nearer the end
C1.example: Of tea and coffee, I prefer the latter.
C1.ielts_writing: In the latter half of the year, sales rose.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "former"; nur bei zwei Dingen, nicht bei mehreren.

C1.def: deserving praise
C1.example: Their goal is laudable.
C1.ielts_writing: It is laudable that she volunteers.
C1.mistake: Verb "laud" (loben); nicht mit "loud" (laut) verwechseln.

C1.def: an area of closely cut grass
C1.example: He mows the lawn every week.
C1.ielts_writing: The house has a large front lawn.
C1.mistake: Verb "mow the lawn" (Rasen mähen); Plural "lawns".

C1.def: a legal case brought to court
C1.example: She filed a lawsuit against the company.
C1.ielts_writing: A class-action lawsuit was filed on behalf of customers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They settled the lawsuit out of court."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "file a lawsuit AGAINST sb"; kürzer "suit".

C1.def: the way parts are arranged on a page or in a space
C1.example: The magazine has a clean layout.
C1.ielts_writing: The layout of the office encourages teamwork.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar oder Zählbar: "a layout"; bei Webdesign wichtig.

C1.def: a short stay between two flights
C1.example: We had a six-hour layover in Chicago.
C1.ielts_writing: A long layover can be used to explore the city.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "a layover IN + Stadt"; kein Direktflug.

C1.def: the position in front, or to guide or direct
C1.example: Our team has a two-point lead.
C1.ielts_writing: She leads a team of ten engineers.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: lead, led, led; "lead" als Metall wird /led/ gesprochen.

C1.def: the most important news story
C1.example: The election was the lead story.
C1.ielts_writing: The lead story dominated the evening news.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Today's lead story is about the economy."
C1.mistake: In Zeitungen der prominenteste Artikel; Plural "lead stories".

C1.def: to escape through a hole, or to reveal secret information
C1.example: The roof leaks when it rains.
C1.ielts_writing: Someone leaked the report to the press.
C1.mistake: Auch Journalismus: "leak sth TO sb"; Nomen "leak" (Leck, Datenleck).

C1.def: a long jump, or a sudden large change
C1.example: The cat leapt onto the table.
C1.ielts_writing: The discovery was a giant leap for science.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: leap, leapt/leaped; "leap year" ist ein Schaltjahr.

C1.def: a year with an extra day, February 29
C1.example: The next leap year is in four years.
C1.ielts_writing: Leap years keep the calendar aligned with the seasons.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She was born on a leap year."
C1.mistake: Alle vier Jahre; "leap day" ist der 29. Februar.

C1.def: time away from work, or to go away from a place
C1.example: She is on maternity leave.
C1.ielts_writing: He decided to leave the company.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig als Verb: leave, left, left; Nomen "leave" bedeutet Urlaub oder Erlaubnis.

C1.def: a long vegetable of the onion family
C1.example: She added leeks to the soup.
C1.ielts_writing: Leeks have a milder flavor than onions.
C1.mistake: Nicht "leak" (Leck); gleiche Aussprache.

C1.def: something handed down from the past
C1.example: The artist left a lasting legacy.
C1.ielts_writing: The legacy of colonialism still shapes politics.
C1.mistake: "legacy system" ist ein Altsystem in der IT; Plural "legacies".

C1.def: the act of making something legal
C1.example: The legalization of the drug was debated.
C1.ielts_writing: Legalization of same-sex marriage passed in several states.
C1.mistake: Verb "legalize"; Gegenteil: "prohibition".

C1.def: famous and admired for a long time
C1.example: He is a legendary guitarist.
C1.ielts_writing: The band's legendary concerts drew huge crowds.
C1.mistake: Nomen "legend"; umgangssprachlich oft "legendär" als Lob.

C1.def: to make laws
C1.example: Congress may legislate on the matter.
C1.ielts_writing: Parliaments legislate to protect consumers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They want to legislate against hate speech."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "legislate AGAINST/ON/FOR sth"; Nomen "legislator".

C1.def: laws collectively, or the process of making them
C1.example: New legislation will protect workers.
C1.ielts_writing: The legislation was passed in March.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some legislation"; Einzelgesetz: "a law" oder "a bill".

C1.def: relating to making laws
C1.example: The legislative branch makes laws.
C1.ielts_writing: Legislative reforms changed the voting system.
C1.mistake: Gewaltenteilung: "legislative, executive, judicial".

C1.def: a body that makes laws
C1.example: The state legislature passed the budget.
C1.ielts_writing: A bicameral legislature has two chambers.
C1.mistake: "state legislature" ist der Landtag; Plural "legislatures".

C1.def: allowed by law, or reasonable
C1.example: She raised a legitimate concern.
C1.ielts_writing: The government lost its legitimate authority.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "illegitimate"; Nomen "legitimacy".

C1.def: things people do for enjoyment in their free time
C1.example: Popular leisure activities include hiking and reading.
C1.ielts_writing: The center offers a range of leisure activities for seniors.
C1.mistake: Singular: "leisure activity"; "leisure" bedeutet Freizeit, unzählbar.

C1.def: time free from work or duties
C1.example: She spends her leisure time painting.
C1.ielts_writing: Leisure time has increased in recent decades.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "at your leisure" bedeutet "in Ruhe".

C1.def: long, often boringly so
C1.example: The lengthy meeting tired everyone.
C1.ielts_writing: A lengthy report followed the investigation.
C1.mistake: Nicht "lange" im neutralen Sinn: "lengthy" impliziert zu lang.

C1.def: in a gentle way that is not strict
C1.example: The judge treated him leniently.
C1.ielts_writing: Parents who deal leniently with rules may raise problems.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "lenient"; Nomen "leniency".

C1.def: a curved piece of glass or plastic that focuses light
C1.example: The camera has a wide-angle lens.
C1.ielts_writing: The lens of the eye focuses light on the retina.
C1.mistake: Plural "lenses"; bildlich: "through the lens of" (aus der Perspektive von).

C1.def: a small edible seed of a legume
C1.example: She cooked a pot of lentil soup.
C1.ielts_writing: Lentils are rich in protein and fiber.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "lens" (optische Linse) verwechseln; meist Plural "lentils".

C1.def: a woman attracted to other women
C1.example: She is a lesbian activist.
C1.ielts_writing: The film portrays a lesbian couple.
C1.mistake: Als Selbstbezeichnung üblich; Nomen "lesbianism" selten.

C1.def: smaller in size or importance
C1.example: He was charged with a lesser offense.
C1.ielts_writing: Lesser known artists deserve attention.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "the lesser of two evils"; nicht "lesser" mit "less" verwechseln.

C1.def: able to cause death
C1.example: The snake's venom is lethal.
C1.ielts_writing: Lethal weapons were confiscated.
C1.mistake: "lethal injection" ist die Giftspritze; Adverb "lethally".

C1.def: lacking energy and enthusiasm
C1.example: The heat made everyone lethargic.
C1.ielts_writing: She felt lethargic after the long flight.
C1.mistake: Nomen "lethargy"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to become steady after a period of change
C1.example: Prices should level out next year.
C1.ielts_writing: The plane leveled out at thirty thousand feet.
C1.mistake: Auch transitiv: "level sth out"; "level off" ist ähnlich.

C1.def: a tax or fee, or to impose one
C1.example: The government imposed a levy on plastic bags.
C1.ielts_writing: Authorities levied a fine on the company.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "levy sth ON sb/sth"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: an abbreviation for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer
C1.example: The group supports LGBTQ rights.
C1.ielts_writing: LGBTQ visibility has increased in the media.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung wird buchstabiert; oft mit Plus: "LGBTQ+".

C1.def: legally responsible, or likely to do something
C1.example: The owner is liable for any damage.
C1.ielts_writing: Prices are liable to change.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "liable FOR sth" (haftbar) und "liable TO + Infinitiv" (neigen zu); Nomen "liability".

C1.def: open to new ideas, or generous
C1.example: She holds liberal views.
C1.ielts_writing: A liberal portion of sauce covered the pasta.
C1.mistake: In den USA oft politisch links; "liberal arts" sind Geistes- und Sozialwissenschaften.

C1.def: a political philosophy that values individual freedom
C1.example: Classical liberalism emphasizes free markets.
C1.ielts_writing: Liberalism shaped modern democracy.
C1.mistake: Nomen zu "liberal"; "neoliberalism" ist Weiterentwicklung.

C1.def: the freedom to act or think without restriction
C1.example: They fought for liberty.
C1.ielts_writing: The prisoner was at liberty to leave.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Give me liberty or give me death."
C1.mistake: "at liberty to do sth" heißt "befugt"; "take liberties with" bedeutet "sich Freiheiten herausnehmen".

C1.def: to give official permission
C1.example: The state licenses doctors.
C1.ielts_writing: Only licensed drivers may rent a car.
C1.mistake: Nomen und Verb mit gleicher Schreibung "license"; "licensed" ist "zugelassen".

C1.def: a boat used to save people at sea
C1.example: Passengers boarded the lifeboat.
C1.ielts_writing: The ship carries enough lifeboats for everyone.
C1.mistake: Plural "lifeboats"; oft Einrichtung der Seenotrettung.

C1.def: a person employed to watch swimmers and rescue them
C1.example: The lifeguard blew his whistle.
C1.ielts_writing: Lifeguards must be trained in first aid.
C1.mistake: Auch "pool lifeguard"; Plural "lifeguards".

C1.def: lasting for a whole lifetime
C1.example: They are lifelong friends.
C1.ielts_writing: A lifelong passion for music shaped her career.
C1.mistake: Ein Wort; nicht "life-long" mit Bindestrich in modernem Text.

C1.def: continuing to learn throughout life
C1.example: Lifelong learning keeps the mind active.
C1.ielts_writing: Employers support lifelong learning to keep skills current.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Konzept in Bildungspolitik.

C1.def: to leave the ground, as a rocket or plane
C1.example: The rocket lifted off at dawn.
C1.ielts_writing: The helicopter lifts off from the roof.
C1.mistake: Nomen "liftoff" (Start, einer Rakete); bei Flugzeugen "take off".

C1.def: a tower with a bright light to guide ships
C1.example: The lighthouse stood on the cliff.
C1.ielts_writing: Lighthouses warn ships of dangerous rocks.
C1.mistake: "lighthouse keeper" ist der Leuchtturmwärter; Plural "lighthouses".

C1.def: used to emphasize something strongly
C1.example: He ran like hell to catch the bus.
C1.ielts_writing: It hurt like hell when I stubbed my toe.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'm going to fight like hell for this."
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich und derb; vermeiden im formellen Kontext.

C1.def: the chance that something will happen
C1.example: There is a high likelihood of rain.
C1.ielts_writing: The likelihood of success is small.
C1.mistake: "in all likelihood" bedeutet "höchstwahrscheinlich"; Konstruktion: "likelihood OF doing sth".

C1.def: an arm, leg, or large branch
C1.example: She lost a limb in the accident.
C1.ielts_writing: A dead limb fell from the tree.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Out on a limb, he supported the plan."
C1.mistake: "out on a limb" bedeutet "sich weit aus dem Fenster lehnen"; "b" ist stumm.

C1.def: a rule or condition that limits something
C1.example: The study has several limitations.
C1.ielts_writing: Age is not a limitation for learning.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural "limitations"; Verb "limit".

C1.def: a large, luxurious car
C1.example: They arrived by limo.
C1.ielts_writing: The bride rode in a white limo.
C1.mistake: Kurzform von "limousine"; Plural "limos".

C1.def: a group of performers or players selected for an event
C1.example: The festival announced its line-up.
C1.ielts_writing: The team changed its starting line-up.
C1.mistake: Auch "lineup" ohne Bindestrich; Plural "line-ups".

C1.def: arranged in a straight line, or progressing in steps
C1.example: The graph shows a linear increase.
C1.ielts_writing: Linear thinking can limit creativity.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "nonlinear"; Mathematik: "linear equation".

C1.def: to stay longer than expected
C1.example: Guests lingered after dinner.
C1.ielts_writing: The smell of smoke lingered in the room.
C1.mistake: "linger on" bedeutet "fortbestehen"; Adjektiv "lingering" (anhaltend).

C1.def: relating to language
C1.example: She has strong linguistic skills.
C1.ielts_writing: Linguistic diversity enriches culture.
C1.mistake: Nomen "linguistics"; Person "linguist".

C1.def: a list of items, or an entry in a list
C1.example: The listing includes prices and photos.
C1.ielts_writing: Check the TV listings for tonight's films.
C1.mistake: Plural "listings" oft für Programmübersicht; Verb "list".

C1.def: the ability to read and write
C1.example: Literacy rates have improved.
C1.ielts_writing: Digital literacy is essential in modern workplaces.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "illiteracy"; neuere Bedeutungen: "media literacy".

C1.def: able to read and write
C1.example: Most adults in the country are literate.
C1.ielts_writing: A literate population is key to development.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "illiterate"; "-literate" bildet Komposita wie "computer-literate".

C1.def: written works valued for artistic merit
C1.example: She studies English literature.
C1.ielts_writing: Modern literature explores identity and change.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "literary"; auch "Fachliteratur": "scientific literature".

C1.def: categories of literary works
C1.example: Poetry and drama are major literature genres.
C1.ielts_writing: Students analyze different literature genres in class.
C1.mistake: Mehrzahl; Gattung = "genre"; Aussprache "genre" /ˈʒɑːnrə/.

C1.def: to meet expectations
C1.example: She lived up to her promise.
C1.ielts_writing: The new phone failed to live up to expectations.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I hope I can live up to your standards."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "live up TO + Erwartung"; Gegenteil: "fall short of".

C1.def: a large organ that cleans the blood
C1.example: The liver filters toxins from the blood.
C1.ielts_writing: Excessive alcohol can damage the liver.
C1.mistake: Als Speise unzählbar: "liver and onions"; Adjektiv medizinisch "hepatic".

C1.def: to put things into or onto something
C1.example: The workers loaded the truck.
C1.ielts_writing: The page takes too long to load.
C1.mistake: Auch IT: "the page is loading"; "loaded question" ist eine suggestive Frage.

C1.def: an entrance hall, or a group that tries to influence politicians
C1.example: We waited in the hotel lobby.
C1.ielts_writing: Environmental groups lobby the government for stricter laws.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "lobby FOR/AGAINST sth"; Person: "lobbyist".

C1.def: to store something in a secure place
C1.example: She locked away the jewelry.
C1.ielts_writing: Criminals are locked away for years.
C1.mistake: Trennbar: "lock sth away"; bildlich auch "inhaftieren".

C1.def: to record events, or a thick piece of wood
C1.example: Please log your hours each day.
C1.ielts_writing: Users must log in to access the site.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verbs: "log in/out/on"; Nomen "log" auch Logbuch oder Baumstamm.

C1.def: cutting down trees, or recording data
C1.example: Illegal logging destroys forests.
C1.ielts_writing: Event logging helps administrators find errors.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Forstwirtschaft und IT; Person "logger" (Holzfäller).

C1.def: reasoning based on strict principles
C1.example: The logic of her argument was clear.
C1.ielts_writing: Formal logic is a branch of philosophy.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "logical"; Gegenteil "illogical".

C1.def: covering a long distance
C1.example: They took a long-haul flight to Australia.
C1.ielts_writing: Long-haul truckers spend weeks on the road.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "short-haul"; Bindestrich bei Adjektiv.

C1.def: having existed for a long time
C1.example: They have a long-standing friendship.
C1.ielts_writing: The long-standing dispute remains unresolved.
C1.mistake: Auch zusammengeschrieben "longstanding"; bedeutet "lange bestehend".

C1.def: having been something for a long time
C1.example: He is a long-time supporter of the club.
C1.ielts_writing: A long-time resident remembered the old days.
C1.mistake: Auch "longtime" ohne Bindestrich; steht nur vor Nomen.

C1.def: the distance east or west of the prime meridian
C1.example: The city lies at ten degrees east longitude.
C1.ielts_writing: Longitude and latitude help sailors navigate.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "latitude"; Adjektiv "longitudinal" (Längs-).

C1.def: existing for a long period
C1.example: A longstanding agreement ended last year.
C1.ielts_writing: Longstanding rivalries shape the region's politics.
C1.mistake: Variante zu "long-standing"; steht meist vor dem Nomen.

C1.def: having lasted or been something for a long time
C1.example: My longtime partner supports me.
C1.ielts_writing: The longtime editor retired after thirty years.
C1.mistake: Variante zu "long-time"; nur vor Nomen.

C1.def: to appear as a large threatening shape, or to seem likely to happen
C1.example: Dark clouds loomed over the city.
C1.ielts_writing: A budget crisis looms.
C1.mistake: "loom large" bedeutet "bedrohlich nahe sein"; Nomen "loom" ist ein Webstuhl.

C1.def: crazy or silly
C1.example: He has a loony idea.
C1.ielts_writing: The loony plan never worked.
C1.mistake: Abwertend und umgangssprachlich; kann beleidigend gegenüber psychisch Kranken wirken.

C1.def: a shape formed by a curve crossing itself, or to form such a shape
C1.example: The rope formed a loop.
C1.ielts_writing: The video plays in an endless loop.
C1.mistake: "in the loop" bedeutet "auf dem Laufenden"; "out of the loop" ist das Gegenteil.

C1.def: a place where lost items are kept until claimed
C1.example: I asked at the lost and found.
C1.ielts_writing: The lost and found office returned my umbrella.
collocations: turn in to lost and found
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung; kein Plural; Fundstücke sind "lost items".

C1.def: a person who talks too much, especially about boastful things
C1.example: The loudmouth embarrassed his friends.
C1.ielts_writing: Nobody trusted the loudmouth to keep a secret.
C1.mistake: Abwertend; Adjektiv "loudmouthed".

C1.def: easy to love or like
C1.example: The puppy is lovable.
C1.ielts_writing: He is a lovable rogue.
C1.mistake: Auch "loveable" erlaubt; "lovable" ist die gängige Form.

C1.def: having a low neckline
C1.example: She wore a low-cut dress.
C1.ielts_writing: Low-cut tops are not allowed in the office.
C1.mistake: Auch für Schuhe: "low-cut sneakers"; Gegenteil "high-necked".

C1.def: faithful support for a person or group
C1.example: Customer loyalty is hard to earn.
C1.ielts_writing: His loyalty to the team never wavered.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "loyalty TO sb/sth"; Adjektiv "loyal".

C1.def: an abbreviation for a company with limited liability
C1.example: The firm is registered as Smith Ltd.
C1.ielts_writing: Ltd. after a company name indicates limited liability.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung von "limited"; im US-Geschäftsleben meist "Inc." oder "LLC".

C1.def: clearly expressed or thinking clearly
C1.example: She gave a lucid explanation.
C1.ielts_writing: Despite the illness, he remained lucid.
C1.mistake: "lucid dream" ist ein Klartraum; Nomen "lucidity".

C1.def: completely unreasonable or silly
C1.example: The price is ludicrous.
C1.ielts_writing: A ludicrous rumor spread through the office.
C1.mistake: Adverb "ludicrously"; Aussprache /ˈluːdɪkrəs/.

C1.def: a small solid mass, or to treat as a group
C1.example: She found a lump under her skin.
C1.ielts_writing: Add a lump of butter to the pan.
C1.mistake: "lump sum" ist ein Pauschalbetrag; "lump in one's throat" bedeutet "Kloß im Hals".

C1.def: rich and abundant, especially of plants
C1.example: The valley was lush and green.
C1.ielts_writing: Lush vegetation covered the hillsides.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich auch "Trinker"; hauptsächlich für Vegetation.

C1.def: very comfortable and expensive
C1.example: They stayed in a luxurious hotel.
C1.ielts_writing: The spa offers luxurious treatments.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "luxuriant" (üppig); Nomen "luxury".

C1.def: a broad heavy knife used for cutting plants
C1.example: He cleared the path with a machete.
C1.ielts_writing: Farmers use machetes to harvest sugar cane.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /məˈʃeti/; Plural "machetes".

C1.def: an automatic weapon that fires bullets rapidly
C1.example: Soldiers mounted a machine gun on the truck.
C1.ielts_writing: Machine guns changed warfare in the early twentieth century.
C1.mistake: Plural "machine guns"; Abkürzung "MG" im Deutschen, nicht im Englischen.

C1.def: machines considered as a group
C1.example: Heavy machinery is used in construction.
C1.ielts_writing: The machinery of government can be slow.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some machinery", nicht "a machinery"; bildlich "Apparat".

C1.def: extremely foolish behavior, or serious mental illness
C1.example: It would be madness to try.
C1.ielts_writing: The madness of war scarred a generation.
C1.mistake: "There's method in the madness" ist ein Zitat; "March Madness" ist US-College-Basketball.

C1.def: a periodical with articles and pictures
C1.example: She reads a fashion magazine.
C1.ielts_writing: The magazine publishes a monthly feature on science.
C1.mistake: Auch Magazin einer Schusswaffe; Betonung auf der letzten Silbe.

C1.def: having or seeming to have special powers
C1.example: The evening was magical.
C1.ielts_writing: Children believe in magical creatures.
C1.mistake: Nomen "magic"; Adverb "magically".

C1.def: a judge who handles minor cases
C1.example: The magistrate fined him fifty dollars.
C1.ielts_writing: A magistrate heard the case.
C1.mistake: Untere Gerichtsbarkeit; nicht gleichzusetzen mit "Staatsanwalt".

C1.def: an object that attracts iron
C1.example: The magnet attracted the pins.
C1.ielts_writing: The city is a magnet for tourists.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Keep the magnet away from your phone."
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "a magnet FOR sth" (Anziehungspunkt); Adjektiv "magnetic".

C1.def: having the properties of a magnet, or very attractive
C1.example: The needle follows the magnetic field.
C1.ielts_writing: He has a magnetic personality.
C1.mistake: "magnetic personality" bedeutet "große Anziehungskraft"; Nomen "magnetism".

C1.def: extremely beautiful or impressive
C1.example: The palace is magnificent.
C1.ielts_writing: A magnificent view stretched across the valley.
C1.mistake: Nomen "magnificence"; Aussprache /mæɡˈnɪfɪsənt/.

C1.def: the great size or importance of something
C1.example: They didn't grasp the magnitude of the disaster.
C1.ielts_writing: The earthquake had a magnitude of seven.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The magnitude of the task is huge."
C1.mistake: "order of magnitude" bedeutet "Größenordnung"; Erdbeben: "magnitude" (Stärke).

C1.def: a tree or shrub with large fragrant flowers
C1.example: A magnolia bloomed in the yard.
C1.ielts_writing: Magnolias flower early in spring.
C1.mistake: Plural "magnolias".

C1.def: a woman employed to clean rooms
C1.example: The hotel maid changed the sheets.
C1.ielts_writing: Maids once worked long hours for little pay.
C1.mistake: "maid of honor" ist die Trauzeugin; wirkt heute teils altmodisch.

C1.def: the main part of a country, not including islands
C1.example: The ferry crosses to the mainland.
C1.ielts_writing: Islanders travel to the mainland for supplies.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "island"; "mainland China" ist das chinesische Festland.

C1.def: the ideas and attitudes of most people
C1.example: The band hit the mainstream last year.
C1.ielts_writing: Mainstream media shape public discourse.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "alternative" oder "fringe"; oft bildlich zu "mainstream media".

C1.def: keeping something in good condition
C1.example: The elevator is under maintenance.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular maintenance prevents breakdowns.
C1.mistake: Verb "maintain"; "maintenance" auch Unterhalt (Familienrecht).

C1.def: a student's main field of study, or a military officer
C1.example: My major is biology.
C1.ielts_writing: She majored in English.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "major IN sth" (etwas als Hauptfach studieren); Gegenteil "minor" (Nebenfach).

C1.def: to dismiss an employee because the job is no longer needed
C1.example: The company will make fifty workers redundant.
C1.ielts_writing: Many employees were made redundant during the recession.
C1.mistake: Nomen "redundancy" (Stellenstreichung); Passiv üblich: "be made redundant".

C1.def: to form something, invent something, or reconcile
C1.example: Women make up half of the workforce.
C1.ielts_writing: She made up an excuse.
C1.mistake: Nomen "makeup" (Schminke/Zusammensetzung); "make up for" heißt "wettmachen".

C1.def: a failure to work correctly
C1.example: A malfunction stopped the machine.
C1.ielts_writing: The engine malfunction caused a delay.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb "malfunction"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: intended to harm
C1.example: He spread malicious rumors.
C1.ielts_writing: Malicious software damages computers.
C1.mistake: Nomen "malice" (Bosheit); "malware" ist Schadsoftware.

C1.def: easily shaped, or easily influenced
C1.example: Gold is a malleable metal.
C1.ielts_writing: Children's minds are malleable.
C1.mistake: Nomen "malleability"; Ableitung zum Hammer.

C1.def: relating to managers
C1.example: She holds a managerial position.
C1.ielts_writing: Managerial skills include planning and delegation.
C1.mistake: Nomen "manager"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: an official order or authority to act
C1.example: The president claimed a mandate from voters.
C1.ielts_writing: The agency has a mandate to protect the environment.
C1.mistake: Verb "mandate" (vorschreiben); Adjektiv "mandatory".

C1.def: required by law or rule
C1.example: Attendance is mandatory.
C1.ielts_writing: Mandatory training must be completed by Friday.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "optional"; "mandatory minimum" ist eine Mindeststrafe.

C1.def: to show clearly, or to appear
C1.example: Stress can manifest as headaches.
C1.ielts_writing: The disease manifests itself in several ways.
C1.mistake: Auch Adjektiv "offensichtlich"; Nomen "manifestation"; "manifest" auch Ladungsliste.

C1.def: to control or influence someone cleverly, often unfairly
C1.example: Advertisers manipulate consumers' emotions.
C1.ielts_writing: He manipulated the data to fit his theory.
C1.mistake: Nomen "manipulation"; im Technischen neutral: "manipulate objects".

C1.def: clever or unfair control of people or things
C1.example: Media manipulation shaped public opinion.
C1.ielts_writing: Emotional manipulation can damage relationships.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "manipulative"; Verb "manipulate".

C1.def: a tree with lobed leaves that yields sweet sap
C1.example: The maple turned bright red in the fall.
C1.ielts_writing: Maple syrup comes from the sap of sugar maples.
C1.mistake: "maple syrup" ist Ahornsirup.

C1.def: a hard stone used in sculpture, or a small glass ball
C1.example: The statue was carved from marble.
C1.ielts_writing: The children played with marbles.
C1.mistake: "lose one's marbles" bedeutet "den Verstand verlieren"; Plural "marbles" für das Spiel.

C1.def: a walk by a group to protest, or to walk in step
C1.example: Thousands joined the march to the capital.
C1.ielts_writing: The soldiers march through the town every morning.
C1.mistake: "march on" bedeutet "weitermarschieren"; Monat "March" großgeschrieben.

C1.def: the edge of something, or the amount by which something is won
C1.example: She wrote notes in the margin.
C1.ielts_writing: He won by a narrow margin.
C1.mistake: "margin of error" bedeutet "Fehlerspanne"; Plural "margins".

C1.def: small and not very important
C1.example: There was a marginal improvement.
C1.ielts_writing: Marginal costs rise as production increases.
C1.mistake: Adverb "marginally"; in der Ökonomie "marginal cost" (Grenzkosten).

C1.def: treated as unimportant or excluded from society
C1.example: Marginalized communities often lack resources.
C1.ielts_writing: Policies should not leave marginalized groups behind.
C1.mistake: Verb "marginalize"; Nomen "marginalization".

C1.def: relating to the sea
C1.example: Marine life is diverse in coral reefs.
C1.ielts_writing: Marine biologists study ocean ecosystems.
C1.mistake: Nomen "marine" (Marinesoldat) und "Marine Corps"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: an economic system based on supply and demand
C1.example: The country shifted to a market economy.
C1.ielts_writing: A market economy relies on competition between firms.
C1.mistake: "social market economy" ist die soziale Marktwirtschaft; Gegenteil: "planned economy".

C1.def: a place or arena where goods are bought and sold
C1.example: Ideas compete in the marketplace.
C1.ielts_writing: The company struggles in a crowded marketplace.
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "marketplace of ideas"; Plural "marketplaces".

C1.def: a preserve made from citrus fruit
C1.example: She spread marmalade on her toast.
C1.ielts_writing: Marmalade is traditionally made from bitter oranges.
C1.mistake: Im Deutschen allgemein "Marmelade"; im Englischen nur Zitrusfrüchte.

C1.def: temporary military rule over a region
C1.example: The government declared martial law.
C1.ielts_writing: Martial law was imposed after the coup.
C1.mistake: Immer unzählbar; "martial arts" sind Kampfkünste.

C1.def: having qualities associated with men
C1.example: He has a deep, masculine voice.
C1.ielts_writing: Masculine stereotypes can limit boys' emotions.
C1.mistake: Nomen "masculinity"; nicht dasselbe wie "male" (biologisch).

C1.def: to crush food into a soft mass
C1.example: Mash the potatoes with butter.
C1.ielts_writing: He mashed the bananas for the pancakes.
C1.mistake: "mashed potatoes" ist Kartoffelpüree; Nomen "mash" (Brei).

C1.def: a covering for the face
C1.example: She wore a mask to the party.
C1.ielts_writing: The surgeon put on a mask.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb "mask": "mask one's feelings" (Gefühle verbergen).

C1.def: the killing of many people brutally
C1.example: Villagers survived the massacre.
C1.ielts_writing: The massacre shocked the international community.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb; Aussprache /ˈmæsəkər/, das "cre" wird /kər/.

C1.def: a friend or partner, or to breed
C1.example: He shared a room with his mate.
C1.ielts_writing: Animals mate in the spring.
C1.mistake: Auch "checkmate" beim Schach; "soul mate" ist Seelenverwandte(r).

C1.def: paid time off work for a mother after birth
C1.example: She is on maternity leave.
C1.ielts_writing: Companies must offer maternity leave under the law.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "paternity leave"; Adjektiv "maternal".

C1.def: relating to mathematics
C1.example: The mathematical model predicts growth.
C1.ielts_writing: He has a mathematical mind.
C1.mistake: Nomen "mathematics" (Kurzform "math"); Adverb "mathematically".

C1.def: fully developed, or sensible
C1.example: She is mature for her age.
C1.ielts_writing: The wine matures in oak barrels.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He handled it in a mature way."
C1.mistake: Nomen "maturity"; Gegenteil: "immature".

C1.def: to make as large or great as possible
C1.example: The company seeks to maximize profits.
C1.ielts_writing: We should maximize the space in the kitchen.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "minimize"; Nomen "maximum".

C1.def: a master's degree in business administration
C1.example: She earned an MBA at Harvard.
C1.ielts_writing: An MBA can open doors to leadership roles.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "Master of Business Administration"; als Buchstaben gesprochen.

C1.def: having importance or value
C1.example: They had a meaningful conversation.
C1.ielts_writing: Meaningful work increases job satisfaction.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "meaningless"; Nomen "meaning".

C1.def: the time between two events
C1.example: In the meantime, please wait here.
C1.ielts_writing: The meantime was spent preparing the report.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung "in the meantime" (inzwischen); Adverb "meanwhile".

C1.def: an infectious disease causing a red rash
C1.example: The child caught measles.
C1.ielts_writing: Measles outbreaks follow drops in vaccination.
C1.mistake: Plural-Form, aber Singular verwendet: "Measles is contagious".

C1.def: a pencil with a refillable lead
C1.example: He sketched with a mechanical pencil.
C1.ielts_writing: Mechanical pencils produce a consistent line width.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I need a refill for my mechanical pencil."
C1.mistake: Plural "mechanical pencils"; Mine: "lead".

C1.def: relating to the Middle Ages
C1.example: The town has a medieval castle.
C1.ielts_writing: Medieval literature includes tales of knights.
C1.mistake: Auch "mediaeval" in alten Texten; zeitlich 5. bis 15. Jahrhundert.

C1.def: the practice of focusing the mind
C1.example: She practices meditation daily.
C1.ielts_writing: Meditation reduces stress and improves focus.
C1.mistake: Verb "meditate"; Person "meditator".

C1.def: a unit of computer memory equal to about one million bytes
C1.example: The photo is five megabytes.
C1.ielts_writing: A megabyte holds about a million characters.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "MB"; größer als "kilobyte", kleiner als "gigabyte".

C1.def: a weapon used in close combat
C1.example: The knight carried a melee weapon.
C1.ielts_writing: Video games often include both melee weapons and guns.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "ranged weapon"; Aussprache /ˈmeɪleɪ/.

C1.def: a sequence of musical notes forming a tune
C1.example: The melody was easy to remember.
C1.ielts_writing: The composer wrote a haunting melody.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I can't get the melody out of my head."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "melodic"; im Gegensatz zu "harmony".

C1.def: a humorous image or idea spread online
C1.example: The meme went viral in a day.
C1.ielts_writing: Internet memes reflect cultural trends.
C1.mistake: Plural "memes"; ursprünglich von Richard Dawkins geprägt.

C1.def: a short written message in an office
C1.example: The manager sent a memo to all staff.
C1.ielts_writing: A memo outlined the new policy.
C1.mistake: Langform "memorandum"; Plural "memos".

C1.def: a written account of someone's own life experiences
C1.example: She wrote a memoir about her childhood.
C1.ielts_writing: The politician's memoir became a bestseller.
C1.mistake: Oft Plural "memoirs" für Lebenserinnerungen; Aussprache /ˈmemwɑːr/.

C1.def: worth remembering
C1.example: It was a memorable trip.
C1.ielts_writing: The play ends with a memorable scene.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "forgettable"; Adverb "memorably".

C1.def: something built to remember a person or event
C1.example: They built a memorial to the soldiers.
C1.ielts_writing: The memorial honors victims of the disaster.
C1.mistake: "Memorial Day" ist ein Feiertag in den USA; Verb "memorialize".

C1.def: a person or thing that causes danger or trouble
C1.example: Reckless drivers are a menace.
C1.ielts_writing: The gang became a menace to the neighborhood.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "menacing" (bedrohlich); "public menace" ist eine Gefahr für die Allgemeinheit.

C1.def: an experienced person who advises a younger one
C1.example: She was my mentor at the firm.
C1.ielts_writing: He mentors young entrepreneurs.
C1.mistake: Gegenstück: "mentee"; Nomen "mentorship".

C1.def: goods bought and sold, or products connected to a brand
C1.example: The store sells band merchandise.
C1.ielts_writing: Official merchandise is available at the stadium.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; umgangssprachlich "merch".

C1.def: a person who buys and sells goods
C1.example: The merchant sold silk and spices.
C1.ielts_writing: Online merchants must protect customers' data.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The Merchant of Venice is a play."
C1.mistake: "merchant ship" ist ein Handelsschiff; Adjektiv "mercantile".

C1.def: kindness shown when you could punish
C1.example: The judge showed mercy.
C1.ielts_writing: The prisoners begged for mercy.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We were at the mercy of the weather."
C1.mistake: "at the mercy of" bedeutet "ausgeliefert"; Adjektiv "merciful".

C1.def: nothing more than
C1.example: It was a mere coincidence.
C1.ielts_writing: The mere thought of it scares me.
C1.mistake: Steht nur vor dem Nomen; Superlativ "merest".

C1.def: only or simply
C1.example: I was merely asking.
C1.ielts_writing: It is merely a suggestion.
C1.mistake: Formeller als "just"; Stellung vor dem Verb.

C1.def: to combine into one
C1.example: The two banks will merge next year.
C1.ielts_writing: The rivers merge near the coast.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "merge WITH/INTO sth"; im Verkehr: "merge into traffic".

C1.def: the joining of two companies
C1.example: The merger created a giant firm.
C1.ielts_writing: Regulators approved the merger of the two airlines.
C1.mistake: Feste Verbindung: "mergers and acquisitions" (M&A); Verb "merge".

C1.def: good quality that deserves praise
C1.example: The proposal has some merit.
C1.ielts_writing: She was promoted on merit.
C1.mistake: "on merit" bedeutet "nach Leistung"; Nomen "meritocracy" (Leistungsgesellschaft).

C1.def: an untidy or difficult situation
C1.example: The kitchen was a mess.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't mess with the settings.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I made a mess of the project."
C1.mistake: "mess up" bedeutet "vermasseln"; "mess around" heißt "herumalbern".

C1.def: the chemical processes that keep a body alive
C1.example: A fast metabolism burns calories quickly.
C1.ielts_writing: Exercise speeds up metabolism.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "metabolic"; Verb "metabolize".

C1.def: a bright streak of light from a burning space rock
C1.example: We saw a meteor streak across the sky.
C1.ielts_writing: A meteor burns up when it enters the atmosphere.
C1.mistake: "meteoric rise" bedeutet "kometenhafter Aufstieg"; verglüht in der Atmosphäre.

C1.def: a piece of rock from space that reaches the ground
C1.example: A meteorite landed in the desert.
C1.ielts_writing: Scientists study meteorites to learn about the early solar system.
C1.mistake: Unterschied zu "meteor": Meteorit erreicht den Boden.

C1.def: the science of weather
C1.example: She studied meteorology at university.
C1.ielts_writing: Meteorology uses satellites to predict storms.
C1.mistake: Person: "meteorologist"; nicht mit "meteor" verwechseln.

C1.def: the system of methods used in a study
C1.example: The study's methodology was criticized.
C1.ielts_writing: A sound methodology is essential for reliable results.
C1.mistake: Nicht "method" (einzelne Methode); "methodology" ist das System.

C1.def: showing great attention to detail
C1.example: She keeps meticulous records.
C1.ielts_writing: The meticulous planning paid off.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "meticulous ABOUT sth"; Adverb "meticulously".

C1.def: a measurement system based on meters, grams, and liters
C1.example: Most countries use the metric system.
C1.ielts_writing: The metric system simplifies conversions.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "imperial system"; Einheiten: Meter, Gramm, Liter.

C1.def: a tiny piece of plastic in the environment
C1.example: Microplastics are found in oceans worldwide.
C1.ielts_writing: Fish often ingest microplastics.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural "microplastics"; Umweltthema.

C1.def: a tiny computer chip that processes data
C1.example: The microprocessor controls the device.
C1.ielts_writing: Microprocessors power phones and cars.
C1.mistake: Kurzform "processor"; Plural "microprocessors".

C1.def: twelve o'clock at night
C1.example: The party ended at midnight.
C1.ielts_writing: Midnight struck as the guests left.
C1.mistake: "burn the midnight oil" bedeutet "bis spät in die Nacht arbeiten".

C1.def: the middle of something
C1.example: They found themselves in the midst of a crisis.
C1.ielts_writing: She stood in the midst of the crowd.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "in the midst of"; nicht pluralfähig.

C1.def: the middle of summer
C1.example: Midsummer festivals celebrate the longest day.
C1.ielts_writing: The orchard blooms in midsummer.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "midwinter"; Shakespeare: "A Midsummer Night's Dream".

C1.def: the middle of winter
C1.example: The days are short in midwinter.
C1.ielts_writing: They lit candles in midwinter.
C1.mistake: Oft poetisch: "deep midwinter"; Gegenteil "midsummer".

C1.def: a person who moves to another place for work
C1.example: Migrants cross the border seeking work.
C1.ielts_writing: Migrant workers harvest the crops.
C1.mistake: Nicht "immigrant" (Einwanderer): "migrant" kann vorübergehend sein.

C1.def: movement of people or animals from one place to another
C1.example: Bird migration begins in autumn.
C1.ielts_writing: Labor migration affects local economies.
C1.mistake: Verb "migrate"; auch in der IT: "data migration".

C1.def: a unit of speed
C1.example: The car reached sixty miles per hour.
C1.ielts_writing: Speed limits are posted in miles per hour.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The wind blew at fifty miles per hour."
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "mph"; eine Meile entspricht etwa 1,6 km.

C1.def: an important event in the development of something
C1.example: Graduation is a major milestone.
C1.ielts_writing: The project reached an important milestone.
C1.ielts_speaking: "This is a milestone for the company."
C1.mistake: Wörtlich Meilenstein am Straßenrand; Plural "milestones".

C1.def: aggressively supporting a cause
C1.example: Militant groups attacked the base.
C1.ielts_writing: The militants demanded the release of prisoners.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen oft Bezeichnung für bewaffnete Kämpfer; Nomen "militancy".

C1.def: a group of civilians trained as soldiers
C1.example: The local militia defended the town.
C1.ielts_writing: Armed militias operate in the region.
C1.mistake: Nicht "military": Miliz besteht aus Zivilisten.

C1.def: a building where grain is ground, or a factory
C1.example: The old mill is now a museum.
C1.ielts_writing: Workers at the steel mill went on strike.
C1.mistake: "run of the mill" bedeutet "durchschnittlich"; Verb "mill" (mahlen).

C1.def: a tropical shrub, or a drink of juice and champagne
C1.example: The mimosa blooms with yellow flowers.
C1.ielts_writing: They ordered mimosas with brunch.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Pflanze und Cocktail; Plural "mimosas".

C1.def: a person's attitudes and beliefs
C1.example: A positive mindset helps in difficult times.
C1.ielts_writing: Companies try to develop a growth mindset.
C1.mistake: "growth mindset" ist ein Konzept aus der Psychologie; Plural "mindsets".

C1.def: a small bus for a few passengers
C1.example: The team traveled in a minibus.
C1.ielts_writing: A minibus took guests to the hotel.
C1.mistake: Plural "minibuses"; Fahrzeug für etwa zehn bis zwanzig Personen.

C1.def: very small in amount
C1.example: The damage was minimal.
C1.ielts_writing: Minimal effort is required.
C1.mistake: Verb "minimize"; Nomen "minimum".

C1.def: to reduce to the smallest possible amount
C1.example: We must minimize the risk of injury.
C1.ielts_writing: He tried to minimize his mistakes.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "maximize"; auch am Computer: Fenster minimieren.

C1.def: the process of digging minerals from the earth
C1.example: Coal mining employs thousands.
C1.ielts_writing: Data mining reveals patterns in large databases.
C1.mistake: "data mining" ist Datenanalyse; Person "miner" (Bergmann).

C1.def: a government department, or the work of a priest
C1.example: The ministry announced new regulations.
C1.ielts_writing: She dedicated her life to ministry.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He works at the Ministry of Education."
C1.mistake: Auch "ministry" bei Kirche: Pfarr- und Seelsorgedienst.

C1.def: extremely small, or very detailed
C1.example: The minute details were checked carefully.
C1.ielts_writing: A minute fraction of the budget remained.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe, anders als das Nomen "minute" (/ˈmɪnɪt/ = Minute).

C1.def: an extraordinary event that cannot be explained
C1.example: It was a miracle that nobody died.
C1.ielts_writing: The medical recovery was nothing short of a miracle.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "miraculous"; "work miracles" bedeutet "Wunder vollbringen".

C1.def: great suffering or unhappiness
C1.example: The war brought misery to millions.
C1.ielts_writing: He lived in misery after the loss.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "miserable" (elend); nicht mit "Misere" verwechseln.

C1.def: an unlucky accident
C1.example: A minor mishap delayed the flight.
C1.ielts_writing: The trip ended without further mishap.
C1.mistake: Meist harmlos: "minor mishap"; Plural "mishaps".

C1.def: giving a wrong idea
C1.example: The advertisement was misleading.
C1.ielts_writing: Misleading statistics distort public debate.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: mislead, misled, misled; Nomen "misrepresentation".

C1.def: to fail to catch the next transport
C1.example: We might miss a connection at the airport.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't miss a connection due to the delay.
C1.mistake: Nicht "verpassen" allgemein: "miss a connection" ist speziell der Anschlussflug oder -zug.

C1.def: a weapon that flies and explodes on target
C1.example: The missile hit its target.
C1.ielts_writing: Missile defense systems protect the capital.
C1.mistake: "ballistic missile" ist ein ballistischer Flugkörper; Plural "missiles".

C1.def: an important task or purpose
C1.example: The mission was a success.
C1.ielts_writing: The company's mission is to reduce waste.
C1.mistake: "mission statement" ist ein Leitbild; "mission impossible" Filmtitel.

C1.def: a person sent to spread a religion
C1.example: The missionary built a school in the village.
C1.ielts_writing: Missionaries often provide health care.
C1.mistake: Plural "missionaries"; Nomen "mission".

C1.def: wrong in belief or opinion
C1.example: You are mistaken.
C1.ielts_writing: He was mistaken for his brother.
C1.mistake: "mistaken identity" bedeutet "Verwechslung"; Konstruktion: "be mistaken ABOUT sth".

C1.def: covered with a thin cloud of water
C1.example: The valley was misty this morning.
C1.ielts_writing: Misty eyes betrayed his emotion.
C1.mistake: Nomen "mist" (Dunst); "misty-eyed" bedeutet "gerührt".

C1.def: to make something less severe
C1.example: Trees help mitigate air pollution.
C1.ielts_writing: Measures to mitigate the damage were announced.
C1.mistake: "mitigating circumstances" sind mildernde Umstände; nicht mit "militate" verwechseln.

C1.def: a large disorderly crowd
C1.example: An angry mob gathered outside.
C1.ielts_writing: Fans mobbed the singer at the airport.
C1.mistake: Auch organisiertes Verbrechen: "the mob"; Verb "mob" (belagern).

C1.def: the ability to move easily
C1.example: Social mobility improves with education.
C1.ielts_writing: The injury limited his mobility.
C1.mistake: "upward mobility" bedeutet "sozialer Aufstieg"; Adjektiv "mobile".

C1.def: to organize people or resources for action
C1.example: The party mobilized thousands of volunteers.
C1.ielts_writing: The country mobilized its army.
C1.mistake: Nomen "mobilization"; Gegenteil: "demobilize".

C1.def: creating a model of a system, or working as a fashion model
C1.example: Computer modeling predicts weather patterns.
C1.ielts_writing: She earned money through modeling.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Simulation oder Modeln.

C1.def: average in amount, or not extreme
C1.example: He holds moderate views.
C1.ielts_writing: The soup needs moderate heat.
C1.mistake: Aussprache: Adjektiv /ˈmɑːdərət/, Verb /ˈmɑːdəreɪt/; Nomen "moderation".

C1.def: a style in art and architecture that rejects tradition
C1.example: The museum features literary modernism.
C1.ielts_writing: Modernism changed architecture in the early twentieth century.
C1.mistake: Nomen "modernist" (Vertreter); nicht mit "modernization".

C1.def: a small change made to improve something
C1.example: The design needed several modifications.
C1.ielts_writing: Genetic modification raises ethical questions.
C1.mistake: Verb "modify"; Konstruktion: "modification TO sth".

C1.def: a unit that forms part of a course or system
C1.example: Students complete one module each term.
C1.ielts_writing: The software has a payment module.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "modular"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to shape something, or a fungal growth
C1.example: She molded the clay into a bowl.
C1.ielts_writing: Mold grew on the old bread.
C1.mistake: Nomen auch "Form" (Gussform); Adjektiv "moldy" (schimmelig).

C1.def: relating to molecules
C1.example: He studies molecular biology.
C1.ielts_writing: Molecular structures determine a material's properties.
C1.mistake: Nomen "molecule"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: the force that keeps something moving or developing
C1.example: The campaign gained momentum.
C1.ielts_writing: The team lost momentum after the injury.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; bildlich: "gain momentum" bedeutet "in Fahrt kommen".

C1.def: a building where monks live
C1.example: The monastery sits on a hill.
C1.ielts_writing: Monasteries preserved ancient manuscripts.
C1.mistake: Für Nonnen: "convent"; Adjektiv "monastic".

C1.def: a computer screen, or to observe over time
C1.example: The monitor flickered.
C1.ielts_writing: Doctors monitor patients' vital signs.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "monitor sth" (überwachen); Nomen "monitoring".

C1.def: a man belonging to a religious community
C1.example: The monk lived a simple life.
C1.ielts_writing: Monks rise early to pray.
C1.mistake: Weibliches Gegenstück: "nun"; Aussprache /mʌŋk/.

C1.def: exclusive control of a market
C1.example: The firm held a monopoly on gas supply.
C1.ielts_writing: Monopolies can raise prices without competition.
C1.mistake: Verb "monopolize"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a train that runs on a single rail
C1.example: The monorail connects the airport and the city.
C1.ielts_writing: Monorails glide above city streets.
C1.mistake: Plural "monorails"; "mono" bedeutet "eins".

C1.def: dull because of lack of variety
C1.example: The monotonous work bored him.
C1.ielts_writing: A monotonous voice put the audience to sleep.
C1.mistake: Nomen "monotony"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a small motorized bicycle
C1.example: He rode a moped to work.
C1.ielts_writing: Mopeds are popular in crowded cities.
C1.mistake: Plural "mopeds"; Name aus "motor" und "pedal".

C1.def: nausea caused by travel movement
C1.example: She gets motion sickness on boats.
C1.ielts_writing: Motion sickness can be reduced by looking at the horizon.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I took a pill for motion sickness."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "sea sickness" ist Seekrankheit.

C1.def: the reason or drive to do something
C1.example: He lacks motivation.
C1.ielts_writing: Students need motivation to learn.
C1.mistake: Verb "motivate"; Adjektiv "motivated".

C1.def: a reason for doing something
C1.example: The police could not find a motive.
C1.ielts_writing: Greed was the motive for the crime.
C1.mistake: "ulterior motive" bedeutet "Hintergedanke"; auch Musik- oder Kunstmotiv.

C1.def: a person who drives a car
C1.example: Motorists were stuck in traffic.
C1.ielts_writing: The new law affects all motorists.
C1.mistake: Offizieller als "driver"; Plural "motorists".

C1.def: a light creamy dish
C1.example: She ordered chocolate mousse.
C1.ielts_writing: Mousse is made with whipped cream and eggs.
C1.mistake: Auch Schaumfestiger fürs Haar: "hair mousse"; Aussprache /muːs/ wie "moose".

C1.def: a group working for a cause, or the act of moving
C1.example: The civil rights movement changed laws.
C1.ielts_writing: Slow movements helped calm him.
C1.mistake: Auch Musik: "the third movement"; Verb "move".

C1.def: a person who often goes to the cinema
C1.example: Moviegoers lined up for tickets.
C1.ielts_writing: The film attracted millions of moviegoers.
C1.mistake: Plural "moviegoers"; "-goer" wie "churchgoer".

C1.def: a vehicle used to transport household items
C1.example: The moving van arrived at nine.
C1.ielts_writing: They loaded furniture into a moving van.
C1.mistake: Plural "moving vans"; "movers" sind die Umzugshelfer.

C1.def: a slippery substance produced by the body
C1.example: Mucus protects the nose from dust.
C1.ielts_writing: A cold produces extra mucus.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "mucous" (z. B. "mucous membrane" für Schleimhaut).

C1.def: to attack and rob someone, or a large cup
C1.example: A thief mugged him on the street.
C1.ielts_writing: She drank tea from a mug.
C1.mistake: Nomen "mugging" (Raubüberfall); "mug shot" ist ein Polizeifoto.

C1.def: the founder of Islam
C1.example: Muhammad received revelations in Mecca.
C1.ielts_writing: Muslims believe Muhammad was the last prophet.
C1.mistake: Schreibung variiert (Mohammed, Muhammad); immer großgeschrieben.

C1.def: including many cultures
C1.example: The city is multicultural.
C1.ielts_writing: Multicultural classrooms enrich learning.
C1.mistake: Nomen "multiculturalism"; ohne Bindestrich.

C1.def: using text, sound, and video together
C1.example: The presentation used multimedia.
C1.ielts_writing: Multimedia content is popular online.
C1.mistake: Wird auch als Adjektiv verwendet; kein Plural nötig.

C1.def: to do several things at once
C1.example: Few people can multitask effectively.
C1.ielts_writing: She multitasks between calls and emails.
C1.mistake: Nomen "multitasking"; Verb nicht trennbar.

C1.def: doing several tasks at the same time
C1.example: Multitasking can reduce productivity.
C1.ielts_writing: Heavy multitasking makes it hard to concentrate.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Verb "multitask".

C1.def: ordinary and lacking excitement
C1.example: She wrote about mundane tasks.
C1.ielts_writing: The mundane details of daily life fill the novel.
C1.mistake: Nicht "mondän" (elegant): falscher Freund; "mundane" ist negativ.

C1.def: relating to a city or town
C1.example: Municipal elections take place in May.
C1.ielts_writing: The municipal government maintains the parks.
C1.mistake: Nomen "municipality" (Gemeinde); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a painting made directly on a wall
C1.example: Artists painted a mural on the school wall.
C1.ielts_writing: The mural depicts local history.
C1.mistake: Plural "murals"; Technik "fresco" ist Malerei auf Putz.

C1.def: the idea that anything that can go wrong will
C1.example: Murphy's law struck again when the printer jammed.
C1.ielts_writing: According to Murphy's law, the rain started right after the picnic began.
C1.mistake: Humorvolle Regel; wird oft im Alltag zitiert.

C1.def: having strong muscles
C1.example: He has a muscular build.
C1.ielts_writing: Muscular tissue contracts under stress.
C1.mistake: "muscular dystrophy" ist Muskeldystrophie; Nomen "muscle".

C1.def: something that is essential
C1.example: A good map is a must for hikers.
C1.ielts_writing: Comfortable shoes are a must.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen: "a must"; "must-see" und "must-have" sind Adjektive.

C1.def: a change in genetic material
C1.example: A mutation caused the disease.
C1.ielts_writing: Virus mutations can affect vaccine effectiveness.
C1.mistake: Verb "mutate"; Person/Organismus "mutant".

C1.def: felt or done by both sides
C1.example: They have a mutual friend.
C1.ielts_writing: The feeling is mutual.
C1.mistake: "The feeling is mutual" heißt "das beruht auf Gegenseitigkeit"; Adverb "mutually".

C1.def: an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers
C1.example: A myrtle grew by the door.
C1.ielts_writing: Myrtle branches decorate wedding bouquets.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She planted a myrtle in the garden."
C1.mistake: Plural "myrtles"; auch Vorname "Myrtle".

C1.def: a collection of myths belonging to a culture
C1.example: Greek mythology tells of gods and heroes.
C1.ielts_writing: The film borrows from Norse mythology.
C1.mistake: Nomen "myth" (Mythos); Adjektiv "mythological".

C1.def: lacking experience or caution
C1.example: It was naive to trust him.
C1.ielts_writing: Naive optimism can lead to disappointment.
C1.mistake: Nomen "naivety"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: used to introduce details
C1.example: Two options remain, namely waiting or leaving.
C1.ielts_writing: Only one factor matters, namely cost.
C1.mistake: Steht vor einer Erklärung, nicht am Satzanfang; nicht "nämlich" als Begründung.

C1.def: a woman who cares for children in their home
C1.example: The nanny picked up the children from school.
C1.ielts_writing: Nannies often live with the family.
C1.mistake: "nanny state" ist ein bevormundender Staat; Plural "nannies".

C1.def: to tell a story
C1.example: He narrates the documentary.
C1.ielts_writing: She narrated her journey to the audience.
C1.mistake: Nomen "narrator" (Erzähler); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: the act of telling a story, or a spoken commentary
C1.example: The narration of the documentary was calm.
C1.ielts_writing: The book is written in first-person narration.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Verb "narrate".

C1.def: unwilling to accept different views
C1.example: His narrow-minded attitude caused conflict.
C1.ielts_writing: Narrow-minded people dismiss new ideas.
C1.mistake: Nomen "narrow-mindedness"; Gegenteil: "broad-minded".

C1.def: the US space agency
C1.example: NASA launched a new probe.
C1.ielts_writing: NASA scientists study planets and stars.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "National Aeronautics and Space Administration"; wird als Wort gesprochen.

C1.def: across a whole country
C1.example: The campaign has nationwide reach.
C1.ielts_writing: A nationwide search began.
C1.mistake: Auch Adverb: "available nationwide"; kein Bindestrich.

C1.def: relating to a navy
C1.example: The naval base was heavily guarded.
C1.ielts_writing: Naval forces patrolled the coast.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "navel" (Nabel) verwechseln; gleiche Aussprache.

C1.def: the small scar in the middle of the abdomen
C1.example: The baby's navel needs care.
C1.ielts_writing: The navel marks where the umbilical cord was attached.
C1.mistake: Gleiche Aussprache wie "naval"; "navel-gazing" bedeutet "Nabelschau".

C1.def: to find your way, or to move through something
C1.example: She navigated the boat through the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: Users can navigate the site easily.
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "navigate a difficult situation"; Nomen "navigation".

C1.def: a cloud of gas and dust in space
C1.example: The telescope photographed a nebula.
C1.ielts_writing: Stars form inside a nebula.
C1.mistake: Plural "nebulae"; Adjektiv "nebulous" (vage).

C1.def: a thin metal tool used for sewing or injections
C1.example: She threaded the needle.
C1.ielts_writing: The nurse inserted the needle into his arm.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A needle in a haystack is hard to find."
C1.mistake: "needle in a haystack" bedeutet "Stecknadel im Heuhaufen"; Kiefernnadel: "pine needle".

C1.def: to fail to care for or do something
C1.example: Parents who neglect their children face charges.
C1.ielts_writing: He neglected his duties.
C1.mistake: Auch Nomen "neglect"; Adjektiv "neglected".

C1.def: failing to take proper care
C1.example: The driver was found negligent.
C1.ielts_writing: Negligent behavior can lead to lawsuits.
C1.mistake: Nomen "negligence" (Fahrlässigkeit); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: located next to something
C1.example: The neighboring country opened its border.
C1.ielts_writing: Neighboring villages cooperate on fairs.
C1.mistake: Nomen "neighbor"; Plural "neighbors".

C1.def: a chemical weapon that attacks the nervous system
C1.example: Inspectors found traces of a nerve agent.
C1.ielts_writing: Nerve agents are banned under international treaties.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Doctors treated victims of the nerve agent."
C1.mistake: Auch "nerve gas"; Plural "nerve agents".

C1.def: a poisonous gas that damages the nervous system
C1.example: The nerve gas killed hundreds.
C1.ielts_writing: Nerve gas was used in the attack.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; synonym oft "nerve agent".

C1.def: a structure built by birds to lay eggs
C1.example: The bird built a nest in the tree.
C1.ielts_writing: Wasps nest under the roof every summer.
C1.mistake: "nest egg" bedeutet "Notgroschen"; "empty nest" ist die Zeit nach dem Auszug der Kinder.

C1.def: remaining after deductions
C1.example: Her net salary is lower than gross pay.
C1.ielts_writing: The net profit rose by ten percent.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "gross"; auch Nomen "net" (Netz).

C1.def: the phase when the moon is not visible
C1.example: The new moon appears once a month.
C1.ielts_writing: During the new moon, stars are easier to see.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "full moon"; Plural "new moons".

C1.def: the process of collecting news
C1.example: Digital tools changed newsgathering.
C1.ielts_writing: Newsgathering requires fast sources and accurate verification.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; auch "news gathering" getrennt.

C1.def: a regular bulletin sent to subscribers
C1.example: She subscribed to the company newsletter.
C1.ielts_writing: A weekly newsletter keeps members informed.
C1.mistake: Plural "newsletters"; per E-Mail oder Print.

C1.def: the place where news is prepared
C1.example: Reporters rushed into the newsroom.
C1.ielts_writing: The newsroom was busy after the announcement.
C1.mistake: Plural "newsrooms"; "editorial office" ist formeller.

C1.def: a printed sheet of news
C1.example: The newssheet was handed out at the station.
C1.ielts_writing: The union publishes a weekly newssheet.
C1.mistake: Selten; häufiger "newsletter" oder "bulletin".

C1.def: the closest living relative of a person
C1.example: The police notified the next of kin.
C1.ielts_writing: Hospitals ask for the next of kin in emergencies.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung; Plural bleibt "next of kin".

C1.def: the pointed metal tip of a pen
C1.example: The nib of the fountain pen broke.
C1.ielts_writing: Different nibs produce different line widths.
C1.mistake: Plural "nibs"; Teil des Füllfederhalters.

C1.def: a specialized market segment, or a recess in a wall
C1.example: The company found a niche in organic snacks.
C1.ielts_writing: A niche in the wall held a statue.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He carved out a niche for himself."
