C1.mistake: Aussprache /nɪtʃ/ oder /niːʃ/; Adjektiv "niche" (Nischen-).

C1.def: a silver-white metal, or a five-cent coin
C1.example: Nickel is used in stainless steel.
C1.ielts_writing: A nickel is worth five cents.
C1.mistake: "nickel and dime sb" bedeutet "jemanden mit Kleinbeträgen schröpfen".

C1.def: a light dress worn in bed
C1.example: She put on her nightie.
C1.ielts_writing: A cotton nightie is comfortable in summer.
C1.mistake: Kurzform von "nightgown"; Plural "nighties".

C1.def: happening every night
C1.example: The nightly news starts at nine.
C1.ielts_writing: Nightly patrols guard the compound.
C1.mistake: Auch Adverb "nightly"; "daily" ist täglich.

C1.def: the small part of a breast, or a rubber part of a baby bottle
C1.example: The baby bottle has a silicone nipple.
C1.ielts_writing: Nipples vary in size and shape.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb "nipple" selten; im Alltag vorsichtig verwenden.

C1.def: having high moral qualities, or of high social rank
C1.example: It was a noble gesture.
C1.ielts_writing: The noble family owned vast estates.
C1.mistake: Nomen "nobility" (Adel, Edelmut); "noble gas" ist Edelgas.

C1.def: to move the head up and down
C1.example: She nodded in agreement.
C1.ielts_writing: He nodded off during the lecture.
C1.mistake: "nod off" bedeutet "einnicken"; Nomen "a nod".

C1.def: to formally suggest someone for a position or prize
C1.example: She was nominated for an award.
C1.ielts_writing: The party will nominate a candidate in June.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "nominate sb FOR sth" oder "AS sth".

C1.def: the act of formally proposing someone
C1.example: His nomination was approved.
C1.ielts_writing: The film received three Oscar nominations.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "nomination FOR sth"; Verb "nominate".

C1.def: a person who is proposed for a position or prize
C1.example: Each nominee gave a short speech.
C1.ielts_writing: The nominees were announced on Monday.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der letzten Silbe; Verb "nominate".

C1.def: not following rules or requirements
C1.example: The company was found non-compliant.
C1.ielts_writing: Non-compliant patients may need extra support.
C1.mistake: Auch "noncompliant"; Nomen "non-compliance".

C1.def: not operated to make a profit
C1.example: She works for a non-profit organization.
C1.ielts_writing: Non-profit groups depend on donations.
C1.mistake: Auch "nonprofit"; Gegenteil: "for-profit".

C1.def: calm and not showing worry
C1.example: He shrugged in a nonchalant way.
C1.ielts_writing: Her nonchalant attitude surprised everyone.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˌnɑːnʃəˈlɑːnt/ französisch; Nomen "nonchalance".

C1.def: in spite of that
C1.example: The task was difficult; nonetheless, they succeeded.
C1.ielts_writing: The weather was poor, but the match went ahead nonetheless.
C1.mistake: Ein Wort geschrieben; formeller als "still".

C1.def: words or ideas that make no sense
C1.example: That's complete nonsense.
C1.ielts_writing: He talked nonsense all evening.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Adjektiv "nonsensical".

C1.def: twelve o'clock in the day
C1.example: We will meet at noon.
C1.ielts_writing: By noon, the temperature had reached forty degrees.
C1.mistake: "high noon" bedeutet "Höhepunkt, Showdown"; Gegenteil: "midnight".

C1.def: plastic surgery on the nose
C1.example: She had a nose job last year.
C1.ielts_writing: A nose job changes the shape of the nose.
C1.mistake: Fachbegriff: "rhinoplasty"; umgangssprachlich "nose job".

C1.def: a longing for the past
C1.example: He felt nostalgia for his hometown.
C1.ielts_writing: The film is full of nostalgia for the sixties.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "nostalgic"; Konstruktion: "nostalgia FOR sth".

C1.def: worthy of attention
C1.example: She is a notable scientist.
C1.ielts_writing: There were several notable exceptions.
C1.mistake: Adverb "notably"; "notable" auch Nomen für bedeutende Person.

C1.def: especially or in a way worth noting
C1.example: Many countries, notably Germany, supported the plan.
C1.ielts_writing: The film was notably successful.
C1.mistake: Steht oft vor dem Beispiel; nicht mit "notorious".

C1.def: a block of paper for notes
C1.example: He wrote the address on a notepad.
C1.ielts_writing: A notepad lies next to the phone.
C1.mistake: Auch digitales Programm "Notepad"; Plural "notepads".

C1.def: a warning or announcement, or to become aware
C1.example: The landlord gave two weeks' notice.
C1.ielts_writing: I noticed a strange smell.
C1.mistake: "until further notice" bedeutet "bis auf Weiteres"; Verb "notice".

C1.def: a message that informs you of something
C1.example: I received a notification on my phone.
C1.ielts_writing: Notifications can be turned off in the settings.
C1.mistake: Verb "notify"; Plural "notifications".

C1.def: to formally tell someone
C1.example: The bank will notify you by mail.
C1.ielts_writing: Please notify the office if you are late.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "notify sb OF sth".

C1.def: famous for something bad
C1.example: He is a notorious criminal.
C1.ielts_writing: The area is notorious for its traffic.
C1.mistake: Nicht "berühmt": "notorious" ist negativ; Konstruktion: "notorious FOR sth".

C1.def: new and different
C1.example: They proposed a novel approach.
C1.ielts_writing: A novel technique reduced costs.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Roman": als Adjektiv "novel" bedeutet "neuartig"; Nomen "novelty".

C1.def: used to draw attention or introduce a point
C1.example: Now then, let's get started.
C1.ielts_writing: Now then, who wants coffee?
C1.mistake: Eher umgangssprachlich; leitet einen neuen Gedanken ein.

C1.def: a slight difference in meaning or feeling
C1.example: He explained every nuance of the text.
C1.ielts_writing: Translators must capture cultural nuance.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "nuanced" (differenziert); aus dem Französischen.

C1.def: nuclear weapons kept to discourage attack
C1.example: The country maintains a nuclear deterrent.
C1.ielts_writing: A nuclear deterrent aims to prevent war.
C1.mistake: Nomen "deterrence"; Verb "deter" (abschrecken).

C1.def: energy produced from nuclear reactions
C1.example: Nuclear power provides low-carbon energy.
C1.ielts_writing: The debate on nuclear power continues.
C1.mistake: Kurzform "nuclear"; "nuclear power plant" ist das Kernkraftwerk.

C1.def: the central part of an atom or cell
C1.example: The nucleus controls the cell.
C1.ielts_writing: Protons and neutrons form the nucleus.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The family is the nucleus of society."
C1.mistake: Plural "nuclei" (/ˈnuːkliaɪ/); bildlich "Kern".

C1.def: a quantity, or a symbol that represents it
C1.example: What is your phone number?
C1.ielts_writing: A number of students were absent.
C1.mistake: "a number of" bedeutet "einige"; "the number of" bedeutet "die Anzahl".

C1.def: relating to numbers
C1.example: The files are sorted in numerical order.
C1.ielts_writing: Numerical data supports the claim.
C1.mistake: Adverb "numerically"; Gegenteil in Kontext: "verbal".

C1.def: a woman belonging to a religious community
C1.example: The nun taught at the school.
C1.ielts_writing: Nuns live in a convent.
C1.mistake: Männliche Entsprechung: "monk"; Aussprache /nʌn/.

C1.def: a place for young children, or a place for growing plants
C1.example: The toddler goes to nursery.
C1.ielts_writing: The nursery sells young trees.
C1.mistake: "nursery school" ist Vorschule; "nursery rhyme" ist Kinderreim.

C1.def: containing substances that keep you healthy
C1.example: The soup is nutritious.
C1.ielts_writing: Nutritious meals support growth.
C1.mistake: Nomen "nutrition"; Adjektiv "nutritional".

C1.def: the act of following orders
C1.example: The dog showed perfect obedience.
C1.ielts_writing: Blind obedience can be dangerous.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "disobedience"; Konstruktion: "obedience TO sb".

C1.def: a medical condition of having too much body fat
C1.example: Obesity increases the risk of heart disease.
C1.ielts_writing: Childhood obesity has risen over decades.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "obese"; Fachbegriff, nicht umgangssprachlich "fat".

C1.def: a statement of disagreement or opposition
C1.example: The lawyer raised an objection.
C1.ielts_writing: I have no objection to the plan.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "objection TO sth"; Verb "object (TO)".

C1.def: the quality of being fair and not influenced by feelings
C1.example: Judges must maintain objectivity.
C1.ielts_writing: The journalist praised the report's objectivity.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "objective"; Gegenteil: "subjectivity".

C1.def: required by rule or custom
C1.example: Attendance at the briefing is obligatory.
C1.ielts_writing: It's obligatory to wear a helmet.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Nomen "obligation".

C1.def: to force someone to do something, or to do a favor
C1.example: The law obliges companies to publish reports.
C1.ielts_writing: I'm happy to oblige.
C1.mistake: Passiv: "be obliged TO do sth" (gezwungen sein); "obliging" bedeutet "entgegenkommend".

C1.def: to watch carefully, or to follow a rule
C1.example: Scientists observed the planet for months.
C1.ielts_writing: Drivers must observe the speed limit.
C1.mistake: Nomen "observation"; "observe" auch "feiern": "observe a holiday".

C1.def: to think about something all the time
C1.example: He obsesses about his weight.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't obsess over small details.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "obsess ABOUT/OVER sth"; Passiv: "be obsessed WITH sth".

C1.def: a persistent, excessive preoccupation
C1.example: He has an obsession with cleanliness.
C1.ielts_writing: Her obsession with success hurt her health.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "obsession WITH sth"; Verb "obsess".

C1.def: thinking about or doing something to an excessive degree
C1.example: She is obsessive about order.
C1.ielts_writing: Obsessive behavior can disrupt daily life.
C1.mistake: "obsessive-compulsive disorder" ist Zwangsstörung; Adverb "obsessively".

C1.def: no longer used because newer things exist
C1.example: The old software is obsolete.
C1.ielts_writing: Floppy disks have become obsolete.
C1.mistake: Nomen "obsolescence"; "planned obsolescence" ist geplante Obsoleszenz.

C1.def: refusing to change one's opinion
C1.example: The obstinate child refused to eat.
C1.ielts_writing: An obstinate stain would not come out.
C1.mistake: Nomen "obstinacy"; leicht stärker als "stubborn".

C1.def: happening sometimes but not often
C1.example: He enjoys an occasional cigar.
C1.ielts_writing: Occasional showers are expected.
C1.mistake: Adverb "occasionally"; Nomen "occasion" (Anlass).

C1.def: a person's job, or the act of taking control of a place
C1.example: State your name and occupation.
C1.ielts_writing: The occupation of the city lasted five years.
C1.mistake: Verb "occupy"; "Occupation" im Formular bedeutet Beruf.

C1.def: something that happens, or how often it happens
C1.example: Such storms are a rare occurrence.
C1.ielts_writing: The occurrence of the disease is increasing.
C1.mistake: Verb "occur" (Doppel-r); Konstruktion: "occurrence OF sth".

C1.def: the likelihood that something will happen
C1.example: The odds of winning are low.
C1.ielts_writing: Against all odds, they survived.
C1.mistake: Nur Plural; "at odds with" bedeutet "im Widerspruch zu"; "odds and ends" sind Kleinkram.

C1.def: the quiet period when few people travel
C1.example: Hotels are cheaper in the off season.
C1.ielts_writing: Many cafés close during the off season.
C1.mistake: Auch "off-season" mit Bindestrich als Adjektiv; Gegenteil: "peak season".

C1.def: no longer under consideration
C1.example: Tax increases are off the table.
C1.ielts_writing: The offer is now off the table.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "on the table"; bildlich im Verhandeln.

C1.def: to present something for acceptance
C1.example: She offered me a seat.
C1.ielts_writing: The store offers a ten percent discount.
C1.mistake: Nomen "offer" (Angebot); Konstruktion: "offer sth TO sb".

C1.def: something offered, such as products or donations
C1.example: The restaurant's offerings include vegan dishes.
C1.ielts_writing: Churches collect an offering on Sundays.
C1.mistake: Im Plural "offerings" oft Produktpalette; auch religiöses Opfer.

C1.def: to balance something against something else
C1.example: Savings will offset the higher costs.
C1.ielts_writing: Gains in one area offset losses in another.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We planted trees to offset our emissions."
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: offset, offset, offset; Nomen "offset" (Ausgleich).

C1.def: located at sea or abroad, often for tax reasons
C1.example: They set up an offshore account.
C1.ielts_writing: Offshore wind farms generate clean power.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "onshore"; auch Adverb "offshore".

C1.def: a painting made with oil paints
C1.example: The oil painting hangs in the museum.
C1.ielts_writing: Oil paintings dry slowly.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil in Technik: "watercolor"; Plural "oil paintings".

C1.def: a large structure for drilling oil
C1.example: The oil rig burned for days.
C1.ielts_writing: Workers live on the oil rig for weeks.
C1.mistake: Plural "oil rigs"; Bohrinsel im Meer: "offshore rig".

C1.def: containing or covered with oil
C1.example: The salad dressing was too oily.
C1.ielts_writing: An oily film covered the water.
C1.mistake: Nomen "oil"; "oily fish" sind fettreiche Fische wie Lachs.

C1.def: a green vegetable with edible pods
C1.example: She fried okra for dinner.
C1.ielts_writing: Okra is used to thicken stews.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: "some okra"; in Gumbo üblich.

C1.def: dark yellowish green
C1.example: He wore an olive jacket.
C1.ielts_writing: Olive tones suit warm skin.
C1.mistake: Nomen "olive" (Olive); "olive branch" ist Friedensangebot.

C1.def: suggesting that something bad will happen
C1.example: Ominous clouds gathered.
C1.ielts_writing: An ominous silence fell over the room.
C1.mistake: Nomen "omen" (Vorzeichen); Adverb "ominously".

C1.def: available at a reduced price, or available to buy
C1.example: The jacket is on sale.
C1.ielts_writing: Tickets go on sale next week.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: reduziert und erhältlich; Gegenteil: "full price".

C1.def: between two people only
C1.example: The coach offers one-on-one training.
C1.ielts_writing: A one-on-one meeting with the manager was arranged.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen "a one-on-one"; Gegenteil: "group session".

C1.def: not transparent, or hard to understand
C1.example: The window glass is opaque.
C1.ielts_writing: The company's accounting is opaque.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "transparent"; Nomen "opacity".

C1.def: willing to consider new ideas
C1.example: She is open-minded about different cultures.
C1.ielts_writing: Open-minded readers value diverse views.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "narrow-minded"; Konstruktion: "open-minded ABOUT sth".

C1.def: having a collar that is not buttoned
C1.example: He wore an open-necked shirt.
C1.ielts_writing: Open-necked shirts are popular in summer.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The tie was unnecessary with an open-necked shirt."
C1.mistake: Bindestrich bei Adjektiv; kein Nomen "open neck".

C1.def: ready for use, or relating to operations
C1.example: The new plant is fully operational.
C1.ielts_writing: Operational costs have risen.
C1.mistake: Verb "operate"; Gegenteil: "inoperative".

C1.def: to make a choice
C1.example: Many voters opted for change.
C1.ielts_writing: She opted to stay at home.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "opt FOR sth" oder "opt TO + Infinitiv"; "opt out" bedeutet "aussteigen".

C1.def: relating to sight or light
C1.example: The camera has an optical zoom.
C1.ielts_writing: Optical illusions trick the eye.
C1.mistake: Nomen "optics" (Optik); "optical illusion" bedeutet "optische Täuschung".

C1.def: a hopeful attitude about the future
C1.example: Her optimism was contagious.
C1.ielts_writing: There is cautious optimism about the economy.
C1.mistake: Person: "optimist"; Gegenteil: "pessimism".

C1.def: a professional who tests eyesight
C1.example: The optometrist checked my vision.
C1.ielts_writing: An optometrist can prescribe glasses.
C1.mistake: Nicht Augenarzt: dieser heißt "ophthalmologist".

C1.def: used at the end of a question to ask for confirmation
C1.example: Are you coming or what?
C1.ielts_writing: Are we leaving or what?
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich; kann ungeduldig klingen.

C1.def: spoken, or relating to the mouth
C1.example: There will be an oral exam.
C1.ielts_writing: Oral hygiene prevents cavities.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "written"; "oral history" ist mündliche Überlieferung.

C1.def: a large black-and-white marine mammal
C1.example: An orca leapt out of the water.
C1.ielts_writing: Orcas hunt in coordinated groups.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw an orca near the coast."
C1.mistake: Auch "killer whale"; Plural "orcas".

C1.def: a number showing position in a series
C1.example: "First" is an ordinal.
C1.ielts_writing: Ordinal numbers show rank, not quantity.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "cardinal"; Beispiele: first, second, third.

C1.def: produced without chemicals, or relating to living things
C1.example: We buy organic vegetables.
C1.ielts_writing: Organic compounds contain carbon.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "synthetic"; "organic" im Lebensmittelbereich entspricht "Bio-".

C1.def: relating to the way something is organized
C1.example: She has strong organizational skills.
C1.ielts_writing: Organizational change takes time.
C1.mistake: Nomen "organization"; Verb "organize".

C1.def: a direction of interest, or an introduction for new people
C1.example: New employees attend an orientation.
C1.ielts_writing: Her political orientation is liberal.
C1.mistake: Verb "orient" (ausrichten); "orientation week" ist Einführungswoche.

C1.def: to begin or come from a particular place or cause
C1.example: The tradition originated in Italy.
C1.ielts_writing: The fire originated in the kitchen.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "originate IN/FROM a place"; Nomen "origin".

C1.def: a child whose parents have died
C1.example: The orphan lived with his aunt.
C1.ielts_writing: War left many orphans.
C1.mistake: Nomen "orphanage" (Waisenhaus); Plural "orphans".

C1.def: impossible or not allowed
C1.example: Leaving early is out of the question.
C1.ielts_writing: A vacation this year is out of the question.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Paying that much is out of the question."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung; nicht "außerhalb der Frage".

C1.def: a tray for outgoing documents
C1.example: Place the letters in the out-basket.
C1.ielts_writing: The out-basket was empty by noon.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "in-basket"; Plural "out-baskets".

C1.def: a sudden start of disease or violence
C1.example: An outbreak of flu closed the school.
C1.ielts_writing: The outbreak of war surprised everyone.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "outbreak OF sth"; Plural "outbreaks".

C1.def: a short trip for pleasure
C1.example: We went on a family outing.
C1.ielts_writing: The class outing was canceled.
C1.mistake: Auch "outing" im Sinn von öffentlich machen (Outing).

C1.def: a person who has broken the law and is hiding
C1.example: The outlaw robbed the stagecoach.
C1.ielts_writing: Outlaws roamed the frontier.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb "outlaw" (verbieten); Gegenteil: "lawman".

C1.def: a place that sells goods, a power socket, or a means of expression
C1.example: The outlet sells factory-reduced clothing.
C1.ielts_writing: She found a creative outlet in painting.
C1.mistake: Drei Bedeutungen: Laden, Steckdose, Ventil; "outlet mall" ist Einkaufszentrum.

C1.def: a view of the future, or a person's attitude
C1.example: The economic outlook is uncertain.
C1.ielts_writing: She has a positive outlook on life.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The outlook for next week is sunny."
C1.mistake: Meist Singular; auch E-Mail-Programm "Outlook".

C1.def: strong anger or shock
C1.example: The decision caused public outrage.
C1.ielts_writing: The news outraged the community.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "outrageous" (empörend); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a person not belonging to a group
C1.example: She felt like an outsider at school.
C1.ielts_writing: Outsiders often see problems more clearly.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "insider"; Plural "outsiders".

C1.def: a female organ that produces eggs
C1.example: The ovary releases an egg each month.
C1.ielts_writing: Surgery removed one ovary.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She has a cyst on her ovary."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "ovarian"; Plural "ovaries".

C1.def: using resources faster than they can renew
C1.example: Overexploitation threatens fish populations.
C1.ielts_writing: Overexploitation of forests leads to erosion.
C1.mistake: Verb "overexploit"; unzählbar.

C1.def: to fail to notice, or to have a view over
C1.example: I overlooked a mistake.
C1.ielts_writing: The balcony overlooks the sea.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: übersehen und Ausblick haben; Passiv: "be overlooked".

C1.def: too much
C1.example: I'm not overly concerned.
C1.ielts_writing: He is overly cautious.
C1.mistake: Wird oft verneint: "not overly happy" (nicht besonders glücklich).

C1.def: to watch and direct work
C1.example: She oversees the entire project.
C1.ielts_writing: Inspectors oversee food safety.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: oversee, oversaw, overseen; Nomen "oversight".

C1.def: to make less important, or to cast a shadow
C1.example: His success overshadowed her work.
C1.ielts_writing: A tall building overshadows the garden.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "be overshadowed BY sth"; bildlich und wörtlich.

C1.def: a mistake from not noticing, or supervision
C1.example: It was a simple oversight.
C1.ielts_writing: Congress exercises oversight of the agency.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Fehler und Aufsicht; nicht "Übersicht".

C1.def: extra hours worked beyond the regular schedule
C1.example: She worked overtime all week.
C1.ielts_writing: Overtime pay is time and a half.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; auch Verlängerung im Sport.

C1.def: to cancel a decision, or to turn upside down
C1.example: The court overturned the verdict.
C1.ielts_writing: The storm overturned several boats.
C1.mistake: Gericht kippt Urteil: "overturn a ruling"; Gegenteil: "uphold".

C1.def: to affect strongly, or to defeat with great force
C1.example: The workload overwhelmed her.
C1.ielts_writing: Emotions overwhelmed him at the ceremony.
C1.mistake: Passiv: "be overwhelmed BY/WITH sth"; Adjektiv "overwhelming".

C1.def: very great in amount or effect
C1.example: The support was overwhelming.
C1.ielts_writing: There is overwhelming evidence against him.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I felt an overwhelming sense of relief."
C1.mistake: Adverb "overwhelmingly"; "overwhelming majority" ist eine überwältigende Mehrheit.

C1.def: the thinning of the ozone layer
C1.example: Ozone depletion increases ultraviolet radiation.
C1.ielts_writing: International agreements target ozone depletion.
C1.mistake: Verb "deplete" (aufbrauchen); Unzählbar.

C1.def: a layer of gas that absorbs ultraviolet rays
C1.example: The ozone layer protects us from sunlight.
C1.ielts_writing: Chemicals damaged the ozone layer.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The hole in the ozone layer shrank."
C1.mistake: Mit "hole in the ozone layer" (Ozonloch).

C1.def: the speed at which something happens
C1.example: She set a fast pace.
C1.ielts_writing: He paced the room nervously.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I can't keep up with the pace."
C1.mistake: "keep pace with" bedeutet "Schritt halten mit"; Verb "pace" (auf und ab gehen).

C1.def: to calm or bring peace to
C1.example: The mother pacified the crying child.
C1.ielts_writing: Leaders tried to pacify the rebellious region.
C1.mistake: Nomen "pacifier" (Schnuller); Wortstamm "peace".

C1.def: a trip with transport and accommodation sold together
C1.example: They booked a package holiday to Spain.
C1.ielts_writing: Package holidays often include meals and airport transfers.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A package holiday is easy to arrange."
C1.mistake: Plural "package holidays"; Pauschalreise inklusive Flug und Unterkunft.

C1.def: a soft cushion, or a block of paper
C1.example: She wrote on a legal pad.
C1.ielts_writing: Shoulder pads protect the player.
C1.mistake: Auch "pad" für Wohnung (umgangssprachlich: "bachelor pad").

C1.def: a game where players shoot paint pellets
C1.example: They played paintball at the weekend.
C1.ielts_writing: Paintball is popular at team events.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Ausrüstung: "paintball gun".

C1.def: a friend
C1.example: He's my pal from school.
C1.ielts_writing: Old pals gathered for lunch.
C1.mistake: "pen pal" ist ein Brieffreund; Verb "pal around" (rumhängen).

C1.def: a board for mixing paints, or a range of colors
C1.example: The artist mixed colors on the palette.
C1.ielts_writing: The room has a warm color palette.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Palette" im Sinn von Transportpalette (das ist "pallet"); gleiche Aussprache.

C1.def: predicting the future by studying the hand
C1.example: She tried palm reading at the fair.
C1.ielts_writing: Palm reading is often considered entertainment.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Person: "palm reader".

C1.def: a small unbound booklet
C1.example: The clinic gave her a pamphlet.
C1.ielts_writing: Political pamphlets circulated in the city.
C1.mistake: Plural "pamphlets"; ähnlich "brochure", aber einfacher.

C1.def: a disease outbreak spreading across the world
C1.example: The pandemic changed daily life.
C1.ielts_writing: Pandemic planning requires international cooperation.
C1.mistake: Gegenstück zu "epidemic" (lokal) und "endemic" (dauerhaft in Region).

C1.def: a large black wild cat
C1.example: A panther stalked through the jungle.
C1.ielts_writing: Panthers are excellent climbers.
C1.mistake: Meist schwarzer Leopard oder Jaguar; Plural "panthers".

C1.def: photographers who follow celebrities
C1.example: Paparazzi followed the actress.
C1.ielts_writing: Paparazzi crowded outside the hotel.
C1.mistake: Singular "paparazzo"; Plural "paparazzi".

C1.def: a book with a flexible paper cover
C1.example: I bought a paperback at the airport.
C1.ielts_writing: Paperbacks are cheaper than hardcovers.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "hardcover"; Plural "paperbacks".

C1.def: a small bent wire used to hold papers
C1.example: He attached the papers with a paperclip.
C1.ielts_writing: A paperclip can reset the device.
C1.mistake: Auch "paper clip" getrennt; Plural "paperclips".

C1.def: jumping from an aircraft with a parachute
C1.example: Parachuting requires training.
C1.ielts_writing: She tried parachuting for her birthday.
C1.mistake: Verb "parachute"; synonym "skydiving".

C1.def: a typical model or pattern of thinking
C1.example: The discovery changed the scientific paradigm.
C1.ielts_writing: A paradigm shift occurred in education.
C1.mistake: "paradigm shift" bedeutet "Paradigmenwechsel"; Aussprache /ˈpærədaɪm/ (das "g" ist stumm).

C1.def: a statement or situation that seems contradictory but may be true
C1.example: It's a paradox that silence can be loud.
C1.ielts_writing: The paradox puzzled mathematicians.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "paradoxical"; Plural "paradoxes".

C1.def: a limit or value that defines something
C1.example: Set the parameters before running the test.
C1.ielts_writing: Budget parameters limit our options.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Plural "parameters".

C1.def: an organism that lives on another, or a person who takes without giving
C1.example: The dog had a parasite.
C1.ielts_writing: He's a parasite who lives off others.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "parasitic"; Gegenstück: "host" (Wirt).

C1.def: relating to parents
C1.example: He needs parental consent.
C1.ielts_writing: Parental guidance is advised.
C1.mistake: Nomen "parent"; "parental leave" ist Elternzeit.

C1.def: a bracket used in writing, or an inserted remark
C1.example: Put the date in parenthesis.
C1.ielts_writing: The parenthesis explains the term.
C1.mistake: Plural "parentheses"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: the activity of raising children
C1.example: Parenting is demanding.
C1.ielts_writing: Good parenting involves patience and consistency.
C1.mistake: Verb "parent" (Kinder aufziehen); unzählbar.

C1.def: a small local area with its own church
C1.example: The parish church was built in 1800.
C1.ielts_writing: The parish council meets monthly.
C1.mistake: Kirchliche Gemeinde; Person: "parishioner".

C1.def: a sport of moving over obstacles quickly
C1.example: He practices parkour on the rooftops.
C1.ielts_writing: Parkour requires strength and balance.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈpɑːrkʊr/; Person: "traceur".

C1.def: relating to a parliament
C1.example: The country has a parliamentary system.
C1.ielts_writing: Parliamentary elections will be held in March.
C1.mistake: Nomen "parliament"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: a green herb used for flavor
C1.example: Sprinkle parsley on the soup.
C1.ielts_writing: Fresh parsley adds color and flavor.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "curly parsley" ist krause Petersilie.

C1.def: to take part in something, or to eat or drink
C1.example: They partook of the feast.
C1.ielts_writing: Only members may partake in the ceremony.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "partake OF food" und "partake IN an activity"; gehoben.

C1.def: incomplete, or favoring one side
C1.example: The agreement was only a partial success.
C1.ielts_writing: The referee seemed partial to the home team.
C1.mistake: "partial TO sth" bedeutet "etwas besonders mögen"; Gegenteil: "impartial".

C1.def: to some extent but not completely
C1.example: The road is partially blocked.
C1.ielts_writing: He was partially responsible.
C1.mistake: Nicht "partly": "partially" betont das Ausmaß; Adjektiv "partial".

C1.def: a very small piece of matter
C1.example: Dust particles filled the air.
C1.ielts_writing: Particles carry electric charge.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A particle of dust landed on the lens."
C1.mistake: Auch Grammatik: "particle" (z. B. "up" in "give up").

C1.def: strongly supporting one side
C1.example: The debate was highly partisan.
C1.ielts_writing: Partisan politics divide the country.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen auch "Partisan" (Widerstandskämpfer); Nomen "partisanship".

C1.def: the act of going by, or a gentle way to say death
C1.example: The passing of time heals wounds.
C1.ielts_writing: We mourned the passing of a friend.
C1.mistake: "in passing" bedeutet "nebenbei"; Euphemismus für Tod: "his passing".

C1.def: a tropical fruit with wrinkled skin and sweet pulp
C1.example: She added passion fruit to the juice.
C1.ielts_writing: Passion fruit has a tart, sweet flavor.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "passion" ist hier nicht Leidenschaft.

C1.def: not taking action, or in grammar the passive voice
C1.example: He played a passive role.
C1.ielts_writing: The passive voice is used in formal writing.
C1.mistake: Grammatik: "passive voice"; "passive income" ist passives Einkommen.

C1.def: a minister who leads a Christian congregation
C1.example: The pastor gave a moving sermon.
C1.ielts_writing: Our pastor visits the sick every week.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "pastoral" (seelsorgerisch oder ländlich); Plural "pastors".

C1.def: a piece of material used to repair something
C1.example: She sewed a patch on the knee.
C1.ielts_writing: Developers released a patch to fix the bug.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a bare patch in the lawn."
C1.mistake: "patch up" bedeutet "kitten, notdürftig reparieren"; auch Software-Update.

C1.def: an official right to make or sell an invention
C1.example: The firm filed a patent for the device.
C1.ielts_writing: Patent protection lasts twenty years.
C1.mistake: Aussprache Nomen /ˈpætnt/; Verb "patent"; "patent leather" ist Lackleder.

C1.def: a path or route, or a way to achieve something
C1.example: A gravel pathway led to the house.
C1.ielts_writing: Education is a pathway to success.
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "pathway TO sth"; Plural "pathways".

C1.def: a group that regularly checks an area
C1.example: Police patrol the area at night.
C1.ielts_writing: The patrol found nothing unusual.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "on patrol" (auf Streife); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a person who supports an organization with money
C1.example: The museum thanked its patrons.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular patrons get a discount.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She is a patron of the arts."
C1.mistake: "patron saint" ist Schutzheilige(r); Verb "patronize" auch "herablassend behandeln".

C1.def: to give good results, or to finish paying a debt
C1.example: Her hard work paid off.
C1.ielts_writing: He paid off his mortgage in ten years.
C1.ielts_speaking: "It will pay off in the end."
C1.mistake: Nomen "payoff" (Gewinn, Schmiergeld); auch "jemanden bestechen".

C1.def: a public telephone operated by coins or cards
C1.example: He called from a payphone.
C1.ielts_writing: Payphones have almost disappeared.
C1.mistake: Heute selten; Plural "payphones".

C1.def: a personal computer
C1.example: She works on a PC.
C1.ielts_writing: A PC runs most business software.
C1.mistake: Auch "political correctness" (politisch korrekt); als Buchstaben gesprochen.

C1.def: a large bird with colorful tail feathers
C1.example: The peacock spread its tail.
C1.ielts_writing: Peacocks display feathers to attract mates.
C1.mistake: Weibchen: "peahen"; "proud as a peacock" bedeutet "stolz wie ein Pfau".

C1.def: the highest point of something
C1.example: The climbers reached the peak at dawn.
C1.ielts_writing: Sales peaked in December.
C1.ielts_speaking: "He's at the peak of his career."
C1.mistake: Verb "peak" (den Höhepunkt erreichen); nicht mit "peek" (spähen).

C1.def: a time when traffic or demand is highest
C1.example: Trains are crowded during peak hour.
C1.ielts_writing: Avoid the highway at peak hour.
C1.mistake: Auch "rush hour"; Gegenteil: "off-peak".

C1.def: the busiest time of year for travel
C1.example: Hotels cost more in peak season.
C1.ielts_writing: Peak season starts in July.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "off season"; Plural "peak seasons".

C1.def: a smooth round gem formed in an oyster
C1.example: She wore a pearl necklace.
C1.ielts_writing: Pearls form inside oysters.
C1.mistake: "pearls of wisdom" bedeutet "weise Ratschläge"; Adjektiv "pearly".

C1.def: a poor farmer in past or poor societies
C1.example: Peasants worked the land.
C1.ielts_writing: The peasant revolt shook the kingdom.
C1.mistake: Historisch oder abwertend; Nomen "peasantry".

C1.def: strange or unusual
C1.example: There's a peculiar smell.
C1.ielts_writing: He has a peculiar habit of whistling.
C1.mistake: "peculiar TO sb/sth" bedeutet "typisch für"; Nomen "peculiarity".

C1.def: a person of the same age, status, or ability
C1.example: He is popular among his peers.
C1.ielts_writing: Peers review each other's work.
C1.mistake: "peer pressure" ist Gruppenzwang; Verb "peer" (spähen).

C1.def: evaluation of work by experts in the same field
C1.example: The study passed peer review.
C1.ielts_writing: Peer review ensures academic quality.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "peer-reviewed"; unzählbar.

C1.def: a strong liking for something
C1.example: She has a penchant for jazz.
C1.ielts_writing: His penchant for risk worried colleagues.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "penchant FOR sth"; aus dem Französischen, Aussprache /ˈpentʃɑːnt/.

C1.def: a tool for sharpening pencils
C1.example: He sharpened it with a pencil sharpener.
C1.ielts_writing: The pencil sharpener jammed.
C1.mistake: Verb "sharpen"; Plural "pencil sharpeners".

C1.def: land almost surrounded by water
C1.example: Florida is a peninsula.
C1.ielts_writing: The Iberian Peninsula includes Spain and Portugal.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "peninsular"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: regular payments to a person who has retired
C1.example: He receives a pension.
C1.ielts_writing: Pension funds invest in stocks.
C1.mistake: Person: "pensioner"; "pension fund" ist Pensionskasse.

C1.def: musical instruments played by striking
C1.example: The percussion section kept the rhythm.
C1.ielts_writing: Percussion instruments include drums and cymbals.
C1.mistake: Person: "percussionist"; unzählbar.

C1.def: lasting for a long time, or recurring
C1.example: Funding is a perennial problem.
C1.ielts_writing: Perennial plants bloom every year.
C1.mistake: Bei Pflanzen "perennial" (mehrjährig) im Gegensatz zu "annual".

C1.def: serious danger
C1.example: The sailors were in peril.
C1.ielts_writing: They face peril on the journey.
C1.mistake: "at your own peril" bedeutet "auf eigene Gefahr"; Adjektiv "perilous".

C1.def: full of danger
C1.example: The journey was perilous.
C1.ielts_writing: They crossed a perilous mountain pass.
C1.mistake: Nomen "peril"; Adverb "perilously"; gehobener als "dangerous".

C1.def: a magazine or journal published regularly
C1.example: The library subscribes to many periodicals.
C1.ielts_writing: Academic periodicals publish new research.
C1.mistake: Auch Adjektiv "periodical" (periodisch); Nomen "periodical".

C1.def: ground that stays frozen all year
C1.example: Permafrost is thawing in the Arctic.
C1.ielts_writing: Melting permafrost releases methane.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Klimathema.

C1.def: to spread throughout something
C1.example: The smell of smoke permeated the house.
C1.ielts_writing: Fear permeated the town.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "permeable" (durchlässig); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to make something bad continue
C1.example: Stereotypes perpetuate inequality.
C1.ielts_writing: The system perpetuates poverty.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "perpetual" (ewig); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: continued effort despite difficulty
C1.example: Success requires perseverance.
C1.ielts_writing: Her perseverance paid off.
C1.mistake: Verb "persevere"; Konstruktion: "perseverance IN doing sth".

C1.def: an orange fruit with sweet flesh
C1.example: She ate a ripe persimmon.
C1.ielts_writing: Persimmons are best when soft.
C1.mistake: Plural "persimmons"; unreif herb.

C1.def: to continue firmly despite opposition
C1.example: The cough persisted for weeks.
C1.ielts_writing: She persisted in her efforts.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "persist IN/WITH sth"; Nomen "persistence".

C1.def: continuing firmly or for a long time
C1.example: He is a persistent salesman.
C1.ielts_writing: A persistent cough worried her.
C1.mistake: Nomen "persistence"; Verb "persist".

C1.def: an individual human being
C1.example: She is a kind person.
C1.ielts_writing: Each person must sign the form.
C1.mistake: Plural meist "people", offiziell "persons"; "in person" bedeutet "persönlich".

C1.def: an athlete's best result
C1.example: She ran a personal best.
C1.ielts_writing: He set a new personal best in the marathon.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "PB"; Plural "personal bests".

C1.def: something that makes a thing friendlier or unique
C1.example: A handwritten card adds a personal touch.
C1.ielts_writing: The hotel provides a personal touch.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We try to add a personal touch."
C1.mistake: Verb meist "add a personal touch"; unzählbar.

C1.def: the people employed by an organization
C1.example: Military personnel were evacuated.
C1.ielts_writing: The personnel department handles hiring.
C1.mistake: Immer Plural verwendet; "human resources" ist moderner.

C1.def: able to make others believe or do something
C1.example: She gave a persuasive speech.
C1.ielts_writing: Persuasive arguments changed his mind.
C1.mistake: Verb "persuade"; Nomen "persuasion".

C1.def: relevant to a matter
C1.example: She asked a pertinent question.
C1.ielts_writing: Please provide all pertinent information.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "pertinent TO sth"; Verb "pertain".

C1.def: spreading widely in a place
C1.example: Social media is pervasive.
C1.ielts_writing: A pervasive sense of doubt remained.
C1.mistake: Verb "pervade"; Aussprache mit der Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: one of the colored parts of a flower
C1.example: A petal fell to the ground.
C1.ielts_writing: Rose petals decorated the path.
C1.mistake: Plural "petals"; Gegenstück: "sepal" (Kelchblatt).

C1.def: small and slim, said of a woman
C1.example: She is petite and graceful.
C1.ielts_writing: The shop sells petite sizes.
C1.mistake: Oft in Kleidergrößen: "petite size"; nur für Frauen.

C1.def: the lower middle class
C1.example: Marx described the petite bourgeoisie.
C1.ielts_writing: The petite bourgeoisie includes small business owners.
C1.mistake: Aus dem Französischen; Adjektiv "petit-bourgeois".

C1.def: a formal request signed by many people
C1.example: Residents signed a petition.
C1.ielts_writing: They petitioned the council for change.
C1.mistake: Verb "petition"; Konstruktion: "petition FOR/AGAINST sth".

C1.def: a large smartphone between phone and tablet size
C1.example: He bought a phablet for videos.
C1.ielts_writing: Phablets are bigger than regular smartphones.
C1.ielts_speaking: "My phablet barely fits in my pocket."
C1.mistake: Wortmischung aus "phone" und "tablet"; Plural "phablets".

C1.def: a ruler of ancient Egypt
C1.example: The pharaoh ruled Egypt for decades.
C1.ielts_writing: Pharaohs were buried in pyramids.
C1.mistake: Plural "pharaohs"; Aussprache /ˈferoʊ/ mit stummem h.

C1.def: relating to medicines
C1.example: The pharmaceutical industry funds research.
C1.ielts_writing: Pharmaceutical companies develop new drugs.
C1.mistake: Nomen "pharmaceuticals" (Arzneimittel); Nomen "pharmacy".

C1.def: a person who studies the nature of knowledge and existence
C1.example: The philosopher questioned every assumption.
C1.ielts_writing: Greek philosophers shaped Western thought.
C1.mistake: Nomen "philosophy"; Adjektiv "philosophical".

C1.def: a fraud attempt to steal data by fake messages
C1.example: Phishing emails look like real messages.
C1.ielts_writing: Phishing attacks target passwords and bank details.
C1.mistake: Verb "phish"; Aussprache wie "fishing".

C1.def: the study of speech sounds
C1.example: She studied phonetics at university.
C1.ielts_writing: Phonetics helps learners improve pronunciation.
C1.mistake: Nomen im Singular verwendet: "phonetics is"; Adjektiv "phonetic".

C1.def: an arranged event for taking pictures of a famous person
C1.example: The mayor attended a photo op at the school.
C1.ielts_writing: Politicians love a good photo op.
C1.mistake: Kurzform von "photo opportunity"; oft leicht ironisch.

C1.def: to appear unexpectedly in someone's picture
C1.example: He photobombed the wedding picture.
C1.ielts_writing: Friends love to photobomb group photos.
C1.mistake: Auch Nomen "photobomb"; Verb "photobombed".

C1.def: reporting news mainly through photographs
C1.example: She works in photojournalism.
C1.ielts_writing: Photojournalism captures history in images.
C1.mistake: Person: "photojournalist"; unzählbar.

C1.def: a doctor of medicine
C1.example: The physician examined the patient.
C1.ielts_writing: A family physician knows your medical history.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Physiker" (das ist "physicist"); falscher Freund.

C1.def: a professional who treats injuries with exercise and movement
C1.example: The physiotherapist designed an exercise plan.
C1.ielts_writing: A physiotherapist helped him walk again.
C1.mistake: Im Alltag oft "physical therapist"; Nomen "physiotherapy".

C1.def: a structure extending from the shore into the water
C1.example: They walked to the end of the pier.
C1.ielts_writing: Fishermen gathered on the pier.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We watched the sunset from the pier."
C1.mistake: Nicht "peer" (Gleichgestellter); gleiche Aussprache.

C1.def: a person who travels to a holy place
C1.example: The pilgrim walked for weeks.
C1.ielts_writing: Pilgrims visit shrines around the world.
C1.mistake: Nomen "pilgrimage" (Wallfahrt); "Pilgrim Fathers" sind die Gründerväter von Plymouth.

C1.def: a light golden lager beer
C1.example: He ordered a cold pilsner.
C1.ielts_writing: Pilsner originated in the Czech town of Plzeň.
C1.mistake: Auch "pilsener"; Bierart; Plural "pilsners".

C1.def: a cocktail of rum, coconut, and pineapple
C1.example: She ordered a pina colada on the beach.
C1.ielts_writing: A pina colada is sweet and creamy.
C1.mistake: Spanisch für "gepresste Ananas"; Plural "pina coladas".

C1.def: to squeeze skin between finger and thumb
C1.example: She pinched his arm.
C1.ielts_writing: Prices pinch family budgets.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen "a pinch of" (eine Prise); "feel the pinch" heißt "den Geldmangel spüren".

C1.def: a unit of liquid equal to about half a liter
C1.example: He drank a pint of beer.
C1.ielts_writing: A pint of milk costs one dollar.
C1.mistake: Ca. 0,47 Liter; Aussprache /paɪnt/.

C1.def: a person who first explores or develops something
C1.example: She was a pioneer in computing.
C1.ielts_writing: The team pioneered a new method.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "pioneering"; Konstruktion: "pioneer IN a field".

C1.def: a long pipe for carrying liquids or gas, or a process
C1.example: The pipeline carries oil.
C1.ielts_writing: New products are in the pipeline.
C1.mistake: "in the pipeline" bedeutet "in Vorbereitung"; Plural "pipelines".

C1.def: a person who robs ships, or who copies things illegally
C1.example: Pirates attacked the ship.
C1.ielts_writing: The film was pirated online.
C1.mistake: Nomen "piracy" (Piraterie, Raubkopie); Verb "pirate".

C1.def: a hole in the ground, or a fruit stone
C1.example: They dug a pit for the fire.
C1.ielts_writing: Remove the pit from the cherry.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "pit sb AGAINST sb" (gegeneinander antreten lassen); "pit stop" ist Boxenstopp.

C1.def: the quality of a sound, a sports field, or a sales talk
C1.example: The singer's pitch was perfect.
C1.ielts_writing: He pitched the idea to investors.
C1.mistake: Mehrdeutig: Tonhöhe, Spielfeld, Verkaufsgespräch; "pitch a tent" bedeutet "Zelt aufbauen".

C1.def: to make someone less angry
C1.example: The manager tried to placate the customer.
C1.ielts_writing: Leaders placated protesters with promises.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; ähnlich "appease".

C1.def: a harmless substance given as medicine to test effects
C1.example: Half the group received a placebo.
C1.ielts_writing: The placebo effect can improve symptoms.
C1.mistake: Plural "placebos"; "placebo effect" ist Placeboeffekt.

C1.def: a deadly disease, or a large number of pests
C1.example: The plague spread through Europe.
C1.ielts_writing: A plague of locusts destroyed the crops.
C1.mistake: Verb "plague sb WITH/BY sth"; "avoid like the plague" heißt "meiden wie die Pest".

C1.def: simple, or obvious, or a flat area
C1.example: She wore a plain white dress.
C1.ielts_writing: The truth is plain to see.
C1.mistake: Nicht "plane" (Flugzeug); "in plain sight" bedeutet "für alle sichtbar".

C1.def: wearing ordinary clothes, not uniform
C1.example: A plain-clothes officer arrested him.
C1.ielts_writing: Plain-clothes detectives patrolled the station.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "uniformed"; Bindestrich bei Adjektiv.

C1.def: to organize a route for a trip
C1.example: We should plan an itinerary before leaving.
C1.ielts_writing: It helps to plan an itinerary around the main sights.
C1.mistake: Nomen "itinerary"; Verb "plan".

C1.def: a flat area of high land, or a period of no progress
C1.example: The village sits on a plateau.
C1.ielts_writing: Sales hit a plateau.
C1.mistake: Verb "plateau" (stagnieren); Plural "plateaus" oder "plateaux".

C1.def: likely to be true
C1.example: It was a plausible explanation.
C1.ielts_writing: The theory sounds plausible.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "implausible"; Nomen "plausibility".

C1.def: to act according to one's own standards
C1.example: She likes to play by her own rules.
C1.ielts_writing: They play by their own rules.
C1.mistake: Variante: "play by one's own rules"; bedeutet "sich nicht anpassen".

C1.def: a list of songs to be played
C1.example: She made a playlist for the party.
C1.ielts_writing: Streaming services create personalized playlists.
C1.mistake: Plural "playlists"; auch bei Videos.

C1.def: a person who writes plays
C1.example: The playwright won a prize.
C1.ielts_writing: Shakespeare is the world's best-known playwright.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A young playwright staged her first play."
C1.mistake: "wright" bedeutet "Handwerker"; Aussprache wie "right".

C1.def: an urgent request, or a statement in court
C1.example: He made a plea for help.
C1.ielts_writing: The defendant entered a guilty plea.
C1.mistake: "plea bargain" ist Absprache im Strafverfahren; Konstruktion: "plea FOR sth".

C1.def: to beg, or to state in court
C1.example: She pleaded for mercy.
C1.ielts_writing: He pleaded guilty to the charge.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: plead, pleaded/pled; "plead guilty/not guilty".

C1.def: to promise formally
C1.example: The company pledged to cut emissions.
C1.ielts_writing: She made a pledge to donate.
C1.mistake: "pledge allegiance" bedeutet "Treue schwören"; Konstruktion: "pledge TO do sth".

C1.def: a very large amount
C1.example: The store offers a plethora of options.
C1.ielts_writing: A plethora of reasons supports the decision.
C1.ielts_speaking: "There's a plethora of books on the topic."
C1.mistake: Immer mit "of": "a plethora OF sth"; kann auch "zu viel" bedeuten.

C1.def: a device for connecting to electricity, or to block a hole
C1.example: Pull the plug from the socket.
C1.ielts_writing: They plugged the leak.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb "plug in/into"; "pull the plug" bedeutet "den Stecker ziehen".

C1.def: the system of pipes in a building
C1.example: The old plumbing leaked.
C1.ielts_writing: Plumbing repairs can be expensive.
C1.mistake: Person: "plumber"; "b" ist stumm: /ˈplʌmɪŋ/.

C1.def: fairly fat or rounded
C1.example: She picked plump tomatoes.
C1.ielts_writing: The baby has plump cheeks.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "plump up" (aufschütteln); positiv oder neutral bei Früchten.

C1.def: to fall or dive suddenly
C1.example: The car plunged into the river.
C1.ielts_writing: Prices plunged last month.
C1.mistake: "take the plunge" bedeutet "den Sprung wagen"; Nomen "plunge".

C1.def: a seed case, or a small group of whales
C1.example: The pea pod split open.
C1.ielts_writing: A pod of dolphins swam by.
C1.mistake: Auch Technik: "pod" als Kapsel; "podcast" ist ein anderes Wort.

C1.def: causing sadness or sympathy
C1.example: It was a poignant moment.
C1.ielts_writing: The film gives a poignant portrait of loss.
C1.mistake: Aussprache /ˈpɔɪnjənt/; "g" ist stumm; Nomen "poignancy".

C1.def: to direct attention to something with a finger
C1.example: She pointed at the map.
C1.ielts_writing: The evidence points to a different suspect.
C1.mistake: "point out" bedeutet "darauf hinweisen"; "point at sb" heißt "auf jemanden zeigen".

C1.def: an expressionless face hiding true feelings
C1.example: He kept a poker face during the negotiations.
C1.ielts_writing: A poker face helps in bluffing.
C1.mistake: Meist "keep a poker face"; Plural "poker faces".

C1.def: either end of the earth's axis, or a long thin stick
C1.example: Explorers reached the North Pole.
C1.ielts_writing: A flag hung from the pole.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "polar"; "pole" auch Mensch aus Polen: "Pole" (großgeschrieben).

C1.def: a person who creates government or company policy
C1.example: Policy makers debated the new tax.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers inform policy makers with data.
C1.mistake: Auch "policymaker" zusammengeschrieben; Plural "policy makers".

C1.def: a survey of opinions, or a voting place
C1.example: A poll showed support for the plan.
C1.ielts_writing: Voters went to the polls.
C1.mistake: Person: "pollster"; "polls" auch Wahllokale.

C1.def: to transfer pollen to fertilize plants
C1.example: Bees pollinate fruit trees.
C1.ielts_writing: Wind can pollinate some crops.
C1.mistake: Nomen "pollination"; Person/Tier: "pollinator".

C1.def: the transfer of pollen to fertilize a plant
C1.example: Pollination depends on bees.
C1.ielts_writing: Cross-pollination improves crop diversity.
C1.mistake: Verb "pollinate"; unzählbar.

C1.def: a substance that pollutes the environment
C1.example: Factories release pollutants into the air.
C1.ielts_writing: Carbon monoxide is a common pollutant.
C1.mistake: Verb "pollute"; Nomen "pollution".

C1.def: a small body of still water
C1.example: Ducks swam in the pond.
C1.ielts_writing: The pond froze over in winter.
C1.mistake: "big fish in a small pond" ist eine Redewendung; kleiner als "lake".

C1.def: to burst with a short sound, or to go quickly
C1.example: The balloon popped.
C1.ielts_writing: She popped into the store.
C1.mistake: "pop the question" bedeutet "einen Heiratsantrag machen"; "pop up" heißt "auftauchen".

C1.def: the head of the Roman Catholic Church
C1.example: The pope addressed the crowd.
C1.ielts_writing: Millions watched the pope's visit.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "papal"; Titel großgeschrieben vor Namen: "Pope Francis".

C1.def: a harbor for ships, or a computer connection point
C1.example: The ship arrived at the port.
C1.ielts_writing: The laptop has a USB port.
C1.mistake: "port" auch Portwein; Adjektiv "portable" (tragbar).

C1.def: a person who carries luggage, or a doorkeeper
C1.example: The porter carried our bags.
C1.ielts_writing: The hotel porter called a taxi.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A porter helped her with the suitcases."
C1.mistake: Auch dunkles Bier "porter"; Plural "porters".

C1.def: a collection of work or investments
C1.example: She showed her design portfolio.
C1.ielts_writing: Diversifying an investment portfolio reduces risk.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I'll bring my portfolio to the interview."
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Arbeitsmappe und Geldanlagen; Plural "portfolios".

C1.def: to show or describe in a particular way
C1.example: The film portrays the war realistically.
C1.ielts_writing: She portrays a brave nurse.
C1.mistake: Nomen "portrayal"; Konstruktion: "portray sb AS sth".

C1.def: to create a problem, or to stand for a picture
C1.example: The virus poses a serious threat.
C1.ielts_writing: They posed for a photo.
C1.mistake: "pose a question" und "pose a threat" sind feste Wendungen; Nomen "pose" (Haltung).

C1.def: a small sticky note
C1.example: She left a post-it on the screen.
C1.ielts_writing: Post-its help organize tasks.
C1.mistake: Markenname; allgemeiner "sticky note"; Plural "post-its".

C1.def: to delay until a later time
C1.example: They postponed the meeting.
C1.ielts_writing: The match was postponed due to rain.
C1.mistake: Nomen "postponement"; Konstruktion: "postpone sth UNTIL/TO + Zeit".

C1.def: birds raised for meat or eggs
C1.example: Poultry is a common source of protein.
C1.ielts_writing: The farm raises poultry and cattle.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Wash your hands after handling raw poultry."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar, wird mit Plural-Verb verwendet: "poultry are"; Haustiere: "domestic fowl".

C1.def: the state of being very poor
C1.example: Millions live in poverty.
C1.ielts_writing: Poverty affects children's education.
C1.mistake: "poverty line" ist die Armutsgrenze; Adjektiv "poor".

C1.def: a fast boat with a powerful engine
C1.example: The powerboat raced across the bay.
C1.ielts_writing: Powerboats need a lot of fuel.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "sailboat"; Plural "powerboats".

C1.def: activities to create a good public image
C1.example: PR helped repair the brand's image.
C1.ielts_writing: The firm hired a PR agency after the scandal.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung "public relations"; "PR disaster" ist ein Imageschaden.

C1.def: a person actively engaged in a profession
C1.example: The doctor is a general practitioner.
C1.ielts_writing: Practitioners need up-to-date training.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "theorist"; "general practitioner" ist Hausarzt.

C1.def: dealing with things in a practical way
C1.example: She took a pragmatic approach.
C1.ielts_writing: Pragmatic solutions work better than ideal plans.
C1.mistake: Nomen "pragmatism"; im Deutschen auch "pragmatisch".

C1.def: an order for something before it is released
C1.example: Fans lined up for the pre-order.
C1.ielts_writing: You can pre-order the album today.
C1.mistake: Auch Verb "pre-order"; Bindestrich möglich: "preorder".

C1.def: to give a religious talk, or to advise in a moralizing way
C1.example: The priest preached on Sunday.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't preach to me about honesty.
C1.mistake: "preach to the choir" bedeutet "offene Türen einrennen"; Person "preacher".

C1.def: not secure or stable
C1.example: He held a precarious position.
C1.ielts_writing: The company's finances are precarious.
C1.mistake: Adverb "precariously"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: an action taken to avoid danger
C1.example: They took precautions against the flood.
C1.ielts_writing: Take precautions when traveling alone.
C1.ielts_speaking: "As a precaution, we closed the road."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "precautionary"; Konstruktion: "precaution AGAINST sth".

C1.def: an earlier case used as a guide
C1.example: The ruling set a precedent.
C1.ielts_writing: There is no precedent for this decision.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Verb "precede".

C1.def: exactness
C1.example: Surgeons work with precision.
C1.ielts_writing: The machine ensures precision.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The precision of the measurement is astonishing."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "precise"; unzählbar.

C1.def: an animal that hunts other animals
C1.example: The lion is a top predator.
C1.ielts_writing: Predators keep prey populations balanced.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "prey"; Adjektiv "predatory".

C1.def: a person who held a job before someone else
C1.example: She praised her predecessor.
C1.ielts_writing: The new CEO reversed her predecessor's decision.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "successor"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: mainly
C1.example: The area is predominantly rural.
C1.ielts_writing: The audience was predominantly young.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "predominant"; ähnlich "mainly" aber formeller.

C1.def: better or more suitable
C1.example: Walking is preferable to driving.
C1.ielts_writing: A quiet room is preferable.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "preferable TO sth"; Verb "prefer".

C1.def: the state of carrying a baby
C1.example: Pregnancy lasts about nine months.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular checkups are important during pregnancy.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "pregnant"; "pregnancy test" ist Schwangerschaftstest.

C1.def: from before written records
C1.example: Prehistoric tools were found in the cave.
C1.ielts_writing: Prehistoric humans hunted large animals.
C1.mistake: Nomen "prehistory"; umgangssprachlich "ewig alt".

C1.def: an unfair opinion formed without knowledge
C1.example: Prejudice against minorities persists.
C1.ielts_writing: The statement could prejudice the jury.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "prejudice AGAINST sb"; Adjektiv "prejudiced".

C1.def: coming before the main event
C1.example: Preliminary results look promising.
C1.ielts_writing: A preliminary meeting set the agenda.
C1.mistake: Nomen "preliminaries" (Vorrunde, Vorbereitungen).

C1.def: first in importance or quality
C1.example: It's the premier event of the year.
C1.ielts_writing: She is the nation's premier scientist.
C1.mistake: Als Nomen "premier" (Ministerpräsident); Aussprache /prɪˈmɪr/, gleich wie "premiere".

C1.def: the first public performance of a show
C1.example: The film's premiere was a big event.
C1.ielts_writing: The play premiered in Paris.
C1.mistake: Als Verb "premiere" (Premiere haben); Aussprache gleich wie "premier".

C1.def: an idea on which an argument is based
C1.example: The argument's premise was flawed.
C1.ielts_writing: On the premise that prices will rise, he invested.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The premise of the film is simple."
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "premises" (Gelände) verwechseln; Logik: Prämisse vs. Konklusion.

C1.def: a building and the land around it
C1.example: Smoking is banned on the premises.
C1.ielts_writing: The company's premises were searched.
C1.mistake: Immer Plural; "on the premises" bedeutet "vor Ort".

C1.def: an extra payment, or a regular insurance fee
C1.example: The insurance premium rose.
C1.ielts_writing: Quality goods sell at a premium.
C1.mistake: "at a premium" bedeutet "zu erhöhtem Preis" oder "knapp"; Adjektiv "premium" (hochwertig).

C1.def: paid for in advance
C1.example: She bought a prepaid card.
C1.ielts_writing: Prepaid phones require no contract.
C1.mistake: Verb "prepay"; Gegenteil: "postpaid".

C1.def: to authorize a medicine, or to state a rule
C1.example: The doctor prescribed antibiotics.
C1.ielts_writing: The rules prescribe how to vote.
C1.mistake: Nicht mit "proscribe" (verbieten) verwechseln; Nomen "prescription".

C1.def: a doctor's written order for medicine
C1.example: I need a prescription for the cream.
C1.ielts_writing: The pharmacist filled my prescription.
C1.ielts_speaking: "This medicine is available only by prescription."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "over-the-counter"; "prescription drug" ist verschreibungspflichtig.

C1.def: neat and fit to be seen
C1.example: He wanted to look presentable.
C1.ielts_writing: The room was barely presentable.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "make oneself presentable" (sich herrichten); nicht "present" (Geschenk).

C1.def: at the moment, or soon
C1.example: He is presently unavailable.
C1.ielts_writing: The manager will see you presently.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: "derzeit" und "bald"; im Alltag meist "currently".

C1.def: the act of keeping something safe or unchanged
C1.example: The preservation of forests is vital.
C1.ielts_writing: Food preservation extends shelf life.
C1.mistake: Verb "preserve"; Gegenteil: "destruction".

C1.def: to be in charge of a meeting or event
C1.example: The judge presided over the trial.
C1.ielts_writing: She will preside at the ceremony.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "preside OVER/AT sth"; Verwandt mit "president".

C1.def: the office or term of a president
C1.example: His presidency lasted eight years.
C1.ielts_writing: The presidency changed hands in January.
C1.mistake: Nomen "president"; Plural "presidencies".

C1.def: relating to a president
C1.example: The presidential election takes place in November.
C1.ielts_writing: A presidential debate attracted millions of viewers.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe; Nomen "presidency".

C1.def: having high status or reputation
C1.example: She won a prestigious award.
C1.ielts_writing: He attends a prestigious university.
C1.mistake: Nomen "prestige" (Ansehen); nicht "prestissimo".

C1.def: used to say something is probably true
C1.example: Presumably, he forgot.
C1.ielts_writing: You presumably know the way.
C1.mistake: Verb "presume"; Konstruktion: Satzadverb am Anfang.

C1.def: to suppose that something is true
C1.example: I presume you've heard the news.
C1.ielts_writing: She presumed they were at home.
C1.mistake: Nomen "presumption"; "presume innocent" ist Unschuldsvermutung.

C1.def: to be most common or win over
C1.example: Common sense prevailed.
C1.ielts_writing: Justice must prevail.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "prevail OVER sb/sth"; Adjektiv "prevailing" (vorherrschend).

C1.def: how common something is
C1.example: The prevalence of obesity is rising.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers measure disease prevalence.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "prevalent"; Konstruktion: "prevalence OF sth".

C1.def: actions to stop something from happening
C1.example: Prevention is better than cure.
C1.ielts_writing: Crime prevention programs reduce burglary.
C1.mistake: Verb "prevent"; Adjektiv "preventive".

C1.def: an animal hunted by another, or a victim
C1.example: The lion chased its prey.
C1.ielts_writing: Elderly people fall prey to scams.
C1.mistake: "fall prey to" bedeutet "zum Opfer fallen"; Verb "prey on sb" (jagen auf).

C1.def: a label showing cost, or the total cost
C1.example: The jacket had a high price tag.
C1.ielts_writing: The project carries a hefty price tag.
C1.ielts_speaking: "That comes with a big price tag."
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "a price tag of five million"; Plural "price tags".

C1.def: so valuable that its price cannot be measured
C1.example: The painting is priceless.
C1.ielts_writing: Their support was priceless.
C1.mistake: Nicht "wertlos": "priceless" bedeutet unbezahlbar (positiv); Gegenteil "worthless".

C1.def: the hours when most people watch TV
C1.example: The show airs in prime time.
C1.ielts_writing: Prime-time ratings drive advertising prices.
C1.mistake: Auch "prime-time" als Adjektiv; Plural "prime times".

C1.def: belonging to an early stage of development
C1.example: They lived in primitive conditions.
C1.ielts_writing: Primitive tools were made of stone.
C1.mistake: Kann abwertend wirken; "primitive" in der Kunst: naive Kunst.

C1.def: most important, or the head of a school
C1.example: Cost is the principal concern.
C1.ielts_writing: The principal welcomed the new students.
C1.mistake: Nicht "principle" (Prinzip): gleiche Aussprache, andere Bedeutung.

C1.def: acting according to firm moral rules
C1.example: She is a principled leader.
C1.ielts_writing: A principled stand cost him his job.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "unprincipled"; Nomen "principle".

C1.def: text or images on paper, or to produce copies
C1.example: Please print the document.
C1.ielts_writing: The book is in large print.
C1.mistake: "in print" bedeutet "im Handel"; "fine print" ist das Kleingedruckte.

C1.def: to decide which things are most important
C1.example: We need to prioritize our tasks.
C1.ielts_writing: The government prioritizes health care.
C1.mistake: Nomen "priority"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: in perfect condition, or untouched
C1.example: The beach was pristine.
C1.ielts_writing: He kept his car in pristine condition.
C1.mistake: "in pristine condition" bedeutet "in Bestzustand"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a school funded by fees, not the government
C1.example: She attended a private school.
C1.ielts_writing: Private schools often have small classes.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "public school" (staatliche Schule in den USA).

C1.def: to transfer from public to private ownership
C1.example: The government plans to privatize the railway.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics oppose efforts to privatize schools.
C1.mistake: Nomen "privatization"; Gegenteil: "nationalize".

C1.def: a special right granted to a person or group
C1.example: Education is a privilege.
C1.ielts_writing: He used his privilege to help others.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "privileged"; "It's a privilege to ..." ist höfliche Formel.

C1.def: done without charge for the public good
C1.example: The lawyer took the case pro bono.
C1.ielts_writing: Pro bono work helps people who cannot afford fees.
C1.mistake: Aus dem Lateinischen "pro bono publico"; meist bei Anwälten.

C1.def: a period of supervision instead of prison, or a trial period
C1.example: He was sentenced to probation.
C1.ielts_writing: New employees are on probation for three months.
C1.mistake: "probation officer" ist Bewährungshelfer; Adjektiv "probationary".

C1.def: an investigation, or a device for exploring
C1.example: A probe was launched to Mars.
C1.ielts_writing: Police probed the company's accounts.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "probe INTO sth"; Plural "probes".

C1.def: presenting difficulties or doubts
C1.example: The situation is problematic.
C1.ielts_writing: Problematic behavior should be addressed.
C1.mistake: Nomen "problem"; kein Wort "problematisch" als Euphemismus.

C1.def: a legal action, or an event with set steps
C1.example: Legal proceedings began in March.
C1.ielts_writing: The proceedings were broadcast live.
C1.mistake: Immer Plural; "start proceedings AGAINST sb" bedeutet "klagen gegen".

C1.def: money received from an event or sale
C1.example: Proceeds go to charity.
C1.ielts_writing: The proceeds from the sale were divided equally.
C1.mistake: Immer Plural; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe, anders als Verb "proceed".

C1.def: the act of handling or changing information or goods
C1.example: Payment processing takes two days.
C1.ielts_writing: Food processing preserves nutrients.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "word processing" ist Textverarbeitung.

C1.def: a machine that processes data, or a kitchen device
C1.example: The laptop has a fast processor.
C1.ielts_writing: A food processor chops vegetables.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Computer-Chip und Küchenmaschine.

C1.def: to announce publicly
C1.example: They proclaimed a national holiday.
C1.ielts_writing: The banner proclaimed victory.
C1.mistake: Nomen "proclamation"; gehobener als "announce".

C1.def: to delay doing something unnecessarily
C1.example: I procrastinate until the last minute.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't procrastinate on important tasks.
C1.mistake: Nomen "procrastination"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: achieving a lot
C1.example: It was a productive meeting.
C1.ielts_writing: She is highly productive at work.
C1.mistake: Nomen "productivity"; Gegenteil: "unproductive".

C1.def: the rate at which work is done
C1.example: Workers' productivity rose.
C1.ielts_writing: Flexible hours increase productivity.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: making money
C1.example: The company became profitable.
C1.ielts_writing: A profitable business pays its debts.
C1.mistake: Nomen "profit"; Nomen "profitability".

C1.def: having great depth or intensity
C1.example: The discovery had a profound effect.
C1.ielts_writing: She felt profound sadness.
C1.mistake: Adverb "profoundly"; Nomen "profundity".

C1.def: an estimate of future figures, or a projected image
C1.example: Sales projections look strong.
C1.ielts_writing: The projection shows a tight budget.
C1.mistake: Verb "project" (/prəˈdʒekt/ = prognostizieren); Plural "projections".

C1.def: a device that shows images on a screen
C1.example: The projector failed during the talk.
C1.ielts_writing: A video projector sits on the ceiling.
C1.mistake: Verb "project"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: producing many works or offspring
C1.example: She is a prolific writer.
C1.ielts_writing: Prolific authors publish every year.
C1.mistake: Bei Autoren im Sinn von "vielschreibend"; Adverb "prolifically".

C1.def: important or easily noticed
C1.example: He is a prominent lawyer.
C1.ielts_writing: A prominent feature of the city is its tower.
C1.mistake: Nomen "prominence"; Adverb "prominently".

C1.def: a person who organizes events or supports something
C1.example: The promoter arranged the concert.
C1.ielts_writing: A boxing promoter signed the fighter.
C1.mistake: Verb "promote"; "real estate promoter" ist ein Bauträger.

C1.def: advancement to a higher position, or advertising
C1.example: She received a promotion.
C1.ielts_writing: The store runs a special promotion.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "promotion TO + Stelle"; Verb "promote".

C1.def: to cause something to happen
C1.example: The report prompted a debate.
C1.ielts_writing: What prompted you to change your mind?
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "prompt sb TO do sth"; auch Adjektiv "prompt" (pünktlich).

C1.def: very noticeable
C1.example: She has a pronounced accent.
C1.ielts_writing: The effects were more pronounced in winter.
C1.mistake: Verb "pronounce" (aussprechen, verkünden); hier nicht "ausgesprochen" als Aussprache.

C1.def: evidence that shows something is true
C1.example: Show me proof of purchase.
C1.ielts_writing: There is no proof that he was there.
C1.mistake: Verb "prove"; "proof of purchase" ist Kaufbeleg.

C1.def: to check text for errors
C1.example: Always proofread your essays.
C1.ielts_writing: She proofread the manuscript twice.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: proofread, proofread, proofread; Person "proofreader".

C1.def: information used to influence opinion, often misleading
C1.example: The film was banned as propaganda.
C1.ielts_writing: Governments use propaganda in wartime.
C1.mistake: Person: "propagandist"; unzählbar.

C1.def: a natural tendency to behave in a certain way
C1.example: He has a propensity for exaggeration.
C1.ielts_writing: A propensity to take risks defines her career.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "propensity FOR/TO sth"; gehoben.

C1.def: something owned, or a quality of something
C1.example: The property was sold last year.
C1.ielts_writing: Water has unusual chemical properties.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Besitz und Eigenschaft; Plural "properties".

C1.def: a person who supports an idea or cause
C1.example: She is a proponent of free trade.
C1.ielts_writing: Proponents of the law say it saves lives.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "opponent"; Konstruktion: "proponent OF sth".

C1.def: to put forward an idea, or to ask someone to marry
C1.example: I propose a new schedule.
C1.ielts_writing: He proposed to her on the beach.
C1.mistake: Nomen "proposal"; Konstruktion: "propose TO sb" (Heiratsantrag machen).

C1.def: an idea or offer put forward
C1.example: He made her a business proposition.
C1.ielts_writing: The proposition was rejected.
C1.mistake: Auch in der Logik Aussage; "value proposition" ist Nutzenversprechen.

C1.def: ordinary written language, not poetry
C1.example: The novel is written in elegant prose.
C1.ielts_writing: She prefers prose to poetry.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "poetry"; Adjektiv "prosaic" (nüchtern).

C1.def: to take legal action against someone for a crime
C1.example: Shoplifters will be prosecuted.
C1.ielts_writing: The state decided to prosecute the case.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "prosecute sb FOR sth"; Nomen "prosecution".

C1.def: legal action against someone, or the lawyers who bring it
C1.example: The prosecution presented new evidence.
C1.ielts_writing: He faces prosecution for tax fraud.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "defense"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: a lawyer who represents the state in criminal cases
C1.example: The prosecutor questioned the witness.
C1.ielts_writing: Federal prosecutors opened an investigation.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The prosecutor asked for a long sentence."
C1.mistake: In den USA oft "district attorney"; Gegenteil: "defense attorney".

C1.def: likely to happen or become something
C1.example: The prospective buyers viewed the house.
C1.ielts_writing: Prospective students attended the open day.
C1.mistake: Nomen "prospect" (Aussicht); Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to be successful and rich
C1.example: Small businesses prosper here.
C1.ielts_writing: The town prospered after the railway arrived.
C1.mistake: Nomen "prosperity"; Adjektiv "prosperous".

C1.def: a state of success and wealth
C1.example: The country enjoyed a period of prosperity.
C1.ielts_writing: Economic prosperity improves living standards.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Gegenteil: "poverty".

C1.def: a gland in men near the bladder
C1.example: Prostate cancer is common in older men.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular screening checks the prostate.
C1.mistake: Nicht "prostrate" (ausgestreckt); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: intended to protect
C1.example: She wore protective gloves.
C1.ielts_writing: Parents can be overly protective.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "protective OF sb/sth"; Nomen "protection".

C1.def: relating to a branch of Christianity from the Reformation
C1.example: The town has a Protestant church.
C1.ielts_writing: Protestant reformers challenged the Church.
C1.mistake: Immer großgeschrieben; Nomen "Protestantism".

C1.def: an official procedure or set of rules
C1.example: Hospitals follow strict safety protocols.
C1.ielts_writing: Diplomatic protocol governs official visits.
C1.mistake: Auch IT: Netzwerkprotokoll; Gerichtsprotokoll heißt "minutes"/"transcript".

C1.def: a short well-known saying that expresses a truth
C1.example: An old proverb says that haste makes waste.
C1.ielts_writing: Proverbs reflect a culture's wisdom.
C1.ielts_speaking: "As the proverb goes, practice makes perfect."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "proverbial" (sprichwörtlich); Plural "proverbs".

C1.def: a main administrative region of a country
C1.example: Quebec is a Canadian province.
C1.ielts_writing: The province was divided into districts.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Ontario is the largest province by population."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "provincial"; "outside the province" bedeutet "außerhalb des Zuständigkeitsbereichs".

C1.def: relating to a province, or unsophisticated
C1.example: The provincial government passed the law.
C1.ielts_writing: He had a provincial outlook.
C1.mistake: Kann abwertend sein (kleinstädtisch); neutral: "provincial capital".

C1.def: a condition in a law, or the supply of something
C1.example: The treaty contains a key provision.
C1.ielts_writing: The provision of clean water is essential.
C1.mistake: "make provision for" bedeutet "Vorkehrungen treffen für"; Plural "provisions" auch Vorräte.

C1.def: intended to cause strong reactions
C1.example: The film is provocative.
C1.ielts_writing: She asked a provocative question.
C1.mistake: Verb "provoke"; Nomen "provocation".

C1.def: to cause a reaction, especially anger
C1.example: The speech provoked anger.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't provoke the dog.
C1.mistake: Nomen "provocation"; Konstruktion: "provoke sb INTO doing sth".

C1.def: careful and sensible about the future
C1.example: It's prudent to save money.
C1.ielts_writing: A prudent investor diversifies.
C1.mistake: Nomen "prudence"; Gegenteil: "imprudent".

C1.def: beliefs presented as scientific without proof
C1.example: Astrology is often called pseudoscience.
C1.ielts_writing: Pseudoscience lacks testable evidence.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "pseudoscientific"; abwertend.

C1.def: a doctor who treats mental illness
C1.example: The psychiatrist prescribed medication.
C1.ielts_writing: A psychiatrist can diagnose mental disorders.
C1.mistake: Unterschied zu "psychologist" (kein Arzt); "p" ist stumm.

C1.def: an official who prosecutes crimes on behalf of the state
C1.example: The public prosecutor filed charges.
C1.ielts_writing: A public prosecutor leads the investigation.
C1.mistake: In den USA eher "district attorney" oder "prosecutor"; im Deutschen "Staatsanwalt".

C1.def: to make something known to the public
C1.example: The charity publicized its campaign.
C1.ielts_writing: Authors publicize new books on tour.
C1.mistake: Nomen "publicity"; Partizip "publicized" (viel beachtet).

C1.def: a small pool of water on the ground
C1.example: He jumped in a puddle.
C1.ielts_writing: The road was full of puddles after the rain.
C1.mistake: Plural "puddles"; "big fish in a small puddle" ist ähnlich "pond".

C1.def: the regular beat of the heart
C1.example: The nurse checked his pulse.
C1.ielts_writing: Her pulse quickened.
C1.mistake: "have a finger on the pulse" bedeutet "am Puls der Zeit sein"; auch Hülsenfrüchte.

C1.def: to move liquid with a machine
C1.example: They pumped water out of the basement.
C1.ielts_writing: Investors pumped millions into the startup.
C1.mistake: "pump up" bedeutet "aufpumpen"; "gas pump" ist die Zapfsäule.

C1.def: a hit with the fist, or a fruit drink
C1.example: He threw a punch.
C1.ielts_writing: They served fruit punch.
C1.mistake: Mehrere Bedeutungen: Schlag, Locher, Punsch; "beat to the punch" bedeutet "zuvorkommen".

C1.def: arriving at the agreed time
C1.example: He is always punctual.
C1.ielts_writing: Punctual arrival is expected.
C1.mistake: Nomen "punctuality"; Adverb "punctually".

C1.def: to add punctuation, or to interrupt at intervals
C1.example: Remember to punctuate your sentences.
C1.ielts_writing: Laughter punctuated his speech.
C1.mistake: Nomen "punctuation" (Zeichensetzung); bildlich: "punctuated BY sth".

C1.def: a young learner, or the dark center of the eye
C1.example: The pupil raised her hand.
C1.ielts_writing: His pupils widened in the dark.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Schüler und Augenpupille; Plural "pupils".

C1.def: only or completely
C1.example: It was purely coincidental.
C1.ielts_writing: The offer is purely optional.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I did it purely out of curiosity."
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "pure"; "purely" betont Ausschließlichkeit.

C1.def: a pin with a large head for fastening notes
C1.example: She fixed the map with a pushpin.
C1.ielts_writing: Pushpins mark locations on the board.
C1.mistake: Plural "pushpins"; auch "thumbtack".

C1.def: too eager to get what you want
C1.example: The salesman was pushy.
C1.ielts_writing: A pushy parent can harm a child's confidence.
