C1.mistake: Abwertend; Gegenteil: "laid-back".

C1.def: to suggest for consideration
C1.example: She put forward a new idea.
C1.ielts_writing: The committee put forward several candidates.
C1.mistake: Trennbar: "put an idea forward" (selten); Nomen: "forward".

C1.def: to delay, or to discourage
C1.example: We had to put off the meeting.
C1.ielts_writing: The smell put me off.
C1.mistake: Trennbar bei Pronomen: "put it off"; auch "jemanden abstoßen".

C1.def: to present to someone for a decision or answer
C1.example: The proposal was put to a vote.
C1.ielts_writing: The question will be put to the committee.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The matter was put to the test."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendungen: "put sth TO a vote/the test"; Passiv häufig.

C1.def: a tall metal tower that supports power cables
C1.example: A pylon stood in the field.
C1.ielts_writing: Pylons carry electricity across the country.
C1.mistake: Plural "pylons"; im Alltag auch "transmission tower".

C1.def: a large nonvenomous snake, or a programming language
C1.example: A python wrapped around the branch.
C1.ielts_writing: Many students learn Python as their first programming language.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Schlange und Programmiersprache; Schlange wird kleingeschrieben.

C1.def: relating to quality rather than quantity
C1.example: Qualitative research uses interviews.
C1.ielts_writing: A qualitative analysis explores people's experiences.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "quantitative"; Nomen "quality".

C1.def: a difficult situation with no obvious solution
C1.example: She was in a quandary about the offer.
C1.ielts_writing: The company faces a quandary over prices.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "in a quandary ABOUT/OVER sth".

C1.def: relating to numbers or amounts
C1.example: Quantitative research relies on statistics.
C1.ielts_writing: A quantitative study measured the effects.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "qualitative"; Nomen "quantity".

C1.def: the smallest amount of energy, or relating to quantum physics
C1.example: Quantum physics explains atomic behavior.
C1.ielts_writing: A quantum leap in technology occurred.
C1.mistake: "quantum leap" bedeutet "großer Sprung"; Plural "quanta".

C1.def: a unit of liquid equal to about one liter
C1.example: She bought a quart of milk.
C1.ielts_writing: A quart equals two pints.
C1.mistake: Ein US-Quart entspricht etwa 0,95 Liter; vier Quarts ergeben eine Gallone.

C1.def: one of four equal parts, or a three-month period
C1.example: She ate a quarter of the pie.
C1.ielts_writing: Profits rose in the first quarter.
C1.mistake: Auch 25-Cent-Münze: "a quarter"; Stadtteil: "the French Quarter".

C1.def: happening every three months
C1.example: The company issues quarterly reports.
C1.ielts_writing: Quarterly earnings beat expectations.
C1.mistake: Auch Adverb "quarterly"; als Nomen: vierteljährliche Zeitschrift.

C1.def: a question, or a request for information from a database
C1.example: Send us your query.
C1.ielts_writing: The system queries the database.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have a query about my bill."
C1.mistake: Als Verb "query sth/sb" (befragen, abfragen); Plural "queries".

C1.def: a long search for something
C1.example: They began a quest for treasure.
C1.ielts_writing: Her quest for knowledge never ended.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "quest FOR sth"; in Spielen: "quest" als Aufgabe.

C1.def: a hard yellow fruit used for jam
C1.example: She made quince jelly.
C1.ielts_writing: Quinces are too sour to eat raw.
C1.mistake: Unreif sehr herb; Plural "quinces".

C1.def: being a perfect example of something
C1.example: He is the quintessential gentleman.
C1.ielts_writing: The village is quintessential Italy.
C1.mistake: Nomen "quintessence" (Inbegriff); Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: a fixed share or limit
C1.example: The country set an immigration quota.
C1.ielts_writing: Employers must meet a hiring quota.
C1.mistake: Plural "quotas"; im Verkauf: "sales quota" (Verkaufsziel).

C1.def: a passage from a text, or an estimate of costs
C1.example: She included a quotation from Shakespeare.
C1.ielts_writing: The contractor sent a quotation for the repairs.
C1.mistake: "quotation marks" sind Anführungszeichen; Verb "quote".

C1.def: words repeated from a speaker, or to state a price
C1.example: He misquoted the author.
C1.ielts_writing: The agent quoted a price of fifty dollars.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "quote sb/sth"; umgangssprachlich für "quotation".

C1.def: a frame for holding things
C1.example: Put the coat on the rack.
C1.ielts_writing: The pain racked his body.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I racked my brain for an answer."
C1.mistake: Idiom: "rack one's brain" bedeutet "sich den Kopf zerbrechen"; Plural "racks".

C1.def: a system that detects objects using radio waves
C1.example: The plane disappeared from the radar.
C1.ielts_writing: Radar helps air traffic controllers track flights.
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "under the radar" bedeutet "unbemerkt"; Akronym "radio detection and ranging".

C1.def: extreme, or very different from the usual
C1.example: They proposed a radical change.
C1.ielts_writing: Radical views divide the party.
C1.mistake: Adverb "radically"; als Nomen Person: "a radical".

C1.def: giving off dangerous radiation
C1.example: Radioactive waste must be stored safely.
C1.ielts_writing: The leak released radioactive material.
C1.mistake: Nomen "radioactivity"; Betonung auf der vierten Silbe.

C1.def: the distance from the center of a circle to its edge
C1.example: The radius of the circle is five centimeters.
C1.ielts_writing: Police searched within a ten-mile radius.
C1.mistake: Plural "radii"; "within a radius of" bedeutet "im Umkreis von".

C1.def: violent anger, or to continue with great force
C1.example: He was shaking with rage.
C1.ielts_writing: The fire raged for three days.
C1.mistake: "road rage" ist Aggression im Straßenverkehr; Verb "rage".

C1.def: a sudden attack or police search
C1.example: Police raided the building.
C1.ielts_writing: The raid led to ten arrests.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "raid ON a place"; Nomen "raider".

C1.def: to cause a lot of trouble or fuss
C1.example: The students raised hell at the meeting.
C1.ielts_writing: He raised hell when the order was late.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich und derb; Plural nicht verwendet.

C1.def: a large public meeting, or to come together
C1.example: Thousands attended the rally.
C1.ielts_writing: The team rallied in the second half.
C1.mistake: "rally around sb" bedeutet "sich hinter jemanden stellen"; auch Autorennen "rally".

C1.def: a male sheep, computer memory, or to hit hard
C1.example: The ram butted the gate.
C1.ielts_writing: The truck rammed the fence.
C1.mistake: "RAM" ist Abkürzung für "random access memory"; Verb "ram" (rammen).

C1.def: spreading uncontrolled and widely
C1.example: Corruption is rampant in the industry.
C1.ielts_writing: Rampant inflation worried investors.
C1.mistake: Steht oft nach "run rampant"; meist bei negativen Dingen.

C1.def: the process of making something random
C1.example: Randomization reduces bias in trials.
C1.ielts_writing: The study used randomization to assign groups.
C1.mistake: Verb "randomize"; Betonung auf der vierten Silbe.

C1.def: the extent or variety of something
C1.example: The store offers a wide range of products.
C1.ielts_writing: Prices range from ten to fifty dollars.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "range FROM x TO y"; "in the range of" bedeutet "etwa".

C1.def: a weapon used to attack from a distance
C1.example: Archers carry ranged weapons.
C1.ielts_writing: Ranged weapons give players a safe distance.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "melee weapon"; vor allem in Spielen.

C1.def: a person who looks after a park or forest
C1.example: The ranger led the hikers.
C1.ielts_writing: Park rangers protect wildlife.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Revierförster"; US-Nationalparks haben "park rangers".

C1.def: a position in an ordered list
C1.example: The school improved its ranking.
C1.ielts_writing: The team's ranking dropped.
C1.mistake: Verb "rank"; Plural "rankings".

C1.def: money demanded for a kidnapped person
C1.example: The kidnappers demanded a ransom.
C1.ielts_writing: The company paid the ransom to recover its data.
C1.mistake: "held for ransom" bedeutet "gegen Lösegeld festgehalten"; "ransomware" ist Erpressersoftware.

C1.def: a serious sexual crime of forced sexual intercourse
C1.example: Rape is a serious crime.
C1.ielts_writing: The court convicted him of rape.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She reported the rape to the police."
C1.mistake: Täter "rapist"; juristisch auch "sexual assault".

C1.def: a close and friendly relationship
C1.example: She quickly built rapport with her clients.
C1.ielts_writing: The teacher has a good rapport with students.
C1.mistake: Das "t" ist stumm; Konstruktion: "rapport WITH sb".

C1.def: done without thinking
C1.example: It was a rash decision.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't make rash promises.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She got a rash on her arm."
C1.mistake: Als Nomen auch "Hautausschlag"; Adverb "rashly".

C1.def: a large rodent with a long tail
C1.example: A rat ran across the floor.
C1.ielts_writing: Researchers tested the drug on rats.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "smell a rat" bedeutet "Lunte riechen"; "rat race" ist der Hamsterrad-Alltag.

C1.def: to inform on someone
C1.example: He would rat out his friends.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't rat out your coworkers.
C1.mistake: Umgangssprachlich; trennbar: "rat him out".

C1.def: the relationship between two amounts
C1.example: The ratio of boys to girls is two to one.
C1.ielts_writing: A high debt ratio concerns lenders.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "ratio OF A TO B"; Plural "ratios".

C1.def: based on reason rather than emotion
C1.example: She made a rational choice.
C1.ielts_writing: There is a rational explanation for it.
C1.mistake: Nomen "rationality"; Gegenteil: "irrational".

C1.def: a large black bird of the crow family
C1.example: A raven perched on the fence.
C1.ielts_writing: Ravens are known for their intelligence.
C1.mistake: "raven-haired" bedeutet "rabenschwarzes Haar"; größer als "crow".

C1.def: a deep narrow valley
C1.example: The path crossed a ravine.
C1.ielts_writing: A stream ran through the ravine.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; kleiner als "canyon".

C1.def: a narrow beam of light or energy, or a fish
C1.example: A ray of sunlight came through the window.
C1.ielts_writing: X-rays reveal broken bones.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "ray of hope" bedeutet "Hoffnungsschimmer"; auch Fisch "manta ray".

C1.def: a device in which a nuclear or chemical reaction takes place
C1.example: The reactor was shut down.
C1.ielts_writing: A nuclear reactor produces energy.
C1.mistake: Verb "react"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: the people who read a publication
C1.example: The magazine has a large readership.
C1.ielts_writing: Its readership is mostly young people.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Konstruktion: "readership OF a paper".

C1.def: without difficulty or delay
C1.example: She readily agreed to help.
C1.ielts_writing: Tickets are readily available online.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "ready"; steht oft vor Partizip: "readily available".

C1.def: a style showing life as it really is
C1.example: The novel is a classic of realism.
C1.ielts_writing: Political realism accepts power struggles.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Her art is known for its realism."
C1.mistake: Person "realist"; Gegenteil: "idealism".

C1.def: the act of understanding something, or making it real
C1.example: The realization hit her suddenly.
C1.ielts_writing: He came to the realization that he was wrong.
C1.mistake: Verb "realize"; Konstruktion: "realization THAT ..."

C1.def: a field or area of activity or interest
C1.example: This falls in the realm of possibility.
C1.ielts_writing: The realm of politics is complicated.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Peace is beyond the realm of reality."
C1.mistake: Idiom: "beyond the realm of possibility" bedeutet "unmöglich"; auch "Königreich".

C1.def: located at the back
C1.example: He sat in the rear seat.
C1.ielts_writing: The rear of the building faces the river.
C1.mistake: Verb "rear" (aufziehen) hat gleiche Form; "bring up the rear" bedeutet "den Schluss bilden".

C1.def: the process of thinking logically
C1.example: Her reasoning was sound.
C1.ielts_writing: I don't follow his reasoning.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The reasoning behind the policy is clear."
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Verb "reason" (schlussfolgern).

C1.def: to remove someone's doubts or fears
C1.example: The doctor reassured the patient.
C1.ielts_writing: The mayor tried to reassure residents.
C1.mistake: Nomen "reassurance"; Konstruktion: "reassure sb THAT ..."

C1.def: a person who resists authority
C1.example: The rebels seized the town.
C1.ielts_writing: Teenagers often rebel against their parents.
C1.mistake: Betonung beim Nomen vorn ("REBel"), beim Verb hinten ("reBEL").

C1.def: an organized act of resistance against authority
C1.example: The rebellion was crushed.
C1.ielts_writing: Teenage rebellion is a normal phase.
C1.mistake: Verb "rebel"; Konstruktion: "rebellion AGAINST sb".

C1.def: refusing to obey rules
C1.example: He was a rebellious child.
C1.ielts_writing: Her rebellious streak worried her parents.
C1.mistake: Nomen "rebelliousness"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to prove that a claim is false
C1.example: She tried to rebut the accusation.
C1.ielts_writing: The lawyer rebutted every claim.
C1.mistake: Nomen "rebuttal"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to get something that is given or sent
C1.example: I received your email yesterday.
C1.ielts_writing: She received an award for her research.
C1.mistake: Regel: "i before e except after c"; Nomen "receipt" mit stummem "p".

C1.def: willing to listen to new ideas
C1.example: The audience was receptive to the idea.
C1.ielts_writing: She is receptive to feedback.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "receptive TO sth"; nicht "rezeptiv" im Sinn von nur empfangend.

C1.def: a person who receives something
C1.example: She was the recipient of an award.
C1.ielts_writing: Each recipient gets a certificate.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "recipient OF sth"; Gegenteil: "sender".

C1.def: careless about danger or consequences
C1.example: He was fined for reckless driving.
C1.ielts_writing: Her reckless spending led to debt.
C1.mistake: Nomen "recklessness"; Adverb "recklessly".

C1.def: to make two ideas or people agree
C1.example: They finally reconciled after years.
C1.ielts_writing: It is hard to reconcile work and family.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "reconcile sth WITH sth"; "reconcile oneself to sth" bedeutet "sich abfinden".

C1.def: to think again about a decision
C1.example: Please reconsider your offer.
C1.ielts_writing: She reconsidered her plans.
C1.mistake: Nomen "reconsideration"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: the act of building or creating again
C1.example: The reconstruction took ten years.
C1.ielts_writing: Police used a reconstruction of the crime.
C1.mistake: Verb "reconstruct"; auch Tatrekonstruktion.

C1.def: written evidence, or the best achievement
C1.example: She broke the world record.
C1.ielts_writing: Keep a record of your expenses.
C1.mistake: Betonung beim Nomen vorn ("REcord"), beim Verb hinten ("reCORD").

C1.def: to tell a story or events
C1.example: He recounted his adventures.
C1.ielts_writing: The report recounts the events of the night.
C1.mistake: Nicht "recount" im Sinn von nachzählen (Stimmen): dort Betonung vorn.

C1.def: the process of becoming well or strong again
C1.example: She made a full recovery.
C1.ielts_writing: Economic recovery is slow.
C1.mistake: Verb "recover"; Konstruktion: "recovery FROM an illness".

C1.def: to find new people to join an organization
C1.example: The firm plans to recruit new graduates.
C1.ielts_writing: The army recruited thousands of volunteers.
C1.mistake: Nomen "recruitment"; auch Nomen "recruit" (Rekrut(in)).

C1.def: a cell in the blood that carries oxygen
C1.example: Red blood cells carry oxygen.
C1.ielts_writing: A low red blood cell count causes fatigue.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Doctors checked her red blood cell levels."
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "white blood cell"; fachsprachlich "erythrocyte".

C1.def: no longer needed, especially at work
C1.example: Many workers were made redundant.
C1.ielts_writing: The old software has become redundant.
C1.mistake: In den USA eher "laid off"; "redundant" bedeutet "überflüssig".

C1.def: a tall plant that grows near water
C1.example: Reeds grew along the lake.
C1.ielts_writing: The clarinet reed vibrated.
C1.mistake: Aussprache wie "read" (Präsens); auch Rohrblatt bei Blasinstrumenten.

C1.def: a cylinder for winding thread, film or line
C1.example: He cast the line and turned the reel.
C1.ielts_writing: She reeled in a large fish.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A film reel sat on the table."
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb: "reel in" bedeutet "einholen"; auch Instagram "Reel".

C1.def: a mention of something, or a recommendation
C1.example: Please include a reference list.
C1.ielts_writing: He gave me a reference for the job.
C1.mistake: Verb "refer"; "with reference to" bedeutet "bezugnehmend auf".

C1.def: a public vote on a single question
C1.example: The country held a referendum on the treaty.
C1.ielts_writing: Voters rejected the referendum.
C1.mistake: Plural "referendums" oder "referenda"; Konstruktion: "referendum ON sth".

C1.def: to improve by making small changes
C1.example: The team refined its approach.
C1.ielts_writing: Crude oil is refined into gasoline.
C1.mistake: Nomen "refinement"; Partizip "refined" auch "kultiviert".

C1.def: careful thought, or an image in a mirror
C1.example: On reflection, I agree with you.
C1.ielts_writing: Her face was visible in the reflection.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The results are a reflection of hard work."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "reflection ON/OF sth"; "on reflection" bedeutet "nach reiflicher Überlegung".

C1.def: a change that improves a system
C1.example: The government announced a major reform.
C1.ielts_writing: The law was reformed last year.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Reform" im Sinn von Umbau eines Hauses; Nomen "reformer".

C1.def: a place or state of safety
C1.example: They took refuge in a cave.
C1.ielts_writing: Many families sought refuge from the war.
C1.mistake: Person: "refugee"; Konstruktion: "refuge FROM sth".

C1.def: to clean and improve something so it looks new
C1.example: They refurbished the old hotel.
C1.ielts_writing: The company refurbishes used laptops.
C1.mistake: Nomen "refurbishment"; "refurbished" bedeutet "generalüberholt".

C1.def: the act of saying no to something
C1.example: His refusal to apologize angered her.
C1.ielts_writing: A refusal to cooperate delayed the project.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "refusal TO do sth"; Verb "refuse".

C1.def: to prove that a claim is wrong
C1.example: Scientists refuted the theory.
C1.ielts_writing: The data refute his argument.
C1.mistake: Nomen "refutation"; stärker als "deny".

C1.def: to get something back after losing it
C1.example: She regained her strength.
C1.ielts_writing: The team regained the lead.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßigkeit fehlt: regain, regained, regained; "regain consciousness" bedeutet "wieder zu Bewusstsein kommen".

C1.def: despite everything
C1.example: He went regardless of the danger.
C1.ielts_writing: She kept going regardless.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "regardless OF sth"; nicht "irregardless".

C1.def: a government, often authoritarian
C1.example: The regime was overthrown.
C1.ielts_writing: A strict diet regime helped him lose weight.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; auch "Kur, Regelwerk".

C1.def: an official list, or a style of language
C1.example: Please register for the course.
C1.ielts_writing: Formal register is used in essays.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Liste und Sprachebene; "cash register" ist die Kasse.

C1.def: a frequent customer, or happening at fixed times
C1.example: He is a regular at the café.
C1.ielts_writing: Regular exercise improves health.
C1.mistake: Nomen im Plural: "the regulars"; "on a regular basis" bedeutet "regelmäßig".

C1.def: an agency that enforces rules in an industry
C1.example: The regulator fined the bank.
C1.ielts_writing: Financial regulators demand stricter reporting.
C1.mistake: Verb "regulate"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: relating to rules set by an authority
C1.example: The firm faces regulatory scrutiny.
C1.ielts_writing: New regulatory requirements apply to banks.
C1.mistake: Verb "regulate"; Nomen "regulation".

C1.def: treatment or training to return to normal life
C1.example: He is in rehabilitation after surgery.
C1.ielts_writing: Prison rehabilitation reduces crime.
C1.mistake: Verb "rehabilitate"; umgangssprachlich "rehab".

C1.def: to present old ideas again without much change
C1.example: The film just rehashes old ideas.
C1.ielts_writing: He rehashed the same argument.
C1.mistake: Meist abwertend; auch Nomen "rehash".

C1.def: to heat food again
C1.example: Reheat the soup before serving.
C1.ielts_writing: She reheated the leftovers in the microwave.
C1.mistake: Regelmäßig: reheated; nicht "heat up again".

C1.def: the period when a monarch rules
C1.example: Queen Victoria's reign lasted sixty-three years.
C1.ielts_writing: Terror reigned in the city.
C1.mistake: Nicht "rain" (Regen) oder "rein"; "reign supreme" bedeutet "unangefochten herrschen".

C1.def: to say again to make a point clear
C1.example: I want to reiterate my main point.
C1.ielts_writing: The minister reiterated his support.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Let me reiterate that this is urgent."
C1.mistake: Nomen "reiteration"; Konstruktion: "reiterate THAT ..."

C1.def: the act of refusing to accept someone or something
C1.example: She feared rejection.
C1.ielts_writing: His rejection of the offer surprised everyone.
C1.mistake: Verb "reject"; Betonung beim Verb hinten ("reJECT").

C1.def: easy to understand or identify with
C1.example: The character is very relatable.
C1.ielts_writing: Relatable stories connect with readers.
C1.mistake: Eher umgangssprachlich; Verb "relate TO sth".

C1.def: the quality of being closely connected to the matter
C1.example: The relevance of this study is clear.
C1.ielts_writing: I don't see the relevance of that question.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "relevant"; Konstruktion: "relevance TO sth".

C1.def: the quality of being trustworthy
C1.example: The reliability of the data is questionable.
C1.ielts_writing: Car buyers value reliability.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "reliable"; Verb "rely ON sb".

C1.def: to give up something, such as power
C1.example: He relinquished control of the company.
C1.ielts_writing: She refused to relinquish her claim.
C1.mistake: Sehr formell; Konstruktion: "relinquish sth TO sb".

C1.def: unwilling and hesitant
C1.example: She was reluctant to speak.
C1.ielts_writing: The reluctant witness finally agreed.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "reluctant TO do sth"; nicht "reluctant FOR".

C1.def: the part that is left
C1.example: The remainder of the money was donated.
C1.ielts_writing: Pay the remainder by Friday.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The remainder of the day was quiet."
C1.mistake: Verb "remain"; "remainder" ist in der Mathematik der Rest bei Division.

C1.def: what is left after something has been destroyed
C1.example: Archaeologists found human remains.
C1.ielts_writing: The remains of the castle stand on the hill.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw the remains of an ancient wall."
C1.mistake: Immer Plural; Verb "remain" (bleiben).

C1.def: a treatment or solution for a problem
C1.example: A hot drink is a good remedy for colds.
C1.ielts_writing: The court ordered a legal remedy.
C1.mistake: Verb "remedy" (beheben); Adjektiv "remedial".

C1.def: something that helps you remember
C1.example: She set a reminder on her phone.
C1.ielts_writing: The letter was a gentle reminder to pay.
C1.mistake: Verb "remind sb OF/ABOUT sth"; Konstruktion: "a reminder OF sth".

C1.def: bringing back memories of something
C1.example: The song is reminiscent of the sixties.
C1.ielts_writing: Her style is reminiscent of Picasso.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "reminiscent OF sth"; Verb "reminisce".

C1.def: the act of taking something away
C1.example: The removal of the tumor was successful.
C1.ielts_writing: Snow removal began at dawn.
C1.mistake: Verb "remove"; "removal" nicht "Umzug" (das ist "move").

C1.def: to cause to be in a state, or to produce a result
C1.example: The accident rendered him speechless.
C1.ielts_writing: The software renders images quickly.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "render sb + Adjektiv"; Nomen "rendering".

C1.def: to extend, or to make fresh again
C1.example: I need to renew my passport.
C1.ielts_writing: The contract was renewed for two years.
C1.mistake: Nomen "renewal"; auch "erneut aufnehmen".

C1.def: able to be replaced naturally
C1.example: Wind is a renewable energy source.
C1.ielts_writing: Renewable power has become cheaper.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "nonrenewable"; Nomen im Plural: "renewables".

C1.def: to repair and improve a building
C1.example: They plan to renovate the kitchen.
C1.ielts_writing: The city renovated the old theater.
C1.mistake: Nomen "renovation"; im Alltag oft "remodel".

C1.def: famous for a special skill or achievement
C1.example: She is a renowned scientist.
C1.ielts_writing: The restaurant is renowned for its seafood.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "renowned FOR sth"; Nomen "renown".

C1.def: an arrangement to pay for use of something
C1.example: They offer car rentals at the airport.
C1.ielts_writing: The rental was too expensive.
C1.mistake: Verb "rent"; Plural "rentals"; Verb "rent".

C1.def: a person or thing that takes the place of another
C1.example: We need a replacement for the broken lamp.
C1.ielts_writing: The company is seeking a replacement for the manager.
C1.mistake: Verb "replace"; Konstruktion: "replacement FOR sth".

C1.def: to fill something up again
C1.example: They replenish the supplies each week.
C1.ielts_writing: Athletes replenish fluids after a race.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The shop needs to replenish its stock."
C1.mistake: Nomen "replenishment"; gehobener als "refill".

C1.def: according to what people say, but not confirmed
C1.example: The singer is reportedly retiring.
C1.ielts_writing: The company reportedly lost millions.
C1.mistake: Verb "report"; unbestätigte Information.

C1.def: the way someone or something is shown, or acting for others
C1.example: The film's representation of women is complex.
C1.ielts_writing: Citizens demand fair representation in parliament.
C1.mistake: Verb "represent"; Konstruktion: "representation OF sb/sth".

C1.def: to make a copy or produce again
C1.example: Scientists could not reproduce the result.
C1.ielts_writing: Animals reproduce by laying eggs.
C1.mistake: Nomen "reproduction"; auch "sich fortpflanzen".

C1.def: the process of producing offspring, or a copy
C1.example: Sexual reproduction increases genetic variety.
C1.ielts_writing: The gallery sells reproductions of famous paintings.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe; Verb "reproduce".

C1.def: a state led by elected representatives
C1.example: The country became a republic in 1918.
C1.ielts_writing: A republic has an elected president.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "republican"; Großschreibung bei Parteinamen in den USA.

C1.def: the act of saving someone from danger
C1.example: Rescue teams searched the mountain.
C1.ielts_writing: Firefighters rescued the child.
C1.mistake: Person "rescuer"; "come to sb's rescue" bedeutet "zu Hilfe kommen".

C1.def: careful study to discover facts
C1.example: She conducts research on climate change.
C1.ielts_writing: Further research is needed.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar: nicht "researches" im Sinn von Studien; Betonung vorn ("REsearch").

C1.def: to look or be similar to
C1.example: She resembles her mother.
C1.ielts_writing: The two designs closely resemble each other.
C1.mistake: Kein "like" nach resemble; Nomen "resemblance".

C1.def: feeling bitter about unfair treatment
C1.example: He felt resentful toward his boss.
C1.ielts_writing: She grew resentful over the unfair treatment.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "resentful OF/TOWARD sb"; Nomen "resentment".

C1.def: quiet and slow to show feelings
C1.example: He is a reserved person.
C1.ielts_writing: A reserved seat was waiting for her.
C1.mistake: Auch "reserviert" (Platz); Verb "reserve".

C1.def: a large natural or man-made lake for storing water
C1.example: The reservoir supplies the city with water.
C1.ielts_writing: A drought lowered the reservoir.
C1.mistake: Auch bildlich: "a reservoir of talent".

C1.def: to live in a particular place
C1.example: Many citizens reside in the suburbs.
C1.ielts_writing: The power to decide resides with the board.
C1.mistake: Nomen "resident"; Konstruktion: "reside IN a place".

C1.def: the place where someone lives
C1.example: The president's official residence is in the capital.
C1.ielts_writing: You need proof of residence.
C1.mistake: "take up residence" bedeutet "sich niederlassen"; Verb "reside".

C1.def: a building where college students live
C1.example: She lives in a residence hall on campus.
C1.ielts_writing: Residence halls offer single and shared rooms.
C1.mistake: Alltagssprachlich "dorm"; Plural "residence halls".

C1.def: relating to areas where people live
C1.example: They moved to a quiet residential area.
C1.ielts_writing: Residential buildings line the street.
C1.mistake: Nomen "resident"; Gegenteil: "commercial".

C1.def: a small amount that remains after a process
C1.example: The cleaner left a sticky residue.
C1.ielts_writing: Chemical residue was found on the soil.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "residual"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to leave a job or position officially
C1.example: She resigned from her post.
C1.ielts_writing: The minister resigned after the scandal.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "resign FROM a post"; Nomen "resignation".

C1.def: the act of leaving a position, or acceptance of a bad situation
C1.example: He handed in his resignation.
C1.ielts_writing: She accepted the news with resignation.
C1.mistake: Zwei Bedeutungen: Rücktritt und Ergebenheit; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: the ability to recover quickly from difficulties
C1.example: The community showed great resilience.
C1.ielts_writing: Resilience helps people cope with stress.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "resilient"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: able to recover quickly
C1.example: Children are often resilient.
C1.ielts_writing: The economy proved resilient.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Be resilient in the face of failure."
C1.mistake: Nomen "resilience"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: the refusal to accept something, or the force that opposes
C1.example: The plan met strong resistance.
C1.ielts_writing: Electrical resistance causes heat.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "resistance TO sth"; Verb "resist".

C1.def: firm determination, or to settle a problem
C1.example: His resolve never wavered.
C1.ielts_writing: They worked to resolve the dispute.
C1.mistake: Verb "resolve" (lösen) und Nomen "resolve" (Entschlossenheit).

C1.def: to use something unwanted because there is no alternative
C1.example: They resorted to violence.
C1.ielts_writing: He resorted to selling his car.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "resort TO sth"; Nomen "resort" (Urlaubsort, letzter Ausweg).

C1.def: belonging separately to each person mentioned
C1.example: They returned to their respective homes.
C1.ielts_writing: The two scientists defended their respective theories.
C1.mistake: Steht vor Nomen; nicht "respektvoll" (respectful).

C1.def: in the order mentioned
C1.example: The ages are 4 and 7, respectively.
C1.ielts_writing: Sales rose by 5% and 8%, respectively.
C1.mistake: Nicht "respektvoll" (respectfully); steht am Ende einer Aufzählung.

C1.def: the work of repairing something to its original state
C1.example: The restoration took three years.
C1.ielts_writing: Restoration of the old church began last month.
C1.mistake: Verb "restore"; auch "Restoration" als Epoche (England, 1660).

C1.def: control over feelings or actions
C1.example: He showed great restraint.
C1.ielts_writing: Financial restraint is necessary.
C1.mistake: Verb "restrain"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: limited in amount, size or access
C1.example: Access is restricted to staff.
C1.ielts_writing: This is a restricted area.
C1.mistake: Verb "restrict"; Gegenteil: "unrestricted".

C1.def: to continue after a pause
C1.example: The meeting will resume after lunch.
C1.ielts_writing: Talks resumed on Monday.
C1.mistake: Nomen "resumption"; Nomen "résumé" ist der Lebenslauf.

C1.def: to appear again after being hidden
C1.example: Old rumors resurfaced.
C1.ielts_writing: The issue resurfaced during the debate.
C1.mistake: Auch "neu asphaltieren": "resurface a road".

C1.def: the selling of goods directly to consumers
C1.example: Retail sales rose last quarter.
C1.ielts_writing: The book retails for twenty dollars.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "wholesale"; Nomen "retailer".

C1.def: a business that sells goods to the public
C1.example: The retailer offers free shipping.
C1.ielts_writing: Large retailers dominate the market.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "wholesaler"; Verb "retail".

C1.def: unwilling to share thoughts or feelings
C1.example: He was reticent about his past.
C1.ielts_writing: She remained reticent in meetings.
C1.mistake: Nicht "reluctant" (widerwillig); Nomen "reticence".

C1.def: a withdrawal, or a quiet place to rest
C1.example: The army ordered a retreat.
C1.ielts_writing: They retreated to the mountains.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "beat a hasty retreat" bedeutet "eilig den Rückzug antreten".

C1.def: to get something back or find stored information
C1.example: He retrieved his bag from the car.
C1.ielts_writing: The system can retrieve old files.
C1.mistake: Nomen "retrieval"; "i before e".

C1.def: to use something again
C1.example: Please reuse your bags.
C1.ielts_writing: We reuse glass jars for storage.
C1.mistake: Aussprache Nomen /riːˈjuːs/, Verb /riːˈjuːz/; Adjektiv "reusable".

C1.def: a surprising piece of information that is made known
C1.example: The article contained a shocking revelation.
C1.ielts_writing: The revelation changed everything.
C1.mistake: Verb "reveal"; "Revelation" auch Offenbarung (Bibel).

C1.def: punishment given in return for harm
C1.example: He swore revenge on his enemies.
C1.ielts_writing: She did it out of revenge.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "revenge ON sb/FOR sth".

C1.def: to admire deeply
C1.example: They revere their ancestors.
C1.ielts_writing: The poet is revered in his country.
C1.mistake: Nomen "reverence"; Passiv "be revered as/by".

C1.def: to change something to the opposite
C1.example: The court reversed the decision.
C1.ielts_writing: He reversed the car into the garage.
C1.mistake: Nomen "reversal"; "in reverse" bedeutet "rückwärts".

C1.def: the process of becoming active or popular again
C1.example: The town saw an economic revival.
C1.ielts_writing: A revival of the musical opened last week.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Interest in the craft saw a revival."
C1.mistake: Verb "revive"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to bring back to life or strength
C1.example: Paramedics revived the patient.
C1.ielts_writing: The government hopes to revive the economy.
C1.mistake: Nomen "revival"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: causing a complete change
C1.example: The invention was revolutionary.
C1.ielts_writing: Revolutionary ideas shaped the country.
C1.mistake: Nomen "revolution"; Betonung auf der vierten Silbe.

C1.def: the art of persuasive speaking or writing
C1.example: His rhetoric inspired the crowd.
C1.ielts_writing: Empty rhetoric does not solve problems.
C1.mistake: Oft abwertend: "empty rhetoric" bedeutet "leere Phrasen".

C1.def: a large animal with one or two horns on its nose
C1.example: A rhinoceros charged at the jeep.
C1.ielts_writing: The rhinoceros is endangered.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw a rhinoceros at the zoo."
C1.mistake: Kurzform "rhino"; Plural "rhinoceroses" oder "rhinoceros".

C1.def: a light two-wheeled vehicle pulled by a person
C1.example: We took a rickshaw through the old town.
C1.ielts_writing: The rickshaw driver knew every street.
C1.mistake: Plural "rickshaws"; in Asien verbreitet.

C1.def: a long gun fired from the shoulder
C1.example: The soldier carried a rifle.
C1.ielts_writing: Hunters need a license for a rifle.
C1.mistake: Verb "rifle through" bedeutet "durchwühlen".

C1.def: an angle of ninety degrees
C1.example: The two lines form a right angle.
C1.ielts_writing: A square has four right angles.
C1.mistake: "at right angles to" bedeutet "im rechten Winkel zu".

C1.def: extremely thorough and careful
C1.example: The study used rigorous methods.
C1.ielts_writing: Rigorous testing protects patients.
C1.mistake: Nomen "rigor"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a folder with metal rings that hold papers
C1.example: She keeps notes in a ring binder.
C1.ielts_writing: A ring binder holds the handouts.
C1.mistake: In den USA oft "three-ring binder"; Plural "ring binders".

C1.def: a violent public disturbance
C1.example: A riot broke out downtown.
C1.ielts_writing: Police used tear gas to stop the riot.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "run riot" bedeutet "außer Kontrolle geraten"; Person "rioter".

C1.def: to tear something quickly
C1.example: He ripped the letter open.
C1.ielts_writing: The nail ripped her sleeve.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb: "rip off" bedeutet "übers Ohr hauen"; Partizip "ripped".

C1.def: a set of actions done in a fixed way
C1.example: They performed an ancient ritual.
C1.ielts_writing: Coffee is her morning ritual.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "ritualistic"; auch Alltagsgewohnheit.

C1.def: strong and healthy, or able to withstand stress
C1.example: The company posted robust growth.
C1.ielts_writing: The software is robust and reliable.
C1.mistake: Nomen "robustness"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: to move gently back and forth, or to shock
C1.example: The boat rocked in the waves.
C1.ielts_writing: The scandal rocked the nation.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "rock the boat" bedeutet "für Unruhe sorgen"; Nomen "rock" (Fels, Musik).

C1.def: a vehicle propelled into space, or to rise quickly
C1.example: The rocket launched at dawn.
C1.ielts_writing: Prices rocketed last year.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "It's not rocket science" bedeutet "Das ist nicht schwer".

C1.def: a small mammal with strong front teeth
C1.example: A rodent chewed the cable.
C1.ielts_writing: Rodents carry diseases.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They set a trap for the rodent."
C1.mistake: Beispiele: rats, mice, squirrels; Plural "rodents".

C1.def: the sport of skating with in-line wheels
C1.example: Rollerblading is popular along the river.
C1.ielts_writing: She goes rollerblading on weekends.
C1.mistake: Markenname "Rollerblade"; Verb "go rollerblading".

C1.def: a love affair, or a story about love
C1.example: Their romance began in college.
C1.ielts_writing: She reads romance novels.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe; Adjektiv "romantic".

C1.def: an artistic movement stressing emotion and nature
C1.example: Romanticism flourished in the nineteenth century.
C1.ielts_writing: Many poets embraced Romanticism.
C1.mistake: Meist großgeschrieben als Epoche; Gegenteil: "classicism".

C1.def: the upper inside surface of the mouth
C1.example: The food stuck to the roof of the mouth.
C1.ielts_writing: The dentist checked the roof of the mouth.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Press your tongue to the roof of your mouth."
collocations: touch the roof of the mouth
burn the roof of the mouth
stick to the roof of the mouth
C1.mistake: Fachsprachlich "palate".

C1.def: the process of decay, or to decay
C1.example: The wood was full of rot.
C1.ielts_writing: Food will rot in the heat.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "rotten"; Verb "rot" mit Partizip "rotted".

C1.def: to turn around a center, or to take turns
C1.example: The Earth rotates once a day.
C1.ielts_writing: Staff rotate shifts every week.
C1.mistake: Nomen "rotation"; Betonung beim Verb vorn ("ROtate").

C1.def: a movement in a circle, or a taking of turns
C1.example: Earth's rotation causes day and night.
C1.ielts_writing: Crop rotation keeps soil healthy.
C1.mistake: Verb "rotate"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a person or body that approves without real review
C1.example: The committee was just a rubber stamp.
C1.ielts_writing: Critics call the council a rubber stamp for the mayor.
C1.mistake: Verb "rubber-stamp"; abwertend.

C1.def: deep red in color
C1.example: She wore ruby lipstick.
C1.ielts_writing: The ruby sunset lit the sky.
C1.mistake: Nomen "ruby" (Rubin); hier als Farbadjektiv.

C1.def: to govern, or to decide officially
C1.example: The king ruled for forty years.
C1.ielts_writing: The judge ruled in her favor.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb: "rule out" bedeutet "ausschließen"; Nomen "ruling".

C1.def: an official decision by a court
C1.example: The ruling surprised many lawyers.
C1.ielts_writing: A court ruling blocked the plan.
C1.mistake: Verb "rule"; Konstruktion: "ruling ON sth".

C1.def: an unverified story that spreads among people
C1.example: A rumor spread through the office.
C1.ielts_writing: Rumors about layoffs worried staff.
C1.mistake: "Rumor has it that ..." bedeutet "es heißt, dass ..."; Adjektiv "rumored".

C1.def: a motor vehicle that people can live in on trips
C1.example: They bought an RV for the trip.
C1.ielts_writing: Many retirees travel in an RV.
C1.mistake: Abkürzung für "recreational vehicle"; typisch US.

C1.def: to deliberately damage or ruin something
C1.example: Workers tried to sabotage the machines.
C1.ielts_writing: Rivals sabotaged the negotiations.
C1.mistake: Person "saboteur"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: to dismiss someone from a job
C1.example: The company sacked ten workers.
C1.ielts_writing: He was sacked for lateness.
C1.mistake: Bei uns auch "get the sack"; Nomen "sack" (Sack).

C1.def: connected with religion and deserving respect
C1.example: The temple is a sacred place.
C1.ielts_writing: Cows are sacred in India.
C1.mistake: Nomen "sacredness"; Gegenteil: "profane".

C1.def: giving up something valuable for something else
C1.example: Parents make many sacrifices.
C1.ielts_writing: He sacrificed his career for his family.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "sacrifice sth FOR sth"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: a strong locked box for valuables
C1.example: She locked the jewels in a safe.
C1.ielts_writing: A safe stood in the office.
C1.mistake: Auch Adjektiv "safe" (sicher); Nomen mit Plural "safes".

C1.def: unharmed and in good condition
C1.example: They arrived safe and sound.
C1.ielts_writing: The children returned safe and sound.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung; nicht verändern.

C1.def: a measure that protects against harm
C1.example: The law is a safeguard against abuse.
C1.ielts_writing: Safeguards protect personal data.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "safeguard AGAINST sth"; Verb "safeguard".

C1.def: a person recognized for holiness
C1.example: The church honors a saint.
C1.ielts_writing: Saint Nicholas is celebrated in December.
C1.mistake: Als Titel "St."; idiomatisch: "a saint" bedeutet "sehr gutmütig".

C1.def: benefit or purpose
C1.example: For goodness' sake, be careful!
C1.ielts_writing: He did it for his children's sake.
C1.ielts_speaking: "For the sake of peace, we agreed."
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung "for the sake of"; nicht "für den Zweck von" falsch übersetzen.

C1.def: a person who sells goods in a shop
C1.example: The salesclerk wrapped the gift.
C1.ielts_writing: A salesclerk helped me find a size.
C1.mistake: Plural "salesclerks"; im Alltag auch "sales associate".

C1.def: most noticeable or important
C1.example: She summarized the salient points.
C1.ielts_writing: The salient feature is its speed.
C1.ielts_speaking: "The most salient fact is the cost."
C1.mistake: Nomen "salience"; meist vor "point" oder "feature".

C1.def: the liquid produced in the mouth
C1.example: Saliva helps digestion.
C1.ielts_writing: Doctors collected a saliva sample.
C1.mistake: Verb "salivate"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a lively Brazilian dance and music
C1.example: They danced the samba.
C1.ielts_writing: Samba music filled the street.
C1.mistake: Aus Brasilien; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: official permission, or a penalty
C1.example: The plan needs official sanction.
C1.ielts_writing: The country imposed a sanction on imports.
C1.mistake: Doppelte Bedeutung: Erlaubnis und Strafe; Verb "sanction".

C1.def: penalties imposed on a country
C1.example: The UN imposed sanctions on the regime.
C1.ielts_writing: Sanctions hurt ordinary citizens.
C1.mistake: Meist Plural; Konstruktion: "sanctions ON/AGAINST a country".

C1.def: a safe place, or a protected area for animals
C1.example: The island is a bird sanctuary.
C1.ielts_writing: Churches offered sanctuary to refugees.
C1.mistake: Auch "Heiligtum"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: bold and a little rude in a lively way
C1.example: She gave a sassy reply.
C1.ielts_writing: The sassy character won the audience.
C1.mistake: Nomen "sass"; umgangssprachlich.

C1.def: a standardized test for U.S. college admission
C1.example: He studied for the SAT.
C1.ielts_writing: A high SAT score helps admission.
C1.mistake: Typisch für US-Colleges; Abkürzung, nicht "sat" (Past von "sit").

C1.def: a room heated for sweating
C1.example: We relaxed in the sauna.
C1.ielts_writing: A sauna is common in Finland.
C1.mistake: Auch "go to a sauna"; Plural "saunas".

C1.def: salty or spicy rather than sweet
C1.example: I prefer savory snacks.
C1.ielts_writing: The soup has a savory flavor.
C1.mistake: Nicht "schmackhaft" allgemein; Gegenteil: "sweet".

C1.def: the right to take part in a decision
C1.example: Everyone should have a say.
C1.ielts_writing: Citizens want a say in the plan.
C1.ielts_speaking: "I have no say in the matter."
C1.mistake: "have a say IN sth" bedeutet "Mitspracherecht haben".

C1.def: permission or authority from a person
C1.example: He did it on her say-so.
C1.ielts_writing: Nothing happens without his say-so.
C1.mistake: Feste Wendung: "on sb's say-so".

C1.def: the size or extent of something, or a series of levels
C1.example: The scale of the damage was huge.
C1.ielts_writing: The map has a scale of 1:100,000.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Use a scale from one to ten."
C1.mistake: Auch Waage und Fischschuppe; Idiom: "scale up/down".

C1.def: a dishonest scheme to get money
C1.example: It was a phone scam.
C1.ielts_writing: Scammers scammed elderly people.
C1.mistake: Person "scammer"; auf Deutsch "Betrugsmasche".

C1.def: a person who cheats people out of money
C1.example: The scammer posed as a bank.
C1.ielts_writing: Scammers target elderly victims.
C1.mistake: Nomen "scam"; Verb "scam".

C1.def: a mark left on skin after a wound
C1.example: The scar on his hand is old.
C1.ielts_writing: The war scarred the country.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She has a scar on her face."
C1.mistake: Bildlich: "emotional scar"; Partizip "scarred".

C1.def: bright red
C1.example: She wore a scarlet dress.
C1.ielts_writing: The scarlet flowers stood out.
C1.mistake: "scarlet fever" bedeutet "Scharlach"; leuchtendes Rot.

C1.def: spread over a wide area
C1.example: Scattered showers are expected.
C1.ielts_writing: Scattered villages dot the valley.
C1.mistake: Verb "scatter"; Wetterbericht: "scattered showers".

C1.def: doubting that something is true
C1.example: I am skeptical about the claims.
C1.ielts_writing: Skeptical voters demanded proof.
C1.mistake: Nomen "skeptic"; Konstruktion: "skeptical ABOUT/OF sth".

C1.def: a plan of times when things will happen
C1.example: My schedule is full today.
C1.ielts_writing: The train runs on schedule.
C1.mistake: "on schedule" bedeutet "planmäßig"; Betonung beginnt mit /sk/.

C1.def: a thin fried cut of meat
C1.example: We ordered a schnitzel.
C1.ielts_writing: Schnitzel is served with potatoes.
C1.mistake: Aus dem Deutschen entlehnt; Aussprache mit /ʃn/.

C1.def: a person who studies a subject in depth
C1.example: She is a respected scholar.
C1.ielts_writing: Scholars debate the text's origin.
C1.mistake: Nomen "scholarship" (Stipendium oder Gelehrsamkeit).

C1.def: relating to serious academic study
C1.example: He wrote a scholarly article.
C1.ielts_writing: The scholarly journal publishes research.
C1.mistake: Nomen "scholar"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: the range of a subject or activity
C1.example: The scope of the study is broad.
C1.ielts_writing: There is scope for improvement.
C1.ielts_speaking: "That is outside the scope of this report."
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "scope FOR improvement"; "beyond the scope" bedeutet "den Rahmen sprengen".

C1.def: extremely hot
C1.example: It was a scorching afternoon.
C1.ielts_writing: Scorching heat hit the city.
C1.mistake: Verb "scorch" (versengen); Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: extremely hot weather or temperature
C1.example: The pavement was scorching hot.
C1.ielts_writing: It is scorching hot outside.
C1.mistake: Adjektivisch benutzt; Gegenteil: "freezing cold".

C1.def: the number of points in a game or test
C1.example: The final score was three to one.
C1.ielts_writing: She scored highly on the test.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "on that score" bedeutet "in dieser Hinsicht"; auch 20 Stück.

C1.def: a clear sticky tape
C1.example: She used scotch tape to fix the paper.
C1.ielts_writing: Scotch tape holds the poster.
C1.mistake: Markenname im US-Alltag; allgemein "tape".

C1.def: to cancel or throw away something
C1.example: They scrapped the plan.
C1.ielts_writing: Scrap metal is recycled.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "scrap a plan" bedeutet "einen Plan verwerfen".

C1.def: the written text of a film
C1.example: He wrote the screenplay.
C1.ielts_writing: The screenplay won an award.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She's adapting the novel into a screenplay."
C1.mistake: Person "screenwriter"; synonym "script".

C1.def: to fasten with a screw, or to spoil something
C1.example: He screwed the shelf to the wall.
C1.ielts_writing: I screwed up the exam.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb: "screw up" bedeutet "etwas vermasseln"; teils vulgär.

C1.def: to write the text of a performance
C1.example: The writer scripted the film.
C1.ielts_writing: The speech was scripted in advance.
C1.mistake: Partizip "scripted" (einstudiert); Nomen "script".

C1.def: untidy and dirty
C1.example: He looked scruffy.
C1.ielts_writing: A scruffy dog barked at us.
C1.mistake: Adverb "scruffily"; Gegenteil: "neat".

C1.def: close and critical examination
C1.example: The plan came under scrutiny.
C1.ielts_writing: Public figures face intense scrutiny.
C1.mistake: Verb "scrutinize"; unzählbar.

C1.def: swimming underwater with air tanks
C1.example: She loves scuba diving.
C1.ielts_writing: Scuba diving requires training.
C1.mistake: "scuba" steht für "self-contained underwater breathing apparatus"; Unterschied zu "snorkeling".

C1.def: an artist who makes three-dimensional works
C1.example: The sculptor carved a marble figure.
C1.ielts_writing: A famous sculptor designed the monument.
C1.mistake: Nomen "sculpture"; Verb "sculpt".

C1.def: having a bluish-green color
C1.example: She painted the wall sea-green.
C1.ielts_writing: The sea-green dress matched her eyes.
C1.mistake: Meist mit Bindestrich; Nomen: "sea green".

C1.def: to close tightly, or an official stamp or animal
C1.example: Seal the envelope before mailing.
C1.ielts_writing: The deal was sealed with a handshake.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "seal the deal" bedeutet "den Deal besiegeln"; auch Tier.

C1.def: depending on or typical of a season
C1.example: Seasonal workers pick the fruit.
C1.ielts_writing: Seasonal changes affect sales.
C1.mistake: Nomen "season"; Gegenteil: "year-round".

C1.def: a plant that grows in the sea
C1.example: Seaweed washed up on the beach.
C1.ielts_writing: Seaweed is used in sushi.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Wortteile: "sea" und "weed".

C1.def: to produce a liquid in the body
C1.example: The gland secretes a hormone.
C1.ielts_writing: Plants secrete a sticky fluid.
C1.mistake: Nomen "secretion"; "secrete" kann auch "verbergen" bedeuten.

C1.def: tending to hide information
C1.example: He was secretive about his plans.
C1.ielts_writing: The secretive company refused to comment.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "secretive ABOUT sth"; abwertend.

C1.def: not connected with religion
C1.example: The country has a secular government.
C1.ielts_writing: Secular schools do not teach religion.
C1.mistake: Nomen "secularism"; Gegenteil: "religious".

C1.def: involving much sitting and little exercise
C1.example: He has a sedentary job.
C1.ielts_writing: A sedentary lifestyle harms health.
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe; Gegenteil: "active".

C1.def: appearing to be so
C1.example: The task seemed seemingly impossible.
C1.ielts_writing: She seemingly forgot the meeting.
C1.mistake: Verb "seem"; steht oft vor Adjektiv.

C1.def: a part into which something is divided
C1.example: The show has a funny segment.
C1.ielts_writing: The company targets a new market segment.
C1.mistake: Verb "segment"; Betonung beim Verb hinten.

C1.def: the separation of people into groups
C1.example: Racial segregation was outlawed.
C1.ielts_writing: The city fought school segregation.
C1.mistake: Verb "segregate"; Gegenteil: "integration".

C1.def: to take hold of something suddenly or by force
C1.example: Police seized the drugs.
C1.ielts_writing: She seized the chance to speak.
C1.mistake: Nomen "seizure"; Regel: "i before e except after c" gilt hier nicht.

C1.def: not often
C1.example: He seldom visits us.
C1.ielts_writing: She is seldom late.
C1.mistake: Steht vor dem Verb, nicht danach; Verneinung nicht nötig.

C1.def: choosing carefully
C1.example: The college is highly selective.
C1.ielts_writing: She is selective about her friends.
C1.mistake: Nomen "selection"; Konstruktion: "selective ABOUT sth".

C1.def: only interested in yourself
C1.example: He is a self-centered person.
C1.ielts_writing: Self-centered behavior drives friends away.
C1.mistake: Nicht "selbstbewusst"; Nomen "self-centeredness".

C1.def: nervous about how others see you
C1.example: He felt self-conscious on stage.
C1.ielts_writing: A self-conscious teenager avoided the camera.
C1.mistake: Nicht "selbstbewusst" (das ist "self-confident"); Konstruktion: "self-conscious ABOUT sth".

C1.def: able to work hard without being pushed
C1.example: She is a self-motivated learner.
C1.ielts_writing: Self-motivated employees need little supervision.
C1.mistake: Nomen "self-motivation"; häufig in Stellenanzeigen.

C1.def: to give information about yourself
C1.example: Participants self-report their sleep.
C1.ielts_writing: Patients often self-report symptoms.
C1.mistake: Auch Nomen "self-report"; in der Forschung häufig.

C1.def: where customers serve themselves
C1.example: The cafe has a self-service counter.
C1.ielts_writing: Self-service checkouts save time.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "full-service"; oft vor Nomen.

C1.def: a photo you take of yourself
C1.example: She took a selfie at the beach.
C1.ielts_writing: Selfies dominate social media.
C1.mistake: Plural "selfies"; "selfie stick" ist der Selfie-Stick.

C1.def: to sell all stock, or to betray your principles
C1.example: Tickets sell out fast.
C1.ielts_writing: The band sold out to commercial interests.
C1.mistake: Nomen "sellout"; Partizip "sold out" bedeutet "ausverkauft".

C1.def: a punctuation mark used between clauses
C1.example: Use a semicolon between related clauses.
C1.ielts_writing: Place a semicolon before a connector.
C1.mistake: Zeichen ";"; Plural "semicolons".

C1.def: a member of a senate
C1.example: The senator introduced a bill.
C1.ielts_writing: Senators debated the law.
C1.mistake: Nomen "senate"; Konstruktion: "senator FROM a state".

C1.def: an older person, usually over sixty-five
C1.example: Senior citizens receive discounts.
C1.ielts_writing: Many senior citizens live alone.
C1.mistake: Höfliche Bezeichnung; Plural "senior citizens".

C1.def: a physical feeling, or great public excitement
C1.example: She felt a burning sensation.
C1.ielts_writing: The film caused a sensation.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "sensational"; "sensation" nicht nur Aufsehen.

C1.def: the quality of being easily affected, or of caring about feelings
C1.example: He handled the issue with sensitivity.
C1.ielts_writing: Skin sensitivity varies from person to person.
C1.mistake: Nicht "Sensibilität" im Sinn von Gefühlsduselei; Adjektiv "sensitive".

C1.def: a view or feeling about something
C1.example: Public sentiment turned against the war.
C1.ielts_writing: I share your sentiment.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "sentimental"; "sentiment" meint Haltung, nicht nur Rührseligkeit.

C1.def: showing tender feelings, often too much
C1.example: He keeps the ring for sentimental reasons.
C1.ielts_writing: The film is too sentimental.
C1.mistake: "sentimental value" bedeutet "ideeller Wert"; Nomen "sentiment".

C1.def: the act of dividing or being apart
C1.example: The separation of church and state is key.
C1.ielts_writing: They announced their separation last year.
C1.mistake: Betonung beim Verb hinten, Aussprache "separate" /ˈsepəreɪt/.

C1.def: a book or film that continues an earlier story
C1.example: The sequel was released last year.
C1.ielts_writing: A sequel to the novel is planned.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "prequel"; Konstruktion: "sequel TO sth".

C1.def: happening in a series
C1.example: He is a serial entrepreneur.
C1.ielts_writing: Serial killers dominate crime stories.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A serial number is printed on it."
C1.mistake: Nicht "Cerealien" (cereal): gleiche Aussprache, andere Bedeutung.

C1.def: amounts of food for one person
C1.example: The recipe makes four servings.
C1.ielts_writing: Two servings of vegetables are advised.
C1.mistake: Singular "serving"; "serving size" ist die Portionsgröße.

C1.def: fixed or arranged in advance
C1.example: The set price is fifty dollars.
C1.ielts_writing: We have a set routine.
C1.mistake: "set in one's ways" bedeutet "festgefahren"; "all set" bedeutet "bereit".

C1.def: the way something is arranged or organized
C1.example: The set-up of the office is modern.
C1.ielts_writing: A quick set-up saves time.
C1.mistake: Verb "set up"; auch Falle: "It was a set-up".

C1.def: something that delays or reverses progress
C1.example: The injury was a major setback.
C1.ielts_writing: Setbacks teach resilience.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "a setback TO sth"; Plural "setbacks".

C1.def: stable and not changing
C1.example: The weather is settled.
C1.ielts_writing: She wanted a settled life.
C1.ielts_speaking: "They are settled in their new home."
C1.mistake: Verb "settle"; Gegenteil: "unsettled".

C1.def: an agreement ending a dispute, or a small community
C1.example: The parties reached a settlement.
C1.ielts_writing: A new settlement grew near the river.
C1.mistake: Verb "settle"; Plural "settlements".

C1.def: the activity of making things with needle and thread
C1.example: Sewing is her hobby.
C1.ielts_writing: She bought a sewing machine.
C1.mistake: Verb "sew" (Aussprache /soʊ/); nicht "sowing" (säen).

C1.def: a person's sexual orientation or capacity
C1.example: He talked about his sexuality openly.
C1.ielts_writing: Education about sexuality is important.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "sexual"; Betonung auf der vierten Silbe.

C1.def: worn-out and in poor condition
C1.example: He wore a shabby coat.
C1.ielts_writing: The shabby hotel needed repairs.
C1.mistake: Adverb "shabbily"; auch "unfair": "shabby treatment".

C1.def: to protect from light, or to darken
C1.example: Trees shade the street.
C1.ielts_writing: She shaded her eyes from the sun.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "shady" (schattig, zwielichtig); "shade of blue" bedeutet "Blauton".

C1.def: having an attractive shape
C1.example: She has shapely legs.
C1.ielts_writing: The vase is shapely and elegant.
C1.mistake: Nomen "shape"; häufig bei Beschreibungen von Körpern.

C1.def: a person who owns shares in a company
C1.example: Shareholders approved the merger.
C1.ielts_writing: Each shareholder receives a dividend.
C1.mistake: Synonym "stockholder"; Plural "shareholders".

C1.def: to break suddenly into small pieces
C1.example: The glass shattered on the floor.
C1.ielts_writing: The news shattered her hopes.
C1.mistake: Partizip "shattered" auch "am Boden zerstört".

C1.def: a piece of cloth worn around the shoulders
C1.example: She wore a wool shawl.
C1.ielts_writing: A shawl kept her warm.
C1.mistake: Plural "shawls"; größer als "scarf".

C1.def: to lose or drop something naturally
C1.example: Snakes shed their skin.
C1.ielts_writing: The company shed ten thousand jobs.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: shed, shed, shed; Idiom: "shed light on" bedeutet "Licht auf etwas werfen".

C1.def: nothing but, or very steep
C1.example: It was sheer luck.
C1.ielts_writing: A sheer cliff rose above us.
C1.mistake: Auch "hauchdünn" bei Stoffen; "sheer" verstärkt.

C1.def: something that protects against harm
C1.example: The riot police carried shields.
C1.ielts_writing: The law shields whistleblowers.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "shield sb FROM sth"; auch Verb.

C1.def: work done in scheduled periods, often at night
C1.example: Shift work disrupts sleep.
C1.ielts_writing: Nurses often do shift work.
C1.mistake: Person "shift worker"; Konstruktion: "work in shifts".

C1.def: the transport of goods, or the cost of sending them
C1.example: Shipping is free for orders over fifty dollars.
C1.ielts_writing: The shipping industry faces new rules.
C1.mistake: Verb "ship" (versenden); nicht nur per Schiff.

C1.def: to an extreme degree, used for fear
C1.example: The noise scared him shitless.
C1.ielts_writing: The film scared us shitless.
C1.mistake: Sehr vulgär; nur mit "scared" oder "bored".

C1.def: a quick shake of the body from cold or fear
C1.example: A shiver ran down her spine.
C1.ielts_writing: He shivered in the cold.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "shivery"; bei Kälte oder Angst.

C1.def: a cord used to fasten a shoe
C1.example: She tied her shoelace.
C1.ielts_writing: His shoelace came undone.
C1.mistake: Plural "shoelaces"; nicht "shoestring" (Budget).

C1.def: a new part growing from a plant, or to fire
C1.example: A green shoot appeared.
C1.ielts_writing: They shoot photos at dawn.
C1.mistake: Mehrere Bedeutungen: Spross, Dreh, schießen; "photo shoot" ist die Fotosession.

C1.def: to rise very fast
C1.example: Prices shoot up in summer.
C1.ielts_writing: Her hand shot up to answer.
C1.mistake: Auch derb für Drogeninjektion; Gegenteil: "plummet".

C1.def: a person who loves shopping too much
C1.example: She admits she is a shopaholic.
C1.ielts_writing: The shopaholic maxed out her cards.
C1.mistake: Zusammensetzung aus "shop" und "alcoholic"; scherzhaft.

C1.def: ready for construction to begin
C1.example: The city listed shovel-ready projects.
C1.ielts_writing: Shovel-ready plans speed up growth.
C1.mistake: Aus der US-Politik; meist bei Infrastruktur.

C1.def: a holy place connected with a saint or god
C1.example: Pilgrims visited the shrine.
C1.ielts_writing: A small shrine stood by the road.
C1.mistake: "shrine to sb" bedeutet "Gedenkstätte für jemanden"; Plural "shrines".

C1.def: to become smaller
C1.example: The shirt shrank in the wash.
C1.ielts_writing: Profits shrank last year.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: shrink, shrank, shrunk; Konstruktion: "shrink FROM sth".

C1.def: to raise the shoulders to show indifference
C1.example: She shrugged and walked away.
C1.ielts_writing: He shrugged off the criticism.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb: "shrug off" bedeutet "abtun".

C1.def: paid time off because of illness
C1.example: She is on sick leave.
C1.ielts_writing: Employees get ten days of sick leave.
C1.mistake: "on sick leave" bedeutet "krankgeschrieben"; unzählbar.

C1.def: an unwanted effect of a drug
C1.example: The pills have a side effect.
C1.ielts_writing: Side effects include nausea.
C1.mistake: Plural "side effects"; Konstruktion: "side effect OF a drug".

C1.def: to breathe out loudly to show tiredness
C1.example: She sighed with relief.
C1.ielts_writing: He sighed and closed the book.
C1.mistake: "sigh of relief" bedeutet "Seufzer der Erleichterung"; Aussprache wie "sigh" /saɪ/.

C1.def: able to see
C1.example: A sighted guide helped the hiker.
C1.ielts_writing: Sighted people rely on vision.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "blind"; Nomen "sight".

C1.def: to write your name to approve
C1.example: Please sign the form.
C1.ielts_writing: She signed the contract today.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verbs: "sign up" (anmelden), "sign in" (einloggen); Nomen "signature".

C1.def: to show clearly where something is
C1.example: The trail was signposted.
C1.ielts_writing: Authors signpost key ideas for readers.
C1.mistake: Auch Nomen "signpost" (Wegweiser); in Texten: "signposting".

C1.def: a dark outline against a light background
C1.example: A silhouette stood in the window.
C1.ielts_writing: The dress shows off her silhouette.
C1.ielts_speaking: "We saw the silhouette of the mountains."
C1.mistake: Betonung auf der dritten Silbe; "in silhouette" bedeutet "als Umriss".

C1.def: to cook gently just below boiling
C1.example: Let the sauce simmer.
C1.ielts_writing: Anger simmered beneath the surface.
C1.mistake: "simmer down" bedeutet "sich beruhigen".

C1.def: to imitate a real process
C1.example: The program can simulate a flood.
C1.ielts_writing: Pilots simulate emergencies in training.
C1.mistake: Nomen "simulation"; Partizip "simulated" (künstlich).

C1.def: a computer model or practice copy of reality
C1.example: The simulation predicted the outcome.
C1.ielts_writing: Flight simulations train pilots.
C1.mistake: Verb "simulate"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: happening at the same time
C1.example: The two events were simultaneous.
C1.ielts_writing: Simultaneous translation is difficult.
C1.mistake: Adverb "simultaneously"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: at the same time
C1.example: She works and studies simultaneously.
C1.ielts_writing: Both teams scored simultaneously.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "simultaneous"; steht oft am Satzende.

C1.def: an act that breaks moral or religious law
C1.example: Pride is considered a sin.
C1.ielts_writing: He sinned and asked forgiveness.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "sinful"; Person "sinner".

C1.def: to go down below the surface
C1.example: The ship sank in the storm.
C1.ielts_writing: Her heart sank at the news.
C1.mistake: Unregelmäßig: sink, sank, sunk; "sink in" bedeutet "ins Bewusstsein dringen".

C1.def: like or typical of a sister
C1.example: She gave him sisterly advice.
C1.ielts_writing: A sisterly bond connected them.
C1.mistake: Nomen "sister"; "sisterhood" bedeutet "Schwesternschaft".

C1.def: in a particular place
C1.example: The hotel is situated by the lake.
C1.ielts_writing: The village is situated in a valley.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "situated IN/ON/NEAR"; formeller als "located".

C1.def: a quick rough drawing
C1.example: He made a sketch of the building.
C1.ielts_writing: A comedy sketch made the crowd laugh.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "sketchy" (ungenau, dubios); auch Sketch im TV.

C1.def: fitting very closely to the body
C1.example: She wore skintight jeans.
C1.ielts_writing: A skintight suit helped swimmers.
C1.mistake: Meist bei Kleidung; Gegenteil: "baggy".

C1.def: to miss something deliberately, or to move lightly
C1.example: Don't skip breakfast.
C1.ielts_writing: He skipped class to study.
C1.mistake: Auch "seilspringen": "skip rope"; Phrasal verb: "skip over".

C1.def: a small black and white animal that sprays a bad smell
C1.example: A skunk sprayed the dog.
C1.ielts_writing: The skunk left a terrible smell.
C1.mistake: Plural "skunks"; Verb "to skunk" (hoch besiegen).

C1.def: light blue like a clear sky
C1.example: She wore a sky-blue shirt.
C1.ielts_writing: The room was painted sky-blue.
C1.mistake: Meist mit Bindestrich; Nomen "sky blue".

C1.def: to shut or hit with great force
C1.example: He slammed the door.
C1.ielts_writing: The critic slammed the film.
C1.mistake: Auch "scharf kritisieren"; "poetry slam" ist ein Dichterwettstreit.

C1.def: very informal words used by a group
C1.example: Teenagers use a lot of slang.
C1.ielts_writing: The slang term spread quickly.
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; Plural selten.

C1.def: to hit with the flat of the hand
C1.example: She slapped his face.
C1.ielts_writing: He slapped her on the back.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "slap on the wrist" bedeutet "milde Strafe"; Nomen "slap".

C1.def: a sloping line, or to cut with a quick stroke
C1.example: Use a slash between the two words.
C1.ielts_writing: The company slashed prices.
C1.mistake: "forward slash" ist "/"; "backslash" ist "\".

C1.def: the practice of owning people as property
C1.example: Slavery was abolished in 1865.
C1.ielts_writing: Many fought to end slavery.
C1.mistake: Nomen "slave"; "wage slavery" ist Lohnsklaverei.

C1.def: without sleeves
C1.example: She wore a sleeveless dress.
C1.ielts_writing: A sleeveless top suits warm weather.
C1.mistake: Nomen "sleeve"; Gegenteil: "long-sleeved".

C1.def: gracefully thin, or small in amount
C1.example: She has a slender figure.
C1.ielts_writing: The team won by a slender margin.
C1.mistake: Positiver als "skinny"; "slender chance" bedeutet "geringe Chance".

C1.def: a narrow opening, or a time period set aside
C1.example: Insert a coin in the slot.
C1.ielts_writing: We have a slot at three o'clock.
C1.mistake: Auch "slot machine" (Spielautomat); bei Terminen: "free slot".

C1.def: to break violently into pieces
C1.example: The thief smashed the window.
C1.ielts_writing: The ball smashed into the wall.
C1.mistake: "smash hit" bedeutet "Riesenerfolg"; Nomen "smash".

C1.def: a long reptile without legs
C1.example: A snake slid through the grass.
C1.ielts_writing: The road snaked up the hill.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "snake in the grass" bedeutet "falscher Freund".

C1.def: to break with a sharp sound, or to speak sharply
C1.example: The twig snapped under his foot.
C1.ielts_writing: She snapped at her brother.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb: "snap out of it" bedeutet "sich zusammenreißen"; "in a snap" bedeutet "im Nu".

C1.def: to swim with a tube and mask
C1.example: They snorkel in the reef.
C1.ielts_writing: We snorkeled in clear water.
C1.mistake: Nomen "snorkel"; "go snorkeling" als Aktivität.

C1.def: completely white like snow
C1.example: She wore a snow-white dress.
C1.ielts_writing: The snow-white cat sat on the sill.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "jet-black"; Mit Bindestrich als Adjektiv.

C1.def: a deep pile of snow blown by the wind
C1.example: A snowdrift blocked the road.
C1.ielts_writing: Cars were stuck in the snowdrift.
C1.mistake: Plural "snowdrifts"; nicht "snowbank" (aufgeschobener Schnee).

C1.def: a small white flower that blooms in late winter
C1.example: A snowdrop pushed through the snow.
C1.ielts_writing: Snowdrops bloom in February.
C1.mistake: Plural "snowdrops"; blüht sehr früh im Jahr.

C1.def: a vehicle that clears snow from roads
C1.example: A snowplow cleared the street.
C1.ielts_writing: The snowplow was out all night.
C1.mistake: Schreibweise mit "plow", nicht "plough".

C1.def: to put something in liquid so it becomes wet
C1.example: Soak the beans overnight.
C1.ielts_writing: The rain soaked her clothes.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb: "soak up" bedeutet "aufsaugen"; "soaked" bedeutet "klitschnass".

C1.def: to rise high or increase quickly
C1.example: Eagles soar above the mountains.
C1.ielts_writing: Prices soared last year.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "soaring"; Gegenteil: "plunge".

C1.def: a sad story told to get sympathy
C1.example: He gave us a sob story.
C1.ielts_writing: Don't fall for his sob story.
C1.ielts_speaking: "She told a sob story to get help."
C1.mistake: Abwertend; meist von jemandem, der Mitleid erregen will.

C1.def: the state of being cut off from society
C1.example: Social exclusion affects the poor.
C1.ielts_writing: Policies aim to reduce social exclusion.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "social inclusion"; Verb "exclude".

C1.def: a system where means of production are owned by the community
C1.example: Socialism emphasizes equality.
C1.ielts_writing: Debates about socialism shape politics.
C1.ielts_speaking: "Democratic socialism is popular in some countries."
C1.mistake: Person "socialist"; Gegenteil: "capitalism".

C1.def: supporting or based on socialism
C1.example: The party has a socialist platform.
C1.ielts_writing: Socialist ideas spread in the nineteenth century.
C1.mistake: Nomen "socialism"; auch Nomen "socialist" (Anhänger).

C1.def: relating to the study of society
C1.example: She wrote a sociological study.
C1.ielts_writing: Sociological research examines inequality.
C1.mistake: Nomen "sociology"; Betonung auf der vierten Silbe.

C1.def: a device that turns sunlight into electricity
C1.example: A solar cell converts sunlight into power.
C1.ielts_writing: Solar cells are getting cheaper.
C1.mistake: Auch "photovoltaic cell"; Plural "solar cells".

C1.def: only one
C1.example: She is the sole heir.
C1.ielts_writing: His sole concern was safety.
C1.mistake: Nicht "soul" (Seele) oder "sole" (Schuhsohle); Adverb "solely".

C1.def: only and nothing else
C1.example: The decision rests solely with her.
C1.ielts_writing: He works solely for money.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "sole"; Konstruktion: "solely FOR sth".

C1.def: a lawyer who prepares legal documents and advises clients
C1.example: A solicitor drafted the contract.
C1.ielts_writing: She consulted a solicitor about the will.
C1.mistake: Synonym "attorney"; Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

C1.def: a substance that is not liquid or gas
C1.example: Ice is a solid.
C1.ielts_writing: The table is made of solid oak.
C1.mistake: Nomen "solidity"; Gegenteil: "liquid".

C1.def: unity among people with shared interests
C1.example: They showed solidarity with the strikers.
C1.ielts_writing: Solidarity can unite a community.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "solidarity WITH sb"; Betonung auf der dritten Silbe.

C1.def: a performance by one person, or done alone
C1.example: She sang a solo.
C1.ielts_writing: He took a solo trip around the world.
C1.mistake: Person "soloist"; Plural "solos".

C1.def: the longest or shortest day of the year
C1.example: The summer solstice falls in June.
C1.ielts_writing: The winter solstice is the shortest day.
C1.mistake: Gegenteil: "equinox" (Tagundnachtgleiche).

C1.def: to calm or ease pain
C1.example: A warm bath soothes tired muscles.
C1.ielts_writing: She soothed the crying baby.
C1.mistake: Aussprache mit stimmhaftem "th"; Adjektiv "soothing".

C1.def: the spiritual part of a person
C1.example: He put his heart and soul into it.
C1.ielts_writing: Music feeds the soul.
C1.mistake: "not a soul" bedeutet "keine Menschenseele"; Genre "soul".

C1.def: in good condition or based on good judgment
C1.example: He gave sound advice.
C1.ielts_writing: The building is structurally sound.
C1.mistake: Auch Nomen "sound" (Geräusch); "sound asleep" bedeutet "tief schlafend".

C1.def: having supreme power or independence
C1.example: The country is a sovereign state.
C1.ielts_writing: Sovereign nations can set their own laws.
C1.mistake: Nomen "sovereignty"; auch Nomen "sovereign" (Herrscher).

C1.def: supreme authority over a territory
C1.example: The treaty respects national sovereignty.
C1.ielts_writing: They fought for sovereignty over the islands.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "sovereignty OVER a territory"; Adjektiv "sovereign".

C1.def: a spacecraft that can be reused
C1.example: The space shuttle landed safely.
C1.ielts_writing: Astronauts flew on the space shuttle.
C1.mistake: Plural "space shuttles"; Programm endete 2011.

C1.def: to send unwanted messages in bulk
C1.example: Marketers spam our inboxes.
C1.ielts_writing: Bots spam the comment section.
C1.mistake: Nomen "spam"; Person "spammer".

C1.def: to extend across a period or area
C1.example: Her career spans forty years.
C1.ielts_writing: A bridge spans the river.
C1.mistake: Nomen: "attention span" ist Aufmerksamkeitsspanne.

C1.def: extra and not in use, or to keep from harm
C1.example: I have a spare key.
C1.ielts_writing: The judge spared his life.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "spare no expense" bedeutet "keine Kosten scheuen"; Verb auch "verschonen".

C1.def: time that is not used for work
C1.example: She paints in her spare time.
C1.ielts_writing: Spare time is limited for students.
C1.ielts_speaking: "What do you do in your spare time?"
C1.mistake: Unzählbar; "in your spare time" ist die typische Frage.

C1.def: to cause something to start
C1.example: The comment sparked a debate.
C1.ielts_writing: Dry grass can spark a fire.
C1.mistake: Auch Nomen "spark" (Funke); Konstruktion: "spark sth off".

C1.def: very simple and without comfort
C1.example: The room was spartan.
C1.ielts_writing: They lived a spartan life.
C1.mistake: Kleingeschrieben im allgemeinen Gebrauch; Herkunft: Sparta.

C1.def: a weapon with a long pole and sharp point
C1.example: He threw a spear.
C1.ielts_writing: Hunters carried spears.
C1.ielts_speaking: "A spear was found at the site."
C1.mistake: Verb "spear" (aufspießen); Plural "spears".

C1.def: trained or designed for a particular purpose
C1.example: She has a specialized degree.
C1.ielts_writing: The firm sells specialized equipment.
C1.mistake: Verb "specialize IN sth"; Nomen "specialist".

C1.def: something a person or place does best
C1.example: Pasta is the house specialty.
C1.ielts_writing: Her specialty is eye surgery.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "specialty OF the house"; Plural "specialties".

C1.def: a detailed description of requirements
C1.example: The product meets the specification.
C1.ielts_writing: The specifications list every part.
C1.mistake: Verb "specify"; Plural "specifications" (kurz: "specs").

C1.def: a sample used as an example or for tests
C1.example: The lab examined a blood specimen.
C1.ielts_writing: A rare specimen of the plant was found.
C1.mistake: Plural "specimens"; auch "a fine specimen" (ein Prachtexemplar).

C1.def: an impressive public display
C1.example: The fireworks were a spectacle.
C1.ielts_writing: The parade was a grand spectacle.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "make a spectacle of oneself" bedeutet "sich zum Gespött machen".

C1.def: a range of different things
C1.example: The party covers the political spectrum.
C1.ielts_writing: Colors form a spectrum.
C1.mistake: Plural "spectra" oder "spectrums"; Betonung auf der ersten Silbe.

C1.def: based on guesses rather than facts
C1.example: It was a speculative investment.
C1.ielts_writing: The report was purely speculative.
C1.mistake: Verb "speculate"; Nomen "speculation".

C1.def: unable to speak because of strong emotion
C1.example: She was speechless with joy.
C1.ielts_writing: The news left him speechless.
C1.mistake: Konstruktion: "speechless WITH sth"; Nomen "speech".

C1.def: a fast motorboat
C1.example: They rented a speedboat.
C1.ielts_writing: A speedboat raced across the bay.
C1.mistake: Plural "speedboats"; Gegenteil: "sailboat".

C1.def: a short period, or a magic charm
C1.example: A cold spell hit the city.
C1.ielts_writing: The witch cast a spell.
C1.mistake: Phrasal verb: "spell out" bedeutet "deutlich erklären"; Verb "spell" (buchstabieren).

C1.def: an area of activity or influence
C1.example: He is famous in the political sphere.
C1.ielts_writing: The sphere of influence grew.
C1.mistake: Auch Kugel; Adjektiv "spherical".

C1.def: to turn quickly around
C1.example: The top spun on the table.
C1.ielts_writing: The company put a positive spin on the news.
C1.mistake: Idiom: "spin doctor" bedeutet "PR-Berater"; Unregelmäßig: spin, spun, spun.

C1.def: the row of bones along the back, or a book's edge
C1.example: She injured her spine.
C1.ielts_writing: A shiver ran down his spine.
C1.mistake: Adjektiv "spinal"; Plural "spines".

C1.def: a curve that winds around a center
C1.example: A spiral staircase led upstairs.
